thesis.insider_ownership: Founder Mariusz Tuchlin controls approximately 77.33% of voting rights through the OMT Family Foundation, making Dekpol a tightly founder-controlled company ([BiznesRadar](https://www.biznesradar.pl/akcjonariat/DEKPOL))
thesis.red_flags: Very high insider/founder ownership concentration (~77% of votes via a family foundation) leaves a thin free float and limited minority-shareholder influence. No other red flags identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Croatian universal commercial bank (founded October 1991, originally by Croatian Post) offering retail, corporate and public-sector banking products, distinguished by a distribution network combining its own branches (68 as of March 2024) with financial-service counters located in Croatian Post offices nationwide.
thesis.competitive_position: The largest financial institution in Croatian domestic ownership, with total assets of €7.046bn and net income of €80.6M (2023); its unique Croatian Post branch-network partnership gives it Croatia's largest basic-banking-services distribution footprint versus foreign-owned competitor banks.
thesis.main_shareholders: Republic of Croatia (42.43% direct, ~74.57% combined with state-owned entities), Croatian Post (11.93%), State Agency for Deposit Insurance and Bank Resolution (8.98%), Croatian Pension Insurance Institute (8.76%); state directly/indirectly owns ~77% ([HPB Annual Report 2024](https://www.hpb.hr/UserDocsImages/Financijska-izvjesca/Annual%20Report%20-%2031.12.2024.pdf))
thesis.red_flags: Majority state ownership (~77% direct/indirect via the Republic of Croatia and state entities) creates governance considerations typical of state-controlled banks, including potential political influence over strategy; no specific litigation or compliance issue identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: LEWAG Holding Aktiengesellschaft is a German management/financial holding company based in Beverungen, whose main asset is a 100% stake in HEGLA GmbH & Co. KG, a producer of machines and systems for glass cutting, sorting, storage, and logistics, together with other German and international subsidiaries. [LEWAG company profile](https://www.lewag.de/pdf/jahres_kja_2022_lewag_holding_ag.pdf)
thesis.competitive_position: Through its HEGLA subsidiary, LEWAG holds a position as a specialist supplier of flat-glass cutting, sorting, and automation machinery -- a niche industrial equipment maker rather than a diversified conglomerate; no independent market-share figures were found to size this position precisely. [Westfalen-Blatt: LEWAG-HEGLA growth course](https://www.westfalen-blatt.de/owl/kreis-hoexter/beverungen/lewag-hegla-konzern-hauptversammlung-wachstumskurs-3013279)
thesis.main_shareholders: HELVEJOS Beteiligungs GmbH holds approximately 70.28% of LEWAG Holding; individual shareholders Jochen H. Hesselbach (~16.56%) and Jörn C. Hesselbach (~10%) are also named holders, with Carsten Beckenbach holding a minimal stake (~0.02%). [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/de/capital-goods/fra-kgr/lewag-holding-shares/ownership)
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is high and family-linked: Jörn C. Hesselbach (Chairman since June 2023) and Jochen H. Hesselbach together hold roughly 26.5% directly, in addition to their apparent interest in the controlling holder HELVEJOS Beteiligungs GmbH (~70.28%); board member Carsten Beckenbach holds a small stake. [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/de/capital-goods/fra-kgr/lewag-holding-shares/ownership)
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources searched.

thesis.business_description: Viscom SE is a German developer and manufacturer of optical and X-ray inspection systems (plus related software and services) used in automotive electronics, industrial/consumer electronics, aerospace, medical technology and telecommunications manufacturing, headquartered in Hanover.
thesis.competitive_position: A specialist inspection-systems maker for electronics manufacturing (founded 1984); recently converted its legal form to a European SE; FY2025 revenue of EUR 81.7 million came with a negative EBIT of approximately EUR -1.8 million, driven by elevated inventories and currency effects, indicating cyclical/margin pressure in its niche. [Viscom press release](https://www.viscom.com/en-us/company/press/press-releases/detail/viscom-completes-change-of-legal-form-to-a-european-company-societas-europaea-se/)
thesis.main_shareholders: HPC Vermögensverwaltung GmbH (controlled by Managing Directors Martin Heuser and Volker Pape) holds approximately 53.98% of voting rights; Martin Heuser separately holds approximately 3.43% and rubicon equities GmbH approximately 2.95%. [Northdata/HPC Vermögensverwaltung](https://www.northdata.com/HPC%20Verm%C3%B6gensverwaltung%20GmbH,%20Hannover/HRB%2059094)
thesis.insider_ownership: High insider/control-vehicle ownership: HPC Vermögensverwaltung GmbH, run by insiders Martin Heuser and Volker Pape, controls approximately 54% of voting rights, with Heuser holding a further ~3.4% personally. [Northdata](https://www.northdata.com/HPC%20Verm%C3%B6gensverwaltung%20GmbH,%20Hannover/HRB%2059094)
thesis.red_flags: FY2025 results showed a negative EBIT of approximately EUR -1.8 million against EUR 81.7 million revenue, attributed to high material inventories and adverse currency effects - a profitability concern worth monitoring, though not a governance or fraud red flag. No governance disputes or auditor concerns were found.

thesis.business_description: OVB Holding AG (Cologne, Germany) is a pan-European independent financial advisory/broker group providing retail clients with insurance, pension and investment product intermediation through a network of self-employed financial advisors.
thesis.competitive_position: OVB describes itself as one of Europe's leading independent financial advisory groups, operating in 15 European countries via roughly 5,000+ financial advisors serving millions of clients, working with over 100 product providers rather than manufacturing products itself - a distribution/broker model rather than a product-risk-bearing one. [OVB 2016 Fact Sheet](https://www.ovb.eu/fileadmin/assets/Dokumente/ovb_holding/factsheets/2016_OVB_Fact_Sheet_E.pdf)
thesis.main_shareholders: As of a 31 December 2015 fact sheet, the largest holders were Basler Beteiligungsholding (~32.6%), IDUNA Vereinigte Lebensversicherung (~31.7%), Balance Vermittlungs- und Beteiligungs-AG (~17.5%) and Generali Lebensversicherung AG (~11.5%), with free float around 3% ([OVB 2016 Fact Sheet](https://www.ovb.eu/fileadmin/assets/Dokumente/ovb_holding/factsheets/2016_OVB_Fact_Sheet_E.pdf)). These figures are a decade old; a current shareholder notification was not located in this search and should be checked directly.
thesis.insider_ownership: No management/board insider ownership percentage was found in search results; the disclosed large holders are insurance-company/holding-company shareholders rather than named individual executives. Not disclosed in public filings found.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in this search.

thesis.business_description: German manufacturer (since 1962) of structured glass, glass-silicon and quartz wafers used in MEMS and microsystems technology, serving consumer electronics, automotive, aerospace and pharma industries via subsidiaries Little Things Factory GmbH and MMT GmbH.
thesis.competitive_position: Described as the world's leading manufacturer of glass/glass-silicon/quartz wafers for MEMS applications; completed an uplisting to Frankfurt's General Standard segment and IFRS transition in 2025, simplifying its corporate structure under a single Planoptik brand.
thesis.main_shareholders: Specific named holders not found in available sources beyond an aggregate insider figure; company has ~4.5 million shares outstanding ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/PLANOPTIK-AG-477350/company/))
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider shareholders hold approximately 60.46% of shares outstanding ([extraETF](https://extraetf.com/de/stock-profile/DE000A0HGQS8))
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; note recent corporate restructuring (divestiture of AIRTUNE GmbH, Dec 2025) and accounting-standard transition to IFRS.

thesis.business_description: Oeneo SA is a French company and self-described world No.1 in cooperage for winemaking and world No.2 in wine-bottle closures, operating via two segments: Closures (including its DIAM technology) and Barrels (ageing solutions for wine and spirits). [Cork Maker Regains Sparkle - Wine-Searcher](https://www.wine-searcher.com/m/2012/10/cork-maker-oeneo-diam-closures-success)
thesis.competitive_position: Oeneo holds global leadership positions in both wine barrel cooperage (No.1) and wine closures (No.2, via its patented DIAM cork-alternative technology), giving it a scale/technology moat in a specialized wine- and spirits-industry supply niche. [Wine-Searcher: Cork Maker Regains Sparkle](https://www.wine-searcher.com/m/2012/10/cork-maker-oeneo-diam-closures-success)
thesis.main_shareholders: Andromède SAS (controlled by the Hériard Dubreuil family) holds a controlling stake, historically built up to approximately 63.1%-71.6% of Oeneo's capital and voting rights through its subsidiary Caspar; other shareholders include Tetragon Partners UK LLP (~17.59%) and Lazard Frères Gestion SAS (~2.06%). [MarketScreener shareholders](https://in.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/OENEO-151073694/company-shareholders/)
thesis.insider_ownership: The Hériard Dubreuil family, via Andromède SAS/Caspar, is the controlling insider shareholder, holding a majority stake (reported between ~63% and ~72% depending on the date) and having previously launched a tender offer with squeeze-out procedure for remaining shares, overseen by an independent expert (Eight Advisory). [Caspar tender offer filing](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Caspar-has-filed-a-draft-simplified-tender-offer-for-Oeneo-shares-with-the-AMF-29707871/)
thesis.red_flags: Oeneo was subject to a simplified tender offer plus potential squeeze-out by its controlling shareholder (Caspar/Andromède, Hériard Dubreuil family); an independent expert and ad hoc board committee were used to assess fairness, which is a standard minority-protection process but worth noting as a controlling-shareholder related transaction. [Tender offer and squeeze-out details](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Caspar-has-filed-a-draft-simplified-tender-offer-for-Oeneo-shares-with-the-AMF-29707871/)

thesis.business_description: Card Factory plc is a UK-based specialist retailer of greeting cards, gifts and celebration essentials, operating through store, online (including Getting Personal), partnership and in-house print (Printcraft) channels.
thesis.competitive_position: Card Factory holds a dominant roughly 33% volume share of the GBP 1.3 billion UK greeting card market (around 20% by value given its low-price positioning), nearly triple its nearest specialist rival, underpinned by producing about 80% of its cards in UK facilities allowing price leadership from 29p while preserving margins. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/card-factory-shares-drop-on-profit-warning-issue-amid-weak-uk-footfall-ce7d50dbd08bf52d)
thesis.main_shareholders: Major institutional holders include Invesco (~27%), Artemis Investment Management (~12%, also cited at ~6.1% in another breakdown), Old Mutual Global Investors (~10%), Aberforth Partners (~10.02%), and BBFIT Investments Pte Ltd (~8.145%). [MarketScreener](https://uk.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/CARD-FACTORY-PLC-16490238/company-shareholders/)
thesis.insider_ownership: No evidence of significant founder/management insider ownership was found; the register is dominated by institutional fund managers rather than board/founder stakes. Not disclosed as a meaningful insider stake in sources reviewed.
thesis.red_flags: The company issued a profit warning in December 2025, cutting adjusted pretax profit guidance for FY2026 to GBP 55-60 million (down from prior guidance of mid-to-high single-digit growth off GBP 66.0 million FY2025), citing weak UK high-street footfall; shares fell around 22% on the announcement. [AJ Bell](https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/card-factory-shares-drop-profit-warning-issue-amid-weak-uk-footfall)

thesis.business_description: Platzer Fastigheter Holding AB is a Gothenburg-based Swedish commercial real estate company that owns, manages and develops office, retail and other commercial properties primarily in the Gothenburg region; founded in 1969.
thesis.competitive_position: Platzer is a regionally-focused commercial landlord concentrated in the Gothenburg metropolitan area, giving it local market knowledge and relationships versus nationally-diversified Swedish REITs, though this also concentrates its risk to one regional economy. [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/real-estate-management-and-development/sto-plaz-b/platzer-fastigheter-holding-shares/ownership)
thesis.main_shareholders: Ernström & Co AB ~15% (~18m shares); Familjen Hielte/Hobohm (a family holding entity) ~14.5-14.7% (~17.3m shares); Länsförsäkringar Göteborg och Bohuslän ~13.7% (~16.4m shares); Länsförsäkringar Fondförvaltning AB ~7.2%; Lf Skaraborg Förvaltning AB ~5.4%. Top 25 shareholders own ~85% of the company. [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/real-estate-management-and-development/sto-plaz-b/platzer-fastigheter-holding-shares/ownership)
thesis.insider_ownership: Individual insider ownership is reported as under 1% of the register by Simply Wall St's category breakdown; recent disclosed insider transactions include Karoliina Callavik selling ~171,000 shares (May 2025) and Henrik Schoultz buying 2,500 shares (July 2025). No evidence found linking the 'Platzer' name itself to a controlling family stake distinct from Ernström & Co or Familjen Hielte/Hobohm. [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/real-estate-management-and-development/sto-plaz-b/platzer-fastigheter-holding-shares/ownership)
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Aspo Oyj is a Finland-based conglomerate (holding company) that owns and develops several business-to-business brands, including ESL Shipping (dry bulk shipping), Leipurin (bakery ingredients), Telko (plastics/chemicals distribution), and Kaukomarkkinat. [Aspo Oyj company overview](https://www.aspo.com/)
thesis.competitive_position: Aspo is a diversified Nordic industrial/trading conglomerate whose segments each hold established regional positions (e.g., ESL Shipping in Baltic/Nordic dry bulk shipping); the company recently approved a demerger plan to separate ESL Shipping (in which Aspo holds a 78.6% stake) into its own independently listed company, a structural unbundling intended to let the market value each business more clearly. [Aspo stock exchange release: ESL Shipping demerger plan](https://www.aspo.com/stock-exchange-releases/inside-information-the-board-of-directors-of-aspo-plc-has-approved-a-demerger-plan-concerning-the-separation-of-esl-shipping-into-a-new-listed-company-3337215)
thesis.main_shareholders: Major shareholders include the Nyberg Family (~10.86%), AEV Capital Holding Oy (~10.49%), pension insurer Keskinäinen Työeläkevakuutusyhtiö Varma (~4.53%), Tapio Vehmas (~4.06%), and pension insurer Keskinäinen Eläkevakuutusyhtiö Ilmarinen (~2.79%). [MarketScreener shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ASPO-OYJ-1412432/company/)
thesis.insider_ownership: The Nyberg family is the largest named insider/founder-linked holder at approximately 10.86%; individual holder Tapio Vehmas (~4.06%) is also a notable named shareholder, though overall insider concentration is moderate compared to many other companies in this batch. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ASPO-OYJ-1412432/company/)
thesis.red_flags: Aspo disclosed that its ESL Shipping and Leipurin units suspended/reduced operations in Russia following the 2022 invasion of Ukraine (a disclosed compliance action, not a governance scandal); no lawsuit or fraud allegation was identified in the sources searched. [Leave Russia tracker: Aspo](https://leave-russia.org/aspo)

thesis.business_description: French software company (headquartered in Boulogne-Billancourt) providing an AI-native Order-to-Cash (O2C) SaaS platform - including AI agent 'Aimie' - that predicts customer payment behavior, automates cash-collection and dematerializes B2B transactions.
thesis.competitive_position: Positioned by Gartner as a Leader in the Magic Quadrant for Invoice-to-Cash applications; global leader in AI-powered Order-to-Cash software with clients in 85+ countries; 2025 revenue of €61.4M with North America now 30% of subscription revenue, and management targeting €18-23M in AI-native revenue with 185-215% CAGR through 2030.
thesis.main_shareholders: Olivier Novasque (founder/CEO, 37.8%, 533,844 shares), Herald Investment Management Ltd (3.98%), Deka Investment GmbH (2.83%); top 16 shareholders own 48.76% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/fr/software/epa-albfr/sidetrade-shares/ownership))
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder and CEO Olivier Novasque holds approximately 37.8% of shares, giving him effective control ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/fr/software/epa-albfr/sidetrade-shares/ownership))
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Transilvania Broker de Asigurare S.A. is a Romanian insurance brokerage, intermediating insurance policies (life, health, property/casualty) between insurers and retail/corporate clients, listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange (BVB) since November 2017.
thesis.competitive_position: TBK is one of the larger independent insurance brokers listed on the Romanian market; it recently attracted a strategic Czech financial-services acquirer (Partners Financial Services), signaling perceived value in its distribution network within the Romanian insurance intermediation market. [Forbes Romania on PFS majority stake](https://www.forbes.ro/?p=521261)
thesis.main_shareholders: Partners Financial Services a.s. (Czech Republic) is now the majority shareholder, having raised its stake from 39.09% to 53.24% of share capital and voting rights (per a September 2026 BVB filing) ([BVB current report](https://m.bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/TBK_20260827164403_TBK-Raport-Semestrul-I-2026.pdf)); it initially acquired ~32.89% in July 2024 by buying shares from founders Gabriel Login and Dan Niculae ([Ziarul Financiar](https://www.zf.ro/burse-fonduri-mutuale/bursa-mesajul-cehilor-care-au-devenit-actionari-majoritari-ai-22428555)).
thesis.insider_ownership: Co-founders Gabriel Login and Dan Niculae remain minority holders after selling down: Login's stake fell from 36.14% to about 14.14% and Niculae's from 15.69% to about 9.79% following the July 2024 sale to Partners Financial Services ([Ziarul Financiar](https://www.zf.ro/burse-fonduri-mutuale/bursa-login-gabriel-si-niculae-dan-actionarii-semnificativi-ai-22425950)).
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; no litigation or governance dispute was found connecting Transilvania Broker or Partners Financial Services (note: unrelated company SIF Transilvania has an extensive, well-documented litigation history, but this does not pertain to Transilvania Broker de Asigurare - the two are separate entities despite similar names).

thesis.business_description: German family-run bank (founded 1983 by Uto Baader) providing market making, capital markets/IPO advisory, multi-asset brokerage, asset management services, banking services and research, headquartered in Unterschleißheim.
thesis.competitive_position: A local broker/market maker in the DACH region acting as lead broker for quoting and executing orders across 800,000+ financial instruments; total assets of €3.235bn and 677 employees (2025), positioning it as a niche capital-markets infrastructure player rather than a universal bank.
thesis.main_shareholders: Baader family (via Baader Beteiligungs AG) controls 71.7% of shares; remainder held by private/institutional investors and management/employees ([Grokipedia/company disclosures](https://www.baaderbank.de/en/about-us/investor-relations/equity-story))
thesis.insider_ownership: Baader family controls approximately 71.7% of shares; founder Uto Baader handed management to son Nico Baader in July 2015 ([Baader Bank](https://www.baaderbank.de/en/about-us/investor-relations/equity-story))
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; concentrated family control (71.7%) limits free float and outside shareholder influence.

thesis.business_description: A.P.N. Promise S.A. is a Polish IT services company (incorporated 1991, headquartered in Warsaw) providing software licensing, implementation and consulting services to large and medium enterprises, public administration and healthcare clients.
thesis.competitive_position: A Polish IT licensing/consulting reseller and systems integrator serving enterprise and public-sector clients, including partnership/distribution deals such as with Allegro; specific market-share data was not found in sources reviewed. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/A-P-N-PROMISE-S-A-47418961/company/)
thesis.main_shareholders: CEO Piotr Paszczyk directly owns approximately 57.24% of shares (worth roughly PLN 52.17m); other major holders include Tomasz Bator (~13.7% personally plus a further ~8.6% via a related entity), and Paweł Kołakowski (~10.2%). [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/pl/software/wse-pro/apn-promise-shares/ownership)
thesis.insider_ownership: Very high insider/founder ownership: CEO Piotr Paszczyk (appointed January 1998) holds approximately 57.24% of shares, giving him effective control of the company. [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/pl/software/wse-pro/apn-promise-shares/ownership)
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in available search results.

thesis.business_description: Socfinaf S.A., based in Luxembourg and founded in 1890, produces, processes and sells palm oil and natural rubber through agro-industrial plantations in Sierra Leone, Liberia, Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana, Nigeria, Cameroon, São Tomé and Príncipe and the Republic of Congo.
thesis.competitive_position: Socfinaf is part of the broader Socfin group, one of the largest palm-oil/rubber plantation operators in Africa, managing a substantial share of the group's more than 190,600 hectares of tropical plantations; 2025 revenue grew 8.5% to EUR641.9m, though earnings fell 17% to EUR47.1m ([StockAnalysis](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/lux/SOFAF/)).
thesis.main_shareholders: SOCFIN (58.85%) and Bolloré (9%) as of 2018 disclosures; SOCFIN itself is controlled by the Fabri family (approximately 52-55%) and Bolloré Participations (approximately 38-40%) ([Tresor.economie.gouv.fr / GRAIN corporate structure report](https://www.grain.org/system/attachments/sources/000/005/823/original/The_corporate_structure_Socfin_EN.pdf))
thesis.insider_ownership: Not separately disclosed for Socfinaf itself; ultimate control runs through SOCFIN, which is majority-owned by the Fabri family and the Bolloré group ([GRAIN corporate structure report](https://www.grain.org/system/attachments/sources/000/005/823/original/The_corporate_structure_Socfin_EN.pdf))
thesis.red_flags: Socfin group plantations (including Socfinaf subsidiaries in West/Central Africa) have faced sustained allegations from NGOs and local communities of land-rights violations, lack of free-prior-informed-consent, water pollution, and gender-based violence by plantation security, per investigations by Earthsight, Mongabay and the Business & Human Rights Resource Centre ([Earthsight](https://www.earthsight.org.uk/news/idm/socfin-under-scrutiny-alleged-abuses-africa-rubber-palm-oil-plantations-despite-pldeges); [Mongabay](https://news.mongabay.com/2025/03/new-allegations-of-abuse-against-oil-palm-giant-socfin-in-cameroon/)).

thesis.business_description: Prime Office A/S is a Denmark-headquartered real estate company focused on acquiring, developing, and managing commercial office and residential properties, primarily in large German cities (population above 200,000), through its subsidiary PO Holding Germany GmbH and various German property subsidiaries. [MarketScreener company profile](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/PRIME-OFFICE-A-S-3782467/company/)
thesis.competitive_position: Prime Office is a small-cap, Denmark-listed vehicle for German commercial/residential property investment founded in 2007 by Mogens Møller; it operates in the challenged German office real estate market, which independent analysts (e.g., Moody's) have flagged as facing a widening quality gap and broader softness. [Bloomberg: German Property Slump to Widen Office Quality Gap](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-02-28/german-property-slump-to-widen-office-quality-gap-moody-s-says)
thesis.main_shareholders: Major shareholders include founder Mogens Vinther Møller (~27.25%), AHJ A/S (~15.72%), BD Invest ApS (~11.01%), and Kjell Bugge (~10.01%). [MarketScreener shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/PRIME-OFFICE-A-S-39433697/company-shareholders/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder Mogens Vinther Møller remains the largest named shareholder at approximately 27.25%, indicating high founder/insider concentration. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/PRIME-OFFICE-A-S-39433697/company-shareholders/)
thesis.red_flags: Some financial-analysis sources flag balance-sheet concerns: a debt/equity ratio around 108.9%, interest payments reported as not well covered by earnings, and profit margins that fell from about 22.3% to 10.9% year-on-year; these are financial-health concerns (elevated leverage in a soft German office market) rather than governance or fraud issues, but are worth flagging to prospective investors. Could not independently verify the precise current debt/equity figure beyond this secondary source.

name: SP Group A/S
gmSourceUrl: [SP Group investor relations key figures](https://www.sp-group.com/investor/financial-information/key-figures), [Nasdaq Copenhagen annual report announcement](https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=bf051d29d42359297fedad33d7908f02f&lang=en), [Perplexity Finance SPG.CO](https://perplexity.ai/finance/SPG.CO)

thesis.business_description: SP Group A/S is a Denmark-based plastics processing group manufacturing molded plastic components and coatings for plastic and metal parts, operating factories in Denmark, China, the USA, Latvia, Slovakia, Sweden, Finland, Thailand, and Poland. [SP Group about page](https://www.sp-group.com/about)
thesis.competitive_position: SP Group is described as a leading international supplier of manufactured plastics parts, with global manufacturing scale across nine countries and growing sales; it serves diverse industrial end markets rather than a single customer segment, which diversifies its competitive exposure. [TPI-Polytechniek: About SP Group](https://www.tpi-polytechniek.com/about-sp-group/)
thesis.main_shareholders: Major shareholders include Chairman Hans Wilhelm Schur (~17.35%), CEO Frank Marius Gad (~10.01%), ODIN Forvaltning AS (~8.67%), and Arbejdsmarkedets Tillægspension/ATP (~7.38%). [MarketScreener shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/SP-GROUP-A-S-43257883/company/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is notably high for a listed industrial company: Chairman Hans Wilhelm Schur holds about 17.35% and CEO Frank Gad holds about 10.01%, together representing over a quarter of the company held by its top two governance figures. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/SP-GROUP-A-S-43257883/company/)

thesis.business_description: Bijou Brigitte modische Accessoires AG is a Hamburg-based retailer that manufactures, imports and sells fashion jewelry, gold and silver jewelry, and fashion accessories through its own store chains across Germany and other European markets.
thesis.competitive_position: A long-established European fashion-accessories chain retailer (founded 1987) deriving the majority of revenue from Germany, with additional store networks in Spain, Italy and Portugal; revenue of roughly EUR 225 million in 2025 with operating margin under pressure (7.3% vs 10.2% prior year) amid cautious German consumer sentiment. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/bijou-brigitte-modische-accessoires-annual-report-2025-incl-consolidated-financial-statements-co-ce7f5adadc8cfe21)
thesis.main_shareholders: Founder-related holder Friedrich-Wilhelm Werner is reported to own approximately 53% of the company; the general public/free float holds roughly 43%, with Dimensional Fund Advisors and Ennismore Fund Management among other notable holders. [Yahoo Finance/Simply Wall St](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/bijou-brigitte-modische-accessoires-aktiengesellschaft-070951105.html)
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is high and concentrated, with Friedrich-Wilhelm Werner reported to hold approximately 53% of shares, giving insiders a controlling stake. [Yahoo Finance/Simply Wall St](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/bijou-brigitte-modische-accessoires-aktiengesellschaft-070951105.html)
thesis.red_flags: An internal investigation confirmed a service provider committed invoice fraud against the company, prompting a forensic examination; separately, Supervisory Board chairmanship changed in June 2025 (Marianne Tochtermann replacing Friedhelm Steinberg) amid declining margins. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/bijou-brigitte-modische-accessoires-annual-report-2025-incl-consolidated-financial-statements-co-ce7f5adadc8cfe21)

thesis.business_description: Lion Capital S.A. (formerly SIF Banat-Crișana) is a Romanian closed-end financial investment company (a former 'SIF') that holds a diversified portfolio of equity stakes, including a near-100% stake in real-estate vehicle SIF Imobiliare.
thesis.competitive_position: One of Romania's legacy privatization-era investment funds (SIFs), trading at a persistent discount to net asset value typical of the SIF sector; governance has been contested by minority shareholder groups. [Lion Capital Key Information](https://www.lion-capital.ro/en/about-lion-capital/key-information/)
thesis.main_shareholders: Infinity Capital Investments SA holds approximately 20%; broader shareholder base split roughly between Romanian legal entities (~45.10%), Romanian individuals (~39.73%), non-resident legal entities (~13.80%) and non-resident individuals (~1.36%) as of September 2025, across roughly 5.7 million shareholders typical of ex-SIF mass-privatization registers. [Lion Capital BoD Report 2025](https://bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/LION_20260327175146_BoD-Report-2025.pdf)
thesis.insider_ownership: Chairman and CEO Bogdan-Alexandru Drăgoi leads management; minority shareholder group Blue Capital (~8.63%) and the Association of SIF Investors (AISIF) have publicly alleged management operates in its own interest rather than reflecting a transparent insider ownership stake. Not clearly disclosed as a specific management ownership percentage. [Bursa.ro](https://www.bursa.ro/aisif-blue-capital-cel-mai-mare-actionar-real-al-lion-capital-a-ajuns-neputincios-in-mainile-unui-management-care-urmareste-exclusiv-interesele-proprii-82983259)
thesis.red_flags: Significant governance disputes: minority shareholder Blue Capital and AISIF (Association of SIF Investors) have publicly accused management of acting in self-interest and of inventing reasons to withhold dividends; Lion Capital's president won a court case annulling an ASF fine over alleged coordinated action with SIF Muntenia; the company was also sued (and the suit later withdrawn) by London-based Lion Capital LLP over use of the 'Lion Capital' name. [Bursa.ro](https://www.bursa.ro/aisif-blue-capital-cel-mai-mare-actionar-real-al-lion-capital-a-ajuns-neputincios-in-mainile-unui-management-care-urmareste-exclusiv-interesele-proprii-82983259)

thesis.business_description: Mo-BRUK S.A. is a Polish company specializing in hazardous and non-hazardous industrial waste management, including solidification/stabilization of inorganic waste, incineration of hazardous and medical waste, and production of alternative fuels.
thesis.competitive_position: A leading Polish hazardous-waste treatment and incineration operator, founded in 1985 by Józef Mokrzycki, occupying a specialist niche in regulated waste disposal infrastructure in Poland. [Mo-BRUK corporate ESDD report](https://mobruk.pl/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/MoBRUKCorporateESDDfinalreport221112.pdf)
thesis.main_shareholders: The Mokrzycki family (via holding vehicle Ginger Capital) holds approximately 20%; other large holders include PTE Allianz Polska (~7.6%), Nationale-Nederlanden OFE (~6.98%), PTE PZU (~6.0%), and PKO BP Bankowy PTE (~5.1%). [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/MO-BRUK-S-A-124007838/company-shareholders/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder Józef Mokrzycki and family remain the largest shareholder group at approximately 20% through Ginger Capital, though he stepped down as Chairman of the Board in June 2022 after 37 years leading the company. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/MO-BRUK-S-A-124007838/company-shareholders/)
thesis.red_flags: The company has been in a multi-year tax dispute with Polish authorities over retroactively increased landfill fees at its Wałbrzych site (2016-2020 periods), which led to a PLN 65.2m provision and a temporary PLN 2.5m bank account freeze in December 2023; some claims (2016, 2020) were later overturned in Mo-BRUK's favor, but disputes for 2018-2019 remain unresolved. [Stockwatch.pl](https://www.stockwatch.pl/wiadomosci/mo-bruk-sko-umarza-ponad-122-mln-zl-podwyzszonych-oplat,akcje,363816)

thesis.business_description: Aplisens S.A. is a Polish manufacturer of industrial process instrumentation, specializing in pressure and differential-pressure transmitters, hydrostatic level probes, level transmitters, temperature sensors, valves and digital indicators used across power, chemical, refining, pharmaceutical and food industries.
thesis.competitive_position: Aplisens describes itself as a leading domestic (Polish) manufacturer and integrator of industrial measurement and control instrumentation, operating six manufacturing plants in Poland plus a branch in Belarus, and selling across the EU, CIS countries (historically including Russia/Belarus/Ukraine) and Asia — giving it a strong niche position in a fragmented, technically specialized market rather than true global scale. [Aplisens - Group overview](https://aplisens.com/grupa-aplisens.html); [Aplisens - About us](https://aplisens.com/ofirmie.html).
thesis.main_shareholders: According to aggregator data sourced from the company's official shareholder-structure disclosures, the largest holders are CEO Adam Żurawski (~27.53%), Mirosław Dawidonis (~13.16%), Sławomir Szewczyk (~11.56%), Mirosław Karczmarczyk (~10.22%), Andrzej Kobiałka (~9.79%) and Dorota Zubkow (~8.82%); together these six hold roughly 81% of shares. [Aplisens - Struktura Akcjonariatu (official)](https://aplisens.pl/struktura-akcjonariatu.html); [BiznesRadar - Aplisens shareholding](https://www.biznesradar.pl/akcjonariat/APLISENS).
thesis.insider_ownership: Ownership is heavily insider-concentrated: CEO Adam Żurawski alone holds roughly 27.5%, and the named individual shareholders above (all appearing to be founding management/engineers) collectively control over 80% of the company, leaving a small free float. [Aplisens - Struktura Akcjonariatu](https://aplisens.pl/struktura-akcjonariatu.html).
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources. No litigation, auditor disputes, or related-party controversies surfaced in available search results; note the company historically had exposure to Russia/Belarus/CIS markets via its Belarus manufacturing branch, which is a geopolitical/sanctions-risk consideration rather than a governance red flag. [Aplisens - Group overview](https://aplisens.com/grupa-aplisens.html).

name: B2 Impact ASA
gmSourceUrl: [Euronext Live - B2 Impact ASA Annual report 2024](https://live.euronext.com/sites/default/files/esg_document_files/2025-12/219548_B2%20Impact%20ASA%20-%20Annual%20report%202024_2025-12-16_11:12.pdf)

thesis.business_description: B2 Impact ASA (formerly B2Holding ASA) is a Norway-based financial services company specializing in the investment and workout of non-performing loans, along with third-party debt collection services, operating across Nordic and European markets. [B2 Impact investor relations](https://www.b2-impact.com/investors/)
thesis.competitive_position: B2 Impact is an established Nordic/European debt-purchasing and collection group (parent to units such as Gothia Financial Group and Bank2), founded by Jon Harald Nordbrekken in 2005; it continues to grow via bolt-on acquisitions such as the Nordic assets of Zolva, though no independent market-share data confirming its competitive scale versus larger pan-European debt purchasers (e.g., Intrum, Hoist) was found. [B2 Impact acquires Nordic assets of Zolva](https://www.b2-impact.com/about-us/news/all/b2-impact-asa-to-acquire-the-nordic-assets-of-zolva/)
thesis.main_shareholders: Reported major shareholders include Gulen Invest AS (~24.35%), Jon Harald Nordbrekken (~8.68%), Egil Stenshagen (~8.28%), DNB Asset Management AS (~5.48%), and the Rasmussen Family (~4.71%); a later disclosure also named Nevedal Invest as holding approximately 24.27% of shares and votes following a transaction. [MarketScreener shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/B2-IMPACT-ASA-27891175/company-shareholders/), [B2 Impact large shareholding disclosure](https://www.b2-impact.com/about-us/news/all/b2-impact-asa-disclosure-of-large-shareholding/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder Jon Harald Nordbrekken remains a significant insider shareholder (~8.68%) and has been an active participant in recent board-composition disputes alongside other large shareholders. [PRNewswire: shareholders request EGM](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/shareholders-request-egm-to-appoint-new-board-of-directors-of-b2-impact-asa-301998953.html)
thesis.red_flags: B2 Impact has experienced a multi-year pattern of shareholder activism and board disputes: in late 2023, a shareholder group (~24% of shares, including founder Nordbrekken) requested an EGM to replace board members; in May 2025 the chairperson stepped down following an ownership-structure change; and in August 2025 another EGM was called over further board composition changes (including a board member's proposed resignation). This repeated governance instability is a notable red flag for prospective investors. [Shareholders request EGM - PRNewswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/shareholders-request-egm-to-appoint-new-board-of-directors-of-b2-impact-asa-301998953.html), [B2 Impact AGM 2025 board update](https://www.b2-impact.com/about-us/news/all/b2-impact-asa-updated-information-to-the-notice-of-annual-general-meeting-2025-proposed-amendments-to-the-board-of-directors-and-the-nomination-committee/)

thesis.business_description: Bouvet ASA is a Norwegian IT consulting and digital services company providing software development, systems integration and consulting to public and private-sector clients across Scandinavia.
thesis.competitive_position: Bouvet is a well-regarded, widely-held Norwegian IT consultancy with no controlling shareholder; the top 15 shareholders together hold only about 50% of the company, reflecting a broad ownership base typical of Norwegian consulting firms that rely on employee/partner equity culture. [Simply Wall St ownership analysis](https://simplywall.st/stocks/no/software/ob-bouv/bouvet-shares/news/institutions-along-with-individual-investors-who-hold-consid-187)
thesis.main_shareholders: No single controlling shareholder; institutional holder Kayne Anderson Rudnick Investment Management is among the largest at approximately 4.5% ([Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/no/software/ob-bouv/bouvet-shares/ownership)); Folketrygdfondet (the Norwegian state pension fund manager) was reported as the largest shareholder at approximately 7.9% in early 2025 data, though this may have changed ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/no/software/ob-bouv/bouvet-shares/ownership)).
thesis.insider_ownership: Board member Egil Dahl is a notable individual/insider holder, reported at 1,413,020 shares in July 2025 via his investment vehicle Velven Kapital after a partial sale, falling further to roughly 1,013,020 shares by November 2025 after an additional 400,000-share sale ([FilingReader - Bouvet board member sells stake](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/oslo/2025-07-17/bouvet-board-member-sells-nok-11m-stake)); aggregate individual-insider ownership is estimated around 2.8-4.9% depending on source/definition.
thesis.red_flags: Recent insider selling pattern: board member Egil Dahl and other insiders (Sverre Hurum, Helene Tonnessen) have been net sellers through 2025, though this followed broad employee insider buying in November 2024 and is not accompanied by any governance allegation found. [Simply Wall St insider trading news](https://simplywall.st/stocks/no/software/ob-bouv/bouvet-shares/news/institutions-along-with-individual-investors-who-hold-consid-187)

thesis.business_description: High Co. SA (HighCo) is a France-based marketing services group providing data marketing and communication solutions for mass-market retailers and consumer goods manufacturers, including coupon issuance, sampling, point-of-sale marketing, and digital marketing services. [Turning Rough Stones: High Co SA overview](https://turningroughstones.substack.com/p/high-co-sa-cheap-french-marketing)
thesis.competitive_position: HighCo operates primarily in France (over 80% of revenue) with additional operations in Spain, the UK, Poland, Russia, and Turkey, serving retailers and CPG brands in promotional/data marketing; it is backed by a large strategic shareholder (WPP), giving it scale/network advantages versus independent promotional agencies, though it remains a smaller-cap player relative to global marketing holding companies. [HighCo company profile - MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/HIGHCO-5002/company/)
thesis.main_shareholders: WPP France Holdings (part of the UK-listed WPP Group) holds approximately 37.4%; Eximium, controlled by the Baulé family, holds about 11.3%; Gérard de Bartillat Participations holds roughly 5.1%; management and employees hold about 3.2% combined. [Turning Rough Stones: High Co SA overview](https://turningroughstones.substack.com/p/high-co-sa-cheap-french-marketing)
thesis.insider_ownership: The chairman personally owns approximately 1.85% of shares, and management/employees collectively hold about 3.2%; the Baulé family's Eximium vehicle (~11.3%) represents a further insider/founder-linked holding distinct from the large external strategic shareholder WPP. [Turning Rough Stones](https://turningroughstones.substack.com/p/high-co-sa-cheap-french-marketing)
thesis.red_flags: No lawsuit or governance controversy specific to HighCo SA was identified in the sources searched; note that parent/large shareholder WPP Group has faced separate, unrelated corporate controversies (a 2021 SEC FCPA settlement, and 2025-era shareholder/whistleblower lawsuits at the group level), but no evidence was found connecting these to HighCo SA itself. [WPP SEC settlement](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2021-191)

name: Manx Financial Group PLC
gmSourceUrl: [Manx Financial Group 2024 Annual Report](https://mfg.im/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/manx-financial-group-plc-ar-web-1.pdf), [Manx Financial Group 2023 Annual Report](https://mfg.im/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/manx-financial-group-annual-report-2023-2.pdf)

thesis.business_description: Manx Financial Group PLC is an Isle of Man-based financial services holding company whose main subsidiary, Conister Bank, provides retail and commercial banking, lending and related financial services to customers in the Isle of Man and the UK.
thesis.competitive_position: Manx Financial Group is a small specialist/niche lender operating through Conister Bank, competing in UK and Isle of Man commercial and consumer finance (including asset finance and newly regulated BNPL) against larger UK specialist lenders; its small market capitalization (~£28m) limits scale and share liquidity relative to peers.
thesis.main_shareholders: Jim Mellon and Burnbrae Group Limited (beneficial owner) ~18.18%, Gregory Bailey (second-largest individual shareholder) ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/MANX-FINANCIAL-GROUP-PLC-4007820/company/))
thesis.insider_ownership: Chairman Jim Mellon and affiliated Burnbrae Group hold ~18.18%; additional board members (Gregory Bailey, Douglas Grant and others) hold further undisclosed amounts, so a full insider aggregate was not found
thesis.red_flags: FY2025 profit before tax fell 26% after a £1.3m provision tied to the FCA's motor finance discretionary-commission review (cumulative provision £1.5m), with the final FCA redress scheme still uncertain; credit impairments nearly doubled in 2025 against a relatively thin £43.6m equity base, and management described conditions as "fragile." ([Kalkine](https://kalkine.co.uk/news/general-news/why-manx-financial-group-plc-mfx-could-be-a-uk-financial-stock-to-watch-in-2026))

thesis.business_description: Spanish designer, manufacturer and marketer (founded 2002, headquartered in Álava) of ball and roller bearings and industrial components for cranes, offshore machinery, wind power, railway, gearboxes and heavy industrial equipment.
thesis.competitive_position: A specialized industrial bearings manufacturer with ~345 employees serving diverse heavy-industry end markets (wind, rail, oil & gas, mining, steel); maintains a strategic partnership/equity relationship with Chinese bearings manufacturer Cronos, giving it manufacturing scale support versus larger global bearing makers (SKF, Schaeffler, Timken).
thesis.main_shareholders: Controlled by Pakel RMI Promoción de Empresas SL; co-founders are also majority shareholders and hold an equity stake in the related Chinese partner Cronos; listed on Spain's MAB/BME Growth market since 2015 with stable core shareholders ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/NBI-BEARINGS-EUROPE-S-A-105514996/company-shareholders/))
thesis.insider_ownership: Co-founders hold majority equity as core/controlling shareholders (via Pakel RMI Promoción de Empresas SL); specific % not disclosed in available sources ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/NBI-BEARINGS-EUROPE-S-A-105514996/company-shareholders/))
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Croatian hotel management and tourism company (established 2005 via merger of Jadran-turist and Anita d.d.) operating 19 hotels, 11 tourist resorts and 6 campsites (13,700+ accommodation units) in Rovinj, Vrsar, Zagreb and Dubrovnik, part of the Adris Group's Maistra Hospitality Group alongside HUP-Zagreb.
thesis.competitive_position: Croatia's second-largest hotel/resort/campsite owner-operator (34 assets along the Adriatic coast and in Zagreb), with ~EUR 300.5M annual revenue and ~4.5 million guests, commanding nearly 4% of Croatia's tourism market and ranking among the top three tourism companies in the country; investing in a 2024-2027 capex program including Hotel Marjan (Split) and a new Vrsar Holiday Village.
thesis.main_shareholders: Majority owned by Adris Grupa d.d. as part of its tourism division (tourism represents 44.5% of Adris Group net sales); specific % stake of Adris in Maistra not confirmed in available sources ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ADRIS-GRUPA-D-D-6497104/company/))
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Scandi Standard AB is a Sweden-based poultry company and the largest producer of chicken-based food products in the Nordic region, operating via Kronfågel (Sweden), Scandinavian Standard/Cardinal Foods (Norway), and Danpo (Denmark), with additional operations in Ireland and the Netherlands. [Matrix BCG company history](https://matrixbcg.com/blogs/brief-history/scandistandard)
thesis.competitive_position: Scandi Standard holds a leading position as the largest Nordic chicken producer, built through consolidation of national poultry champions (Kronfågel, Danpo, Cardinal Foods); it has continued to expand via acquisitions (Irish, Danish, Dutch poultry assets), though it has faced margin pressure from rising feed/raw material costs and Netherlands start-up costs. [Scandi Standard: A Chicken Empire in Transition](https://parsers.vc/news/241022-scandi-standard--a-chicken-empire-in/)
thesis.main_shareholders: Major shareholders include Lusiaves SGPS SA (~21.29%), Investment AB Öresund (~15.29%), Lantmännen Animalieinvest AB (~10.57%), and Nordea Investment Management AB (~6.23%). [MarketScreener shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/SCANDI-STANDARD-AB-16817052/company-shareholders/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Not disclosed as a specific management/board insider percentage separate from the large institutional/strategic holders (Lusiaves, Öresund, Lantmännen) listed above; no distinct founder/management stake was found. Could not verify further.
thesis.red_flags: No profit-warning scandal or governance controversy was identified; the company has faced normal operating headwinds (rising chicken feed costs, Netherlands start-up costs) but these are disclosed business factors, not governance red flags. [Scandi Standard interim report Jan-Dec 2025](https://investors.scandistandard.com/en/reports/scandi-standards-ab-publ-interim-report-january-december-2025)

thesis.business_description: Solar A/S is a Danish technical wholesaler and sourcing/services company supplying electrical, heating, plumbing, ventilation, climate and energy-solution products across Northern Europe.
thesis.competitive_position: Solar describes itself as a leading European sourcing and services company within electrical, heating/plumbing, ventilation and climate/energy solutions, with roughly DKK 12.2bn revenue (2025) and about 3,000 employees; it has operated since 1919 and listed in 1953, giving it long-established distribution relationships versus newer entrants. [Solar A/S investor news](https://www.solar.eu/investor/news/news-page)
thesis.main_shareholders: The company has a dual share class structure (A shares with higher voting power, B shares listed as SOLAR B). Disclosed major holders found are financial institutions trading around regulatory thresholds: UBS Group AG reported holdings fluctuating between roughly 3.2% and 5.2% of B shares through 2025-2026 ([Solar A/S major shareholder announcements via Inderes](https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/solar-as-no-10-2026-major-shareholder-announcement)); Nordea Invest held about 5.03% (2.5% of votes) in a 2014 disclosure ([EQS News 2014](https://eqs-news.com/de/news/corporate/no-7-2014-major-shareholder-announcement/793519)). Holders of the higher-voting A shares (often linked to founding interests at Nordic wholesalers of this type) were not identified in search results - this should be verified directly via Solar's annual report.
thesis.insider_ownership: Not disclosed/found in public filings searched; no named founder-family or management stake was located. Not disclosed in public filings found - verify via Solar's annual report shareholder list.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; frequent trading in/out of disclosure thresholds by UBS suggests active trading rather than a stable anchor holder, but this is not itself a governance red flag.

thesis.business_description: Bio Planet S.A., founded in 2005 and based in Leszno/Wilkowa Wieś, Poland, produces, packages and distributes organic/ecological food for humans and animals (around 4,000 products) under its own Bio Planet brand and third-party brands such as Alce Nero and Bio Planète, both in Poland and internationally.
thesis.competitive_position: Bio Planet is a specialist Polish organic-food producer and distributor with a broad product catalogue (~4,000 SKUs), positioning it as a scaled player in Poland's organic/health-food niche rather than a mainstream grocery supplier. [EMIS company profile](https://www.emis.com/php/company-profile/PL/Bio_Planet_SA_en_3379542.html)
thesis.main_shareholders: Ownership is concentrated among founders under a shareholders' agreement: Grzegorz Mulik (~19.36%), Barbara Mariola Strużyna (~18.53%), Mariusz Krzysztof Ziemiańczyk (~10.5%), GK4 Food sp. z o.o. (~10%), Bio Pole sp. z o.o. (~8%) and Sylwester Strużyna (~7.17%). [BiznesRadar](https://www.biznesradar.pl/akcjonariat/BIO-PLANET)
thesis.insider_ownership: Founders and supervisory board members (Grzegorz, Maciej and Michał Mulik, and the Strużyna family) collectively control a majority of shares under a formal shareholders' agreement, representing high founder/insider concentration (combined founder-linked stakes exceed 50%). [BiznesRadar](https://www.biznesradar.pl/akcjonariat/BIO-PLANET)
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Brd. Klee A/S is a Danish engineering and trading company supplying technical components and semi-manufactured products to the machine-building industry, including gears and gearmotors, motors, pumps and blowers, control/electronic products, pneumatic and hydraulic products, linear motion technology, and rubber/plastic machine parts, plus its own gear assembly/rebuild workshop.
thesis.competitive_position: Founded in 1944 and listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen since 1986, Brd. Klee is a long-standing specialist technical-component distributor/engineering house in Denmark (166 employees, Albertslund HQ), differentiating itself from pure distributors via in-house assembly and rebuilding capability for gears, which shortens delivery times for industrial customers; it is a small, niche B2B player rather than a market leader with global scale. [stockanalysis.com - Brd. Klee company profile](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/cph/KLEE.B/company/); [Brd. Klee (Germany) - About us](https://www.brd-klee.de/en/about-us).
thesis.main_shareholders: Danish businessman Fritz H. Schur, via Fritz Schur A/S and related holding entities (including FS 14 ApS), is the controlling shareholder, having acquired his stake from the Klee family starting in 2016; per the company's 2023-2024 annual report, Schur-controlled entities hold approximately 89.95% of share capital and approximately 97.59% of voting rights. [Brd. Klee - Annual Report 2023-2024 (official PDF via GlobeNewswire)](https://ml-eu.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/de57d923-55fb-4c72-b030-cdcb9d118ecf).
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider/controlling-shareholder concentration is extremely high: Fritz H. Schur and his holding companies control ~90% of capital and ~97.6% of voting rights, and Schur has sat on the Brd. Klee board since 1988 (Vice Chairman since 1999), meaning free-float/minority ownership is very thin. [Brd. Klee - Annual Report 2023-2024](https://ml-eu.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/de57d923-55fb-4c72-b030-cdcb9d118ecf); [Brd. Klee - Board of Directors (official)](https://www.klee.dk/en/board).
thesis.red_flags: No litigation, auditor dispute, or fraud allegation was identified in available sources. The extremely concentrated ownership (~90% capital / ~97.6% votes with one controlling family/individual) is a structural governance point worth flagging for minority investors — it implies very low free float and limited minority influence over corporate actions such as a potential future squeeze-out — though no squeeze-out or dispute has actually occurred per available sources. [Brd. Klee - Annual Report 2023-2024](https://ml-eu.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/de57d923-55fb-4c72-b030-cdcb9d118ecf).

thesis.business_description: EL.En. S.p.A. is an Italian group that designs, develops, manufactures and sells laser systems for three main application areas: medical/aesthetic (surgery, dermatology, aesthetics, physiotherapy), industrial (laser marking, cutting and material processing), and conservation of cultural heritage/artworks.
thesis.competitive_position: EL.En. is described as the world's third-leading provider of medical lasers, generating roughly USD 692 million in group revenue in 2023, with products sold in more than 80 countries and direct sales presences in Japan, Germany, the US and France. It operates through ~26 subsidiaries, 10 production sites and 5 R&D centers, giving it unusual scale and vertical integration (it builds its own laser sources) relative to most laser niche players, which supports a durable technology moat in medical aesthetics in particular ([El.En. Group strategy](https://elengroup.com/en/strategy/); [stock analysis overview](https://stocksafari.substack.com/p/elen-stock-analysis-eln)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Per shareholder disclosures reported via MarketScreener/CONSOB, Andrea Cangioli is the largest shareholder with approximately 14.69% (~11.8M shares), followed by Alberto Pecci with ~10.49% and Gabriele Clementi with ~9.51%. The Cangioli family (founders) is identified as a notable long-term shareholder bloc. [MarketScreener - EL.En. shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/EL-EN-SPA-90767/company/); [CONSOB ownership disclosure, 2024-06-30](https://www.consob.it/web/consob-and-its-activities/w/el.en.-spa-azionariato-2024-06-30).
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder/management-linked holders appear among the largest shareholders: Andrea Cangioli (~14.69%) and Gabriele Clementi (~9.51%) are both associated with company founding/management roles per MarketScreener data; precise current board/management aggregate ownership was not independently confirmed beyond these individual stakes. [MarketScreener - EL.En. shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/EL-EN-SPA-90767/company/).
thesis.red_flags: No specific litigation, auditor disputes, or related-party controversies were found in available search results. The company's 2025 Corporate Governance and Ownership Structure Report references standard CONSOB related-party-transaction rules but no flagged violations were located. None identified from official sources beyond routine related-party-transaction regulatory disclosure. [EL.En. Corporate Governance Report 2025 (via MarketScreener)](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/EL-EN-S-P-A-27753855/news/EL-En-S-p-A-Report-on-the-Corporate-Governance-and-ownership-structure-2025-courtesy-translation-50177658/).

thesis.business_description: Brødrene A & O Johansen A/S (AO Johansen) is a Denmark-based wholesaler of plumbing, heating, electrical supplies, tools, and safety equipment for tradespeople/professionals, founded in 1914 and headquartered in Albertslund. [AO.dk official site](https://ao.dk/)
thesis.competitive_position: AO Johansen is a long-established Danish professional trade-supplies wholesaler, serving tradespeople exclusively (no sales to private individuals) through a combined physical and e-commerce distribution model; it has been publicly listed since 1963. [Export.dk company profile](https://export.dk/broedrene-ao-johansen-a-s/)
thesis.main_shareholders: The company is controlled by Avenir Invest ApS, which is owned equally by Niels A. Johansen and Lili Johansen (reportedly via the Swiss holding entity Evoleska Holding AG); Niels Johansen individually is also listed as the top shareholder at roughly 10.3%, with other large stakes historically disclosed from Avenir Invest ApS. [MarketScreener/Tracxn ownership data](https://tracxn.com/d/companies/brodrene-ao-johansen/__ecmR9I-uHtKTnJO7Ke0u4_y-gLLbibj22V3annr27E0)
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider/founder-family ownership is very high: Niels A. Johansen (CEO since 2013) and Lili Johansen jointly control the company through Avenir Invest ApS, with Niels individually also holding a direct stake (~10.3%) and Lili Johansen separately disclosed holding smaller direct stakes (~1.1%-1.3%). [MarketScreener insider profile: Niels Johansen](https://www.marketscreener.com/insider/NIELS-JOHANSEN-A0YO2N/)
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources searched.

thesis.business_description: Luceco plc is a UK-based manufacturer and distributor of LED lighting products and wiring accessories, operating brands including Luceco (LED lighting), British General (wiring accessories), Masterplug (portable power) and Ross (AV accessories).
thesis.competitive_position: Luceco is a mid-cap UK electrical products manufacturer/distributor with a portfolio of recognized trade brands across lighting, wiring and power accessories, though its 2017-2018 inventory-valuation/accounting restatement episode and 2022 destocking-driven profit warning highlight historical volatility in margins and controls. [Sharecast - accounting error](https://sharecast.com/amp/news/news-and-announcements/luceco-issues-profit-warning-after-accounting-error--3031507.html)
thesis.main_shareholders: CEO Jonathan (John) Hornby holds approximately 16.9-18.9% depending on listing/date; EPIC Investment Partners LLP holds approximately 23.3%; BlackRock, Inc. holds approximately 10.4%; Record Plc ESOP holds approximately 6.71%; Chairman Giles Brand holds approximately 6.21%. [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/capital-goods/lse-luce/luceco-shares/ownership)
thesis.insider_ownership: CEO Jonathan Hornby is the largest individual/insider holder at roughly 16.9-18.9%; Chairman Giles Brand holds roughly 6.21%. No source identified Hornby as the company's original founder; a separate founder, John Harding, founded Kingfisher Lighting, a business Luceco acquired in 2017 for £9.75m from Harding and his wife Barbara as retiring founder/major shareholders - a different, acquired entity rather than Luceco itself. [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/capital-goods/lse-luce/luceco-shares/ownership), [Legal Futures - Kingfisher Lighting sale](https://www.legalfutures.co.uk/associate-news/aaron-partners-llp-cooper-parry-corporate-finance-advise-sale-kingfisher-lighting-limited-luceco-plc/print/)
thesis.red_flags: Significant historical accounting/control failure: in December 2017 Luceco warned that an incorrectly calculated inventory valuation had masked gross-margin deterioration, its Financial Controller resigned, and a further March 2018 review found errors in historic financial information requiring a restatement; shares fell from 232p to as low as 50p during this period. A separate 2022 profit warning was attributed to customer destocking rather than accounting issues. [CityAM](https://www.cityam.com/?p=2068604), [Shares Magazine](https://sharesmagazine.co.uk/news/shares/is-lighting-provider-luceco-over-its-stock-accounting-calamity), [AJ Bell - 2022 warning](https://streaming1.www.ajbell.co.uk/articles/latestnews/251540/brief-luceco-warns-2022-profit-be-below-estimates-destocking)

thesis.business_description: Michelmersh Brick Holdings plc is a UK manufacturer of clay bricks and associated building products, supplying the residential and commercial construction markets from several UK brickworks.
thesis.competitive_position: Michelmersh operates several heritage UK brickworks producing premium/specialist clay bricks, positioning it as a smaller specialist producer rather than a scale commodity brick maker; ownership is fairly concentrated around its largest individual shareholder and a handful of institutions. [Simply Wall St ownership breakdown](https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/materials/aim-mbh/michelmersh-brick-holdings-shares/ownership)
thesis.main_shareholders: Eric Gadsden is the largest shareholder at roughly 24-25% of shares outstanding ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/materials/aim-mbh/michelmersh-brick-holdings-shares/ownership)); Hosking Partners LLP holds approximately 9.4% and BennBridge Ltd approximately 6.9% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/materials/aim-mbh/michelmersh-brick-holdings-shares/ownership)). As of 30 September 2025 the company had 92,714,700 voting rights after treasury share deductions ([Shares Magazine total voting rights notice](https://www.sharesmagazine.co.uk/news/market/LSE20230801070004_4853215/total-voting-rights-31-july-2023)).
thesis.insider_ownership: Chairman Martin Warner held about 4.3% of voting rights following a 2022 share gift (4,129,732 shares) ([RNS via ticker.app](https://www.ticker.app/lse/MBH/rns/2022-01-19/DirectorPDMR-Shareholding/9983Y)); the Ley Hill Discretionary Trust 2004 held about 2.97% as of May 2024, down from 4.31% ([Nasdaq - Michelmersh Stakeholder Trust Reduces Share](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/michelmersh-stakeholder-trust-reduces-share)). Combined individual-insider ownership is estimated around 25.6% per aggregator data.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Delko S.A. is a Poland-based wholesale distributor of fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), primarily cosmetics, personal hygiene and household cleaning products, plus groceries and tobacco, partnering with brands such as Unilever, Gillette, Bella, Lambi and Dove. [Emerging Value: Delko overview](https://emergingvalue.substack.com/p/delko-european-small-cap-distributor)
thesis.competitive_position: Delko is positioned as a consolidator/acquirer among regional Polish FMCG distributors, pursuing growth via acquisitions of smaller distribution companies; independent coverage frames it as a 'discounted distributor' small-cap. [Substack: Delko (DEL) - A Discounted Distributor](https://dismissedandassetbacked.substack.com/p/delko-del-a-discounted-distributor)
thesis.main_shareholders: Former CEO and founder-linked figure Dariusz Kawecki is the largest shareholder with approximately 31% of shares; current CEO Mirosław Dąbrowski holds about 17%; supervisory-board member and long-standing investor Mirosław Newel holds roughly 9%. Free float is about 43.57%. [MarketScreener shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/DELKO-S-A-11193929/company/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is very high and concentrated: together Kawecki (~31%), Dąbrowski (~17%), and Newel (~9%) control well over half of shares and votes. Kawecki resigned as CEO for health reasons in December 2024 but remains the largest shareholder. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/DELKO-S-A-11193929/company/)
thesis.red_flags: Delko experienced a notable governance dispute: its management board was recalled by the supervisory board (citing weak results, falling share price, excessive costs, and alleged violations of legal/internal norms), the company operated for nearly a month without a functioning supervisory board, and the recalled board disputed the stated reasons and signaled intent to pursue legal action, suspecting the recall was actually connected to a planned acquisition of distribution companies owned by existing shareholders. This is a material, documented governance/boardroom conflict that prospective investors should weigh carefully. [Parkiet.com: Odwołany zarząd Delko idzie do sądu](https://www.parkiet.com/handel-i-konsumpcja/art21774621-odwolany-zarzad-delko-idzie-do-sadu)

thesis.business_description: Veteranpoolen AB is a Swedish staffing company, founded in 2007 and headquartered in Gothenburg, that provides flexible staffing of experienced senior/retired workers (Sweden's largest employer of pensioners) to private individuals and corporate clients across finance, real estate, education and project management.
thesis.competitive_position: A niche leader in Sweden's senior/retiree staffing segment with a differentiated workforce model; Q2 2026 revenue grew roughly 19% to about SEK 224 million, with H1 2026 operating margin of 9.7%, though international expansion has modestly weighed on near-term results. [Staffing Industry](https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/veteranpoolen-q1-revenue-climbs-107-profits-jump)
thesis.main_shareholders: Håkan Blomdahl holds approximately 23.0% of capital; House of Service Investment Sverige AB holds approximately 12.7%; board member Fredrik Grevelius holds approximately 4%. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/VETERANPOOLEN-AB-120974629/company/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Meaningful insider ownership, with board member Fredrik Grevelius holding approximately 4% and a board member reported to have sold shares worth SEK 22.7 million in a separate transaction; Håkan Blomdahl's ~23% stake relationship to management was not fully clarified in sources reviewed. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/VETERANPOOLEN-AB-120974629/news/Board-member-of-Veteranpoolen-has-sold-shares-for-SEK-22-7-million-48694066/)
thesis.red_flags: Increased social security contributions tied to Sweden's raised retirement age, and international expansion costs (~SEK 4.5 million drag in H1 2026), have modestly pressured results, but no governance disputes, litigation or auditor concerns were identified. None identified from official sources beyond normal operating cost pressures.

thesis.business_description: Istarska kreditna banka Umag d.d. is a Croatia-based regional bank, incorporated in 1956 and headquartered in Umag, providing retail and business banking products and services to individuals, corporates, and small businesses, primarily in Istria, Primorsko-Goranska County, and Zagreb. [IKB bank official site](https://ikb.hr/o-nama)
thesis.competitive_position: IKB is a small regional Croatian bank, ranked the 9th largest bank in Croatia in 2025 with roughly a 0.90% market share and total assets of about €820.68 million, operating a 19-branch network concentrated in the Istrian region. [SeeNews: Istarska Kreditna Banka Umag company profile](https://seenews.com/companies/profile/istarska-kreditna-banka-umag-d-d-3529)
thesis.main_shareholders: Reported major shareholders include SERFIN d.o.o. (~18.80%), Intercommerce d.o.o. (~17.18%), Interkapital Vrijednosni Papiri d.o.o./Rudan d.o.o. (~7.93%), and Assicurazioni Generali-Società per Azioni (~7.77%); individual shareholders include Edo Ivančić (~5.00%), Branko Kovačić (~4.46%), and Jelena Kovačić (~3.46%). [Investing.com company profile](https://www.investing.com/equities/istarska-kreditna-banka-umag-dd-company-profile)
thesis.insider_ownership: Named individual shareholders Edo Ivančić (~5.00%), Branko Kovačić (~4.46%), and Jelena Kovačić (~3.46%) appear to represent insider/family-linked holdings totaling roughly 13%, though their specific relationship to bank management was not independently confirmed in the sources searched. Could not verify further.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources searched.

thesis.business_description: Ålandsbanken Abp (Bank of Åland) is a Finnish/Åland-based regional bank providing banking, asset management and private banking services, primarily to customers in the Åland Islands, mainland Finland and Sweden.
thesis.competitive_position: Bank of Åland is a small regional bank (market cap roughly €318m per a 2020 analysis) with a dual-class share structure that concentrates voting control with a local business family, differentiating its governance from larger diversified Nordic banks. [Simply Wall St ownership structure analysis](https://simplywall.st/stocks/fi/banks/hel-albav/alandsbanken-abp-shares/news/could-the-landsbanken-abp-helalbav-ownership-structure-tell)
thesis.main_shareholders: The Wiklöf family/companies are the controlling bloc: Anders Wiklöf personally holds approximately 10.4%, Fennogens Investments S.A. approximately 5.09%, and Wiklöf Holding Ab approximately 4.25% of shares per aggregator data ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/banks/lse-0o2n/alandsbanken-abp-shares/ownership)); a 2019 company disclosure showed Wiklöf Holding Ab's voting rights exceeding 25% (18.79% of shares, 25.47% of votes) due to the dual Series A/B share structure (Series A carrying ~20 votes vs. 1 vote for Series B) ([Bank of Åland disclosure, May 2019](https://www.alandsbanken.fi/porssitiedotteet/en-21-05-2019-bank-of-aland-plc-disclosure-of-change-in-shareholdings-pursuant-to-chapter-9-section-10-of-the-securities-markets-act)).
thesis.insider_ownership: Anders Wiklöf (a well-known Åland businessman, not a bank executive) is the leading individual holder at ~10.4% via personal and holding-company stakes, giving the Wiklöf family effective voting control well above its cash-flow stake due to the A-share voting multiplier ([Bank of Åland 2019 disclosure](https://www.alandsbanken.fi/porssitiedotteet/en-21-05-2019-bank-of-aland-plc-disclosure-of-change-in-shareholdings-pursuant-to-chapter-9-section-10-of-the-securities-markets-act)).
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; the dual-class share structure giving ~20x voting power to A shares is a governance feature worth noting for minority holders (not a scandal, but a concentration-of-control consideration).

thesis.business_description: Zespół Elektrociepłowni Wrocławskich KOGENERACJA S.A. is a Polish combined-heat-and-power (cogeneration) company operating three plants (Elektrociepłownia Wrocław, Czechnica and Zawidawie) with roughly 477 MW electric and 1,170 MW thermal capacity, producing and selling district heating and electricity, heat-distribution services, and trading CO2 emission allowances.
thesis.competitive_position: KOGENERACJA is the dominant district-heating and cogeneration supplier for the city of Wrocław, benefiting from a regulated, infrastructure-based local monopoly position typical of district-heating utilities, and is majority-controlled by Poland's state-owned PGE group. [kogeneracja.com.pl](https://kogeneracja.com.pl/en/group/about-us/company)
thesis.main_shareholders: PGE Polska Grupa Energetyczna S.A. (via PGE Energia Ciepła S.A.) is the controlling shareholder with approximately 58.07%; other holders include Aviva Investors Poland TFI (~9.99%) and Nationale-Nederlanden PTE (~5.01%). [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ZESP-L-ELEKTROCIEPLOWNI-W-6500524/company/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Controlling shareholder is the Polish state-controlled utility group PGE rather than individual management/founders; no separate personal management ownership was found disclosed. Not disclosed in public filings reviewed.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; majority state-linked ownership (PGE) means minority shareholder interests may be subordinated to state energy-policy objectives, though no specific dispute was found.

thesis.business_description: Novotek AB (publ) is a Malmö-headquartered Swedish industrial-IT and automation company that resells and integrates digitalization, automation and analytics software/hardware (MES, OEE, SCADA, IoT connectivity, asset performance) from vendors such as GE Vernova (iFIX, Proficy Historian) and PTC Kepware, serving manufacturers across the Nordics, Benelux, Switzerland and UK/Ireland. Source: https://www.novotek.com/?p=834 ; https://gevernova.com/software/industrial-partners/novotek-sverige-ab-1
thesis.competitive_position: Niche value-added reseller/systems integrator (reported ~100-200 employees depending on source/date) serving over 2,500 industrial customers mainly in automotive, food & beverage, pharma and water/wastewater; listed on Nasdaq since 1999, with growth historically driven by bolt-on acquisitions (e.g. Austrian Taschek & Gruber, 2024). Source: https://www.novotek.com/?p=834 ; https://mfn.se/all/a/novotek/novotek-forvarvar-osterrikiska-taschek-and-gruber-automatische-datenverarbeitungs-gmbh
thesis.main_shareholders: Per the company's AGM notice (repeated 2023-2026), Novotek has a dual-class structure of 1,500,000 A-shares (10 votes each) and 9,100,000 B-shares (1 vote each), giving A-shares roughly 62% of total votes despite being only ~14% of capital; the notice does not itself name the A-share holders. Source: https://mfn.se/all/a/novotek/kallelse-till-arsstamma-i-novotek-ab. We could not locate a current named major-shareholder table from the company's own IR 'Ownership' page or a recent annual report in this search; the company directs investors to the Holdings.se shareholder-data service for the current list. This should be treated as a research gap, not a confirmed absence of concentration.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; however, the A/B dual-class share structure concentrates voting control (A-shares ~62% of votes from ~14% of capital) with whichever family/entity holds the A-shares, a standard Swedish minority-shareholder consideration rather than a confirmed governance problem, since we could not confirm the current A-share holder identity in this search. Source: https://mfn.se/all/a/novotek/kallelse-till-arsstamma-i-novotek-ab

thesis.business_description: Mutares SE & Co. KGaA is a Munich-based listed private equity investor specializing in acquiring, operationally transforming and later selling companies in special situations/corporate transitions, organized across Automotive & Mobility, Engineering & Technology, Goods & Services, and Retail & Food segments.
thesis.competitive_position: Mutares follows a distinctive 'buy-low, turn around, harvest' private-equity model focused on corporate carve-outs and distressed/special-situation companies (rather than growth buyouts), generating returns partly through consultancy-style fees charged to its portfolio companies as well as eventual exits. [Mutares 2024 Annual Report](https://live.euronext.com/sites/default/files/company_press_releases/attachments_oslo/2025/05/20/646871_Mutares_2024_Annual_Report_safe.pdf)
thesis.main_shareholders: Founder and CEO Robin Laik, together with his family, is the largest shareholder with a stake reported at over 21-25% (sources vary: ~21.41% per one aggregator, 'over 25%' combined with family per company statements); the Management Board and Supervisory Board jointly are reported to hold more than one-third of voting shares. [Mutares company statement](https://mutares.com/en/supervisory-board-of-mutares-extends-ceo-robin-laiks-management-board-contract-prematurely-by-a-further-five-years/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder/CEO Robin Laik and family hold a large single-largest stake (~21-25%+), and combined Management + Supervisory Board ownership exceeds one-third of voting shares; insiders increased holdings (e.g., Laik purchased ~€320,000 of shares in September 2024) during and after a 2024 short-seller attack. [2iqresearch](https://www.2iqresearch.com/blog/mutares-executives-increase-holdings-in-company-stock-defying-short-sellers-2025-03-21)
thesis.red_flags: In September 2024, short-seller Gotham City Research published a report alleging accounting irregularities (including a cash-balance discrepancy between Mutares' balance sheet and cash-flow statement) and a business model overly reliant on debt-funded dividends and consultancy fees charged to portfolio companies; the stock fell as much as 28% in a single day, erasing roughly €150 million of market value.
