thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources beyond the standard family-control structure; the inconsistency between different aggregator snapshots (49% 'private companies' vs. a scattered sub-3% family-individual breakdown) is a data-quality gap that should be resolved by pulling the exact percentages from Euronext Athens' >5% shareholder disclosure (https://athens.euronext.com/en/market-data/issuers/134) rather than being treated as a confirmed discrepancy in the company's actual ownership.

thesis.business_description: Neodecortech S.p.A. (formerly Confalonieri S.p.A., founded 1947), headquartered in Filago, Italy, is a vertically integrated Italian manufacturer of decorative papers, printed/laminated films and laminates for the furniture, flooring and interior-design industries, selling under the Confalonieri, Plana, Texte and EOS brands, with three Italian production sites and cogeneration plants supplying its own energy. Source: https://it.finance.yahoo.com/quote/NDT.MI/profile?p=NDT.MI ; https://eqs-news.com/news/corporate/european-large-midcap-conference-2018-neodecortech-meets-the-financial-community-in-paris/1095821
thesis.competitive_position: Describes itself as the Italian leader in decorative paper production for laminated panels and flooring in the interior-design sector, with roughly 51 products across 5 categories and sales split roughly 42% Italy / 49.4% rest of Europe (dated to a 2018 company release); a relatively small-cap (~390 employees) but vertically integrated niche materials producer. Source: https://eqs-news.com/news/corporate/european-large-midcap-conference-2018-neodecortech-meets-the-financial-community-in-paris/1095821
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Consob's official 'Neodecortech SpA Azionariato' register, snapshot dated 31/12/2022: controlling shareholder Finanziaria Valentini S.p.A. held 61.600% of voting rights (direct ownership); Azimut Investments S.A. held 5.569% via discretionary asset management. A separate (non-official, dated 2020) Websim profile states that following an Accelerated Book-Building completed 30 October 2019, the Valentini family's combined stake rose to 63.86% (a family-level figure that does not exactly match the holding-company-level 61.6% from the 2022 Consob snapshot, consistent with slightly different measurement dates/scopes). The company held 440,295 treasury shares (3.097% of capital) as of 5 July 2024 per a Borsa Italiana disclosure. Gianluca Valentini is Chairman of the Board per the Consob 'Organi Sociali' page (updated 29/04/2025). Source: https://www.consob.it/web/consob-and-its-activities/w/neodecortech-spa-azionariato-2022-12-31 ; https://www.consob.it/web/consob-and-its-activities/w/neodecortech-spa-organi-sociali- ; https://borsaitaliana.it/borsa/notizie/price-sensitive/download/20111_143137_2024_oneinfo.html
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; majority family control (Valentini family, ~62-64% depending on measurement) via Finanziaria Valentini S.p.A. is a standard Italian family-controlled small-cap structure, with the chairman (Gianluca Valentini) drawn from the controlling family — a related-party governance consideration but not evidence of misconduct. No litigation or going-concern issues were identified.

thesis.business_description: Eurofins-Cerep SA is a France-based (Poitiers-founded, 1989) contract research company specializing in in vitro drug profiling, pharmacological screening and pre-clinical drug research services for the pharmaceutical industry, now operating as part of Eurofins Pharma Discovery Services.
thesis.competitive_position: A niche pre-clinical CRO (contract research organization) that has been majority- and now near-fully-owned by global testing/laboratory group Eurofins Scientific since 2013, operating as part of Eurofins' broader Pharma Discovery Services division rather than as an independent competitive entity. [Eurofins press release](https://www.eurofins.com/media-centre/press-releases-archive/2012-12-21/)
thesis.main_shareholders: Parent Eurofins Scientific SE holds approximately 95.78% of Eurofins-Cerep SA as of December 31, 2024, following a series of acquisitions beginning in December 2012 (75.13% stake acquired for EUR 18.9 million) and a subsequent tender offer. [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/equities/cerep-ownership)
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is effectively the parent company Eurofins Scientific SE (~95.78%); minimal free float remains, meaning minority shareholders have very limited influence and the stock trades with low liquidity typical of a company nearing full absorption by its parent. [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/equities/cerep-ownership)
thesis.red_flags: Extremely low free float (~4.2% non-Eurofins-Scientific ownership) presents liquidity and potential future squeeze-out/delisting risk for minority holders, though no specific litigation or fraud was identified in sources reviewed.

thesis.business_description: S.C. Ropharma S.A. operates a chain of pharmacies and pharmaceutical wholesale/distribution business in Romania, headquartered in Brașov, with pharmacies across multiple Romanian counties (including Iași, Suceava, Bacău, Sibiu, and Brașov). [Ropharma company profile - EMIS](https://www.emis.com/php/company-profile/RO/Ropharma_SA_en_1482328.html)
thesis.competitive_position: Ropharma is one of Romania's established pharmacy-chain and pharmaceutical distribution operators, founded by entrepreneur Mihai Miron (who previously built and sold Europharm to GlaxoSmithKline); it is a mid-sized regional player expanding into rural pharmacy coverage rather than a dominant national leader. [ZF.ro interview with Mihai Miron](https://www.zf.ro/te-inspira/brasov/brasov-inspira-mihai-gabriel-miron-ropharma-ne-dorim-ne-extindem-22460787)
thesis.main_shareholders: Founder and chairman/CEO Mihai Miron is the controlling shareholder, holding approximately 20.5% directly, with related entities ADD Pharmaceuticals Limited (~17.8%) and Rimia Investments also controlled by Miron; Goa Capital SA holds about 3.91%. Ownership breakdown: private companies ~21.7%, individual insiders ~23.7%, general public ~54.6%. [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/ro/consumer-retailing/bvb-rph/sc-ropharma-shares/ownership)
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder Mihai Miron and entities he controls (ADD Pharmaceuticals Limited, Rimia Investments) together constitute the dominant insider ownership bloc, with Miron personally holding around 20.5% and serving as President/General Director. [BusinessPedia profile of Mihai Miron](https://businesspedia.ro/wiki/mihai-miron-presedintele-consiliului-de-administratie-si-director-general-ropharma-sa/)
thesis.red_flags: Romanian press reported that employees of a Mihai Miron-owned company (in a separate business context, not confirmed to be Ropharma itself) were investigated by prosecutors over alleged money laundering through a monastery's bank account; Miron denied wrongdoing and suggested the investigation followed his public criticism of the Health Minister. This is a reputational matter involving the controlling shareholder that investors should be aware of, though it was not confirmed to directly implicate Ropharma's own operations. [Adevărul investigation report](https://adevarul.ro/stiri-interne/evenimente/angajatii-companiei-miliardarului-mihai-miron-1424819.html)

thesis.business_description: Piaggio & C. SpA, founded in 1884 and headquartered in Pontedera, Italy, is a two-wheeler and light commercial vehicle manufacturer selling scooters, motorcycles and mopeds under the Vespa, Piaggio, Aprilia, Moto Guzzi, Gilera, Derbi and Scarabeo brands, plus three/four-wheeler light commercial vehicles under the Ape and Porter names, with manufacturing in Italy, India and Vietnam and ~5,700-6,100 employees. Source: https://www.morningstar.com.au/investments/security/MIL/PIA/summary
thesis.competitive_position: Global leader in premium scooters (Vespa) and a diversified two/three/four-wheeler maker with distribution via dealers/importers across EMEA, the Americas, Asia Pacific and India; reporting segments are EMEA and Americas/India/Asia Pacific, with two-wheelers generating the majority of revenue. Source: https://www.morningstar.com.au/investments/security/MIL/PIA/summary
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Consob's official 'Piaggio & C. SpA Azionariato' register (snapshot dated 17 September 2026, based on a notification originally dated 24 April 2009): IMMSI S.p.A. holds 53.59% of Piaggio's share capital/voting rights. Per Consob's 31 December 2023 snapshot, this stake flows through a control chain in which Omniaholding S.p.A. is the ultimate holding company controlling IMMSI (which directly holds 53.588% of voting rights), with Omniaholding itself directly holding a further 0.025% (total ~53.613%); the same 2023 snapshot also lists Diego Della Valle (via Diego Della Valle & C. S.r.l.) at 5.498% of voting rights (notified 3 December 2013 — not confirmed as still current in the 2026 snapshot). Matteo Colaninno is Piaggio's Chairman and is also Executive Chairman of Omniaholding and Omniainvest. Source: https://www.consob.it/web/consob-and-its-activities/w/piaggio-c.-spa-azionariato-2 ; https://www.consob.it/web/area-pubblica/w/piaggio-c.-spa-azionariato-2023-12-31 ; https://www.immsi.it/sites/default/files/documents/Matteo%20Colaninno%20CV%20IMMSI%2003.12.2025%20-%20ENG.pdf
thesis.red_flags: Majority control concentrated in the Colaninno family via a multi-layer holding structure (Omniaholding → IMMSI → Piaggio), with family members (Matteo, Michele, Roberto Colaninno) occupying board/chairman roles — a typical Italian family-controlled listed-company structure rather than a specific misconduct flag; no litigation or going-concern issues were identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Boreo Oyj is a Finnish serial-acquirer holding company that owns and develops small/medium-sized businesses across three segments — Electronics (components distribution, e.g. Yleiselektroniikka, Noretron), Technical Trade (industrial products/services, e.g. Machinery, Muottikolmio) and Heavy Machines — operating in Finland, Sweden, the Baltics and internationally.
thesis.competitive_position: Boreo operates a buy-and-build model similar to other Nordic serial acquirers, consolidating niche electronics-distribution and technical-trade businesses under owned brands (Yleiselektroniikka, YE International, Noretron Komponentit, Milcon, Delfin Technologies, Machinery, Pronius, and others); its competitive advantage derives from disciplined capital allocation/M&A and decentralized operating units rather than a single product moat. [Acquirers.com - Boreo: a Finnish serial acquirer](https://www.acquirers.com/post/boreo-a-finnish-serial-acquirer); [stockanalysis.com - Boreo company profile](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/hel/BOREO/company/).
thesis.main_shareholders: Preato Capital AB, controlled by Chairman Simon Hallqvist, is the dominant shareholder with approximately 70-71% of shares (reported variously as 70.02%-70.9% in different filings); AK Capital Oy holds approximately 1.31%. [MarketScreener - Boreo Oyj PDMR transactions, Preato Capital AB](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/BOREO-OYJ-1412572/news/Boreo-Oyj-Plc-Managers-transactions-Preato-Capital-AB-47265568/); [Inderes - Boreo Ownership](https://www.inderes.fi/en/companies/Boreo/ownership).
thesis.insider_ownership: Chairman Simon Hallqvist controls the company via his majority-owned investment vehicle Preato Capital AB (~70% of Boreo), making him the controlling insider; several operating executives and employees (including Ari Wilhelm Sulin ~1.01%, Mikko Petteri Moilanen ~0.95%, Aku Rumpunen ~0.89%) also hold smaller stakes, with over 8% of shares reportedly held by employees via equity issued as acquisition consideration. [Inderes - Boreo Ownership](https://www.inderes.fi/en/companies/Boreo/ownership).
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources regarding litigation or auditor disputes. The company previously had Russian operations that it divested, which is a disclosed geopolitical-exposure item rather than a governance red flag; the very high single-shareholder concentration (~70% via Preato Capital) also means minority shareholders have limited influence over strategy. [Castren & Snellman - Boreo divestment of Russian operations](https://www.castren.fi/cases/boreo-divestment-of-russian-operations/).

thesis.business_description: Growens S.p.A. (formerly MailUp S.p.A.) is an Italian holding company operating in cloud marketing technology, historically known for its MailUp email-marketing and mobile-messaging (SMS) platforms; following 2022-2023 divestitures (MailUp sold to TeamSystem for ~€76.7M; Contactlab, Acumbamail and Datatrics also sold), the group is repositioning around its remaining marketing-technology assets and investments.
thesis.competitive_position: Growens' historical core, MailUp, was a mid-sized multichannel email/SMS marketing platform aimed at small-and-medium businesses in Italy, Europe, the Americas and Asia, competing against larger international ESPs; the 2023 sale of MailUp and other units to TeamSystem for €76.7 million marks a strategic retrenchment into a smaller, more focused portfolio, meaning its current competitive scale and moat are considerably reduced versus its former MailUp-era positioning. [Tech.eu - TeamSystem acquires Growens' MailUp](https://tech.eu/2023/02/03/cloud-marketing-outfit-growens-snaps-up-e-mail/); [MarketScreener - MailUp/TeamSystem sale](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/GROWENS-S-P-A-17039534/news/Finalized-sale-of-MailUp-business-unit-from-Growens-to-TeamSystem-44332888/).
thesis.main_shareholders: Per the company's own shareholder disclosure page, the main holders are: Nazzareno Gorni (via Poliedriq S.r.l.) ~11.76%, Matteo Monfredini (via MM S.r.l.) ~11.62%, Matteo Bettoni (via Linea S.r.l.) ~11.04%, Alberto Miscia (via AM0 S.r.l.) ~10.43%, Luca Azzali (via Yugen S.r.l.) ~10.05%, treasury shares ~9.28%, and free float ~35.82%. [Growens - Shareholders (official)](https://www.growens.io/en/shareholders/).
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder-managers hold a majority bloc: CEO Nazzareno Gorni and CFO Matteo Monfredini, together with co-founders Matteo Bettoni, Alberto Miscia and Luca Azzali, collectively control roughly 55% of shares through personal holding vehicles, indicating high founder/management alignment. [Growens - Shareholders (official)](https://www.growens.io/en/shareholders/).
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources regarding litigation, auditor disputes, or related-party transactions. The major divestiture of the MailUp/Contactlab/Acumbamail/Datatrics businesses in 2022-2023 represents a significant strategic discontinuity that materially shrank the group and should be understood as a business-model risk factor, though it was presented as a planned strategic sale rather than a distress event. [Tech.eu - Growens MailUp sale](https://tech.eu/2023/02/03/cloud-marketing-outfit-growens-snaps-up-e-mail/).

thesis.business_description: Instal Kraków S.A., founded in 1950 and based in Kraków, Poland (WSE-listed since April 1999), is a construction and installation company specializing in water/wastewater treatment infrastructure, power-plant flue-gas and desulphurization/denitrification systems, steel structures, storage tanks, silos, pipelines and HVAC/heating/sanitary installations, serving mainly public-sector clients (municipalities, water/sewage utilities) in Poland and abroad, and also operates a property-development segment. Source: https://Www.investing.com/equities/instal-krakow
thesis.competitive_position: Established Polish environmental/industrial-infrastructure general contractor organized into six segments (Construction & Assembly, Development, Foreign, Light Production, Rental, Other); headcount reported variously at 337-695 (group) or 411-608 depending on source, indicating a mid-sized, specialized contractor rather than a national-scale builder. Source: https://Www.investing.com/equities/instal-krakow ; https://www.aplikuj.pl/pracodawca/75028/instal-krakow-spolka-akcyjna
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Strefa Inwestorów's shareholder-structure table (dated 22 July 2026, sourced from company/GPW disclosures): Juroszek Holding sp. z o.o. holds 2,164,400 shares = 29.71% of capital / 18.55% of AGM votes; Esaliens TFI SA holds 1,273,456 shares = 17.48% of capital / 10.92% of votes; Piotr Juszczyk (also the company's CEO) holds 694,049 shares = 9.53% of capital but 30.08% of votes (reflecting his holding of preference shares with 5x voting weight — this voting-rights mechanism is our inference from the disclosed figures, not stated verbatim in the source, so should be verified against the company's articles of association); Raimondo Eggink holds 601,011 shares = 8.25% of capital / 5.15% of votes. Together these four hold 64.96% of capital and 64.70% of AGM votes out of 7,285,500 total shares (11,666,900 total votes, reflecting 1,095,800 preference shares with 5x weight). Source: https://strefainwestorow.pl/notowania/spolki/PLINSTK00013/akcjonariat . Bankier.pl shows a closely matching 64.93% for the same four holders but a different free-float figure (52.52% vs. Strefa Inwestorów's 35.04%), a methodological discrepancy not resolved in this search. Source: https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/new-connect/INSTALKRK/akcjonariat
thesis.red_flags: CEO Piotr Juszczyk's disproportionate voting power (9.53% of capital translating to ~30% of votes via preference shares) concentrates control in management's hands relative to economic ownership — a standard Polish dual-class mechanism but a material related-party/governance consideration for minority shareholders to weigh. No litigation or going-concern issues were identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Züblin Immobilien Holding AG, headquartered in Zurich (Hardturmstrasse 76) and listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange, is the parent of the Züblin Group, which manages a Swiss real-estate portfolio (properties including Zurich Holbeinstrasse, Zurich Hardturmstrasse, Egg Gewerbestrasse, Bern Morgenstrasse) through subsidiaries Züblin Immobilien AG and Weilimmo AG, deriving revenue mainly from rental income; as of 31 March 2025 the Group operates solely in Switzerland with only four employees. Source: https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/98398-27 ; (company disclosure cited via search)
thesis.competitive_position: A very small, lean real-estate holding vehicle (only 4 employees as of March 2025) with a concentrated Swiss commercial-property portfolio; one (possibly outdated) third-party profile describes a broader historical strategy of buying, redeveloping and selling commercial property across Switzerland, France and Germany, which conflicts with the company's current Swiss-only focus — the current, narrower Swiss-only scope should be treated as the more reliable, recent description. Source: https://www.stockopedia.com/share-prices/zueblin-immobilien-holding-ag-SWX:ZUBN/ (dated/conflicting)
thesis.main_shareholders: We could not confirm an official SIX disclosure-office significant-shareholder filing in this search. Per Simply Wall St (undated, non-official aggregator): Rolf Hänggi is the largest single shareholder with 20.1% (666,875 shares out of ~3.3 million total), followed by Special Themes SCC Ltd at 6.97% and UBS Asset Management AG at 1.55%; the top 10 shareholders together hold only 29.24%, with institutions at 9.13% and free float/public investors at roughly 70.8%. An older Simply Wall St article conflicts, citing the top 2 shareholders together holding 62%, and graph.swiss shows an apparently erroneous 78.82% insider figure — these inconsistencies were not resolved in this search. Not confirmed from an official filing — recommend checking the SIX Swiss Exchange disclosure-of-shareholdings platform and Züblin's own annual report (zueblin.ch) for the authoritative current register. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ch/real-estate-management-and-development/vtx-zubn/zublin-immobilien-holding-shares/ownership
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in this search, though the materially conflicting third-party ownership figures (ranging from a ~29% top-10 concentration to a ~62% top-2 concentration across different aggregator snapshots) represent a data-quality gap that should be resolved via the SIX disclosure platform before relying on any single shareholder percentage. The company's extremely small headcount (4 employees) for a listed real-estate holding entity is typical for an asset-holding vehicle of this type rather than a red flag per se.

thesis.business_description: Immsi S.p.A., founded in 2000 and headquartered in Mantua, Italy, is a diversified holding company controlling more than 40 companies across industrial (via its Piaggio Group stake — Vespa, Piaggio, Aprilia, Moto Guzzi, Gilera, Derbi two-wheelers and Ape/Porter light commercial vehicles), naval (high-speed vessels, hydrofoils, fast ferries, yachts, mine-hunters, patrol boats), and real-estate/tourism (including the Is Molas golf resort near Cagliari) sectors, controlled by the Colaninno family. Source: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/IMS.MI/profile?p=IMS.MI ; https://ismolasresort.com/en/the-developer.html
thesis.competitive_position: Holding-company structure giving the Colaninno family control over a European two-wheeler market leader (Piaggio) plus naval-defense shipbuilding and real estate/tourism assets; Immsi acquired control of Piaggio in 2003 (initially ~31.25% plus management control in exchange for a $115m cash injection and ~$17.2m short-term loan, per a contemporaneous report), and 2018 net revenues across the group were reported at approximately €1,464.5 million (dated figure). Source: https://powersportsbusiness.com/?p=8637 ; https://www.immsi.it/en/group/our-history
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Consob's official 'IMMSI SPA Azionariato' register: the controlling shareholder Omniaholding S.p.A. (Colaninno family vehicle) held 59.143% of voting/ordinary capital in the 2018, 2022 and 2023 year-end snapshots (comprising 44.141% held indirectly through Omniainvest S.p.A., dated 15/04/2016, plus 15.002% held directly); the most recent Consob snapshot (current through 14/06/2026, reflecting a communication dated 15/12/2025) shows Omniaholding's stake reduced to 53.643% of voting rights, with Consob's page not explaining the ~5.5-point reduction between 2023 and 2025/2026. Source: https://www.consob.it/web/area-pubblica/w/immsi-spa-azionariato-2023-12-31 ; https://www.consob.it/web/consob-and-its-activities/w/immsi-spa-azionariato- . Background: the Colaninno group took control in 2002 when Telecom Italia sold a 45% stake to Omniapartecipazioni S.p.A. (controlled by Roberto Colaninno via Omniainvest/Omniaholding), with a subsequent tender offer raising the stake to 50.35%. Source: https://www.immsi.it/en/group/our-history
thesis.red_flags: The unexplained ~5.5 percentage point reduction in Omniaholding's disclosed stake between the 2023 (59.143%) and 2025/2026 (53.643%) Consob snapshots was not accompanied by an explanatory filing found in this search and should be investigated directly via Consob's threshold-crossing notices before drawing conclusions; otherwise, majority family control via a multi-tier holding structure (Omniainvest → Omniaholding → Immsi) is disclosed and typical for this type of Italian family conglomerate. No litigation or going-concern issues were identified.

name: Vassiliko Cement Works Public Company Ltd

thesis.business_description: Vassiliko Cement Works Public Company Ltd, founded in 1963 and headquartered in Nicosia (listed on the Cyprus Stock Exchange since 1996), produces clinker and cement (ordinary Portland, sulphate-resistant low-alkali, blended, and white low-alkali limestone Portland cement), operates quarries (Pyrga, Latouros), ready-mix concrete and aggregates businesses, provides port services, and generates electricity from an on-site photovoltaic park, with sales extending to Cyprus and Israel. Source: https://circulareconomy.cys.org.cy/local-businesses/vassiliko-cement-works-public-company-ltd/
thesis.competitive_position: Described as the largest heavy industry in Cyprus, with ~236 employees and ~71.9 million shares outstanding; recently invested in a photovoltaic park to reduce its environmental footprint and has interests in waste management/energy recovery (ENERCO). Source: https://circulareconomy.cys.org.cy/local-businesses/vassiliko-cement-works-public-company-ltd/
thesis.main_shareholders: Per a CBN.com.cy major-shareholders listing (undated, sourced from CSE disclosures): the Holy Archbishopric of Cyprus holds approximately 26%, HeidelbergCement (via subsidiaries) holds approximately 25.97%, The Cyprus Cement Public Company Ltd holds approximately 25.30%, and the Anastasios G. Leventis Foundation holds approximately 5.33%, with free float at approximately 17.13%. The same source notes that The Cyprus Cement Public Company Ltd is itself majority-controlled by its Chairman, George S. Galatariotis, at 70.20% — meaning a meaningful portion of Vassiliko's ~25.3% Cyprus Cement-held block traces indirectly to the Galatariotis family, though the source does not state this connection explicitly (this linkage is our inference). Source: https://www.cbn.com.cy/article/132145/major-shareholders-in-30-cypriot-companies-changes-in-the-share-capital-of-listed-firms . Not independently confirmed against a dated, official CSE filing in this search — recommend verifying via the company's current share-capital dispersion statement.
thesis.red_flags: An unusual ownership structure in which a religious institution (Holy Archbishopric of Cyprus, ~26%) and an industry peer/competitor-linked entity (The Cyprus Cement Public Company, ~25.3%) are both large shareholders alongside a global building-materials major (HeidelbergCement, ~25.97%) — this concentrated, cross-holding structure among a small number of large blocks (combined ~77%) leaves limited free float (~17%) and warrants governance attention regarding related-party dynamics between competing cement producers, though no specific misconduct was identified. Source: https://www.cbn.com.cy/article/132145/major-shareholders-in-30-cypriot-companies-changes-in-the-share-capital-of-listed-firms

thesis.business_description: Vertu Motors plc, headquartered in Gateshead, UK (established 2006/2007, AIM-listed), is a car dealership group that sells new and used cars, motorcycles, commercial vehicles and vans and provides aftersales services (servicing, MOT, parts, bodyshop) through more than 200 sites across England and Scotland, trading as franchised dealer for brands including Volkswagen, Land Rover, Audi, Mercedes-Benz, Jaguar, Kia and Toyota, having consolidated legacy brands (Bristol Street Motors, Macklin Motors) under the single Vertu name in early 2025. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertu_Motors
thesis.competitive_position: One of the UK's larger automotive retail groups, grown substantially through acquisitions (Farnell Land Rover 2013, Hughes Group Holdings 2018, Helston Garages 2022, Rowes Garage 2023, Burrows Motors Company), generating the largest share of revenue from used-car sales; named Retailer of the Year at the 2025 Autotrader Retailer Awards. FY2026 revenue reported at roughly £4.8bn by one aggregator (unverified against company accounts). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertu_Motors
thesis.main_shareholders: We did not find Vertu's own Annual Report & Accounts substantial-shareholdings table (Directors' Report) directly in this search; the figures below come from third-party trackers and are not independently confirmed against an official filing. Per Simply Wall St (AIM:VTU, undated snapshot): TDR Capital LLP ~10.7%, Schroder Investment Management ~10.3%, Tweedy, Browne Company ~7.58%, Nivag Holdings ~5.34%, TrinityBridge ~4.68%, with CEO Robert Forrester holding ~5.9 million shares (~1.9%); top 25 shareholders own ~76.98% in total. A separate AJ Bell profile (undated, conflicting) instead shows CAG Vega 2 Ltd at ~10.13% and Artemis Investment Management at ~9.20%, which does not reconcile with the Simply Wall St figures, indicating different snapshot dates or methodologies. Not confirmed from an official filing — recommend checking the 2025/2026 Annual Report & Notice of AGM (published 27 May 2025, at investors.vertumotors.com) directly for the authoritative substantial-shareholdings table. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/retail/aim-vtu/vertu-motors-shares/ownership
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; however, we were unable to locate or verify a current official (company-filed) substantial-shareholdings disclosure in this search, and the two third-party aggregators found materially disagree with each other — this is a research gap requiring direct verification via the company's Annual Report rather than a confirmed governance issue.

thesis.business_description: Zinzino AB, headquartered in Gothenburg, Sweden, is a direct-selling (network-marketing) company specializing in test-based, personalized nutrition, selling omega-6/omega-3 balance supplements (BalanceOil), immune/brain health products, skincare, weight-control products and beverages through independent distributors across 100+ markets, reporting via two segments (Zinzino and Faun, with Zinzino generating the majority of revenue). Source: https://www.plunkettresearch.com/?p=1897137 ; https://morningstar.com.au/investments/security/osto/ZZ%20B
thesis.competitive_position: Scandinavian-headquartered global direct-seller with a differentiated test-based personalized-nutrition model; grew via acquisition, including a June 2025 asset purchase from French direct seller Ecosystem (distributor database, customer records, inventory and IP) to expand distribution in France and DOM-TOM territories. Listed on Nasdaq First North Premier Growth Market. Source: https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/zinzino-zinzino-ab-publ-zinzino-acquires-assets-from-ecosystem-for-increased-distribution-power-in-france-and-dom-tom-20250610
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Inderes (using Millistream data), the controlling shareholders are Örjan and Hilde Saele (via company and family) at approximately 28.5-29.3% of capital but 47.1-47.6% of votes, and Peter Sörensen (via company) at approximately 12.3-12.5% of capital and 25.4-25.7% of votes — indicating a dual-class (A/B) share structure that concentrates voting power well above economic ownership for these two holders. Source: https://www.inderes.fi/en/companies/Zinzino/ownership. CEO Dag Bergheim Pettersen holds a comparatively small stake, reported by Simply Wall St at 3.39% (~1.23 million shares). Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/retail/sto-zz-b/zinzino-shares/news/zinzino-ab-publs-stozz-b-market-cap-rose-kr481m-last-week-in. We could not confirm the exact current percentages from a Finansinspektionen flagging notice in this search; the Inderes figures are aggregator-derived from Millistream data rather than a primary company filing.
thesis.red_flags: Combined, the Saele and Sörensen blocks control roughly 73% of votes from only ~41-42% of capital (per aggregator data), a significant disproportionate-control structure via dual-class shares that substantially limits ordinary (B-share) minority shareholders' influence over governance — a disclosed structural feature rather than misconduct, but a material consideration for minority investors. Source: https://www.inderes.fi/en/companies/Zinzino/ownership. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources; direct-selling/MLM business models generally carry higher regulatory and reputational scrutiny as a sector characteristic.

thesis.business_description: All for One Group SE is a German IT consulting and services group focused on SAP and related enterprise software (ERP/S/4HANA transformation, cloud and managed services, software licences and support) for mid-sized and larger companies, mainly in the DACH region. FY2025/26 (to 30 September) guidance is revenue of EUR 500-530m; nine-month sales to June 2026 were EUR 379.6m, with consulting revenue up 2% only because of the acquired apsolut Group, and software and support down 8%. Sources: https://cdn.all-for-one.com/corporate-media/company/investor_relations/zwischenberichte/quarterly-statement-3-2025-26-all41g-en-040826.pdf ; https://www.all-for-one.com/en/company/news-press/detail/figures-for-q3-2025-26.html
thesis.competitive_position: A large SAP partner in the German-speaking mid-market that grows partly through acquisitions (most recently the apsolut Group). It operates in a competitive SAP services market under a weak macro backdrop, and margins have collapsed: nine-month EBIT before M&A effects was -EUR 9.3m (vs +EUR 17.5m) due to one-off costs of the 'Precision' efficiency programme, which targets about EUR 20m in annual savings from autumn 2026. FY2025/26 EBIT guidance before M&A effects was cut to about EUR 0m (+/- EUR 5m). TAKEOVER: VINCI Energies (subsidiary of VINCI S.A.) launched a EUR 67.50 per share cash offer (announced July 2026, about 94.5% premium to the 15 July 2026 close) with a 75% minimum acceptance; the boards recommended acceptance and the acceptance period ran 12 August - 15 September 2026, with completion expected in Q4 2026. Sources: https://quartr.com/events/all-for-one-group-se-a1os-q2-25-26_FMPWL2uR ; https://live.deutsche-boerse.com/news/EQS-News-Management-Board-and-Supervisory-Board-of-All-for-One-Group-SE-recommend-accepting-the-public-takeover-offer-from-VINCI-Energies-f4e9792a-25f7-4281-b4d4-90265dbddcf2 ; https://www.vinci-energies.de/app/uploads/sites/28/2026/08/2026-08-12-Press-Release-VINCI-Energies-acceptance-period-share-cash-offer-All-for-One-afo.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: Anchor holder Unternehmens Invest AG (UIAG) group: the company IR page (figures from 2023 or earlier) shows Unternehmens Invest AG about 15%, UIAG Informatik-Holding GmbH about 25% and UIAG AFO GmbH about 10%, together just over 50%. Simply Wall St (aggregator, July 2026) shows Unternehmens Invest AG 15.5% and UIAG Informatik-Holding 36.2% (likely combining vehicles). UIAG agreed to tender to VINCI Energies (subject to its own EGM on 10 August 2026), and agreements with the largest shareholders covered about 54.7% of share capital. The final offer acceptance level and whether the 75% threshold was met could NOT be confirmed in this search - check the takeover page for the outcome. Sources: https://all-for-one.com/en/company/investors/share/shareholder-structure ; https://www.evi.gv.at/b/pi/bpj-gbc ; https://www.whitecase.com/news/press-release/white-case-advises-uiag-voluntary-public-takeover-offer-vinci-energies-all-one ; https://www.all-for-one.com/en/company/investors/share/public-takeover-offer/
thesis.red_flags: Pending takeover by VINCI Energies at EUR 67.50 - if completed, the stock is likely to be delisted or squeezed out, so it may no longer be investable as a value idea; the outcome of the 75% acceptance condition was not confirmed here. Operationally, earnings guidance was cut to roughly breakeven EBIT before M&A effects for FY2025/26 because of restructuring costs and weak software/support revenue. Controlling-shareholder influence (UIAG group ~50%). Sources: https://www.rttnews.com/3667497/vinci-energies-launches-tender-offer-to-acquire-all-for-one.aspx ; https://cdn.all-for-one.com/corporate-media/company/investor_relations/zwischenberichte/quarterly-statement-3-2025-26-all41g-en-040826.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: Supervisory board member Dr Rudolf Knuenz (linked to UIAG) dealt via Knuenz Invest Beteiligungs GmbH (purchases in March and April 2026), and a 22 September 2026 directors' dealing notice refers to Knuenz Invest accepting the VINCI offer; he personally held 27,554 shares after a February 2026 purchase (per directors-deals listing). Holdings of management board members Michael Zitz (CEO) and Stefan Land could not be located in this search (research gap). Sources: https://all-for-one.com/en/company/investors/corporate-governance/directors-dealings ; https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/shares-search-results/a/all-for-one-group-se-npv/director-deals ; https://www.boerse-online.de/dpa-afx/eqs-dd-all-for-one-group-se-deutsch-553386.html

thesis.business_description: Ponsse Oyj, founded in 1970 by Einari Vidgrén and headquartered in Vieremä, Finland, develops, manufactures and markets cut-to-length forest harvesting machines (harvesters, forwarders, harvester heads, cranes) together with proprietary forestry information/control systems (Opti) and after-sales service/training. Source: https://web.lib.aalto.fi/fi/old/yrityspalvelin/pdf/2007/Eponsse2007.pdf ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ponsse
thesis.competitive_position: One of the world's leading specialist manufacturers of cut-to-length forest machines, exporting roughly 75% of net sales to 40+ countries through a global subsidiary/dealer network; differentiated by its integrated Opti information-systems ecosystem for harvesting/logistics planning rather than competing purely on hardware. Source: https://www.cbinsights.com/company/ponsse-oyj ; https://www.morningstar.com.au/investments/security/fra/PNS
thesis.main_shareholders: Ponsse is controlled by the founding Vidgrén family: per the company's own 2010 stock-exchange notice, founder Einari Vidgrén's estate held 13,348,074 shares (47.67% of votes) out of 28,000,000 shares, to be divided equally among his four heirs (Janne, Juha, Jarmo and a fourth heir), three of whom (Janne, Juha, Jarmo Vidgrén) are/were employed by or on the board of Ponsse. Source: https://www.ponsse.com/company/investors/releases/-/asset_publisher/XbANRjhQNz7o/content/flagging-announcement-pursuant-to-chapter-2-section-10-of-the-securities-markets-act. Wikipedia (citing company sources, dated ~2024) lists Jarmo Vidgrén as current Chairman. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ponsse. We could not extract a current, itemized 'largest owners' percentage table from Ponsse's investor-relations ownership page or Inderes in this search; the ~47.67% family estate figure is from 2010 and almost certainly understates the family's current combined stake after the inheritance split, so exact present-day percentages per individual family member are not confirmed and should be checked against Ponsse's current flagging announcements.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; family/founder control (Vidgrén family, historically ~48%+ of votes) is a long-standing, disclosed structure typical of Finnish industrial family businesses rather than a governance red flag. Source: https://www.ponsse.com/company/investors/releases/-/asset_publisher/XbANRjhQNz7o/content/flagging-announcement-pursuant-to-chapter-2-section-10-of-the-securities-markets-act

thesis.business_description: Stockholm-headquartered medical-software company (founded 2000 as a spin-off from Karolinska Institute, listed on Nasdaq Stockholm) that develops software for radiation therapy of cancer. Products are grouped into RayStation (proprietary treatment planning system), partner products and research offerings. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RaySearch_Laboratories ; https://www.raysearchlabs.com/organisation/
thesis.competitive_position: Vendor-neutral treatment-planning niche: RayStation works with both Varian and Elekta machines, while those machine makers sell their own planning software (Varian is now owned by Siemens Healthineers). Swedish press analysis puts RaySearch at roughly 11% of the installed base of planning systems and 15-20% of new sales, and strongest in ion (proton/carbon) therapy; these share figures come from secondary press/blog sources and installed-base counts conflict across sources (280 vs 2,600+ clinics), so treat as indicative. Q4 2025 revenue was reported as MSEK 375 (+16.3%) with a 24.5% EBIT margin (secondary-source summary of the year-end report). Elekta's integrated MR-Linac Unity is cited as a competitive threat. Sources: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/raysearch-gar-mot-en-stralande-framtid ; https://mfn.se/a/raysearch-laboratories/year-end-report-2025-record-revenue-and-strong-earnings-growth-despite-currency-headwinds.iframe
thesis.main_shareholders: Founder/CEO Johan Löf is the largest holder: per a Finansinspektionen flagging notice after a March 2025 sell-down of 2,000,000 B-shares he held 10.2% of share capital and 40.5% of votes. Simply Wall St (aggregator, undated) also lists him as largest holder at about 10.2% (3.5m shares), with Anders Brahme about 3.7% and Carl Bergendal about 3.4%. Could not locate a current dated top-shareholder table (annual report / Euroclear-Modular Finance list), and could not confirm any holding by Melker Schorling or Hans Wigzell; treat as a research gap. Share structure at 30 Dec 2025: 34,282,773 shares (3,483,237 A at 10 votes; 30,799,536 B at 1 vote), 65,631,906 votes in total, after 2,171,738 A shares were converted to B in December 2025 (so vote percentages from earlier in 2025 are stale). Sources: https://mfn.se/cis/a/fi-se/finansinspektionen-flaggningsmeddelande-i-raysearch-laboratories-ab-publ-9b750062 ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/healthcare/sto-ray-b/raysearch-laboratories-shares/ownership ; https://mfn.se/a/raysearch-laboratories/new-number-of-votes-in-raysearch-laboratories-ab-due-to-conversion.iframe
thesis.red_flags: Dual-class structure (A shares 10 votes) gives the founder-CEO voting influence well above his ~10% capital stake and concentrates key-person risk in one individual; a 2016 governance report said the board saw no need for a nomination committee given the ownership structure (old, current practice not verified). Planning software competes with the machine makers' own offerings. No lawsuits, investigations, short-seller reports or auditor issues turned up in this search, but this is not an exhaustive legal check. Sources: https://mfn.se/cis/a/fi-se/finansinspektionen-flaggningsmeddelande-i-raysearch-laboratories-ab-publ-9b750062 ; https://www.raysearchlabs.com/siteassets/investors/corporate-governance/corp-gov-reports/corp-gov-report-2016.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder, CEO and board member Johan Löf: 10.2% of capital and 40.5% of votes after the March 2025 sell-down (FI notice). The company's organisation page lists him with 3,443,084 Class A and 77,636 Class B shares (undated). Conflicting/stale data: a December 2021 release gave 19.1% of capital and 56.8% of votes; his vote share after the December 2025 A-to-B conversions could not be confirmed. Other board/management holdings not located in this search; research gap. Sources: https://mfn.se/cis/a/fi-se/finansinspektionen-flaggningsmeddelande-i-raysearch-laboratories-ab-publ-9b750062 ; https://www.raysearchlabs.com/organisation/ ; https://mb.cision.com/Main/1102/3480076/1515984.pdf

thesis.business_description: Nexteq plc (formerly Quixant plc) is a UK-based, AIM-listed supplier of technology to industrial equipment makers. It has two divisions. Quixant designs embedded computing platforms; MarketBeat says it is historically gaming-focused, but this was not confirmed in official sources here. Densitron supplies display, touch and human-machine-interface solutions. FY2025 (to 31 Dec 2025) revenue was USD 90.2m (+4%): Quixant USD 60.1m (+10%), Densitron USD 30.1m (-6%). Adjusted PBT was USD 3.6m (-25%) and year-end net cash USD 25.0m. The exact head-office town was not confirmed in this search (filings show addresses in Crawley and Balsham, Cambridge). Sources: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/nexteq--nxq/audited-final-results/9479239 ; https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/LON/NXQ/earnings/chart/news/news/news/chart
thesis.competitive_position: Nexteq is a niche B2B hardware partner: products are designed into long-life customer equipment, which creates switching costs but also long sales cycles. In 2025 Quixant grew even though its historically largest customer cut activity (linked to that customer's 'corporate activity'), and it won a new largest customer. Densitron was hurt by end-of-life components and slow ramp-up of large new contracts. In December 2025 the board guided 2026 revenue to at least USD 85m and pushed its three-year plan back 12 months, to end-FY28. The company returns cash through buybacks (shares held in treasury) and a proposed 3.9p dividend. Sources: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/nexteq--nxq/audited-final-results/9479239 ; https://www.ticker.app/lse/NXQ/rns/2025-12-18/Trading-Update/0203M
thesis.main_shareholders: Founder Nick Jarmany and connected persons hold 11,131,163 shares, which is 16.74% of issued capital including treasury (RNS) and 20.55% of voting rights at 30 Dec 2025 (MarketScreener, an aggregator). Liontrust Investment Partners holds 10.80% (5,850,088 voting rights; TR-1 notified 4 Aug 2026, down from 11.06% on 31 Jul 2026). Simply Wall St (aggregator, undated, likely stale) also lists Lombard Odier AM about 11%, Chen-Tai Lin about 5.8%, Chelverton AM about 5.3% and Crucible Clarity Fund about 5.0%; these were not verified against TR-1 filings. At 9 Mar 2026 there were 66,539,060 issued shares, of which 9,791,806 in treasury, giving 56,747,254 voting rights; buybacks continued afterwards. Aggregator insider and institutional totals conflict widely (insiders 33-46%). Sources: https://ca.marketscreener.com/insider/NICHOLAS-JARMANY-A046XM/ ; https://kalkinemedia.com/uk/news/announcements/liontrust-investment-partners-lowers-nexteq-plc-nxq-stake-to-1080-after-crossing-august-2026-regulatory-threshold ; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/nexteq--nxq/transaction-in-own-shares-and-total-voting-rights-/9463522 ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/consumer-services/aim-nxq/nexteq-shares/ownership
thesis.red_flags: No accounting or litigation issues found in official sources. Operating risks: (1) customer concentration, with Quixant's historical largest customer cutting orders and a new largest customer now driving growth. (2) Weaker momentum: 2026 guidance of at least USD 85m is below 2025 revenue of USD 90.2m, the three-year plan was delayed to FY28, gross margin fell from 35.9% to 32.8% and operating cash flow dropped from USD 13.0m to USD 3.5m. (3) Shareholdings are concentrated (top 25 holders about 92% per Simply Wall St), so liquidity is thin, and the founder is leaving the board. The balance sheet is a mitigant (USD 25.0m net cash). Sources: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/nexteq--nxq/audited-final-results/9479239 ; https://www.ticker.app/lse/NXQ/rns/2025-12-18/Trading-Update/0203M ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/consumer-services/aim-nxq/nexteq-shares/ownership
thesis.insider_ownership: Nick Jarmany founded Quixant and was CEO until 2018, then Deputy Chair and Interim Chair from August 2024. With connected persons he holds 11.13m shares (about 20.5% of voting rights, about 16.7% of issued capital). He was due to retire from the board on 31 Aug 2026 but stay a significant shareholder, so his stake may no longer count as board insider ownership after that date. Non-Executive Chair Carol Thompson sold 20,000 shares on 2 Apr 2025 (aggregator). Holdings of CEO Duncan Faithfull and CFO Matt Staight were not found in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.stockopedia.com/share-prices/nexteq-LON:NXQ/news/director-pdmr-share-transfers-019e6d7d-f95c-7bf0-9088-f7882b972da0/ ; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/nexteq--nxq/board-transition/8327223 ; https://www.stockopedia.com/share-prices/nexteq-LON:NXQ/news/appointment-of-interim-chair-019e6da4-2d72-77c2-a19f-bce5ae914307/

name: Hellenic Exchanges - Athens Stock Exchange S.A.

thesis.business_description: Hellenic Exchanges - Athens Stock Exchange S.A. (ATHEX: EXAE), founded in 1876 and headquartered in Athens (renamed from Hellenic Exchanges S.A. in December 2013), operates Greece's capital-market infrastructure: equities and derivatives trading venues, an alternative market, clearing and settlement (including acting as central counterparty and system administrator for the Athens Exchange Clearing House), central securities depository services, and listing/registry/regulatory and IT/digital services. Source: https://wealthyhood.com/en/stocks/exae.at ; https://www.roic.ai/quote/EXAE.AT
thesis.competitive_position: The sole operator of Greece's national stock exchange and clearing infrastructure (a natural-monopoly market-infrastructure business); as of 17 November 2025 it operates as a subsidiary of Euronext N.V. following Euronext's tender offer, with reported headcount of 228-244 employees. Source: https://www.roic.ai/quote/EXAE.AT
thesis.main_shareholders: Per official reporting on Euronext's tender offer outcome (Hellenic Capital Market Commission-approved public offer): Euronext N.V. acquired approximately 74.25% of Hellenic Exchanges' voting rights (approximately 42.95 million tendered shares), confirmed via Greek financial press (Skai.gr) and corroborated by RTE's report that Euronext's tender offer for 100% of Hellenic Exchanges became unconditional following Hellenic Capital Market Commission approval (dated 14 November 2025). Source: https://www.skai.gr/news/business/euronext-me-isxyro-7425-apokta-ton-elegxo-tou-xrimatistiriou-athinon ; https://www.rte.ie/news/athex . Sources do not agree on whether Euronext's final stake moved beyond the reported 74.25% after the full offer period closed, and the remaining (~25.75%) free-float/other-shareholder composition was not identified in this search — recommend checking Euronext's or Euronext Athens' (post-rename) official shareholder disclosures for the definitive current stake.
thesis.red_flags: Hellenic Exchanges is now majority/supermajority-controlled by Euronext N.V. (~74.25% as of November 2025), following a full-company tender offer — this is a disclosed, regulator-approved change of control (not a misconduct flag) but represents a fundamental, recent shift in governance and strategic direction (including a targeted move to Euronext's Optiq trading platform and €12m/year targeted cost synergies by 2028) that materially changes the investment profile of any remaining minority stake. Source: https://www.skai.gr/news/business/euronext-me-isxyro-7425-apokta-ton-elegxo-tou-xrimatistiriou-athinon

thesis.business_description: P.A. Nova S.A., based in Gliwice, Poland, is a construction and real-estate development company that acts as general contractor for commercial, residential, office and industrial buildings, provides architectural design services, and develops and leases commercial property — primarily retail parks and shopping centres (e.g., in Jaworzno, Kędzierzyn-Koźle, Przemyśl, Kłodzko, Sosnowiec). Source: https://m.uk.investing.com/equities/p.a.-nova-company-profile ; https://eurobuildcee.com/en/news/22574-pa-nova-busy-on-a-few-fronts
thesis.competitive_position: Dual-revenue model combining construction/general-contracting and design fees with recurring lease income from its own retail-park/shopping-centre portfolio (owned ten commercial buildings including four shopping centres, an office building and five retail parks per a historical report); 2016 revenue was split roughly PLN 106.2m construction/design vs PLN 71m leasing, illustrating the balance between the two business lines (note: figures are dated and should be checked against current reports). Source: https://eurobuildcee.com/en/news/20768-growing-revenue-of-pa-nova-group
thesis.main_shareholders: Per a shareholder-structure table dated 17 June 2026 (Strefa Inwestorów, sourced from GPW/company disclosures): Budoprojekt sp. z o.o. holds 2,436,000 shares = 24.36% of capital and 34.31% of general-meeting votes (reflecting preference shares); PKO BP Bankowy OFE holds 11.60% of shares/8.17% of votes; Generali PTE holds 10.73%/7.56%; Allianz Polska OFE holds 9.24%/6.51% (this Allianz figure matches a separate 2023 ESPI notice); individual holders Stanisław Lessaer (6.38%/7.60%), Ewa Bobkowska (6.20%/7.53%) and Maciej Bobkowski (5.35%/6.58%) are also disclosed; the company itself holds ~0.30% treasury shares. Together these holders control ~74.17% of shares and ~78.47% of votes, leaving free float of ~26.13% of shares. Share capital is 10,000,000 zł with 14,200,000 total general-meeting votes due to 4,200,000 double-voting preference shares. Source: https://strefainwestorow.pl/notowania/spolki/PLPANVA00013/akcjonariat ; https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/new-connect/PANOVA/akcjonariat
thesis.red_flags: Dual-class (preference) share structure concentrates voting power above economic ownership for several insider holders (e.g., Budoprojekt's 24.36% capital stake translates to 34.31% of votes), a standard Polish-market control mechanism rather than a misconduct flag; no litigation or going-concern issues were identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Orsero S.p.A., headquartered in Milan, is a leading Mediterranean-Europe importer, distributor and marketer of fresh fruit and vegetables, operating an integrated supply chain (sourcing, shipping, ripening, distribution, marketing) across three segments — Distribution (citrus, apples, melons, pears, exotics, avocados, bananas, pineapples under F.lli Orsero and Simba brands), Shipping (banana/pineapple imports), and Holding & Services — with subsidiaries in Italy, France, Spain, Portugal, Greece, Costa Rica, Colombia and Mexico. Source: https://de.finance.yahoo.com/quote/WRG.F/profile ; https://bestfoodimporters.com/company/orsero-spa/
thesis.competitive_position: A leading fresh-produce import/distribution player in Mediterranean Europe with roughly €1.7bn in sales, 300+ product items and an 80+ year family-business heritage; most revenue is generated in Europe via the Distribution segment, and the company is listed on Euronext STAR Milan after moving from AIM Italia. Source: https://bestfoodimporters.com/company/orsero-spa/
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Orsero's own regulatory filings (via emarketstorage.it, the official Italian regulated-information storage mechanism): the controlling shareholder is FIF Holding S.p.A., whose capital is held entirely by members of the founding Orsero family together with the Ighina and Ottonello families — per an April 2026 shareholders'-agreement update, the FIF Holding parties are Anna Chiara Orsero, Antonio Orsero, Raffaella Orsero, UMA S.r.l. (wholly owned by Raffaella Orsero, following a 2025 share transfer), Leonardo Ighina, Lorenzo Ighina and Pierangelo Ottonello, with Anna Chiara Orsero's shares in FIF having been assigned to her wholly-owned company ACO S.r.l. Historical FIF Holding stakes in Orsero itself were disclosed at 39.39% (March 2017), 33.51% (August 2017) and 31.61% (late September 2017); Grupo Fernández S.A. crossed the 5% threshold in 2017 with 5.66% (1,000,000 shares), and a separate shareholders' agreement between FIF Holding and Grupo Fernández S.A. covering Orsero shares was renewed in 2025 for a further three years, through 26 September 2028. We did not find a 2024-2026 percentage figure for FIF Holding's current stake in this search — the April 2026 filing itself likely contains it but the exact percentage was not visible in our search excerpt. Source: https://www.emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2026-04/20260410_181795.pdf ; https://emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2022-05/20171002_36158.pdf
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; the FIF Holding/Grupo Fernández shareholders' agreements (renewed through 2028) and governance commitments (e.g., appointment of an independent director at both FIF and Orsero) are disclosed and standard for a family-controlled listed company. The precise current FIF Holding percentage stake should be confirmed directly from the April 2026 emarketstorage.it filing or Orsero's own 'Azionariato' investor-relations page, as we could not extract the exact current figure in this search.

thesis.business_description: Bonduelle SCA, founded in 1853 and headquartered in Renescure (operational base Villeneuve d'Ascq), France, is a global leader in canned, frozen and fresh ready-to-eat vegetables (Bonduelle, Cassegrain, Globus brands and pulses), selling to households and the catering/foodservice sector in 100+ countries via 42 production sites worldwide (as of end-June 2024), ranking first in Europe for prepared salads; France (~33% of sales) and the US (~23%) are its largest markets. Source: https://live.euronext.com/en/product/equities/FR0000063935-XPAR/company-information
thesis.competitive_position: A global leader in processed/ready-to-eat vegetables with annual sales over €2.2 billion (FY2024-25); pursuing a 'Transform to win' strategic plan that included divesting its packaged-salad business in France and Germany (effective 2025); product mix roughly 47% canned, 40% fresh, 13% frozen. Source: https://live.euronext.com/en/product/equities/FR0000063935-XPAR/company-information
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Bonduelle's own AMF regulatory filings: the company is a société en commandite par actions (partnership limited by shares) whose general partner (associé commandité) is Pierre et Benoît Bonduelle SAS, held by family shareholders. Per the AMF declaration of 12 December 2023 (concert-holdings table, following the La Plaine merger on 7 December 2023), the Bonduelle family concert held 48.64% of capital / 60.27% of voting rights, with Pierre et Benoît Bonduelle SAS holding 21.90% of capital / 27.16% of votes within that total. A subsequent AMF regularization filing (26 September 2024) disclosed that the concert had actually crossed the 50% capital threshold on 7 December 2023 (reaching 50.26% of capital / 62.21% of voting rights, due to additional family members — representing 1.62% of capital — joining the concert), and that at the later declaration date the concert held 50.01% of capital / 61.67% of voting rights; the concert requested, and the filing discusses, a derogation from the mandatory tender-offer obligation under the AMF's General Regulation given the family nature of the threshold crossing. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/307/8888/01/FC307555205_20240926.pdf ; https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/307/8888/01/FC307514763_20231213.pdf
thesis.red_flags: The Bonduelle family concert's crossing of the 50% capital / 62% voting-rights threshold in December 2023 (confirmed/regularized in a September 2024 AMF filing) triggered a request for derogation from the mandatory takeover-bid obligation — a disclosed, legitimate family-reorganization mechanism (tied to the La Plaine SA merger) rather than a misconduct flag, but it is a material governance event that materially increased family control and should be understood by any minority investor. No litigation or going-concern issues were identified. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/307/8888/01/FC307555205_20240926.pdf

thesis.business_description: Eimskipafélag Íslands hf. (Eimskip), founded in 1914 and headquartered in Reykjavík, is an Icelandic shipping and logistics company operating two main segments: Liner Services (ocean container transport, terminal operations, cold storage, trucking) focused on the North Atlantic (North America-Iceland-Norway corridor), and Forwarding Services (dry and temperature-controlled freight forwarding via a global partner network). Source: https://ar.eimskip.com/the-company/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eimskip
thesis.competitive_position: Leading Icelandic shipping/logistics operator and a specialist in frozen/chilled cargo (fish, including trawler discharge/re-packing services) between Iceland, mainland Europe and North America, with roughly 1,600+ employees and dozens of offices across ~20 countries (figures vary by year); listed on Nasdaq Iceland (EIM). Source: https://ar.eimskip.com/the-company/
thesis.main_shareholders: Eimskip's own 2026 AGM shareholder-structure summary ('shss 2026') lists Seley ehf. as the top entry in its '20 largest shareholders' table as of year-end 2025, out of total share capital of ISK 165,700,000 (161,725,000 voting shares after treasury-share exclusion) and 1,011 registered shareholders. Source: https://www.eimskip.com/media/chhdd1zv/shss-2026.pdf. We could not extract the exact percentage held by Seley ehf. or the remaining top-20 holders from the available excerpt in this search; a dated third-party (Dun & Bradstreet) profile separately states that investment firms Landsbanki and Yucaipa collectively owned about 75% of Eimskip, but this figure is clearly outdated (pre-2010 era ownership) and should not be relied on for current structure. Source: https://www.dnb.com/business-directory/company-profiles.eimskipafelag_islands_hf.2ce779519f3c5fa52457e4745321079f.html. The current, accurate ownership table should be pulled directly from the full AGM PDF or Nasdaq Iceland's shareholder register.
thesis.red_flags: An indefinite strike by bosuns and able seamen on three Eimskip vessels began around 25 May 2026 after failed wage negotiations, reported to risk disrupting sailing schedules — an operational/labor-relations risk rather than a governance or solvency flag. Source: https://maritime-executive.com/article/seafarers-begin-strike-against-three-ships-owned-by-iceland-s-eimskip. No litigation, going-concern or dilution red flags were identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: TKM Grupp AS (formerly Tallinna Kaubamaja Grupp AS, renamed March 2024), headquartered in Tallinn and tracing back to a 1960 department store, is a diversified Estonian retail and services group whose main business is the Selver supermarket/hypermarket chain (~70 stores), alongside Kaubamaja department stores, Delice food stores, I.L.U. beauty shops, KIA/Peugeot/Škoda/Cadillac car dealerships, Viking Security guarding services, a ready-meal kitchen (Kulinaaria OÜ), and commercial real estate (~30 buildings including shopping centres). Source: https://tkmgrupp.ee/en ; https://m.uk.investing.com/equities/tallinna-kaubamaja-grupp-as
thesis.competitive_position: One of Estonia's largest trading groups, accounting for close to a tenth of all Estonian retail trade with over 4,700 employees and consolidated 2023 sales of €947.3m; its 'Partner Card' loyalty program (750,000+ regular customers) is the largest in Estonia, giving it a strong customer-data/cross-sell advantage across its retail, grocery and car-dealership businesses. Source: https://tkmgrupp.ee/en
thesis.main_shareholders: TKM Grupp AS is itself a subsidiary of OÜ NG Investeeringud per the company's own corporate description. Source: https://tkmgrupp.ee/en. A third-party aggregator (Simply Wall St, undated) lists NG Kapital OÜ as holding approximately 67.1% of shares (27,328,136 shares), with Swedbank-managed Estonian and Latvian investment funds each holding roughly 1-2%. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ee/consumer-retailing/tlse-tkm1t/tkm-grupp-shares/ownership. We could not confirm the exact current percentage directly from a company flagging notice or the Estonian Central Register of Securities (Nasdaq CSD) in this search; the 67.1% figure should be treated as an aggregator estimate pending verification against an official filing. The 2025 AGM record noted 66 shareholders were represented, consistent with a dominant controlling owner plus a modest minority base. Source: https://www.tkmgrupp.ee/wp-content/uploads/2026-Noukogu-aruanne-2025-kohta.pdf
thesis.red_flags: High ownership concentration in a single holding vehicle (NG Kapital OÜ / NG Investeeringud, estimated ~67% per aggregator data) limits free float and minority-shareholder influence, though this is a disclosed family/holding-company control structure rather than evidence of misconduct. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ee/consumer-retailing/tlse-tkm1t/tkm-grupp-shares/ownership. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Helio S.A. is a Polish company, founded in 1992 and based in Zaborów, that produces and markets dried fruits, nuts, candied fruit, cake masses/icings, and microwave popcorn under the HELIO brand, sold to retail chains and wholesalers. [Helio company profile - Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/HEL.WA/profile/)
thesis.competitive_position: Helio is described as a leader in Poland's dried fruits and nuts industry, built as a 100%-Polish-owned family business; it has achieved strong recent earnings growth, though it remains a relatively small-cap niche food producer. [Bridges Magazine: why HELIO is Poland's Dried Fruits & Nuts Industry Leader](https://sms-bridges.com/in-a-nutshell-heres-why-helio-is-polands-dried-fruits-nuts-industry-leader/)
thesis.main_shareholders: Founders Leszek and Justyna Wąsowicz are the controlling shareholders; Leszek Wąsowicz has been reported holding a majority stake historically disclosed at 77.1% of share capital and votes, with company insiders collectively holding roughly 92% of shares per aggregator data. [Helio investor relations - shareholding change notice](https://www.helio.pl/en/investor-relations/public-offering-of-shares/history-of-shares-transactions/change-in-a-shareholders-share-in-the-total-vote-by-the-shareholder-who-held-over-33percent-of-the-total-vote), [Helio company profile - stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/wse/HEL/company/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is very high and founder-controlled: Leszek and Justyna Wąsowicz founded, manage, and are the strategic owners of the company, with Leszek individually disclosed as holding around 77.1% of shares/votes at one point and insiders collectively holding roughly 92%. [Helio investor relations](https://www.helio.pl/en/investor-relations/public-offering-of-shares/history-of-shares-transactions/change-in-a-shareholders-share-in-the-total-vote-by-the-shareholder-who-held-over-33percent-of-the-total-vote)
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources searched; note the earlier web search mistakenly suggested an 'Agora S.A.' subsidiary relationship, but this could not be corroborated and appears to be an aggregator data error -- Helio is reported elsewhere as a founder/family-controlled independent company.

thesis.business_description: Berner Industrier AB (formerly Christian Berner Tech Trade; roots back to 1897) is a Nordic industrial group in 'sustainable technology' made up of nine companies with about 250 employees and annual revenue of around SEK 1,000m, organised into two business areas, one of which is Energy & Environment (which includes the subsidiaries Bullerbekampen and Autofric). Q2 2026 net sales rose 17.3% to SEK 319.9m (8.5pp organic, 8.0pp acquired) and EBITA rose 24.8% to SEK 30.7m (9.6% margin), a record quarter. The name of the second business area was not confirmed in this search. Sources: https://storage.mfn.se/20b67f64-b46b-4242-957f-abdd6d3efdaa/berner-industrier-q2-2026-eng.pdf ; https://www.inderes.se/releases/interim-report-1-january-june-30 ; https://mfn.se/a/berner-industrier/berner-industrier-has-completed-the-acquisition-of-autofric-ab
thesis.competitive_position: A small Nordic serial acquirer of niche industrial and environmental-technology companies (e.g. noise control, friction/brake products), combining organic growth with bolt-on acquisitions; acquisitions contributed about half of Q2 2026 growth, and Affarsvarlden analysis describes an increased acquisition pace. Order intake was broadly flat in Q2 2026 (SEK 283.7m, +1.8%) and operating cash flow fell to SEK 23.0m from SEK 33.8m. Listed on the Nasdaq Stockholm Main Market since 2017. Sources: https://storage.mfn.se/20b67f64-b46b-4242-957f-abdd6d3efdaa/berner-industrier-q2-2026-eng.pdf ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/berner-industrier-okat-forvarvstempo ; https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/berner-industriers-annual-report-2025
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Affarsvarlden's ownership table (aggregator, undated; likely Modular Finance/Euroclear-based): Gardaverken AB 22.4% of capital / 51.2% of votes (controlling via A shares), Isolde Stensdotter Berner 8.4% / 5.3%, Lannebo Fonder 5.3% / 3.3%, Cervantes Capital 4.3% / 2.7%. CONFLICT: Simply Wall St (undated) lists Cervantes Capital at 9.74% and an older Affarsvarlden list shows Cervantes at 11.2%, so Cervantes' stake may have changed; several FI flagging notices were filed in May-June 2026. The 2025 annual report (share section p.32) was not readable in this search. The 2026 nomination committee comprises Cervantes Capital, Lannebo Fonder and Gardaverken. Sources: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/berner-industrier ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/tech/bats-chixe-bernbs/berner-industrier-shares/ownership ; https://storage.mfn.se/bbf0cff3-496d-4aca-9bcb-d9efd47f0819/berner-industrier-arsredovisning-2025.pdf
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources. Standard caveats: dual-class structure gives Gardaverken (Berner family) majority voting control with about 22% of capital; small cap with limited liquidity; acquisition-driven growth brings integration and goodwill risk; order intake growth lagged sales in Q2 2026. Sources: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/berner-industrier ; https://storage.mfn.se/20b67f64-b46b-4242-957f-abdd6d3efdaa/berner-industrier-q2-2026-eng.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: Berner family control: board member Joachim Berner represents Gardaverken AB (22.4% capital / 51.2% votes per Affarsvarlden) on the nomination committee, and Isolde Stensdotter Berner holds 8.4% of capital. Board member Johan Lannebo made repeated share purchases in May-June 2026 (size not confirmed). Precise personal holdings of CEO Caroline Reuterskiold and other directors could not be located in this search (research gap). Sources: https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/nomination-committee-for-the-annual-general-meeting-2026 ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/berner-industrier

name: Digital Bros S.p.A.
gmSourceUrl: [Digital Bros S.p.A. financial statements as of June 30th, 2024](https://digitalbros-com.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Digital-Bros-SpA-Financial-statements-as-of-June-30th-2024_encr.pdf)

thesis.business_description: Digital Bros S.p.A., founded in 1989 by brothers Abramo and Raffaele Galante (originally as Halifax, an Italian video-game distributor) and headquartered in Milan (listed on Euronext STAR Milan), develops, publishes and distributes video games globally across consoles, PC, mobile and streaming platforms, organized into Premium Games (505 Games, Hook brands), Free to Play (505 Games Mobile), Italian Distribution (Halifax brand) and Other Activities (training/professional courses) segments; its 505 Games subsidiary is known for bringing Japanese titles overseas and has shifted toward developing owned IP since 2016. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/505_Games ; https://it.finance.yahoo.com/q/ct?s=DIB.MI
thesis.competitive_position: An established Italian video-game publisher/distributor with international offices (US, UK, Czech Republic, China, Japan, Australia, Canada) and acquisitions including UK-based DR Studios, Italian racing specialist Kunos Simulazioni (developer of Assetto Corsa), Avantgarden (formerly Ovosonico) and Australian developer Infinity Plus; underwent significant cost-cutting, including a ~30% global workforce reduction (~130 employees) announced November 2023, with further 2024 office closures (Germany, Spain, France) at 505 Games. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/505_Games
thesis.main_shareholders: Per official insider-ownership filings (as reported via MarketScreener and Zonebourse, citing filings dated 26/27 October 2025): founder/Chairman & Co-CEO Abramo Galante holds 4,880,812 shares = 34.22% of capital, and co-CEO & Executive Director Raffaele Galante holds 4,678,736 shares = 32.8% of capital — together the Galante brothers control roughly 67% of the company. A 2023 press report (Milano Finanza) had cited a more even 34.734% each for the two brothers with ~32% free float, suggesting a slight relative shift between the brothers' holdings by late 2025 (though their combined stake remains similar). Source: https://uk.marketscreener.com/insider/ABRAMO-GALANTE-A03VDY/ ; https://www.zonebourse.com/insider/RAFFAELE-GALANTE-A03VE0/ ; https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/digital-bros-allarme-in-ritardo-2610097
thesis.red_flags: Very high founder/family concentration (~67% combined between the two Galante brothers, who also serve as Chairman/Co-CEO and Co-CEO respectively) leaves a thin free float (~32-33%) and significant related-party/governance power concentrated in the founding family — a standard structure for this type of founder-led Italian small-cap but a material consideration for minority shareholders. The 2023-2024 workforce reductions (~30% of global headcount) reflect a cost-cutting response to challenging trading conditions rather than a governance or fraud issue. No litigation or going-concern issues were identified.

thesis.business_description: Medika d.d. is Croatia's oldest and leading pharmaceutical wholesaler, primarily engaged in the sale, storage, and distribution of human and veterinary drugs to pharmacies, healthcare facilities, hospitals, community health centers, outpatient clinics, medical practices, other wholesalers, and specialized shops. It supplies the widest range of products among peers and operates Prima Pharma pharmacies as part of Medika Group, employing over 950 people in the group.
thesis.competitive_position: Market leader in Croatia for over 50 years, with the widest product range among pharmaceutical wholesalers. Sets standards in service quality.
thesis.main_shareholders: Agram Brokera d.d./Auctor d.o.o. (48.04%), Fima-vrijednosnice d.o.o./Auctor Pharma d.o.o. (25.32%), Interkapital Vrijednosni Papiri d.o.o./Krka d.d. Novo Mesto (11.97%), Medika d.d. treasury (4.11%), Gradska Ljekarna Zagreb (3.39%).
thesis.red_flags: Recent corporate governance events: shareholder request for extraordinary General Assembly (Feb 2026), Supervisory Board resignation (Dec 2025), multiple voting rights changes, potential trading suspension or delisting notes on ZSE page. Low liquidity. Unable to access full 2024 annual report for de

thesis.business_description: Mountview Estates P.L.C., incorporated in 1937 (established by brothers Frank and Irving Sinclair) and headquartered in Southgate, London, buys, holds and sells UK residential property — primarily regulated, assured, assured-shorthold and life-tenancy residential units plus freehold/leasehold ground-rent units — typically acquiring tenanted properties and selling them once vacant, with a portfolio concentrated in low-value units in high-demand areas of London and southeast England (reportedly 3,500+ units per one source). Source: https://www.glassdoor.com/Overview/X-EI_IE12536.htm ; https://cdn.logokit.com/brands/mountviewplc.co.uk
thesis.competitive_position: A long-established, conservatively-run specialist in the niche UK tenanted/regulated residential and ground-rent property market, listed on the LSE with only ~29-30 employees relative to a market capitalization reported at roughly £343-498 million (sources disagree significantly, likely reflecting different dates); operates via subsidiaries including Hurstway Investment Company, Louise Goodwin Limited and A.L.G. Properties Limited. Source: https://disfold.com/company/mountview-estates-plc/
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Mountview's own 2025 Preliminary Results statement (signed by Duncan Sinclair, CEO), 'despite the 1960 full listing, control of a majority of the shareholdings remains within the Sinclair family' — confirming continued Sinclair family majority control as a matter of the company's own disclosure, though the exact current percentage was not stated in the excerpt found. Source: https://sharesmagazine.co.uk/news/market/LSE20250619070007_5702227/preliminary-results-year-ended-31-march-2025 . Third-party aggregator data (Kalkine, undated) shows 'Private Companies' holding 39%, individual insiders approximately 30%, and the general public approximately 16% — these private-company and insider categories likely substantially overlap with or represent the Sinclair family's holding vehicles, though this was not stated explicitly in the source. We found no evidence of a 'Connaught'-related shareholding in this search. Source: https://kalkine.co.uk/news/stocks/mountview-estates-plcs-lonmtvw-top-owners-are-private-companies-with-39-stake-while30-is-held-by-insiders
thesis.red_flags: Majority family control (Sinclair family, confirmed by the company's own 2025 statement) concentrates governance power despite the company's long public-listing history (since 1960) — a disclosed, long-standing structure rather than a new governance concern. We also noted an unexplained 'Dividend Payment Delay' entry dated 30 March 2026 referenced on a filings-aggregator page (ticker.app), the substance of which we could not determine in this search — this should be checked directly against the company's RNS announcements before being treated as either material or immaterial.

thesis.business_description: Gerresheimer AG, founded in 1864 (as Gerresheimer Glas) and headquartered in Düsseldorf, Germany (MDAX-listed), is a global manufacturer of pharmaceutical and cosmetics primary packaging and drug-delivery systems made from specialty glass and plastics — including prefillable syringes, vials, cartridges, ampoules, inhalers and insulin pens — organized into Plastics & Devices, Primary Packaging Glass, and Advanced Technologies segments, with 2023 revenue of €1,990.5 million and 11,660 employees across 35+ plants in Europe, the Americas and Asia. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerresheimer
thesis.competitive_position: A leading global pharmaceutical-packaging and drug-delivery-device manufacturer, with most revenue generated in Europe (Germany being the largest single country); currently the subject of activist-investor pressure (Active Ownership Corp SARL/AOC Gecko S.à r.l., led by Klaus Röhrig, and Eminence Capital) pushing management for a strategic review, cost cuts, and a possible separation of the glass-forming division. Source: https://www.boersen-zeitung.de/unternehmen-branchen/naechster-aktivist-mischt-bei-gerresheimer-mit
thesis.main_shareholders: Per German WpHG voting-rights notifications (Stimmrechtsmitteilungen) cited via financial press (figures as reported mid-2026, with conflicting precision across sources so treated as approximate): Active Ownership Corp SARL / AOC Gecko S.à r.l. (Klaus Röhrig) holds approximately 13.67% of capital, with voting rights reported at 15.19% including financial instruments / 12.01% in direct voting rights per a separate account; Goldman Sachs Group reported stakes ranging from approximately 14.49% to 18.95% across different disclosure dates (described as the largest institutional investor in one account); JPMorgan Chase reported 7.43% (January 2026, partly via equity swaps/call rights); Eminence Capital increased its position to approximately 6.2%; NN Group N.V. was reported at approximately 9.97% in one source; Norges Bank Investment Management at approximately 3.919%; and Aaron Weitman reduced his stake from 4.08% to 2.90%. Free float is reported inconsistently at either ~34.58% or ~89.8% depending on source/methodology.
