Source: https://de.marketscreener.com/kurs/aktie/GERRESHEIMER-AG-599546/unternehmen-aktionare/ ; https://www.boerse-express.com/news/articles/gerresheimer-aktie-weitman-reduziert-auf-290-prozent-928609 ; https://www.boerse.de/unternehmensprofil/Gerresheimer-Aktie/DE000A0LD6E6 . These figures conflict materially between sources (especially the free-float percentage) and should be verified via the Bundesanzeiger's official Stimmrechtsmitteilungen database or Gerresheimer's own investor relations page before relying on exact numbers. We found no evidence connecting Metric Capital Partners to Gerresheimer's shareholder base in this search.
thesis.red_flags: Active activist-investor campaign (AOC Gecko/Klaus Röhrig and Eminence Capital building significant stakes and publicly pressing for a strategic review, cost cuts and possible divestment of the glass-forming division) represents an unresolved corporate-action/governance situation that could materially affect strategy and shareholder value — this is a disclosed, legitimate shareholder-activism situation rather than misconduct, but is an important live risk/catalyst for investors to track. Source: https://www.boersen-zeitung.de/unternehmen-branchen/naechster-aktivist-mischt-bei-gerresheimer-mit

thesis.business_description: LleidaNetworks Serveis Telemàtics, S.A. (Lleida.net) is a Spanish telecommunications operator and qualified trust service provider (under the EU eIDAS regulation) that manages SMS/MMS messaging traffic over the internet for wholesale and end customers, and provides digital-trust services including electronic signatures, certified electronic contracting, digital identity verification and fraud/data validation. Source: https://suppliers.catalonia.com/detail/lleidanetworks-serveis-telematics-sa/4626 ; https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/60929-74
thesis.competitive_position: Niche Spanish messaging/trust-services operator listed on both BME Growth (Madrid) and Euronext Growth (Paris), reporting ~€20.4m revenue (FY2025) and ~129 employees; differentiated by its eIDAS-qualified trust-service status, which supports expansion into higher-margin digital signature/contracting services beyond commodity SMS traffic. Source: https://site.financialmodelingprep.com/stock-value/ALLLN.PA
thesis.main_shareholders: Founder, CEO and Chairman Francisco Sapena Soler is the controlling shareholder; a 2022 company filing stated his stake at 34.89%, after a September 2021 sale of ~3% to qualified investors (reducing him from 36.74% to 33.74%) and a partial rebuild to 34.27% by December 2021. Source: https://www.bmegrowth.es/docs/documentos/OtraInfRelevante/2021/12/05089_OtraInfRelev_20211201.pdf ; https://app.researchpool.com/provider/globenewswire/lln-sapena-buys-25000-lleidanet-shares-h8WZLolT7V. Historically (2016 filing) Sapena held 46.14%, with SESD F.C.R. at 21.27% and Institut Català de Finances Capital S.A. SGEIC at 3.70%, and the company stated no other holder was above 10%. Source: https://www.bmegrowth.es/docs/documentos/HechosRelev/2016/07/05089_HRelev_20160705.pdf. We could not retrieve a current (post-2022) CNMV/BME Growth significant-holdings notice in this search giving Sapena's exact present-day percentage, so the 34.89%/34.27% figures should be treated as the most recent confirmed data point rather than today's exact stake.
thesis.red_flags: Founder/CEO Sapena periodically trades blocks of his own shares (sales and purchases disclosed via CNMV/BME Growth filings), which is transparent insider activity rather than a governance problem, but the recurring partial sell-downs are worth monitoring for dilution of founder alignment. Source: https://www.bmegrowth.es/docs/documentos/OtraInfRelevante/2021/09/05089_OtraInfRelev_20210930.pdf. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources in this search.

thesis.business_description: Mortgage Advice Bureau (Holdings) plc runs a UK network of mortgage and protection intermediaries: Appointed Representative firms, many trading under the MAB brand on a franchise-style model, use MAB's regulatory permissions, compliance, technology, lead generation and marketing, and MAB takes a share of their procuration fees and commissions. It also owns 75.4% of Fluent (acquired July 2022) and bought Home Loan Services and HomeOwners Alliance in 2025-26. H1 2026 revenue rose 8.6% to GBP 161.0m and adjusted pre-tax profit to GBP 14.8m; the listing moved from AIM to the London Main Market in May 2026 (the dashboard ticker still shows AIM). Sources: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/mortgage-advice-bureau-suffers-uk-property-adjusted-profit ; https://lse.co.uk/rns/MAB1/trading-update-2oly5amt0lindh7.html ; https://hl.co.uk/shares/shares-search-results/m/mortgage-advice-bureau-ltd-ordinary-10p/company-information
thesis.competitive_position: Describes itself as one of the UK's leading consumer mortgage intermediary brands and AR networks, competing with other UK mortgage networks and direct-to-lender channels; the asset-light model scales with adviser numbers and mortgage completions (about GBP 16.5bn of completions in H1 2026, +16%). Strategy combines adviser recruitment, minority/majority stakes in AR firms and lead-generation businesses such as Fluent. In September 2026 it cut 2026 adjusted PBT guidance to about GBP 38.0m (consensus GBP 43.4m), citing roughly GBP 5m lower Fluent profit contribution and a weaker purchase market. No independent market-share figure was found. Sources: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/mortgage-advice-bureau-holdings---mab1/trading-update/9682940 ; https://www.mortgagesolutions.co.uk/mortgage-news/2026/09/09/mab-lowers-profit-expectations-as-challenging-market-knocks-growth/ ; https://ifamagazine.com/mortgage-advice-bureau-makes-strategic-investment-in-the-mortgage-mum/
thesis.main_shareholders: Only aggregator data was found (Simply Wall St, AIM line, snapshot apparently around late 2025): Peter Brodnicki about 18% (10,401,557 shares), Liontrust Asset Management 15.9%, Octopus Investments 8.99%, Aberdeen Group 7.13%, M&G Investment Management 3.63%; top 25 holders 85.21%. CONFLICT: Simply Wall St's OTC page shows Liontrust at 18.1%. Total voting rights were 57,631,831 in April 2026. The company's own significant-shareholder table (investor site / FY2025 annual report) was not retrieved; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/diversified-financials/aim-mab1/mortgage-advice-bureau-holdings-shares/ownership ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/diversified-financials/otc-mabh.f/mortgage-advice-bureau-holdings/ownership ; https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/MAB1/transaction-in-own-shares-253r142qp7f6vw7.html
thesis.red_flags: Profit warning in September 2026 (2026 adjusted PBT guidance cut to about GBP 38m vs GBP 43.4m consensus) and shares fell sharply; H1 2026 statutory pre-tax profit fell 36% to GBP 6.2m due to exceptional costs (acquisitions and the AIM-to-Main-Market move), so there is a large gap between statutory and adjusted profit. Earnings are cyclical with UK housing transactions and mortgage approvals, and there is execution risk in the Fluent business. Sources: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/mortgage-advice-bureau-lowers-2026-guidance-shares-plunge ; https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/mortgage-advice-bureau-suffers-uk-property-adjusted-profit ; https://www.proactiveinvestors.co.uk/companies/news/1098268/mortgage-advice-bureau-cuts-profit-expectations-as-mortgage-market-weakens-1098268.html
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder and CEO Peter Brodnicki holds about 18% (10.4m shares) per Simply Wall St (aggregator); on 57.6m voting rights this is consistent at about 18%, but no official dated RNS confirming the exact figure was located. Directors have been buying shares (tipranks summary of an RNS titled 'directors increase shareholdings'). Other directors' holdings were not confirmed in this search. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/diversified-financials/aim-mab1/mortgage-advice-bureau-holdings-shares/ownership ; https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/mortgage-advice-bureau-directors-increase-shareholdings-3 ; https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/MAB1/directorpdmr-shareholding-fq882uidg881c2v.html

thesis.business_description: Baikowski SA, founded in 1904 and headquartered in Poisy, France, designs, develops, produces and sells ultra-pure alumina powders/formulations and other fine oxides and composites (spinel, ZTA, YAG, ceria) used in technical ceramics, precision polishing, optical crystals, additives and coatings, serving lighting, electronics, automotive, defense and medical end-markets. Source: https://discovery.patsnap.com/company/baikowski/ ; https://www.gophotonics.com/companies/3367/baikowski
thesis.competitive_position: Specialist, century-old global producer of high-purity alumina and rare-earth-adjacent fine oxide materials (ceria, YAG) with operations described as spanning France, the US and Japan; small-cap (~155 employees) listed on Euronext Growth Paris, reporting consolidated 2025 revenue of €50.7m, up 6.3% year-on-year. Source: (2026 French-language news item on 2025 results, as summarized via aggregator search) https://www.boerse-stuttgart.de/en/products/equities/stuttgart/a2pahy-baikowski-sas-eo-1-25/
thesis.main_shareholders: Baikowski was spun off from PSB Industries in 2018 (one Baikowski share distributed per PSB Industries share) and listed on Euronext Growth Paris. Source: https://www.boerse-stuttgart.de/en/products/equities/stuttgart/a2pahy-baikowski-sas-eo-1-25/ ; https://discovery.patsnap.com/company/baikowski/. Its earlier (pre-1984) family ownership passed from the founding Baikowski family to the Entremont/Cachat/Wirth family group and the Provendis company, per an AMF-hosted document. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/ECO/2018/12/FCECO049277_20181220.pdf. Board member François-Xavier Entremont (whose surname matches that historical family group) acquired 19,665 shares at €13.70 in December 2024, per AMF-filed insider-transaction disclosures. Source: https://www.abcbourse.com/marches/transactions_dirigeants/FR0013384369p. We could not locate a current, complete shareholder percentage table (e.g., from an AMF TR-1 threshold notice or Baikowski's own actionnariat page) in this search; the controlling shareholder's exact present-day stake is therefore not confirmed from an official source and should be checked against Baikowski's universal registration document or AMF filings.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources regarding litigation, going-concern or dilution. Mikael Frenkian was named new Group CEO effective 1 June 2026, a recent management change worth monitoring for continuity, though not itself a red flag. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/ECO/2026/06/FCECO082270_20260611.pdf

thesis.business_description: RIAS A/S is a Danish industrial company headquartered in Roskilde that manufactures and distributes plastic building/industrial products, including corrugated plastic roofing and facade panels, ductwork and gutters, serving customers primarily in the Nordic market as well as the food and packaging industry sectors globally. Source: https://www.home.saxo/da-dk/markets/stocks/riasb-xcse
thesis.competitive_position: Small, niche Nordic plastics manufacturer listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen (RIAS B) under the Construction & Materials / Industrials classification, with a concentrated Nordic customer base; limited independent scale information was available from aggregators in this search. Source: https://www.inderes.fi/en/companies/Rias
thesis.main_shareholders: A third-party aggregator (Simply Wall St, citing S&P Global data, dated ~May 2025) lists thyssenkrupp AG as the largest shareholder of the RIAS B share class with 124,880 shares (54.2%), and Expon ApS as second-largest with 25,761 shares (11.2%); the top 3 shareholders together hold 65.38%. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/dk/capital-goods/cph-rias-b/rias-shares/ownership. We could not confirm this directly from an official Danish 'storaktionær' flagging notice or the company's own investor-relations ownership page in this search, nor could we determine how RIAS A-shares (which may carry different voting rights) are distributed; the thyssenkrupp AG stake in particular should be verified against the company's own major-shareholder disclosures or the Danish Business Authority (Erhvervsstyrelsen) register, as an industrial conglomerate holding a majority stake in a small Danish plastics firm is a notable claim that could not be independently corroborated here.
thesis.red_flags: If accurate, majority control by a single large corporate shareholder (thyssenkrupp AG, per aggregator data) would materially limit free float and minority-shareholder influence, but this could not be confirmed from an official source in this search, so it is flagged as a data-verification gap rather than a confirmed governance issue. A board member resignation was noted among recent 2026 regulatory releases; the underlying reason was not identified in this search. Source: https://www.inderes.fi/en/companies/Rias. No litigation or going-concern issues were identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Scanfil Oyj, founded in 1976 and headquartered in Sievi, Finland, is a major European electronics manufacturing services (EMS) company providing design, prototyping, DFM, test development, supply-chain/logistics, PCB assembly, sheet-metal fabrication, box-build and full systems-integration services across 16 production facilities on four continents. Source: https://www.scanfil.com/?p=8807 ; https://tracenable.com/company/scanfil/group-entities
thesis.competitive_position: One of the larger European EMS providers, serving Industrial (~47% of turnover), Energy & Cleantech (~34%) and Medtech & Life Science (~19%) end-markets with full production-chain outsourcing capability; FY2025 revenue reported at roughly €797m with ~3,500-4,700 employees depending on source/date. Source: https://financialfilings.com/companies/scanfil-oyj/
thesis.main_shareholders: A 2023 Finnish major-holder disclosure (flagging notice) reported that Harri Tapio Takanen's stake rose to 28.15% of shares and votes, up from 16.94% previously; his brother and father (Jorma Takanen) are also significant holders, together with early Sievi-area investors historically described as controlling a large combined block. Source: (2023 Finnish FIN-FSA flagging notice, as reported via Inderes investor forum) https://forum.inderes.com/t/scanfil-sopimusvalmistaja-salkun-taytteeksi/1397/541. An Inderes forum post (not an official filing, undated) separately estimates Harri Takanen at ~15.12%, his brother at ~12.59% and Jorma Takanen at ~9.88%, with early Sievi investors together close to 70%, and names Varikot Oy (the Kotila family's investment vehicle) as another significant holder; these unofficial figures appear inconsistent with the 2023 flagging notice and should not be treated as confirmed. We could not locate Scanfil's own current major-shareholder table from its investor-relations site in this search; the 28.15% Harri Takanen figure from the 2023 official flagging notice is the most reliable data point found, but it may be outdated.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources regarding litigation, going-concern or dilution; ownership appears concentrated among the founding Takanen family and early Sievi-based investors, a typical Finnish family-industrial structure rather than a specific governance flag, though the inconsistency between the 2023 official flagging percentage and unofficial aggregator estimates noted above means the degree of concentration is not fully confirmed.

thesis.business_description: Banca Profilo S.p.A. is a Milan-based Italian private and investment bank, operating since 1995 (as a bank; founded 1988 as a finance company per some profiles), active in Private Banking, Investment Banking/Capital Markets and Finance, with offices in Milan, Brescia, Turin, Genoa, Padua, Reggio Emilia and Rome; it also owns asset manager Profilo Asset Management SGR and Profilo Merchant. Source: https://www.bancaprofilo.it/en/?p=2610 ; https://pickthebank.eu/it/banche/italia/banca-profilo-spa-ovvero-profilobank-spa-profitmm001/
thesis.competitive_position: Small, specialist Italian private bank serving high-net-worth private clients and SMEs, offering discretionary/advisory portfolio management, securities custody and trading, Lombard lending against financial assets, and corporate finance for mid/small-cap Italian companies; supervised by Bank of Italy and CONSOB, listed on Euronext Milan (ticker PRO). Source: https://altss.com/profile/banca-profilo
thesis.main_shareholders: Banca Profilo is controlled by Arepo BP S.p.A., itself controlled by the Sator fund founded by Matteo Arpe. Per CONSOB's official 'Azionariato' disclosure register, Arepo BP held 53.538% of voting capital in filings spanning 2013-2017 (with Sator Capital Limited as the fund manager controlling Arepo), alongside Strategy Invest Srl at 3.785% and treasury shares (Banca Profilo itself) at 2.006%. Source: https://www.consob.it/web/consob-and-its-activities/w/banca-profilo-s.p.a.-azionariato-2017-12-31. A more recent trade-press report (Bluerating, undated but referencing a management renewal with Michele Centonze as chairman) states Arepo's stake had risen to 62.403%, and separately reports a conditional binding agreement for Arepo to sell a 29% stake to Twenty First Capital (contingent on Arepo also agreeing to sell a further 22%+ to other investors, total deal value €50.4m) — source: https://www.bluerating.com/banche-e-reti/840084/banca-profilo-rinnova-i-vertici-torna-matteo-arpe-centonze-il-nuovo-presidente. We could not confirm from an official CONSOB filing in this search whether that Twenty First Capital transaction has closed or what Arepo's exact current stake is; this should be verified against Banca Profilo's latest financial report or CONSOB's current azionariato page.
thesis.red_flags: A pending/potential change-of-control transaction (Arepo's reported agreement to sell up to ~51% of the bank to Twenty First Capital and other investors) is a material corporate-governance event to monitor, though it is disclosed in trade press rather than hidden. Source: https://www.bluerating.com/banche-e-reti/840084/banca-profilo-rinnova-i-vertici-torna-matteo-arpe-centonze-il-nuovo-presidente. The bank underwent a 2009 rescue recapitalization (Arepo/Sator injected €70m at €0.20/share, reaching 73.18% control at the time), reflecting historical financial distress, though this is a dated (2009) event. Source: https://www.bancaprofilo.it/allegati/semestrale2009.pdf. No current litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: DLSI (ticker ALDLS), founded in 1992 and listed on Euronext Growth Paris since 2006, is a French temporary-staffing and recruitment group operating a network of more than 70 employment agencies across France, Luxembourg, Germany and Switzerland (the Swiss arm trading as Pemsa, ~40% of sales), providing interim staffing, fixed-term/permanent placement (CDI/CDD) and recruitment services across all industry sectors, with 2024 revenue of approximately €211.9 million. Source: https://businesscoot.com/en/company/dlsi-groupe ; https://www.boursedirect.fr/fr/marche/euronext-growth-paris/dlsi-FR0010404368-ALDLS-EUR-ALXP/societe
thesis.competitive_position: A mid-sized French-headquartered staffing group with meaningful geographic diversification into Switzerland (contributing ~40-43% of revenue via Pemsa) alongside its French core (~55-58% of revenue), grown partly through acquisitions (Alarys, ML Intérim, Prestim) that strengthened its presence in the Grand Est region; a 2024 net result of only ~€425 thousand on ~€212m revenue suggests thin margins in the period. Source: https://businesscoot.com/en/company/dlsi-groupe
thesis.main_shareholders: Per DLSI's own AMF regulatory filing (November 2022, DILA open-data site): the founding Doudot family signed a collective share-retention pact (Dutreil pact, under article 787 B of the French tax code) on 27 July 2022, covering 64.87% of capital and 78.51% of voting rights at signing; signatories included Thierry Doudot (Président du Directoire), Véronique Doudot (Vice-Président du Conseil de surveillance), Anne Doudot (Conseil de surveillance member), and the company RAY International (a non-executive signatory holding ≥5%). A subsequent (undated in our search) press item reports that Anne/Anna Doudot transferred her controlling shares to her son Thierry Doudot, with AMF approval, pushing his individual holding above key thresholds — we could not confirm the resulting exact percentage or date. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/383/2022/11/FC383465344_20221121.pdf . A non-official aggregator (Idéal Investisseur, snapshot dated 1 July 2026) separately estimates insiders/related entities at 72.0% and institutional investors at 6.7%, though it flags that official AMF art. L.233-7 threshold-crossing declarations are not fully integrated into its figures. Source: https://www.ideal-investisseur.fr/actions/d-l-s-i-FR0010404368-societe.html
thesis.red_flags: Very high family ownership concentration (official 2022 AMF filing shows the Doudot family concert at ~65% of capital / ~78.5% of votes, with aggregator data suggesting it may now be even higher at ~72%), combined with the family holding the top executive roles (Président du Directoire) — standard for a French family SA à directoire but leaving very limited free float and outsized related-party/governance influence for the controlling family. No litigation, fraud or going-concern issues were identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Kraft Bank ASA, founded in 2016 and headquartered in Sandnes, Norway, is a licensed Norwegian bank (regulated by Finanstilsynet) offering mortgage refinancing and secured/unsecured consumer loans to individuals, plus deposit/savings products, investment and advisory services; one source (Inderes) additionally describes a focus on small and medium-sized corporate customers including asset management, loan financing, and pension/insurance ancillary services. Its 2018 launch used Tieto's AI-driven core banking platform for automated loan-application processing, aimed partly at customers who could not obtain loans from other banks. Source: https://simplywall.st/stock/ob/krab ; https://tietoevry.com/en/newsroom/all-news-and-releases/press-releases/2018/03/kraft-bank-chooses-tietos-ai-solution-for-processing-loan-applications
thesis.competitive_position: Small, niche Norwegian digital-forward lender (~48 employees per one source) targeting underserved borrowers (those unable to secure loans from mainstream banks) as well as, per some descriptions, SME customers; listed on Euronext Growth Oslo (ticker KRAB). Source: https://www.inderes.se/en/companies/Kraft-Bank
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Kraft Bank's own Q3 2024 quarterly report, BFBK Finans AS (including related parties) was the largest shareholder with 12.6% of outstanding shares (up from 12.2% at year-end 2021). Source: https://live.euronext.com/sites/default/files/company_press_releases/attachments_oslo/2024/10/25/630419_3K24%20Kraft%20Bank%20ASA%20resultatrapport.pdf. An April 2023 company announcement disclosed that BFBK Finans AS owns 44.9% of Kraft Aksjonærer AS, and that following a transaction BFBK Finans AS held 5,308,003 shares (12.7% of outstanding shares) in Kraft Bank directly; BFBK Finans AS is controlled by board member Bjørn Maaseide, who together with related parties controlled 5,440,403 shares (13.0%) post-transaction. Source: https://live.euronext.com/nb/products/equities/company-news/2023-04-26-meldepliktig-handel. Sparebanken Øst was the second-largest shareholder at 6.8% at year-end 2021 (current percentage not confirmed in this search). Source: https://live.euronext.com/sites/default/files/company_press_releases/announcements/552674_4K21%20Kraft%20Bank%20ASA.pdf. The bank had 758 shareholders at end-2021; no updated total was found for 2025/2026.
thesis.red_flags: Board member Bjørn Maaseide controls the largest shareholder block (BFBK Finans AS / Kraft Aksjonærer AS, ~13% combined) while also serving on the board — a related-party governance structure that is disclosed rather than hidden, but worth noting given the bank's stated niche of lending to borrowers turned down elsewhere, which carries inherently higher credit risk. No specific litigation or going-concern issues were identified from official sources in this search. Source: https://live.euronext.com/nb/products/equities/company-news/2023-04-26-meldepliktig-handel

name: Desarrollos Especiales de Sistemas de Anclaje, S.A.

thesis.business_description: Desarrollos Especiales de Sistemas de Anclaje, S.A. (DESA), with 60+ years of history and headquartered in the Barcelona area (Viladecans), manufactures and markets fastening and anchoring systems (metallic, chemical and plastic anchors, nails, staples, rail/suspension hardware, tools) for construction, industry, agriculture and DIY, under brands including Desa, Construsim, Simes, Agrifast and Salki, exporting to more than 70 countries. Source: https://www.bolsasymercados.es/en/bme-exchange/prices-and-markets/shares/detail.desa-es0126251018.html ; https://suppliers.catalonia.com/detail/desarrollos-especiales-de-sistemas-de-anclajes-sa/11236
thesis.competitive_position: Established, internationally diversified Spanish fastening-systems manufacturer with multiple owned brands; a March 2025 BME-hosted analyst note flagged difficulty growing in recent years (2021-2024 revenue CAGR of -0.2% and EBITDA CAGR of -4.7%), and separately discussed a potential acquisition of a construction-sector business, indicating a mature, slow-growth core with M&A as a possible growth lever. Source: https://www.bolsasymercados.es/bme-exchange/docs/analisis/2025/03/26251_Analisis_20250304_1.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: A BME-hosted analyst report dated February 2020 shows DESA's shareholder structure as: Maden S.A. 29.9%, SARM S.A. 20.0%, Gestión Ixua S.L. 16.3%, Board members collectively 8.9%, and free float 24.9%, with reference shareholders together controlling roughly 75% of capital. Source: https://www.bolsasymercados.es/bme-exchange/docs/analisis/2020/02/26251_Analisis_20200203.pdf. This data point is from 2020 and we could not confirm a more current shareholder table or identify the individuals/families behind Maden S.A., SARM S.A. or Gestión Ixua S.L. from an official source in this search; percentages should be treated as dated and verified against DESA's current significant-holdings filings with CNMV/BME.
thesis.red_flags: Revenue and EBITDA have reportedly declined slightly over 2021-2024 (per the March 2025 BME analyst note), a growth-stagnation concern rather than a governance or solvency red flag. Source: https://www.bolsasymercados.es/bme-exchange/docs/analisis/2025/03/26251_Analisis_20250304_1.pdf. High ownership concentration among three holding entities (Maden, SARM, Gestión Ixua, ~66% combined per the 2020 data) limits free float and minority influence, though this is a disclosed structure rather than confirmed misconduct. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Origin Enterprises plc, incorporated in 2006 and headquartered in Dublin, Ireland, is an agri-services group operating two segments: Agriculture (agronomy advice and on-farm inputs — seed, nutrients, crop protection, digital tools — for arable, fruit and vegetable growers, plus prescription blended fertilizers, animal-feed ingredients, grain handling/trading, provender milling and silo operations) and Living Landscapes (products/services for sports and environmental markets), operating across Ireland, the UK, Belgium, Brazil, Poland, Romania, Ukraine and Latin America under brands including Agrii, Goulding, Origin Fertilisers, Origin Amenity Solutions and Origin Digital. Source: https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/DUB:OIZ/summary ; https://morningstar.com.au/investments/security/LSE/OGN
thesis.competitive_position: Diversified, multi-country agri-services group with the majority of revenue from Agriculture; reported ~2,800-3,000 employees (FY2025). Listed on Euronext Dublin / AIM. Source: https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/DUB:OIZ/summary
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Origin's own investor-relations 'significant shareholders' disclosure (last updated 17 October 2024, under the Disclosure and Transparency Rules, holdings ≥3%): Artemis Investment Management 15.1%, FIL Limited (Fidelity) 10.0%, HOLD Alapkezelő Zrt 5.1%, Janus Henderson Group plc 4.99%, UBS Group AG 3.6%, Protector Forsikring ASA 3.2%, and Farringdon Capital Management 3.01%. Source: https://originenterprises.com/investors/significant-shareholders. A later (June 2025) Simply Wall St snapshot shows Artemis at ~15.5%, Cobas Asset Management SGIIC SA at ~7.87% and Hold Zrt at ~7.13%, while TipRanks reports Farringdon Capital Management has since reduced its holding below the notifiable threshold. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ie/food-beverage-tobacco/ise-oiz/origin-enterprises-shares/ownership ; https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/origin-enterprises-sees-change-in-shareholder-composition. Ownership is institutionally dispersed with no single holder above ~15%, and no controlling family stake was identified.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; ownership is spread across multiple institutional asset managers (Artemis, Fidelity/FIL, Janus Henderson, UBS, HOLD Alapkezelő) with no controlling shareholder, which is a governance positive relative to several peers in this batch. No litigation or going-concern issues identified. Source: https://originenterprises.com/investors/significant-shareholders

thesis.business_description: Lordos Hotels (Holdings) Public Limited, founded in 1973 and listed on the Cyprus Stock Exchange (IPO 1996) since 1996, owns and operates three beachfront resort hotels in Cyprus: the 5-star Golden Bay Beach Hotel (Larnaca/Pyla), the 4-star Lordos Beach Hotel (173 rooms, Larnaca Bay), and the 4-star Golden Coast Beach Hotel (Protaras). Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/cy/consumer-services/cse-lhh/lordos-hotels-holdings-shares/information ; https://stockopedia.com/share-prices/lordos-hotels-holdings-public-CSE:LHH
thesis.competitive_position: A small, family-linked Cypriot hospitality operator with a concentrated three-hotel portfolio in the Larnaca/Protaras tourism corridor; market capitalization reported in the roughly €42-54m range and ~403-416 employees depending on source/date, positioning it as a niche regional resort operator rather than a diversified international hotel group. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/cy/consumer-services/cse-lhh/lordos-hotels-holdings-shares/information
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Cyprus Stock Exchange-sourced share capital dispersion statements (reported via InBusinessNews/CBN.com.cy), as of a June 2024 snapshot: Constantinos G. Lordos Sons & Co Limited held 16.732% (consistent across the November 2023 and June 2024 reports); a separate Lordos-family-linked group (Demetrios Lordos, Rodoula and Ariana Lordou, connected to board member Ariana Lordou Anastasiadou) held 14.484% (versus 17.317% in the November 2023 report, a discrepancy the source itself flags as needing verification); Demetra Holdings PLC held 16.009% (no disclosed Lordos-family connection); and holders connected to other board members (Areti Ionidou and Thekla Kyriakidou, linked to directors Theofanis Ionides and Stephanie Phoebe Michaelidou) held roughly 13-15% combined. Free float is estimated at 22-25%. Combined, Lordos-family-linked holders appear to control roughly 31-34% of the company (this combined figure is derived by us from the individual disclosures, not stated as a single number in the source). Source: https://cbn.com.cy/article/2024/6/18/781564/the-key-players-in-cyprus-tourism ; https://www.cbn.com.cy/article/2023/11/27/745237/tourism-the-major-shareholders-in-cyprus-listed-companies
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources beyond standard family/board-linked ownership concentration (several large shareholder blocks are tied to sitting board members, which is disclosed but merits standard related-party governance scrutiny); the inconsistency between the November 2023 and June 2024 reported stakes for the Lordos family group (17.317% vs 14.484%) should be verified against the company's most current CSE share capital dispersion statement before relying on either figure.

thesis.business_description: Soditech SA is a France-based (Cannes-la-Bocca) SME specializing in electronic and mechanical engineering, integrating mechanical, thermal, and electronic subsystems for the Space, Research, and Defence sectors, founded in 1990. [Simply Wall St company information](https://simplywall.st/stocks/fr/commercial-services/epa-alsec/soditech-shares/information)
thesis.competitive_position: Soditech is a small, specialized engineering-services provider serving niche high-reliability sectors (space, research, defense), where technical qualification and long-term customer relationships typically create switching-cost barriers; no independent market-share data was found to size its competitive position precisely.
thesis.main_shareholders: The Caille family holds approximately 54.46% of Soditech's share capital; a BFM Bourse disclosure separately noted that Madenn Caillé's holding rose above 25% of capital at one point. [BFM Bourse: Soditech shareholding disclosures](https://www.tradingsat.com/soditech-ing-FR0000078321/actualites/soditech-ing-m-caille-au-dessus-des-25-du-capital-404857.html)
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider/founder-family ownership is high: founder Maurice Caille's family, now led by Madenn Caillé (Chairman & CEO), collectively holds approximately 54.46% of the company. [BFM Bourse shareholder data](https://www.tradingsat.com/soditech-ing-FR0000078321/actionnariat.html)
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources searched.

thesis.business_description: CLS Holdings plc, headquartered in London, is a commercial property investor (office-focused REIT) owning and managing over 595,000 square meters of workspace across the UK, Germany and France (over half in the UK), with a secondary division covering a hotel (Spring Mews) and small corporate investments; it targets non-central but well-transport-connected locations in large cities and derives most revenue from rental income. Source: https://www.morningstar.com.au/investments/security/lse/cli ; https://sharecast.com/scroll_2/equity/CLS_Holdings-13037/profile
thesis.competitive_position: Mid-sized, pan-European (UK/Germany/France) office-focused REIT listed on the London Stock Exchange, with CEO Fredrik Widlund and CFO Andrew Kirkman leading a strategy of repositioning older office stock into modern workspace; ~113-123 employees depending on source. Source: https://sharecast.com/scroll_2/equity/CLS_Holdings-13037/profile
thesis.main_shareholders: CLS is controlled by the Mortstedt family. A May 2026 TR-1 major-holdings notification lists the Trustees of the Sten and Karin Mortstedt Family & Charity Trust as holding through several 'Creative Value Investment' entities, with Creative Value Investment Group Limited itself disclosing approximately 54.78%. Source: https://www-proxy.stockopedia.com/share-prices/cls-holdings-LON:CLI/news/reg-cls-holdings-plc-tr-1-notification-of-major-holdings-urn:newsml:reuters.com:20260526:nRSZ7633Fa/. This is consistent with a 2016 filing showing Sten Mortstedt's personal interest at 51.02% (20,993,718 ordinary shares) and a Simply Wall St snapshot showing the Mortstedt Family Trust at ~55.2% plus Bengt Mortstedt separately at ~6.55%. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/real-estate/lse-cli/cls-holdings-shares/ownership. TipRanks separately describes CLS Holdings plc as a subsidiary of the Sten and Karin Mortstedt Family & Charity Trust, confirming controlling-family status. Source: https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/gb:cli
thesis.red_flags: Majority, multi-decade family control (Mortstedt family/trust, ~55% of shares via a chain of 'Creative Value Investment' entities) concentrates governance power and limits minority-shareholder influence, though this is fully and repeatedly disclosed via TR-1 filings rather than hidden. Source: https://www-proxy.stockopedia.com/share-prices/cls-holdings-LON:CLI/news/reg-cls-holdings-plc-tr-1-notification-of-major-holdings-urn:newsml:reuters.com:20260526:nRSZ7633Fa/. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources; as an office-REIT, CLS carries general sector exposure to higher interest rates and post-pandemic office-demand softness, a market risk rather than a company-specific flag.

thesis.business_description: Groupe Minoteries SA, founded in 1885 and headquartered in Granges-près-Marnand, Switzerland, is the country's only listed milling group, processing cereals and plant-based raw materials (sourced primarily from Swiss agriculture) into flour, grains, organic flours, muesli, breakfast cereals, flakes, extruded products and breadcrumbs (via subsidiary Bonvita AG), operating five production sites and serving artisan bakers, food service, industrial clients and retailers. Source: https://morningstar.com.au/investments/security/XSWX/GMI ; https://www.t-online.de/finanzen/boerse/aktien/groupe-minoteries-aktie/ch0012949464
thesis.competitive_position: The sole listed Swiss milling group, with a largely domestic sales base reflecting its local-sourcing model; reported 2025 revenue of CHF 151.86m (up 4.70% year-on-year) and 2025 earnings of CHF 5.44m; grew via acquisitions including the 2013 purchase of Cargill/Provimi Kliba's Penthalaz flour business and the 2025 acquisition of E. Zwicky. Source: https://www.t-online.de/finanzen/boerse/aktien/groupe-minoteries-aktie/ch0012949464 ; https://latele.ch/articles/groupe-minoteries-reprend-la-societe-e-zwicky
thesis.main_shareholders: We found conflicting, unconfirmed aggregator data rather than an official shareholder table for Groupe Minoteries. One Simply Wall St ownership page names Northstar Holding AG at ~12.1%, Marco Minder at ~4.9% and Rémy Bersier at ~3.4% (top 11 shareholders together holding 26.02%), while another Simply Wall St page instead names Fondation Groupe Mutuel, Endowment Arm as the largest shareholder at 10.0% — these two aggregator snapshots are inconsistent with each other and neither cites an official company filing. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ch/food-beverage-tobacco/vtx-gmi/groupe-minoteries-shares/ownership. Free float is reported at 52.96%, implying roughly 47% is held by anchor/strategic holders not identified by name in these sources. Source: https://www.t-online.de/finanzen/boerse/aktien/groupe-minoteries-aktie/ch0012949464. We found no link to Swiss agricultural cooperative fenaco beyond a 2011 unrelated asset sale (fenaco acquired Groupe Minoteries' Biomill AG animal-feed unit, not an equity stake). This is a genuine research gap — no SIX-disclosed major-shareholder notification was located in this search — and should be checked against Groupe Minoteries' own annual report or SIX Exchange Regulation's significant-shareholder disclosures.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources regarding litigation or going-concern; the inconsistency between third-party aggregator ownership snapshots (noted above) is a data-reliability issue rather than a confirmed governance problem, but underscores that Groupe Minoteries' true controlling/anchor shareholder(s) are not clearly established from public sources found here.

thesis.business_description: Sopharma AD, founded in 1933 and headquartered in Sofia, Bulgaria, is a vertically integrated pharmaceutical group manufacturing active pharmaceutical ingredients and finished prescription/OTC medicines (including branded originals Tabex for smoking cessation and Nivalin for neurological disorders), plus wholesale/distribution (via subsidiary Sopharma Trading) across Southern and Eastern Europe. Source: https://www.sopharmagroup.com/sites/sopharma2016corp/files/presentation_ind_q2_2022_en.pdf ; https://intuitionlabs.ai/companies/pharma/sopharma-ad
thesis.competitive_position: Leading Bulgarian pharmaceutical manufacturer and self-described No. 1 domestic manufacturer of ampules and suppositories, with a portfolio of 200+ products and manufacturing operations extending to Ukraine (Biopharm Engineering, PAO Vitamini) and Serbia; a joint venture (Momina Krepost AD) makes plastic disposable medical materials. Source: https://www.sopharmagroup.com/sites/sopharma2016corp/files/presentation_ind_q2_2022_en.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Sopharma's own investor-relations shareholder-structure table (as at 31 July 2024, unchanged since 30 November 2023): Donev Investments Holding AD holds 40.09%, Telecomplect Invest AD holds 15.96%, CEO Ognian Donev, PhD personally holds 9.06%, other individuals hold 4.05%, other legal entities hold 21.75%, and treasury shares account for 7.46%. Source: https://sopharmagroup.com/en/node/11 (company investor-relations shareholder structure page). Donev Investments Holding is itself majority-owned by Ognian Donev; Telecomplect Invest's two main shareholders are Ognian Donev and Ventzislav Stoev, each holding an equal ~47.4% of Telecomplect Invest per SeeNews reporting. Source: https://seenews.com/news/ceo-ups-stake-in-bulgarian-drug-maker-sopharma-679502. Combining the direct and indirect holdings, Donev and his affiliated entities control well over half of Sopharma's capital. Minority shareholder Elpharma has reduced its stake to just 0.12%. Source: https://www.ffbham.bg/en/post/elpharma-reduces-stake-in-sopharma-to-0-12--158997823894137
thesis.red_flags: High insider/founder ownership concentration: CEO Ognian Donev and his affiliated holding vehicles (Donev Investments Holding + Telecomplect Invest + personal stake) together control well over 50% of Sopharma per the company's own 31 July 2024 shareholder table, creating significant minority-shareholder dependence on the CEO's decisions, though this is fully disclosed rather than hidden. Source: https://sopharmagroup.com/en/node/11. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Troax Group AB is a Swedish manufacturer of steel mesh panel safety and security partitioning/fencing systems, used to protect machinery, warehouses, robotics cells and property, sold globally.
thesis.competitive_position: Troax is described by itself and analysts as a global leader in mesh partitioning/machine safety systems; it was taken public in 2015 after a series of private-equity ownership stages (Segulah to Accent Equity in 2010, then Accent to FSN Capital in a 2012 buyout), and FSN has since fully exited. [Unquote - FSN Troax exit](https://www.unquote.com/nordics/official-record/63448/fsn-in-sek-347m-troax-exit)
thesis.main_shareholders: Investment AB Latour is the largest and controlling-type shareholder, holding approximately 30.1-30.3% of both capital and votes per current data ([Inderes/Millistream data](https://inderes.dk/en/companies/Troax-Group/ownership); [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/capital-goods/sto-troax/troax-group-shares/ownership)); Thomas Widstrand holds approximately 5.8% ([Inderes](https://inderes.dk/en/companies/Troax-Group/ownership)). Former private-equity owner FSN Capital fully exited by selling its remaining 18.1% stake (3,618,946 shares) to institutional investors ([Unquote](https://www.unquote.com/nordics/official-record/63448/fsn-in-sek-347m-troax-exit)).
thesis.insider_ownership: No founder/management insider stake of significance was identified beyond Thomas Widstrand's ~5.8%; institutions hold roughly 61% in aggregate per Simply Wall St, with Investment AB Latour (classified by some aggregators as a PE/VC-type holder) as the anchor shareholder rather than an operating-management insider.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Rainbow Tours S.A., founded in 1990 and headquartered in Łódź, Poland (WSE-listed, ticker RBW), is a Polish tour operator selling package holidays (including all-inclusive and last-minute deals) to over 100 destinations, with a core focus on Mediterranean and long-haul leisure destinations popular with Polish travelers (Greece, Turkey, Spain, Egypt, Tunisia, Italy, plus Cuba, Kenya, Vietnam, UAE), operating through a capital group of subsidiaries in Poland, Greece, Turkey and the Czech Republic, and having acquired a stake in a Romanian operator in July 2025. Source: https://hk.finance.yahoo.com/quote/RBW.WA/profile
thesis.competitive_position: A top-tier Polish tour operator (self-described as second- or third-largest by sales depending on source/date) with vertical integration into destination-market subsidiaries and an online flight-ticket/loyalty platform; participates in the 'Reliable Company' customer-protection program since 2010. Source: https://vivo-shopping.com/en/pila/shopping/rainbow
thesis.main_shareholders: Per the company's own current report on shareholders holding at least 5% of votes at the Ordinary General Meeting of 25 June 2026 (via Parkiet/ESPI): Sławomir Wysmyk held 3,023,000 votes = approximately 31.59% of votes represented at that meeting; the PZU pension fund held approximately 5.70% of votes at that meeting. Source: https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art44695891-rainbow-tours-spolka-akcyjna-wykaz-akcjonariuszy-posiadajacych-co-najmniej-5-liczby-glosow-na-zwyczajnym-walnym-zgromadzeniu-rainbow-tours-s-a-w-dniu-25-06-2026-r . An earlier snapshot (Stockwatch.pl, dated September 2025) showed Nationale-Nederlanden PTE SA at 2,351,481 shares (16.16%), Sławomir Wysmyk at 1,680,000 shares (11.54%), and Generali OFE at 1,092,223 shares (7.51%), with FLYOO Sp. z o.o. (controlled by Grzegorz Baszczyński) holding 855,000 shares as of March 2025; Bankier.pl separately (undated) reports three large shareholders together holding 36.75% of shares and 42.09% of votes, without naming them. Recent insider sales include a 2024 accelerated bookbuild in which Flyoo Sp. z o.o. sold 425,000 shares and Aironi Quattro Fundacja Rodzinna sold 335,000 shares, and a separate sale of up to 452,200 shares (~3.1% of capital) initiated by the Elephant Rock family foundation. Source: https://www.stockwatch.pl/gpw/rainbow,akcjonariat,dane-finansowe.aspx ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/127986,dwaj-akcjonariusze-rainbow-tours-chca-sprzedac-czesc-akcji-w-abb . We found no mention of 'Wojciech Oleszak' or 'Jacek Tyszkiewicz' as Rainbow Tours shareholders in this search.
thesis.red_flags: A pattern of recent insider/founder-linked share sales via accelerated bookbuilds (Flyoo/Baszczyński, Aironi Quattro, Elephant Rock family foundation, all in 2024-2025) suggests ongoing gradual founder/early-investor divestment, which is disclosed and legal but worth monitoring as a signal; no fraud, litigation or going-concern issues were identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: CTT - Correios de Portugal, S.A. (Lisbon) is Portugal's postal operator (universal mail service), a growing Iberian express & parcels and e-commerce logistics business (CTT Express in Spain, plus Cacesa customs clearance and DHL Parcel Portugal), and owner of retail bank Banco CTT. In H1 2026 revenue rose 12.9% to EUR 674.3m (6.3% organic), EBITDA fell 3% to EUR 84.1m and net profit fell 41.6% to EUR 12.9m; e-commerce solutions revenue grew 22.3% organically. Sources: https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/economia/lucro-dos-ctt-cai-416-no-1o-semestre-para-129-milhoes_n1756396 ; https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9008966/cttcorreios-de-portugal-sa-cttof-h1-2026-earnings-call-highlights-ecommerce-surge-offsets-customs-headwinds-strategic-review-underway
thesis.competitive_position: Incumbent mail operator with a structurally declining letters business, repositioning towards Iberian parcels/e-commerce where scale is increasing via a partnership with DHL that closed in May 2026 (CTT bought DHL Parcel Portugal, DHL bought 25% of CTT Expresso, CTT bought 25% of the parent of DHL Parcel Iberia; net cash inflow EUR 64m). Customs clearance profits fell due to the end of the EU de minimis exemption. CTT is evaluating strategic alternatives for Banco CTT; it says no formal sale process has started, while Observador reported a purchase proposal from Spain's Cajamar (single report, unconfirmed). Guy Pacheco (ex-CFO) became CEO at the April 2026 AGM, succeeding Joao Bento. Sources: https://www.sabado.pt/dinheiro/amp/ctt-fecham-negocio-com-dhl-e-encaixam-64-milhoes-de-euros ; https://econews.pt/?p=46575 ; https://observador.pt/2026/07/28/ctt-baixam-lucros-no-semestre-que-teve-desafio-acrescido-com-a-taxa-europeia-para-encomendas-abaixo-de-150-euros/ ; https://ipc.be/news-portal/general-news/2026/05/07/10/13/ctt-executive-committee-elected
thesis.main_shareholders: CTT qualifying holdings page (updated 8 July 2026; 133,820,000 shares; only holdings of 5% or more now disclosed): Manuel Champalimaud, SGPS 14.76% (19,747,000 shares, attributable to Manuel Carlos de Melo Champalimaud, including a ~0.37% direct stake); Global Portfolio Investments, S.L. 14.29% (19,128,138 shares, attributable to Indumenta Pueri, S.L.); GreenWood Builders Fund I, LP 6.38% (8,533,568 shares); treasury shares 2.22% (2,965,076); others 62.36%. An ongoing share buyback programme (SBB26) may lift these percentages. Sources: https://www.ctt.pt/grupo-ctt/investidores/estrutura-acionista ; https://www.ctt.pt/contentAsset/raw-data/f53ecdb3-44bf-4938-963a-333efde88e8f/ficheiroPdf/20260819_SBB26_Interim_report_
thesis.red_flags: H1 2026 net profit fell 41.6% and group recurring EBIT fell 8.4%; customs-clearance earnings were hit by EU regulatory change. Group net debt was EUR 292.8m (1.8x net debt/EBITDA per the earnings-call summary). The consolidated balance sheet includes a bank (Banco CTT), adding regulatory capital and credit risk and complicating valuation; the outcome of the Banco CTT strategic review is uncertain. Mail volume decline and universal-service regulation are structural risks. Sources: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9008966/cttcorreios-de-portugal-sa-cttof-h1-2026-earnings-call-highlights-ecommerce-surge-offsets-customs-headwinds-strategic-review-underway ; https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/economia/lucro-dos-ctt-cai-416-no-1o-semestre-para-129-milhoes_n1756396
thesis.insider_ownership: No founding family; the board includes shareholder-linked non-executive directors and the 2026 CEO succession was recommended by major shareholders. Manuel Champalimaud's ~14.76% stake is attributable to him personally via his holding company (he is a reference shareholder; his board role was not confirmed in this search). Personal shareholdings of executives (CEO Guy Pacheco, CFO Joana Freitas) and of Chairman Raul Galamba de Oliveira could not be located in this search; check the 2025 Integrated Report governance annex (research gap). Sources: https://www.ctt.pt/grupo-ctt/investidores/estrutura-acionista ; https://econews.pt/2026/01/08/joao-bento-will-step-down-as-head-of-ctt-at-the-end-of-april-major-shareholders-recommend-guy-pacheco-as-his-successor/

thesis.business_description: SALUS, Ljubljana, d.d., founded in 1969, is one of Slovenia's leading wholesale distributors of pharmaceuticals, medical devices, dietary supplements and cosmetics, serving pharmacies, hospitals, community health centers, residential care homes and veterinary institutions in Slovenia and abroad, and also provides warehousing, secondary packaging, regulatory, pharmacoeconomic and pharmacovigilance services. Source: https://sloveniatimes.com/34516/salus-reports-lower-h1-profit-on-higher-revenue ; https://m.uk.investing.com/equities/salus-ljubljana-company-profile
thesis.competitive_position: Leading pharmaceutical/medical wholesaler in Slovenia with a diversified distribution network (own specialized stores plus online); consolidated group net sales revenue grew 8.2% to €495.7m in 2022 with consolidated net profit of €13.1m that year, and subsequent reports show continued profit growth (e.g. net profit up 27% year-on-year in a Jan-Sept period per STA). Source: https://seenews.com/news/slovenias-salus-net-profit-rises-slightly-in-2022-816875 ; https://english.sta.si/3363352/saluss-net-profit-up-27-in-jan-sept
thesis.main_shareholders: We were unable to identify SALUS's current named major shareholders or ownership percentages from an official source in this search. The company's public disclosures (via the Ljubljana Stock Exchange SEOnet portal and its own filings, e.g. notices of the 41st regular shareholders' meeting and a 2025 remuneration report) were located but their shareholder-structure content was not retrievable in this search. Source: https://www.bizi.si/SALUS-Ljubljana-d-d/javne-objave. This is a genuine research gap — not disclosed/confirmed here — and should be checked directly against SALUS's annual report ownership-structure section or SEOnet filings.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources regarding litigation or going-concern. A 2024-era news report (24ur.com) described SALUS discontinuing cooperation with Lekarna Ljubljana (a major pharmacy chain customer/partner), which could represent a commercial relationship risk, though the underlying cause and current status were not confirmed in this search. Source: https://www.24ur.com/novice/gospodarstvo/salus-prekinil-sodelovanje-z-lekarno-ljubljana.html

thesis.business_description: Malteries Franco-Belges Société Anonyme, headquartered in Nogent-sur-Seine, France, produces malt (base, caramelized and roasted malts) mainly for the brewing industry, sourcing French two-row/six-row barley and wheat, and also trades barley; it operates four malting plants in France. Source: https://pro.stockalarm.io/quote/EURONEXT:MALT ; https://financialfilings.com/companies/malteries-franco-belges/
thesis.competitive_position: Established French malt producer supplying craft brewers, distillers and the broader brewing trade across Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas; part of the much larger Soufflet/Malteries Soufflet group (28 malting plants worldwide), giving it scale, sourcing and distribution advantages versus independent malteries. For the fiscal year ended 30 June 2021, malt production was 239,341 tonnes with sales volume of 252,105 tonnes (output reduced by COVID-19 disruption at the Pithiviers and Brazey plants). Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/EQS/2021/12/FCEQS002820_20211221.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: Malteries Franco-Belges is majority-controlled by its parent, Malteries Soufflet, which holds 92.33% of the company per the 2022 annual management report and a matching EasyBourse shareholder-structure profile; the remaining 7.67% is free float. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/EQS/8888/01/FCEQS003923_20221031.pdf ; https://www.easybourse.com/action-societe/malterie-franco-be/profil/FR0000030074-25. Malteries Soufflet is part of Groupe Soufflet, which was itself acquired by the InVivo agricultural cooperative group. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/EQS/8888/01/FCEQS003923_20221031.pdf. We did not find a more recent (2024/2025) percentage update in this search; 92.33% from the 2022 filing is the latest confirmed official figure.
thesis.red_flags: Very low free float (~7.67%) as a result of 92.33% parent-company control limits minority-shareholder influence and stock liquidity; this is a disclosed structure (majority-owned listed subsidiary) rather than evidence of misconduct. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/EQS/8888/01/FCEQS003923_20221031.pdf. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

name: Centrale d'Achat Française pour l'Outre-Mer Société Anonyme

thesis.business_description: Centrale d'Achat Française pour l'Outre-Mer (CAFOM) is a French distribution group specializing in home furnishings and household goods, operating retail stores in France's overseas territories (West Indies, French Guiana, Réunion, New Caledonia) under the But, Darty, Habitat, Nature & Découvertes and Music & Sound brand licenses/franchises, plus e-commerce sites vente-unique.com and directlowcost.com.
thesis.competitive_position: CAFOM holds a strong regional niche as a leading household-goods and furniture retailer in France's overseas departments/territories (DOM-TOM), a geographically isolated market with limited large-scale competition, operating roughly 23 physical stores alongside online retail arms; its moat rests more on logistics/franchise relationships and incumbency in these insular markets than on brand ownership, since several of its retail banners (But, Darty, Habitat, Nature & Découvertes) are licensed rather than proprietary. [Wikipedia - CAFOM](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/CAFOM); [Yahoo Finance - CAFOM company profile](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CAFO.PA/profile/).
thesis.main_shareholders: Per shareholder-structure data, the main holders are Financière HG (~24.80%), SAS Pleiade Investissement (~15.20%), free float (~10.70%), Evelyne Sztark-Wormser (~10.30%), Denis Wormser (~10.30%), SC Gavalak (~10.00%), Global Investissement/SC SPB (~7.20%), and treasury shares (~2.10%). [Tradingsat/BFM Bourse - CAFOM shareholding structure](https://www.tradingsat.com/cafom-FR0010151589/actionnariat.html).
thesis.insider_ownership: Members of the Wormser family are both significant shareholders and board members: Evelyne Sztark-Wormser (~10.30% stake) has served as a Board Director since 2017, and Denis Wormser holds a comparable ~10.30% stake, indicating meaningful family/insider board representation alongside the holding entities Financière HG and SAS Pleiade Investissement. [Tradingsat - CAFOM shareholding structure](https://www.tradingsat.com/cafom-FR0010151589/actionnariat.html).
thesis.red_flags: CAFOM's own annual financial reports disclose ongoing commercial litigation for which management has recorded related provisions; however, no specific detail on the nature, scale, or outcome of these disputes was found in available search results, and no auditor dispute or fraud allegation was identified. This should be treated as an item to verify directly in the latest annual report rather than a confirmed major red flag. [CAFOM - Annual Financial Report (official PDF)](https://cafom.com/ashymuzu/2020/12/20170202_cafom_rfa.pdf).

thesis.business_description: M+S Hydraulic AD, founded in 1963 and headquartered in Kazanlak, Bulgaria, manufactures high-torque, low-speed orbital hydraulic motors, hydrostatic steering units, valves and brakes for agricultural, construction and metalworking machinery, selling across Bulgaria, Europe and internationally; it is an affiliate of the diversified Stara Planina Hold group. Source: https://seenews.com/companies/ms-hydraulic-ad-6168 ; https://en.bia-bg.com/magazine/view/29558
thesis.competitive_position: A leading Bulgarian specialist manufacturer of orbital hydraulic motors and steering units (ISO 9001/14001/45001 certified) with a market capitalization reported around €224.8m and roughly 1,000-1,140 employees depending on source/year; has pursued inorganic growth by acquiring its own distributors, including a planned majority/90% stake in Italian distributor Oleotecno Hydraulic Components Srl and setting up a Serbian subsidiary for acquisitions. Source: https://www.ffbham.bg/en/post/msh-intends-to-acquire-majority-stake-in-its-italy-s-main-distributor-positive--167152378171120 ; https://simplywall.st/stock/bul/msh
thesis.main_shareholders: We could not identify M+S Hydraulic's named majority or controlling shareholder from an official source in this search. The company is described by aggregators as an affiliate of Stara Planina Hold, a diversified Bulgarian holding group, but we could not confirm Stara Planina Hold's exact percentage ownership of M+S Hydraulic from a company filing or the Bulgarian Commercial Register (Търговски регистър) in this search. Source: https://en.bia-bg.com/magazine/view/29558. This is a genuine research gap; the Bulgarian Financial Supervision Commission's major-holdings register or M+S Hydraulic's own annual report should be checked for a confirmed figure.
thesis.red_flags: The company announced it would halt production at its Serbian subsidiary as of August 1 (year not confirmed in this search), an operational discontinuation worth monitoring though the stated reason was not identified. Source: https://seenews.com/companies/ms-hydraulic-ad-6168. No litigation, governance or going-concern issues were identified from official sources; the controlling-shareholder identity gap noted above (Stara Planina Hold's exact stake unconfirmed) is a data-availability issue rather than a confirmed red flag.

thesis.business_description: Artmarket.com, through its Artprice division, is a France-based global leader in accumulating, managing, and exploiting historical and current art-market price information and data for the art market, founded in 1997 by Thierry Ehrmann. [Artmarket.com / Artprice overview](https://www.actusnews.com/en/amp/artmarket/pr/2026/08/17/the-ehrmann-family-increases-its-equity-stake-in-artprice-by-artmarket-as-part-of-its-ai-first-transformation)
thesis.competitive_position: Artprice positions itself as the world leader in art-market price databases and analytics, now pivoting toward AI-driven tools (branded 'Intuitive Artmarket' and 'Blind Spot') to extend this data leadership; the company is controlled and founder-led by Thierry Ehrmann, who has run it continuously since founding. [Artmarket.com H1 2026 financial report](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/09/29/tmt-newswire/pr-newswire/artmarketcom-h1-2026-financial-report-one-of-a-kind-ai-systems-intuitive-artmarket-and-blind-spot-will-drive-the-next-phase-of-growth-for-ai-first-artprice-in-2026-2030/2434489)
thesis.main_shareholders: Groupe Serveur, the founder's holding vehicle, is the largest shareholder, holding approximately 30.16% of share capital and about 45.78% of voting rights (excluding additional Ehrmann family holdings); the Ehrmann family has recently been increasing its equity stake further as part of a company strategic pivot. [Ehrmann family increases stake in Artmarket.com](https://www.toobit.com/en-US/news/ehrmann-family-increases-stake-in-artmarketcom)
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is high and founder-controlled: founder/CEO Thierry Ehrmann and his family (via Groupe Serveur, ~30.16% of capital/~45.78% of votes) are the controlling shareholders, and the family had not sold any shares since 2015 (a 10-year holding period) before recently adding to their stake; board member Nadège Ehrmann (family) has also recently acquired additional shares. [Ehrmann family stake increase disclosure](https://www.actusnews.com/en/amp/artmarket/pr/2026/08/17/the-ehrmann-family-increases-its-equity-stake-in-artprice-by-artmarket-as-part-of-its-ai-first-transformation)
thesis.red_flags: Some older commentary has criticized Artprice/Artmarket's use of aggressive or 'decoy website' marketing practices; no lawsuit, auditor dispute, or dilution issue was identified in the sources searched. Separately, founder Thierry Ehrmann is independently known for his controversial art installation 'Abode of Chaos,' which is a personal/reputational matter distinct from the company's financial governance. Could not independently verify further financial-reporting criticism beyond this general commentary.

thesis.business_description: Manitou BF SA, incorporated in 1954 (tracing to Marcel Braud's 1957 rough-terrain forklift design) and headquartered in Ancenis, France, designs and manufactures material-handling, access and earthmoving equipment, principally rough-terrain/industrial telehandlers and forklift trucks, plus skid-steer/articulated/backhoe/track loaders and aerial work platforms, sold under the Manitou, Gehl and Mustang brands through dealer networks to agriculture, construction, industrial, aeronautics/defense, environment, mining and oil & gas customers. Source: https://www.globaldata.com/company-profile/manitou-bf-sa ; https://fr.finance.yahoo.com/quote/MTU.PA/profile
thesis.competitive_position: Major global player in telehandlers/rough-terrain forklifts, with reported FY2023 revenue of ~€2.87bn (first exceeded €1bn in 2007) and ~5,500 employees, organized into Material Handling & Access, Compact Equipment Products, and Services & Solutions segments; differentiated by its multi-brand portfolio (Manitou/Gehl/Mustang) and a broad after-sales/financing/fleet-management services business. Source: https://www.roic.ai/quote/MAOIF/classic ; https://hl.co.uk/shares/shares-search-results/m/manitou-eur1/company-information
thesis.main_shareholders: Manitou is controlled by the founding Braud family acting in concert under successive shareholder pacts disclosed to the AMF. A May 2017 pact (replacing a 2011 one) set a target of at least 20% of capital for each of two family branches, for a combined family concert target of 40% of capital. Source: https://www.manitou-group.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/170515_CP_PacteActionnaires_FR.pdf. Under the prior 2011 arrangement, the family collectively held about 65% of capital (up from 63%), with the Braud branch specifically covering about 32% of capital/votes (12,719,721 shares = 32.163%, per a January 2012 AMF-hosted filing), partly held via the 'Holding Braud' vehicle (~22%). Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/ECO/2012/03/FCECO024548_20120330.pdf. An undated Dutreil-commitment disclosure lists individual Braud family blocks, including 2,241,214 shares held by Mme Lilianne Braud. Source: https://www.manitou-group.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Engagements-de-conservation-actions-Manitou-120104.pdf. We could not confirm the Braud family's exact current (2025/2026) combined percentage from an official filing in this search — the 2017 pact's 40% floor is the most recent official reference point, but actual holdings may differ; this should be checked against Manitou's current document d'enregistrement universel or AMF TR-1 notices.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources regarding litigation, going-concern or dilution. The company disclosed the deaths of board chair Jacqueline Himsworth and (per the same notice) Marcel Braud, a governance transition point for the controlling family, though succession appears to have been managed via the disclosed shareholder pacts rather than presenting a specific red flag. Source: https://www.boursedirect.fr/fr/actualites/categorie/divers/manitou-evolution-de-la-gouvernance-boursier-e10a99995ab42ac9144219a886efdca414c455d2

thesis.business_description: ENCE Energía y Celulosa, S.A., founded in 1957 and headquartered in Madrid (renamed from Grupo Empresarial ENCE in April 2012), is a Spanish producer of bleached eucalyptus kraft pulp (two mills at Navia and Pontevedra, combined capacity reported around 1.2m tonnes) and renewable energy, mainly biomass power generation through its ~51%-owned subsidiary Magnon Green Energy (multiple biomass plants in southern Spain), supported by its own managed forest land (~60,000+ hectares). Source: https://www.bolsasymercados.es/en/bme-exchange/prices-and-markets/shares/detail.ence-energia-y-celulosa-es0130625512.html ; https://ippjournal.com/company/ence-energia-y-celulosa
thesis.competitive_position: One of Europe's leading hardwood (eucalyptus) pulp producers, with a two-segment model combining cyclical pulp sales against steadier, regulated renewable-energy revenue; in 2020 the company sold a 49% stake in its renewables business to Ancala Partners for ~€359m while retaining 51% control, monetizing the asset while keeping operational control. Source: https://www.bolsamania.com/noticias/empresas/ence-vende-el-49-de-su-negocio-de-renovables-a-ancala-partners-por-359-millones--7710585.html
thesis.main_shareholders: Per a December 2024 EFE report (citing CNMV disclosures), ENCE's largest shareholder is Juan Luis Arregui (former chairman) with 29.4% of capital; Asua Inversiones (vehicle of Víctor Urrutia) had recently raised its stake to 8.9%; José Ignacio Comenge holds 6.38% through Mendibea 2002; and US investment fund Atlas Holdings disclosed a 3.2% stake (7,957,446 shares) in December 2024. Source: https://www.infobae.com/espana/agencias/2024/12/11/atlas-holdings-aflora-el-32-de-ence-un-porcentaje-valorado-en-mas-de-22-millones/. Bestinver separately became a significant shareholder with 3.12% (date unconfirmed in this search). Source: https://valenciaplaza.com/bestinver-se-convierte-en-accionista-significativo-en-ence-con-el-3-12. These figures are the most recent (Dec 2024) data point found; we recommend verifying against CNMV's current 'participaciones significativas' register for ENC for any changes since then.
thesis.red_flags: Ownership is concentrated among a handful of individual investors (Arregui ~29%, Urrutia's Asua ~9%, Comenge ~6%) rather than a single controlling family/strategic parent, which can create shifting-coalition governance dynamics; no specific litigation or going-concern issues were identified from official sources in this search. Source: https://www.infobae.com/espana/agencias/2024/12/11/atlas-holdings-aflora-el-32-de-ence-un-porcentaje-valorado-en-mas-de-22-millones/

thesis.business_description: MaltaPost p.l.c., incorporated in 1998 and Malta's designated Universal Postal Service Provider, handles local/international mail, registered and bulk mail, parcel post, courier/express services, plus retail financial services at post-office counters (Western Union transfers, PostaPay, Save, PostaHomeLoan) and B2B outsourcing (document management/scanning in Gozo, logistics, warehousing, shredding). Source: https://www.maltapost.com/the-company?l=1 ; https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/MaltaPost
thesis.competitive_position: Malta's national postal operator, with retail/financial-services diversification beyond core mail to offset secular mail-volume decline; FY2020 turnover reported at €37.9m, up 11.3% year-on-year; it separately acquired a significant shareholding in GWU's insurance company, indicating further diversification into financial services. Source: https://www.businesstoday.com.mt/business/business/1731/maltapost_plc_turnover_up_by_113_to_379_million_in_2020 ; https://maltatoday.com.mt/business/business_news/105749/maltapost_acquires_significant_shareholding_in_gwu_insurance_company
thesis.main_shareholders: MaltaPost is majority-controlled by Lombard Bank Malta p.l.c. The Government of Malta originally sold 35% to Transend Worldwide Ltd (a New Zealand Post subsidiary) in 2002; Transend sold its stake to Lombard Bank in August 2006, and the government sold a further 25% to Lombard in 2007, raising Lombard's holding to 60% (held via wholly owned subsidiary Red Box Limited); Lombard later increased its stake further, reported at 63.8% and, in a more recent (dated ~May 2025) third-party aggregator snapshot (Simply Wall St, citing S&P Global data), at 70.1% (56,312,483 shares), with minor institutional holders HSBC Global Asset Management (UK) at 1.61% and BOV Asset Management at 0.92%. Source: https://archive.businesstoday.com.mt/2008/01/09/t6.html ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/mt/transportation/mtse-mtp/maltapost-shares/ownership. We could not confirm the exact current percentage (70.1% vs. 72% vs. 63.8% reported across different dated sources) directly from Lombard Bank's own most recent annual report or a Malta Stock Exchange company announcement in this search; this figure should be verified against Lombard Bank Malta's current consolidated financial statements.
thesis.red_flags: Majority, escalating control by a single bank parent (Lombard Bank Malta, now ~63.8-72% depending on source/date) significantly limits MaltaPost's free float and minority-shareholder influence; this is a long-disclosed, government-sanctioned privatization structure rather than evidence of misconduct. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/mt/transportation/mtse-mtp/maltapost-shares/ownership. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

name: init innovation in traffic systems SE

thesis.business_description: init innovation in traffic systems SE, headquartered in Karlsruhe, Germany, is an international supplier of transportation telematics for public-transport operators (buses and trains), providing planning/dispatching systems, ticketing and fare management, operations control, real-time passenger information, and passenger-analytics solutions, organized into three segments: INIT Integrated Systems, INIT Cloud Solutions, and INIT Passenger Intelligence. Source: https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/HAM:IXX/summary
thesis.competitive_position: A specialist global supplier in the public-transport telematics niche with meaningful presence in Germany, North America, Europe, Australia and the UAE (one aggregator states North America generates the largest revenue share); headcount reported between ~1,423 (FY2025) and ~1,810 depending on source/date. Source: https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/HAM:IXX/summary ; https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/CHIX:IXXD/summary
thesis.main_shareholders: Per init SE's own official WpHG voting-rights notifications (EQS/DGAP Stimmrechtsmitteilungen): the company's total voting rights increased to 11,040,000 following a 30 June 2026 accelerated-bookbuild cash capital increase (1,000,000 new shares issued at €46.95, with an agreed lock-up). Historical threshold-crossing notices show Union Investment Luxembourg crossing 3% on 21 December 2020 (3.00077689243%) and again reporting 2.98% as of 1 March 2024 (pre-capital-increase share count of ~10.04m), and Universal-Investment-Gesellschaft reporting 3.003% (1 February 2021), later revised down to 2.97% (3 February 2021). We did not find a current, complete (post-June-2026) shareholder breakdown in this search — these fund-manager notifications also typically represent nominee/asset-manager holdings rather than ultimate beneficial owners. Source: https://www.boerse-online.de/dpa-afx/dgap-stimmrechte-init-innovation-in-traffic-systems-se-deutsch-156541.html ; https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/init-aktie-gesamtzahl-der-stimmrechte-nach-kapitalerhohung-steigt-auf-1104-mio . Recommend checking init SE's investor-relations page or BaFin's voting-rights database directly for the current complete shareholder picture post-capital-increase.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; the June 2026 accelerated-bookbuild placement (1,000,000 new shares, ~9.6% dilution of the prior ~10.04m share base) is a disclosed capital-raise with an agreed lock-up, not evidence of distress, though it does represent recent shareholder dilution that investors should factor into per-share valuation. No litigation or going-concern issues were identified.

thesis.business_description: VP Bank AG, founded in 1956 by Guido Feger and headquartered in Vaduz, Liechtenstein, is a private bank specializing in wealth management, investment advisory and asset servicing for private individuals, financial intermediaries (trustees, family offices) and institutional clients, with banking-licensed subsidiaries in Switzerland, Luxembourg, the British Virgin Islands and Singapore, plus fund administration via VP Fund Solutions. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VP_Bank ; https://www.agplaw.com/corporate/bank-account-opening/vp-bank-liechtenstein/
thesis.competitive_position: One of Liechtenstein's three major banks (alongside LGT Group and LLB), with client assets under management reported around CHF 53.7-56.5bn (mid/full-year 2025, source discrepancy) and roughly 1,000 employees; registered shares (Class A) listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange since conversion from bearer shares in 2016, with non-listed Class B shares held separately. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VP_Bank
thesis.main_shareholders: Per VP Bank's own 2023 Annual Report capital-structure disclosure, three anchor-shareholder foundations hold a significant portion of share capital: Stiftung Fürstl. Kommerzienrat Guido Feger holds 46.6% of voting rights / 23.0% of capital; U.M.M. Hilti-Stiftung holds 10.3% of voting rights / 9.7% of capital; and Marxer Stiftung für Bank- und Unternehmenswerte holds 6.3% of voting rights / 11.4% of capital (all as at 31 December 2023). The company states these three anchor shareholders exist to ensure stability and independence, and that no shareholder agreement exists between them. Source: https://report.vpbank.com/fileadmin/user_upload/2023/ar/pdf/VPBLI_GB2023_K2-02_Kapitalstruktur_de.pdf. We did not find 2024/2025 updated percentages in this search; the 2023 figures are the most recent confirmed official data.
thesis.red_flags: Concentrated voting control via the Feger foundation (46.6% of votes from only 23.0% of capital, reflecting the dual-class A/B share structure) gives the controlling foundation outsized influence relative to its economic stake — a disclosed governance feature of the bank's ownership design rather than a hidden issue. Source: https://report.vpbank.com/fileadmin/user_upload/2023/ar/pdf/VPBLI_GB2023_K2-02_Kapitalstruktur_de.pdf. Vice-chairman Markus Hilti (linked to the Hilti-Stiftung anchor shareholder) did not seek re-election at the April 2022 AGM, though the foundation stated its ties to the bank would not change. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: A.G. BARR p.l.c., founded in 1875 and headquartered in Cumbernauld, Scotland, is a FTSE 250 UK branded soft drinks company whose portfolio includes IRN-BRU, Rubicon, Boost (energy/sports drinks) and the recently acquired premium brands Fentimans and Frobishers, selling mainly in the UK. In the year to January 2026 revenue was GBP 437.3m (+4%) with adjusted PBT of GBP 65.8m (+12.5%); H1 to 1 August 2026 revenue rose 8.5% to GBP 247.4m with adjusted PBT of GBP 36.1m. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.G._Barr ; https://www.directorstalkinterviews.com/a-g-barr-revenue-rises-8-5-as-core-brands-drive-growth/4121264379 ; https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/stock-market-news/company--news/ag-barr-hails-pleasing-performance-from-core-brands-as-fy-profits-rise
thesis.competitive_position: A mid-sized independent challenger in the UK soft drinks market, where it competes with much larger multinationals; its strength is iconic Scottish brand IRN-BRU plus fast-growing Boost and Rubicon, and the company says its core brands outgrew the market (7.2% growth in H1 2026). Strategy includes bolt-on acquisitions of premium brands (Fentimans, Frobishers). Full-year guidance (FY to January 2027) is about 10% revenue growth and an adjusted operating margin of around 15%; net bank debt was GBP 47.0m at the half-year, with an interim dividend of 3.82p. Sources: https://www.foodbusinessmea.com/ag-barr-maintains-full-year-outlook-as-first-half-revenue-rises-8/ ; https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-ag-barr-h1-earnings-call-highlights-2026-09-30/
thesis.main_shareholders: Could not locate an official current substantial-shareholder table (FY2026 annual report filed 12 May 2026) or 2026 TR-1 notices in this search; treat as a research gap. Aggregator data (Simply Wall St, undated): William Robin Barr about 15.3% (roughly 17m shares) is the largest holder; top 25 holders own 79.48%.
