Historical TR-1s named Troy Asset Management (2019) and Lindsell Train (2020) as notifiable holders, but their current stakes are unknown. Shares in issue about 112.0m. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/food-beverage-tobacco/bats-chixe-bagl/ag-barr-shares/ownership ; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/barr-a-g---bag/holding-s-in-company/5952966 ; https://cdn.ticker.app/factsheets/bag/barr-a-g-plc-2026-01.pdf
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources. Operational caveats: about GBP 10m of lost sales in H1 2026 from supply problems linked to a Cumbernauld line refresh, Fentimans/Frobishers integration and a new planning system; statutory PBT fell 3.7% on one-off integration costs. Ongoing exposure to UK sugar levy/regulation, input-cost inflation and competition from larger rivals. Sources: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/ag-barr-says-revenue-hit-stock-availability-issues ; https://kalkinemedia.com/uk/news/announcements/ag-barr-bag-announces-h1-revenue-of-approximately-ps246m-upholds-full-year-profit-forecast-despite-ps10m-supply-chain-setback
thesis.insider_ownership: Founding-family influence remains: William Robin Barr (former chairman, Barr family) is shown at about 15.3% by Simply Wall St (aggregator, undated, not verified against an official filing); the same source puts total individual insiders at about 17%. Director Julie Barr has made small dividend-reinvestment purchases (PDMR notices). Shareholdings of Chairman Mark Allen and CEO Euan Sutherland were not confirmed in this search. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/food-beverage-tobacco/bats-chixe-bagl/ag-barr-shares/ownership ; https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/ag-barr-directors-invest-company-shares ; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/barr-a-g---bag/director-pdmr-shareholding/9659068

thesis.business_description: Taaleri Oyj, founded in 2007 (originally Taaleritehdas) and listed on Nasdaq Helsinki, is a Finnish investment group operating a Private Asset Management segment (renewable energy — wind, solar, biofuels — plus real estate and bioindustry funds, serving private individuals, institutional investors and companies) and a Strategic Investments segment centered on non-life insurer Garantia (Vakuutusosakeyhtiö Garantia). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taaleri ; https://tracenable.com/company/taaleri/group-entities
thesis.competitive_position: Niche Finnish alternative-asset manager specializing in renewable-energy private-equity funds (private equity funds and co-investments held ~€2.2bn AUM at end-2021) combined with a captive insurance subsidiary (Garantia) for earnings diversification; 2025 revenue was reported at €58.94m, down 16.0% from €70.20m in 2024, though Q1 2026 commentary noted strong earnings growth driven by Garantia and renewable energy plus expansion into venture capital and private credit. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taaleri (AUM) ; https://borsvarlden.com/artiklar/taaleri-a-healthy-result-supported-by-fair-values-changes-and-sw3-fees-nordea (2025/2026 revenue and earnings commentary).
thesis.main_shareholders: Juhani Elomaa is Taaleri's Chairman of the Board and a significant, long-standing insider shareholder; company stock-exchange releases disclose his and his spouse Titta Elomaa's periodic transactions, including a June 2024 gift/donation of 112,500 shares by Juhani Elomaa and a February 2025 sale of 4,450 shares by Titta Elomaa. Source: https://taaleri.com/en/news/taaleri-plc-managers-transactions-juhani-elomaa-8 ; https://taaleri.com/en/news/taaleri-plc-managers-transactions-titta-elomaa-7. Taaleri's Shareholders' Nomination Board is composed of representatives of the company's largest shareholders, with Elomaa among the nominating members, implying he represents (or is) a top-tier holder, though his exact current percentage stake was not confirmed in this search. Source: https://www.inderes.se/releases/composition-of-taaleris-shareholders-nomination-board-6. We could not retrieve a full, current 'largest shareholders' percentage table from Taaleri's 2025 annual report or investor-relations ownership page in this search; this should be checked directly (e.g. the shareholder-structure section of https://www.sttinfo.fi/ir-files/54994630/71868589/15026/Taaleri%20Oyj%20Vuosikertomus%202025.pdf).
thesis.red_flags: A FY2025 write-down related to a biocoal investment was disclosed as impacting results (per Q1 2026 commentary), though liquidity and solvency were described as remaining robust — a specific investment-loss item worth monitoring rather than a going-concern flag. Source: https://www.inderes.fi/analyst-comments/taaleri-q325-pikakommentti-sijoitustuotoilla-hurja-tulosylitys. No litigation or governance issues were identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Prodvinalco S.A. is a Romanian spirits maker founded in 1932 and based in Cluj-Napoca. It produces, bottles and sells alcoholic drinks. Its 2025 annual report lists the product groups as tuica and natural fruit brandies, spirit drinks, refined alcohol, aperitifs and liqueurs. Brands such as R 26, V33, Monopoly, Hermannstadt, Iancu, Napoca, Carpathia and Vlad Tepes come from an aggregator profile. Standalone 2025 net turnover was RON 71.3m (+4% vs RON 68.8m in 2024) and net profit RON 19.5m. It made no export deliveries in 2025, so the business is entirely domestic. Shares (31,495,034) trade on BVB's AeRO market. Sources: https://www.bvb.ro/info/Raportari/VAC/VAC_20260324122625_Raportul-anual-aferent-exercitiului-financiar-2025.pdf ; https://snowball-analytics.com/public/asset/VAC.RO.RON ; https://www.economica.net/clujenii-de-la-prodvinalco-vor-face-50-de-apartamente-langa-facultatea-de-litere-a-universitatii-bab_191662.html
thesis.competitive_position: Prodvinalco is a regional mass-market spirits producer focused on lower-priced spirit drinks (e.g. 26-33% ABV products sold through mainstream retail) in Transylvania and the wider Romanian market. Profitability is high for the sector: 2025 net margin was about 27% of turnover (RON 19.5m on RON 71.3m, our calculation from the annual report). ZF has listed it among Romanian entrepreneurial FMCG firms with the highest profit margins and reported net profit up 43% in H1 2024 (RON 11.2m). Management has said in the past that market pressure forces margin cuts and higher promotion spend. No national market-share data or named competitors were found in this search. Sources: https://www.bvb.ro/info/Raportari/VAC/VAC_20260324122625_Raportul-anual-aferent-exercitiului-financiar-2025.pdf ; https://www.zf.ro/analiza/trei-companii-antreprenoriale-romanesti-au-cele-mai-mari-marje-de-profit-din-fmcg-17380381 ; https://www.zfenglish.com/capital-market/spirits-producer-prodvinalco-ends-h1-with-43-rise-in-net-profit-to-22496756 ; https://www.zf.ro/companii/prodvinalco-cluj-piata-ne-obliga-sa-reducem-marjele-de-profit-si-sa-plusam-in-promovare-4446340
thesis.main_shareholders: Economica (undated article) gives: Mircea Todea 25.35%, Vasile Albon 23.58%, Viorel Hosu 15.57%, Alin and Adrian Moraru together 15.97%, and other minorities 20.31%. A 2014 Actual de Cluj article gave Todea about 25% and Albon about 23.57%, which is consistent. ZF names the third holder as 'Marcel Hosu', which conflicts with 'Viorel Hosu' in Economica. An aggregator (Snowball/EMIS) describes the company as a subsidiary of 'Vinton SRL Galati', which conflicts with the individual-holder data and is unverified. No dated shareholder register from the 2025 annual report or BVB was found; treat the percentages as possibly stale. Sources: https://www.economica.net/clujenii-de-la-prodvinalco-vor-face-50-de-apartamente-langa-facultatea-de-litere-a-universitatii-bab_191662.html ; https://actualdecluj.ro/un-producator-de-spirtoase-da-13-milioane-de-lei-actionarilor-din-profit/ ; https://www.zfenglish.com/capital-market/spirits-producer-prodvinalco-ends-h1-with-43-rise-in-net-profit-to-22496756
thesis.red_flags: No accounting or litigation issues found in official sources. Points to watch: (1) a few founding holders and their families control about 65-80%, and the shares trade on the small AeRO MTS segment, so liquidity is thin and minority influence limited. (2) The business is entirely domestic and exposed to Romanian excise duty and VAT changes, alcohol regulation and consumer pressure on cheap spirits. (3) The company has non-core real-estate activity (a 50-apartment residential project in Cluj per Economica) and past management comments about it 'turning into a bank', which raises questions about cash use. (4) Dividend-per-share data differs between aggregators (Primet vs Parqet); use BVB AGM resolutions. Sources: https://www.economica.net/clujenii-de-la-prodvinalco-vor-face-50-de-apartamente-langa-facultatea-de-litere-a-universitatii-bab_191662.html ; https://www.zf.ro/companii/prodvinalco-cluj-ne-am-transformat-intr-o-banca-niciodata-nu-am-pus-un-accent-atat-de-mare-pe-bani-ca-acum-6214473 ; https://primet.ro/actiuni/VAC ; https://bvb.ro/info/Raportari/VAC/VAC_20251118150321_Raport-curent-en---AGOA.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is high and family-linked. Vasile Albon is Chairman of the Board, with about 23.6% per Economica. Mircea Todea, about 25.35%, was described as executive chairman. A 4 May 2026 BVB report lists Todea-Silaghi Alexandra as executive chairman. The 27 Apr 2026 AGM appointed Todea Mircea-Vlad and Todea-Silaghi Alexandra as directors (1 May 2026 to 1 Aug 2027), which suggests a generational handover within the Todea family; the exact family relationships were not confirmed. Directors' holdings at a dated record were not found. Sources: https://www.bvb.ro/info/Raportari/VAC/VAC_20260504135330_Raport-curent-structura-functii.pdf ; https://bvb.ro/info/Raportari/VAC/VAC_20260427151917_2-Raport-curent-en---AGOA.pdf ; https://www.economica.net/clujenii-de-la-prodvinalco-vor-face-50-de-apartamente-langa-facultatea-de-litere-a-universitatii-bab_191662.html

thesis.business_description: BVZ Holding AG, headquartered in Brig/Zermatt area, Valais, Switzerland (SIX Swiss Exchange-listed, ticker BVZN), is a Swiss transport and tourism holding company whose core business is the regional passenger rail concession of the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn (linking Disentis/Göschenen with Zermatt, plus the Täsch-Zermatt shuttle, Furka Pass car shuttle, and Visp-Zermatt freight), alongside tourism flagship brands Gornergrat Bahn (scenic cogwheel railway) and Glacier Express, real estate (via BVZ Asset Management AG), and minority stakes in Matterhorn Terminal Täsch AG (34%) and Zermatt Bergbahnen AG (22%). Source: https://www.bvzholding.ch/en/company/bvz-group/shareholdings/ ; https://www.moneycab.com/company/bvz-holding/
thesis.competitive_position: A regionally dominant Alpine transport and tourism operator controlling essential rail access to Zermatt (a car-free resort), combining a public-service passenger-rail concession with high-margin tourism brands (Glacier Express, Gornergrat Bahn); 2024 revenue reported at CHF 205.16 million with roughly 650-694 employees. Source: https://www.bvzholding.ch/fileadmin/user_upload/BVZ_Halbjahresbericht_2024.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: We could not confirm an official SIX disclosure filing naming the Gemeinde (municipality) of Zermatt or other major shareholders in this search. Per a third-party source (t-online.de, undated), free float is reported at 57.92%, implying that approximately 42% is held by non-free-float (likely strategic/public-sector or long-term) shareholders, but the identity of those holders was not disclosed in the sources found. BVZ's own half-year reports reference subsidiaries 'fully owned by the public sector' but these appear to refer to entities outside BVZ's consolidation scope, not BVZ Holding's own shareholder register. Source: https://www.t-online.de/finanzen/boerse/aktien/bvz-holding-aktie/ch0008207356/ (free-float figure, not an official shareholder-register filing) . Not confirmed from an official filing — recommend checking BVZ's Annual Report Corporate Governance section or SIX's significant-shareholder disclosure platform directly, particularly to verify any Canton Valais or Gemeinde Zermatt public-sector stake.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; however, we were unable to identify BVZ's actual major/controlling shareholders in this search (a notable gap for what appears to be a quasi-public-infrastructure operator), so any assumption about public-sector (cantonal/municipal) control should be verified directly via BVZ's own corporate-governance disclosures before relying on it.

thesis.business_description: Duni Group supplies sustainable dining and food-packaging products to the restaurant/catering market: Dining Solutions (napkins, table covers, candles; napkins are the majority of revenue) and Meal Service (take-away, serving and catering packaging, e.g. the BioPak brand). Production in Sweden, Germany, Poland and Thailand, sales in over 40 markets. FY2025 net sales SEK 7,685m (7,578m), operating income SEK 560m (604m). Headquarters not confirmed in this search. Sources: https://www.dunigroup.com/media/press-releases/2026/year-end-report-january-1-december-31-2025/ ; https://www.dunigroup.com/about-us/history/ ; https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/10858-78
thesis.competitive_position: Describes itself as a market leader in sustainable dining and food-packaging solutions for restaurants, with a consolidating strategy in Europe via bolt-on acquisitions (SETI in 2024; in 2025 Poppies, LinePack and ByGreen per the year-end report). The earlier screen also lists Solserv as completed by Q2 2026; that was not confirmed in this search. Growth in 2025 was acquisition-led (+1.4% reported, +6.0% at fixed FX). Market-share figures and named competitors were not found; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.dunigroup.com/media/press-releases/2026/year-end-report-january-1-december-31-2025/ ; https://dunigroup.com/files/Main/295/4029040/press-release-pdf.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: At 31 Dec 2025 (Duni corporate governance report 2025): Mellby Gard AB 51.49%, Protector Forsikring ASA 6.74%, Carnegie Fonder AB 6.38%; 46,999,032 shares outstanding, one vote each, 9,219 shareholders. Aggregators differ slightly (Affarsvarlden: Mellby Gard Intressenter AB 52.3%, Carnegie 6.4%, Protector 5.5%, undated; Simply Wall St about 51.5%) and the Mellby Gard entity name varies (Mellby Gard AB / Intressenter AB / Holding AB). Mellby Gard raised its stake from 40.14% to over 50% in May 2024 (2024 governance report). Sources: https://www.dunigroup.com/files/Remuneration_reports/corporate_governance_report_2025.pdf ; https://www.dunigroup.com/files/Remuneration_reports/corporate_governance_report_2024.pdf ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/duni
thesis.insider_ownership: Controlling holder Mellby Gard (above) is the dominant insider-type owner; its representative Sven Knutsson sits on the board (described as Mellby Gard vice CEO in a 2023 nomination document). Reported insider purchases (Affarsvarlden insider table): Chairman Thomas Gustafsson and Togus AB each 75,000 shares on 11 Sep 2025 (may be the same transaction reported for person and associated company); Sven Knutsson several purchases in Feb 2026; Magnus Holmberg 3,000 shares on 20 May 2026. Gustafsson held 26,400 shares per the 2023 nomination document (stale). CEO shareholding not located; Robert Dackeskog is named CEO since 2021 in a 2024 article, current status not re-confirmed. Sources: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/duni ; https://www.dunigroup.com/files/Public/295/3748771/duni-ab---information-om-foreslagna-styrelseledamoter-i-duni.pdf
thesis.red_flags: Known event sanity-check: Duni is the ACQUIRER (Poppies, LinePack, ByGreen in 2025; Solserv unconfirmed here); no offer for Duni itself found, and Mellby Gard's earlier mandatory bid dates from 2023 (earlier screen), with its stake passing 50% in May 2024. Risks: (1) controlling shareholder at about 51.5% limits free float and minority influence; the chairman is independent of the company but not of major shareholders (2023 document); (2) operating income fell to SEK 560m from 604m on weaker global restaurant demand and Q4 sales fell 4.5%; (3) acquisition integration risk and growth reliant on M&A; (4) dividend of SEK 5.00 per share held flat; Duni new group targets from 2026. Leverage and accounting issues not assessed in this search. Sources: https://www.dunigroup.com/media/press-releases/2026/year-end-report-january-1-december-31-2025/ ; https://www.dunigroup.com/files/Remuneration_reports/corporate_governance_report_2025.pdf

thesis.business_description: Catering International & Services (CIS), founded in 1992 and headquartered in Marseille, France, is a service integrator providing full-service catering, hospitality, accommodation and facility/utility management (camp design, logistics, water treatment, waste management, maintenance, fire safety) for remote onshore and offshore worksites, mainly serving the energy, mining and construction sectors. Source: https://a-leads.co/company/1429042_878721fc ; https://www.slideshare.net/HoussamElDeeb/cis-introduction
thesis.competitive_position: Established remote-site service provider with historical roots in oil & gas catering, now diversified into mining, construction and institutional/government clients, operating across 20+ countries; listed on Euronext Growth Paris (moved from Euronext Paris to Euronext Growth in 2022 per a shareholder vote with 99.7% approval). Source: https://www.journal-officiel.gouv.fr/publications/balo/pdf/2016/0422/201604221601502.pdf (historical) ; (2022 listing-venue change, per AMF filing).
thesis.main_shareholders: CIS was historically controlled by a concert between the Arnoux family (founder Régis Arnoux, Monique Arnoux, Florence Arnoux, Frédérique Salamon, via holding company Financière Régis Arnoux/'Finra') and the Aloyan family (descendants of Alain and Solange Aloyan), together holding ~68% of capital per 2018/2020 AMF declarations, with Finra alone holding close to half of capital by 2023 and the Arnoux family at ~53.5% of capital / ~64.7% of voting rights. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/307/2018/06/FC307249590_20180615.pdf ; https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/307/8888/01/FC307495778_20230605.pdf. Critically, that same June 2023 AMF filing recorded the termination of the Arnoux-Aloyan shareholder pact, stating that as of 31 May 2023 neither family held any shares in the company — meaning control changed hands around mid-2023. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/307/8888/01/FC307495778_20230605.pdf. A May 2024 Zonebourse snapshot shows free float at 29.76%, implying the remaining ~70% is held by insiders/anchor holders, but we could not identify the new controlling shareholder(s) from an official AMF threshold-crossing filing in this search post-2023; Régis Arnoux and CEO Yannick Morillon are still listed among current leadership. Source: https://ch.zonebourse.com/CATERING-INTL-SCES-5378/
thesis.red_flags: A major, largely undocumented (in this search) change of control occurred around mid-2023 when the founding Arnoux and Aloyan families reportedly exited their entire stake per an AMF filing, yet Régis Arnoux still appears as a leadership figure in 2024 — this discrepancy between a 'zero shares' filing and continued leadership presence is a genuine unresolved question that warrants direct verification against CIS's most recent AMF threshold-crossing notices or annual report before relying on any stated ownership structure. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/307/8888/01/FC307495778_20230605.pdf ; https://ch.zonebourse.com/CATERING-INTL-SCES-5378/. No litigation or going-concern issues were identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: ASBISc Enterprises Plc, founded in 1990 and headquartered in Limassol, Cyprus, distributes IT hardware, components, mobile devices, software and IoT/robotics products and solutions across Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA) and beyond (56+ countries), serving resellers, retailers, e-tailers and SMBs, and also sells its own brands (Prestigio, Canyon, Perenio, AENO, LORGAR, CRON ROBOTICS). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASBIS ; https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ASB.WA/profile
thesis.competitive_position: Large, EMEA-focused value-added IT distributor with reported 2021 revenue of ~US$3.1bn and continued double-digit revenue growth reported in subsequent investor updates; differentiated from pure distributors by a growing own-brand consumer-electronics portfolio. Listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASBIS ; https://investor.asbis.com/news/investor-news/asbis-continues-its-double-digit-growth-of-revenue
thesis.main_shareholders: ASBIS's own investor-relations shareholder table (last updated 2 April 2024) shows KS Holdings Ltd holding 20,448,127 shares, or 36.84% of share capital and votes; a footnote identifies CEO and Board Chairman Siarhei Kostevitch as the ultimate beneficial owner of KS Holdings, making his effective total stake 36.84%. Source: https://investor.asbis.com/share-information. This is broadly consistent with company AGM/EGM voting disclosures from 2021-2022 showing KS Holdings with ~36.8% of votes present (down from 66.37% in 2008, reflecting dilution/share issuance over time). Source: https://investor.asbis.com/news/current-reports/current-report-11-2022.
thesis.red_flags: Majority effective control by founder/CEO Siarhei Kostevitch (~37% direct/indirect, combined with his CEO and Chairman roles) concentrates both operational and governance control in one person — a disclosed structure rather than a hidden issue, but a standard minority-shareholder consideration for this name. Source: https://investor.asbis.com/share-information. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Cateks d.d. (Cakovec, Croatia) is a textile manufacturer: fabrics, artificial leather, household linen, sports products and special-purpose materials, including polyurethane-coated technical fabrics for military, police and fire services, plus medical covers and mattress/pillow protectors; operations span weaving, finishing, coating/laminating and ready-made garments. Aggregator data: about 225 employees, founded 1874, FY2025 revenue about EUR 22.5m and net income about EUR 2.5m (annual report ESEF filing of 30 Apr 2026 as reported by financialfilings.com); H1 2026 revenue EUR 12.1m, +13.9% y/y (company H1 2026 report on the Zagreb Stock Exchange). Sources: https://simplywall.st/stock/zgse/ctks ; https://craft.co/cateks ; https://financialfilings.com/companies/cateks-dd/ ; https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/CTKS/FI-CTKS-08009a2c4513d75c7ba446d3903a9ca2.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: Small Croatian regional textile maker with a niche in coated technical/protective textiles and home/medical textiles; the sources found give no market-share data and name no competitors or moats. Revenue (about EUR 22m) is small in absolute terms. Could not locate a competitor list or market-share figure in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stock/zgse/ctks ; https://financialfilings.com/companies/cateks-dd/
thesis.main_shareholders: Control sits with an SQ Capital-led concert group: at the time of the Hanfa-approved takeover offer (approved 26 Sep 2025, EUR 43/share for the remaining 66,976 shares) the bidder, acting for the 'Primus' fund, and persons acting in concert held 123,369 shares = 64.82%; after the offer closed (only 17 holders / 1,178 shares, 0.61% tendered) the group was reported at about 65.43% (Lider media report, secondary). Company Q1 2026 interim report shareholder table (as surfaced via search, excerpt appears incomplete as listed lines sum to about 78%): HPB d.d. 23.5%, Investarx d.o.o. 22.4%, Erste & Steiermaerkische Bank 8.4%, Matija Bilandzija 5.3%, treasury shares 2.0%, other holders about 16.8%. The relationship of these lines to SQ Capital/Primus (HPB and Erste may be custodian/nominee accounts; Investarx is an SQ Capital-linked fund per press) was not verified. The H1 2026 report may hold a newer table that could not be read. Sources: https://hanfa.hr/news/hanfa-board-meeting-approvals-for-tokic-s-ipo-prospectus-and-for-the-announcement-of-the-takeover-bid-of-cateks/ ; https://en.lider.media/2025/09/26/hanfa-approved-tokics-ipo-and-sq-capitals-acquisition-of-cateks/ ; https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/CTKS/FI-CTKS-dff5946d78211a1b4c6faf174290cfa9.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: Matija Bilandzija holds about 5.3% per the Q1 2026 interim report table and is among the shareholders SQ Capital represented in the offer, i.e. management is inside the controlling concert group. His title is inconsistent across sources (CEO per Simply Wall St/Lider; Chairman of the Board per Craft.co). Treasury shares 2.0%. No holdings found for other board or supervisory board members. Sources: https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/CTKS/FI-CTKS-dff5946d78211a1b4c6faf174290cfa9.pdf ; https://craft.co/cateks ; https://simplywall.st/stock/zgse/ctks
thesis.red_flags: Takeover context (sanity-checked): Cateks was the TARGET of SQ Capital's offer, approved by Hanfa on 26 Sep 2025; offer completed with only 0.61% tendered, so no squeeze-out or delisting and the shares remain listed (H1 2026 and Aug 2026 filings exist on the ZSE). Risks: (1) control by an SQ Capital-led concert group of roughly 65% that includes the CEO, so minority holders have limited influence and potential conflicts; (2) the EUR 43 bid was far below subsequent trading (price reached EUR 82 and about EUR 61 in Nov 2025; EUR 63-109 range in Q1 2026), and observers saw it as an exit route, indicating a thin, illiquid stock; (3) management churn: board member Mario Kovacevic resigned 1 Jul 2025 (Craft.co still lists him as CFO, stale); mandates of the president and a board member were extended at a 27 Aug 2026 supervisory board session; (4) small scale and concentration in a niche; (5) earlier interim reports were explicitly unaudited, and current auditor not identified in this search. Sources: https://en.lider.media/2025/09/26/hanfa-approved-tokics-ipo-and-sq-capitals-acquisition-of-cateks/ ; https://hanfa.hr/news/hanfa-board-meeting-approvals-for-tokic-s-ipo-prospectus-and-for-the-announcement-of-the-takeover-bid-of-cateks/ ; https://financialfilings.com/companies/cateks-dd/ (filing index; underlying notices are on https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/CTKS/)
thesis.website: https://www.cateks.hr (not confirmed by the searches run; verify before publishing). Zagreb Stock Exchange filings: https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/CTKS/

thesis.business_description: LU-VE S.p.A., founded in 1985 (when Iginio Liberali acquired Contardo S.p.A.) and headquartered in Uboldo, near Varese, Italy, manufactures air-cooled heat exchangers and related cooling equipment (unit coolers, condensers, gas coolers, liquid coolers, glass doors for refrigerated display cases) through two business units — Cooling Systems and Components — serving refrigeration (~46.5% of markets), air conditioning (~27.5%) and power generation/industrial processes (~11.4%). Source: https://www.luvegroup.com/en/rd/ ; https://tracenable.com/company/lu-ve/group-entities
thesis.competitive_position: Self-described third-largest global and second-largest European producer of air heat exchangers, with roughly 20 production units across Italy, China, Czech Republic, Finland, India, Poland, Sweden and the USA, 34 sales companies worldwide, and ~4,100 employees (over 1,300 in Italy); exports account for roughly 80-83% of production. Listed on Euronext Milan (Borsa Italiana). Source: https://www.luvegroup.com/en/rd/
thesis.main_shareholders: LU-VE is controlled by the Liberali family via holding company Finami S.p.A. Per a March 2021 company disclosure, after selling a 6% stake, Finami S.p.A. held 10,187,999 ordinary shares = 45.82% of share capital, corresponding to approximately 56% of exercisable voting rights at the shareholders' meeting; a CONSOB azionariato filing (as at 31/12/2020) names Matteo Liberali as the individual at the top of the ownership chain for the Finami-held stake. Source: https://emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2022-05/20210323_92353.pdf ; https://www.consob.it/web/consob-and-its-activities/w/lu-ve-spa-azionariato-2020-12-31. The second-largest shareholder is G4 S.r.l., reported by Il Sole 24 Ore (undated snapshot) at 15.79% of voting rights, with Finami at 56.02% of voting rights in the same table. Source: https://mercati.ilsole24ore.com/azioni/borsa-italiana/dettaglio-completo/LUVE.MI/analisi-fondamentale. A 2015 Affaritaliani article described the ~54.6% controlling stake as 'firmly in the hands of the Liberali family' with a further ~19.2% controlled by the Faggioli family (likely the individuals behind G4 S.r.l., though this link was not independently confirmed). Source: https://www.affaritaliani.it/economia/aim-italia-lu-ve-pronta-a-nuove-acquisizioni-sui-mercati-emergenti-448268.html
thesis.red_flags: Majority voting control sits with the founding Liberali family (~56% of votes via Finami), a long-standing, disclosed family-industrial structure typical of Italian mid-caps rather than a governance red flag. No litigation or going-concern issues were identified from official sources in this search. Source: https://emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2022-05/20210323_92353.pdf

thesis.business_description: Plastika Kritis S.A., founded in 1970 and headquartered in Heraklion, Crete (Athens Stock Exchange-listed, ticker PLAKR, since 1999), manufactures masterbatches (color, white, black, UV-stabilizer, additive and filler concentrates, plus biodegradable compounds), agricultural films (multi-layer greenhouse/silage films), geomembranes, and polyethylene pipes for irrigation/water/telecom/gas distribution, and also operates plastics recycling and renewable-energy assets (wind park, photovoltaic stations) in Greece, exporting to roughly 70-90+ countries. Source: https://knowde.com/stores/plastika-kritis-s-a/brands/kritilen
thesis.competitive_position: A specialized Greek plastics/masterbatch and agri-film producer with facilities reported in Greece plus additional plants cited across France, Romania, Poland, Russia, Turkey and China (sources vary on exact footprint), and 1,000-2,000 employees depending on source; serves agriculture, water management, environmental protection and plastics-processing end markets. Source: https://pro.stockalarm.io/quote/PLAKR.AT/intelligence
thesis.main_shareholders: The company is controlled by the Lempidakis family: per a 2024 financial-press report (newmoney.gr, via naftemporiki.gr reporting), brothers Michalis and Manolis (Emmanouil) Lempidakis jointly run the company and together control approximately 50% of the shares; Ioannis Lempidakis (chairman per board announcements) and other family members also hold direct stakes and board positions — a 2017 Athens Exchange (ATHEX/Hellenic Exchanges) regulatory filing disclosed that Ioannis Lempidakis, son of Michael, held 481,630 ordinary registered shares = 1.173% of a roughly 41-million-share capital structure at that time. A later ATHEX filing (referenced for 2025) shows family share transfers against a different total share count (27,379,200), which we could not reconcile with the 2017 figures in this search — this discrepancy should be checked against the company's current capital structure disclosure. Source: https://www.athexgroup.gr/documents/10180/4617840/687_896_2017_Greek_1.pdf/392ea955-cb36-48e2-83f6-ff41338797df ; https://www.athexgroup.gr/sites/default/files/hermes_3/2025-12/el/4e8af017-1b03-4692-8af0-171b0326927a/687_8388_2025_Greek_1.pdf
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources beyond standard family-control concentration (Lempidakis family ~50%+); the unreconciled change in total share count between the 2017 and 2025 ATHEX filings (approximately 41 million vs. 27.4 million shares) should be verified against the company's annual report (likely reflecting a share consolidation/reverse split or a filing referring to a subset of shares) before relying on either figure for per-share calculations.

thesis.business_description: H&R GmbH & Co. KGaA, founded in 1919 and headquartered in Salzbergen, Germany, is a group of nearly 50 subsidiaries that develops, produces and markets chemical-pharmaceutical specialty products (waxes, wax emulsions, plasticizers, paraffins, petroleum jellies) from fossil, renewable, synthetic and recycled hydrocarbons, serving automotive, cosmetics, pharmaceutical, construction and food customers, plus a Plastics segment making precision plastic parts, organized into ChemPharm Refining, ChemPharm Sales and Plastics segments with refineries in Hamburg-Neuhof and Salzbergen. Source: https://www.hur.com/fileadmin/user_upload/media/Berichte_IR/2026/HuR_AR2025.pdf ; https://morningstar.com.au/investments/security/XETR/2HRA
thesis.competitive_position: Specialty hydrocarbon/wax refiner and precision plastics manufacturer with most revenue generated from ChemPharm Refining within Germany; recently became the subject of a going-private transaction (see below), which typically follows from a controlling shareholder's view that the business is undervalued as a listed entity. Source: https://www.hur.com/fileadmin/user_upload/media/Berichte_IR/2026/HuR_AR2025.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: H&R is controlled by Nils Hansen via H&R Holding GmbH. Per Latham & Watkins' own transaction announcement, H&R Holding GmbH (controlled by Nils Hansen) launched a voluntary public tender offer at €5.00 per share and secured 77.54% of H&R KGaA shares by August 2025; prior to the offer, 61.45% of shares were already attributed to Hansen, with a further 6.06% attributed to Wilhelm Scholten (who retained an indirect stake of the same size post-transaction). Source: https://www.lw.com/en/news/2025/05/latham-watkins-advises-hr-holding-gmbh-voluntary-public-tender-offer-all-outstanding-shares-hr-kgaa. The company's own 2026 AGM data-protection notice confirms its shares are bearer shares, so no share register is maintained and ownership below major-holder thresholds cannot be independently verified from a register. Source: https://www.hur.com/fileadmin/user_upload/media/Hauptversammlung_2026/H_R_HV_2026_Datenschutzinformation.pdf. We could not confirm from this search whether a squeeze-out or delisting has since been completed; this should be checked against current Bundesanzeiger voting-rights notifications.
thesis.red_flags: An active going-private process is underway: H&R Holding GmbH (Nils Hansen) raised its stake to 77.54% via a 2025 tender offer and the deal materials reference potential further delisting or squeeze-out plans, meaning remaining minority shareholders face elevated delisting/forced-buyout risk and reduced liquidity. Source: https://www.lw.com/en/news/2025/05/latham-watkins-advises-hr-holding-gmbh-voluntary-public-tender-offer-all-outstanding-shares-hr-kgaa ; https://finder.techleap.nl/news/feed/h-r-holding-secures-77-54-shares. No litigation or going-concern issues beyond this control-transaction risk were identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Simonds Farsons Cisk plc ('Farsons'), tracing to 1928 and headquartered in Mriehel/Birkirkara, Malta, is a diversified Maltese food and beverage group engaged in brewing and distributing beer (Cisk) and soft drinks (Kinnie), importing and distributing international brands (Pepsi, Carlsberg), operating franchised food retail outlets, and property development. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simonds_Farsons_Cisk ; https://www.farsons.com/simonds-farsons-cisk
thesis.competitive_position: Malta's dominant domestic brewer and a leading beverage/food importer-distributor, listed on the Malta Stock Exchange (SFC) with reported annual turnover above €88m (dated figure) and certifications in ISO 9001, HACCP and BRC; has stated ambitions to expand regionally/internationally beyond Malta. Source: https://jobsinmalta.com/companies/simonds-farsons-cisk-plc-jobs/1687
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Curmi & Partners' company profile (citing disclosed holdings above 5%), three holding companies each hold roughly equal, large stakes: M.S.M. Investments Limited 26.50%, Farrugia Investments Limited 26.50%, and Sciclunas Estates Limited 26.32% — together accounting for just under 80% of the company. Source: https://curmiandpartners.com/en/sfc-company-profile. A Simply Wall St ownership snapshot corroborates these three names and percentages, noting the top 13 shareholders hold 81.28% in total, with Private Companies holding ~79.3% of shares overall, the general public ~18.7%, and individual insiders ~0.6%. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/mt/food-beverage-tobacco/mtse-sfc/simonds-farsons-cisk-shares/ownership. We could not identify the ultimate individuals/families behind M.S.M. Investments, Farrugia Investments or Sciclunas Estates (e.g., any link to the historical Gollcher or Cisk founding families) from an official source in this search; this should be verified against Farsons' own annual report shareholder-structure disclosure.
thesis.red_flags: Very high ownership concentration among three private holding companies (~79% combined) leaves only ~19% in public hands, substantially limiting minority-shareholder influence and free-float liquidity — a disclosed structure rather than evidence of misconduct, but a significant governance consideration for minority investors. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/mt/food-beverage-tobacco/mtse-sfc/simonds-farsons-cisk-shares/ownership. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Luka Ploče d.d., founded in 1952 (as Luke i skladišta, privatized and publicly floated in 2003) and headquartered in Ploče, southern Croatia, operates the Port of Ploče on the Adriatic (between Split and Dubrovnik), handling general, bulk and liquid cargo (loading, unloading, transport, processing, weighing), freight forwarding, ship handling/maintenance and mooring services, with wholly owned subsidiaries including Marine Service, Pločanska Navigacija and Port Sped. Source: https://www.luka-ploce.hr/about-the-port/company-profile/?lang=en ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Plo%C4%8De
thesis.competitive_position: One of Croatia's main strategic ports, positioned at a transport junction linking the Adriatic/Mediterranean to Central Europe and capable of accepting Cape-size vessels up to 180,000 DWT; share capital of €22,417,251, listed on the Zagreb Stock Exchange (ticker LKPC). Q1 2024 cargo throughput was 973,213 tonnes, down 17% year-on-year, and the company agreed to acquire 100% of New Concrete Technologies d.o.o. Source: https://www.luka-ploce.hr/company-id/?lang=en ; https://www.portseurope.com/category/company/luka-ploce-d-d/
thesis.main_shareholders: Luka Ploče was privatized via a 2011 Croatian government-approved sale of shares to Group employees (through the Croatian Privatization Fund) and a 2011 public share offering of 200,353 new ordinary shares at HRK 850/share, raising HRK ~170.3m. Source: https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/migrated/financials/LKPC-fin2011-1Q-NotREV-N-HR.pdf. We could not locate a current named major-shareholder table (e.g., confirming whether the Republic of Croatia retains a stake, or identifying any employee/institutional block) from the company's recent annual reports or the Zagreb Stock Exchange issuer page in this search. AGM attendance figures (328,666 votes = 77.70% of share capital represented at the November 2023 meeting; 318,835 votes = 75.38% at the June 2022 meeting) confirm a high concentration of voting shares among a relatively small number of attendees, but do not identify them by name. Source: https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/LKPC/GS-LKPC-131d0b1f749e4190de8064d2c439be85.pdf. This is a genuine research gap that should be checked against the company's 2023/2024 annual report corporate-governance statement or Croatia's Central Depository & Clearing Company (SKDD) register.
thesis.red_flags: High attendance/voting-share concentration at recent AGMs (75-78% of capital represented, implying few large holders) without a publicly confirmed shareholder identity in this search is itself a transparency gap worth flagging for further diligence, though not evidence of misconduct. Q1 2024 cargo throughput declined 17% year-on-year, an operating-performance item to monitor rather than a governance flag. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources. Source: https://www.portseurope.com/category/company/luka-ploce-d-d/

thesis.business_description: Mincon Group plc, headquartered in Shannon, County Clare, Ireland (founded 1977, renamed from Manrock plc in September 2013), designs, manufactures, sells and services rock-drilling equipment — DTH hammers, rotary and reverse-circulation drill bits, drill pipes, mast attachments, casing-advance systems, and foundation/geotechnical/anchoring and horizontal-directional-drilling products — for mining, construction, water-well drilling and geothermal applications, listed on Euronext Dublin and AIM. Source: https://morningstar.com.au/investments/security/lse/mcon
thesis.competitive_position: Niche global manufacturer of rock-drilling consumables/equipment with its own international sales and distribution network; generates the largest share of revenue from the Americas, with additional presence in Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Ireland and Australasia; ~500-600 employees and market capitalization reported at roughly €140m (single screener, July 2026, unverified). Source: https://morningstar.com.au/investments/security/lse/mcon
thesis.main_shareholders: We did not find official Companies Act substantial-shareholding disclosures or the Purcell founding family's current percentage stake in this search. Per Fidelity's factsheet (2026 data): the largest disclosed institutional holders are Fidelity Management & Research Company LLC (20,296,841 shares), Fidelity Series International Small Cap (10,500,000 shares), Fidelity International Small Cap Opportunities Fund (7,588,943 shares), Dowgate Wealth Ltd (3,590,580 shares) and Onward Opportunities Limited (3,590,580 shares); none of these lists included a Purcell-family holding, though a top-5 institutional list would not necessarily capture smaller insider stakes. CEO Joe (Joseph Michael) Purcell, executive director/COO Thomas Purcell, and non-executive director Patrick Purcell are all named directors, but their individual shareholdings were not found in this search. Source: https://www.fidelity.co.uk/factsheet-data/factsheet/IE00BD64C665-mincon-group-plc/profile . Not confirmed from an official filing — recommend checking Mincon's Annual Report (Directors' Interests note) or Euronext Dublin/London Stock Exchange RNS 'Holding(s) in Company' notices for the Purcell family's current stake and any other substantial holders.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; however, this search could not establish the founding Purcell family's current ownership percentage, which is a material gap for a company with three family members on the board (CEO, COO and a non-executive director) — this related-party/family-governance structure should be reviewed via the company's own Annual Report before forming a view on alignment between family control and minority shareholders.

thesis.business_description: On the Beach Group plc, founded in 2004 by Simon Cooper and headquartered in Manchester, UK, is an online travel agent selling dynamically packaged ATOL-protected 'flight and hotel' holidays (primarily beach destinations, now expanded to long-haul and city breaks) direct to UK consumers mainly via onthebeach.co.uk and sunshine.co.uk, with ancillary self-contracted hotel-bed inventory (On the Beach Beds) and airport transfers (On the Beach Transfers). Source: https://pro.stockalarm.io/quote/OOBHF/intelligence ; https://www.morningstar.com.au/investments/security/LSE/OTB/summary
thesis.competitive_position: UK-focused online travel agent (~550-580 employees) differentiated by a direct-to-consumer, dynamically-packaged model with reported high gross margins (~89.5% per a third-party aggregator); entered a 2024 flight-supply partnership with Ryanair and is winding down its lower-margin Classic Collection B2B business, reporting record results for FY ended 30 September 2025. Listed on the London Stock Exchange. Source: https://pro.stockalarm.io/quote/OOBHF/intelligence
thesis.main_shareholders: Founder Simon Cooper remains a significant shareholder, though his stake has declined over time: at the 2015 IPO he and management held ~21.7%; by 2022 his holding (via Hawksford Trustees Jersey Limited plus a small personally-held portion) stood at ~5.64% (just under 9.4m shares); and per a December 2024 RNS disclosure, after selling 3 million shares at 228p, he held 9,521,226 shares = 5.7% of issued capital (about 1.25% in his own name, the rest via the Hawksford trust), with Cooper stating he remained 'a significant and long term shareholder.' Source: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/on-the-beach-group--otb/director-pdmr-shareholding/7410910 ; https://www.travolution.com/news/people/outgoing-on-the-beach-founder-shows-confidence-in-ota-by-upping-stake/. Cooper stepped down as CEO at end of June (year unconfirmed) and now serves as a non-executive founder director. Institutional holders per a Simply Wall St snapshot include Artemis Investment Management (~11.3%), Schroder Investment Management (~11%), and DNCA Finance (~7.0%); a separate, apparently more recent MarketScreener listing instead shows Artemis ~11.26%, Schroders ~10.95%, DNCA Finance ~6.2%, and does not list Cooper at all. Source: https://uk.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ON-THE-BEACH-GROUP-PLC-23894458/company-shareholders/. The company's own December 2025 'substantial shareholdings' notice exists but its contents were not retrievable in this search — this should be checked directly for the current, authoritative figures.
thesis.red_flags: Founder Simon Cooper's declining stake (from ~21.7% at IPO to ~5.7% by December 2024) alongside his transition from CEO to non-executive director reduces founder alignment over time, though all sales were disclosed via RNS and he stated he remains a long-term shareholder — a transparency-compliant trend rather than a hidden issue. Source: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/on-the-beach-group--otb/director-pdmr-shareholding/7410910. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Pandora Investments Public Limited is a Cyprus-based company, part of the Leptos Group of Companies, primarily engaged in property development and trading, and in investing in securities of listed companies, with subsidiaries active in land investment, real estate development, and tourism. [Pandora Investments company profile](https://www.dnb.com/business-directory/company-profiles.pandora_investments_public_limited.77fe7da635e720b019cbce04d7dd8bdd.html)
thesis.competitive_position: Pandora Investments operates as a listed property/investment arm of the larger, privately-held Leptos Group, one of Cyprus's major real-estate and tourism developers; its competitive position largely derives from the broader Leptos Group's scale in Cyprus property development rather than independent market leadership. [Leptos Estates - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leptos_Estates)
thesis.main_shareholders: As of 2023 data, major shareholders were Pantelis Leptos (Board Member, ~37.50%) and Giorgos Leptos (Chairman, ~37.49%), with the remaining ~24.05% held by the general public. [CBN: major shareholders of 35 listed companies in Cyprus](https://www.cbn.com.cy/article/113087/the-major-shareholders-of-35-listed-companies-in-cyprus)
thesis.insider_ownership: Ownership is very highly concentrated in the founding Leptos family: Giorgos and Pantelis Leptos together hold roughly 75% of the company, with Michalakis G. Leptos chairing the broader board. [CBN major shareholders listing](https://www.cbn.com.cy/article/113087/the-major-shareholders-of-35-listed-companies-in-cyprus)
thesis.red_flags: The broader Leptos Group (Pandora's parent group) has faced significant reputational scrutiny: a 2020 Al Jazeera undercover investigation implicated Leptos Estates in Cyprus's 'golden passport' (citizenship-by-investment) scheme facilitation, and separate reporting has raised concerns about layered Cypriot entity ownership potentially used by politically exposed persons (including Russian buyers) in real estate tied to the golden-visa program; Leptos Estates also withdrew a libel suit against property-news outlets in 2010 after allegations of buyer mistreatment. These are serious, named reputational/regulatory red flags associated with the controlling family and group. [AML Network: Leptos Estates](https://amlnetwork.org/watchdog-database/real-estate-laundering/leptos-estates/)

thesis.business_description: Bulten AB, founded in 1873 and headquartered in Gothenburg, Sweden, develops, manufactures and sells fasteners (screws, nuts, clips, rivets) primarily for the European automotive industry, supplying major OEMs (Volvo, BMW, Audi) under a 'Full Service Provider' model that bundles concept development, prototyping, engineering, vendor-managed inventory and logistics, with manufacturing in Sweden, Germany, Poland, the UK, China and the USA. Source: https://bulten.com/en/About%20Bulten ; https://www.roic.ai/quote/0P49.L/classic
thesis.competitive_position: Specialist automotive fastener/C-parts supplier with ~1,700-1,900+ employees depending on source/year; recent commentary describes a strategic shift toward niche manufacturing and C-parts distribution and away from traditional contract manufacturing, alongside a sales setback tied to a 2025 cyberattack on a key customer. Source: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/bulten-aterhamtningen-tar-skruv
thesis.main_shareholders: Bulten's largest shareholder is AB Axel Granlund, held through Volito AB, whose CEO Ulf Liljedahl chairs Bulten's board; a March 2026 Affärsvärlden analysis puts this stake at approximately 25% of shares/votes, consistent with Bulten's 2020 annual report figure of Volito AB at 23.8% (up from 22.8% the prior year). Source: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/bulten-aterhamtningen-tar-skruv ; https://mb.cision.com/Main/405/2371241/738730.pdf. Other reported holders (undated Affärsvärlden stock-page snapshot) include Nordea Investment Funds at 6.0%, Avanza Pension at 5.0% and Bengt Stillström at 3.0%; the 2020 annual report instead showed Lannebo Fonder at 7.8% and Nordea Investment Funds at 7.2% as the next-largest holders after Volito. Source: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/bulten.
thesis.red_flags: Board chairman Ulf Liljedahl is also CEO of Volito AB, the vehicle for the controlling shareholder (AB Axel Granlund, ~25%) — a related-party governance structure that is disclosed rather than hidden but merits awareness given the overlap between controlling-shareholder management and board leadership. Source: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/bulten-aterhamtningen-tar-skruv. A 2025 cyberattack on a major customer disrupted sales, an operational/counterparty risk rather than a company-specific governance issue. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: AS Amber Latvijas balzams is a Riga-based maker of alcoholic drinks, listed on Nasdaq Riga. It runs two factories in Riga, one for strong spirits and one for sparkling wines and light drinks, and produces more than 1,000 SKUs a year. Its brands include Riga Black Balsam, and it has produced Stolichnaya vodka for the Stoli group. The parent group says more than 70% of output is exported, and the company also does private-label and contract production. Sources: https://amberbev.com/amber_production/amber-latvijas-balzams/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvijas_Balzams
thesis.competitive_position: Its parent group calls it the largest alcoholic-beverage producer in the Baltics, with about 22% of the local market (parent-group marketing figure, undated). Its strength rests on heritage brands like Riga Black Balsam and its scale as a contract bottler. However, it relies heavily on related-party Stoli volumes. Revenue fell 4.8% to EUR 74.5m in 2025 and net profit fell 39% to EUR 2.5m. In H1 2026 revenue fell 30.4% to EUR 24.6m and volumes fell 38.2%, leaving a net loss of EUR 0.95m. The company blamed Stoli Group decisions on the brand and its supply chain, and Russia's confiscation of the group's Talvis distillery. Sources: https://amberbev.com/amber_production/amber-latvijas-balzams/ ; https://www.just-drinks.com/newsletters/amber-latvijas-balzams-in-red-amid-volume-slide ; https://nasdaqbaltic.com/market/upload/reports/bal/2026_q1_en.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: Amber Beverage Group Holding S.a r.l. (Luxembourg, part of the SPI group) holds 89.99% (6,746,460 shares) and has been the controlling shareholder since 7 May 2018, per the 2020 and 2023 annual reports and the 2024 interim reports. The remaining ~10% is free float, and this search did not identify who holds it. Amber Beverage Group itself entered judicial reorganisation in April 2026 after defaulting on its bonds. Control of the stake could therefore change, so check the latest Nasdaq Riga filing. Sources: https://nasdaqbaltic.com/market/upload/reports/bal/2023_ar_en_eur_00_ias.pdf ; https://www.baltictimes.com/latvijas_balzams_distillery_gets_new_owner_as_spi_group_reshuffles_its_holdings ; https://www.just-drinks.com/newsletters/amber-latvijas-balzams-in-red-amid-volume-slide
thesis.red_flags: SEVERE. (1) A Riga court approved legal protection (restructuring) proceedings in early 2026 after a filing around 30 January 2026, and the deadline for the restructuring plan was extended to 5 October 2026. (2) Reports say it owes more than EUR 28m in tax to the Latvian state. (3) According to ERR, the annual report shows tens of millions of euros lent to group/affiliated companies, and the auditor flagged that some may not be fully recoverable. (4) The controlling parent, Amber Beverage Group, defaulted on its bonds and is itself in judicial reorganisation. Stoli Group, a key customer, was reported liquidated in January 2026. (5) Volumes are collapsing and the minority free float is thin, about 10%. Equity value is highly uncertain. Sources: https://drinks-intel.com/spirits/amber-beverage-groups-latvijas-balzams-applies-for-legal-protection/ ; https://eng.lsm.lv/article/economy/business/20.05.2026-latvijas-balzams-still-in-major-financial-difficulty.a647930/ ; https://www.err.ee/1609942850/riia-palsami-tootja-on-pankroti-aarel ; https://www.just-drinks.com/newsletters/amber-latvijas-balzams-in-red-amid-volume-slide
thesis.website: https://amberbev.com/amber_production/amber-latvijas-balzams/ (parent-group company page; this search did not confirm a separate standalone company domain). Source: https://amberbev.com/amber_production/amber-latvijas-balzams/
thesis.insider_ownership: Could not locate current shareholdings of management or supervisory board members in this search; treat as a research gap. With the parent holding 89.99%, direct insider stakes are likely immaterial, but this is unverified. The only insider dealing found was a 2005 notice and is not relevant today. Source: https://nasdaqbaltic.com/statistics/en/news/archive/184736

thesis.business_description: Judges Scientific plc, headquartered in London and listed on AIM, is an acquisitive holding group of roughly 25 scientific-instrument businesses (including Oxford Cryosystems, Scientifica, Quorum Technologies and Deben UK) making instruments for materials science, vacuum technology, geoscience, calorimetry and related fields, sold mainly to higher-education, scientific-research, manufacturing and regulatory customers across the UK, Europe, North America and China. Source: https://hl.co.uk/shares/shares-search-results/j/judges-scientific-plc-ord-gbp0.05/company-information ; https://quartr.com/companies/judges-scientific-plc_12470
thesis.competitive_position: Buy-and-build strategy combining organic growth within subsidiaries with acquisitions of established niche scientific-instrument makers; diversified across Materials Sciences and Vacuum segments with a broad geographic footprint, giving resilience versus single-product competitors, though reliant on continued M&A execution for growth. Source: https://hl.co.uk/shares/shares-search-results/j/judges-scientific-plc-ord-gbp0.05/company-information
thesis.main_shareholders: Per ownership-tracker data referencing 2025 disclosures (cross-checked against company director-dealing RNS announcements): founder/CEO David Cicurel is the largest named individual holder, with his stake reported variously at ~8.2% (544,363 shares per a Share Incentive Plan purchase disclosed 6 May 2025) to ~9.2% (~611,000 shares) depending on how plan-held shares are counted — down from 15.10% in a 2015 company announcement and 10.47% after a 2021 sale of 50,000 shares, with further disposals in 2024 (60,000 shares sold September 2024, ~£6m). Institutional holders include ODIN Forvaltning AS (~8.77%), Puma Investment Management (~5.15% on AIM-listed figures), Capital Research and Management (~2.6-4.9%, sources disagree), Canaccord Genuity Wealth and Liontrust (~3.6-4.2% each); institutions collectively hold roughly 59-61% of shares. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/capital-goods/aim-jdg/judges-scientific-shares/ownership ; https://fidelity.co.uk/factsheet-data/factsheet/GB0032398678-judges-scientific/profile (director dealing disclosure, 6 May 2025)
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; founder David Cicurel's declining stake (from ~15% in 2015 to ~8-9% currently) reflects a long-run, disclosed pattern of partial insider selling as the company has grown via acquisition, which is a normal founder-dilution pattern rather than a governance concern. No litigation or going-concern issues were found.

thesis.business_description: MS INTERNATIONAL plc is a Doncaster-based engineering group listed on AIM. It has historically reported four divisions: Defence and Security (MSI-Defence Systems, which makes naval medium-calibre gun mounts such as the 30mm DS30M/Mk38 Mod 4 and related systems), Forgings (fork-arms), Petrol Station Superstructures, and Corporate Branding. Petrol and Branding have since been merged. For the year to April 2025 revenue was GBP 117.5m and pre-tax profit a record GBP 20.1m. A third-party summary of the FY to April 2026 results (published 16 July 2026) gives revenue of GBP 115.0m, pre-tax profit of GBP 15.1m and cash of GBP 46.5m; this has not been checked against the RNS. Sources: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/earnings-ms-international-hails-record-profit-dekel-loss-narrows ; https://quartr.com/events/ms-international-plc-msi-h2-2026_FTT3GRqV ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/30mm_DS30M_Mark_2_Automated_Small_Calibre_Gun
thesis.competitive_position: MSI-DS is an established niche supplier of lightweight automated naval gun mounts. It supplies the Royal Navy, including 26 ASCG systems for Type 23 frigates, and over 40 other navies, according to the UK Department for Business and Trade. Its US subsidiary supplies the Mk38 Mod 4 30mm mounts to the US Navy and holds a sole-source support contract with a USD 49.8m ceiling running to June 2028. After a two-year review (January 2026 interim report), the group decided to focus on Defence and Security and to sell the non-core Forgings and Petrol/Branding businesses. Market testing found interest mainly from financial buyers, and this search found no completed sale. The search did not identify named competitors. Sources: https://great.gov.uk/international/trade/suppliers/00954839/msi-defence-systems-ltd ; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/ms-international--msi/supply-of-msi-ds-30mm-gun-mounts-to-us-navy/7786226 ; https://www.stockopedia.com/share-prices/ms-international-LON:MSI/news/half-year-report-019e6a04-0d71-7bab-8de1-b803e1f1bfd6/
thesis.main_shareholders: The register is concentrated among directors and long-standing holders. Michael Bell (long-time Executive Chairman, now Life President) had a beneficial interest of 2,995,889 shares, about 18.26% excluding treasury shares, per an October 2025 RNS. Michael O'Connell held 1,069,966 shares (about 6.52%) per a February 2026 RNS, plus 163,263 shares (about 0.99%) held by closely associated person Jamal O'Connell. Aggregators list David Pyle at about 10.8%, but this is unconfirmed by an official filing. Simply Wall St shows Bell at 34.4%, which conflicts with the RNS figures and should not be relied on. Total voting rights were 16,435,889 at 29 April 2026. The annual report's substantial-shareholder table was not located. Sources: https://www.sharesmagazine.co.uk/news/market/LSE20251002124909_5846115/directorpdmr-shareholding-and-total-voting-rights ; https://data.fca.org.uk/artefacts/NSM/RNS/b7cc430d-c113-4aec-8fa2-c9dd0b2cfbe5.html ; https://www.ticker.app/lse/MSI/rns/2026-04-29/Exercise-of-Options-and-TVR/4535C ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/capital-goods/aim-msi/ms-international-shares/ownership
thesis.red_flags: (1) Profits depend on large, lumpy defence contracts. FY2026 pre-tax profit fell about 25% (third-party summary), and management cited delays in placing defence orders and a slightly lower order book. (2) The business relies on a few government customers (Royal Navy and US Navy). (3) The disposal of non-core divisions is uncertain in timing and value. (4) Leadership changed in July 2026: Bell left the board, Anthony Wreford became independent Non-Executive Chairman and O'Connell became Group CEO. (5) Liquidity is low on AIM and the register is concentrated. No accounting or litigation issues were identified from official sources. Sources: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/ms-international-raises-dividend-relatively-flat-first-half ; https://quartr.com/events/ms-international-plc-msi-h2-2026_FTT3GRqV ; https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/directorate-changes-wewz36kq1vb7j86.html
thesis.website: https://www.msiplc.com (domain not directly confirmed in this search; verify). Source: https://www.fidelity.co.uk/factsheet-data/factsheet/GB0005957005-ms-international/profile
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is high. Michael Bell held about 18.26% (October 2025 RNS). He stepped down from the board on 16 July 2026 to become Life President, so he is no longer a director but remains a major holder. Group CEO Michael O'Connell held about 6.52% (February 2026 RNS), or about 7.5% including his associate's 0.99%. Roger Lane-Smith (current board status not re-verified in this search) appears in aggregator data at about 0.6-0.7% (aggregator only). Together, current and former directors hold roughly a quarter or more of the shares, though no consolidated official figure was found. Sources: https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/directorate-changes-wewz36kq1vb7j86.html ; https://data.fca.org.uk/artefacts/NSM/RNS/b7cc430d-c113-4aec-8fa2-c9dd0b2cfbe5.html ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/capital-goods/aim-msi/ms-international-shares/ownership

thesis.business_description: IRCE S.p.A. (Industria Romagnola Conduttori Elettrici), founded in 1947 and headquartered in Imola, Italy, manufactures enamelled copper/aluminum winding wires (for electric motors, generators, transformers, relays, solenoids, compressors, inductors) and low/medium-voltage building, industrial, data (LAN) and power cables, operating five manufacturing plants (Imola, Guglionesi, Umbertide, Miradolo Terme in Italy, plus the Netherlands and UK) with additional production in Brazil, India and Germany. Source: https://it.finance.yahoo.com/q/pr?s=IRC.MI ; https://www.expometals.net/en/hall/finished-products/electrical-wires-and-optical-fibers/stand-free/irce-spa
thesis.competitive_position: Established Italian electrical-wire/cable manufacturer with significant export exposure (nearly half of enamelled wire sales outside Italy, mainly in the EU) and distribution networks in Germany, Spain and Switzerland; ~600-740 employees depending on source/year. Listed on Borsa Italiana (MTA). Source: https://it.finance.yahoo.com/q/pr?s=IRC.MI
thesis.main_shareholders: IRCE is majority-controlled by Aequafin S.p.A., a pure holding company whose only significant asset is its controlling stake in IRCE. Per IRCE's own corporate-governance report (as filed with CONSOB, reference date 24/04/2009 reaffirmed in subsequent governance reports), Aequafin S.p.A. holds 50.004% of share capital and voting rights. Source: https://www.consob.it/web/area-pubblica/w/irce-spa-industria-romagnola-conduttori-elettrici-azionariato-2019-06-30. This was reconfirmed as recently as a 30 April 2026 company announcement describing Aequafin as the majority shareholder (noting only Aequafin's list was filed for the 2026-2028 Board of Statutory Auditors election). Source: https://www.emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2026-04/20260430_183230.pdf. A separate Investing.com data page cites a higher, seemingly outdated/differently-calculated figure of 53.24% (14,065,125 shares) for Aequafin, which is inconsistent with the official CONSOB-filed 50.004%; the CONSOB figure should be treated as authoritative. A 2018 governance report also names Anna Maria Mongardi as a minor significant shareholder at 4.828% (dated, not independently reconfirmed here).
thesis.red_flags: Majority control sits with a single-purpose holding company (Aequafin S.p.A., just above the 50% control threshold), a disclosed and stable structure rather than a governance red flag, though it does mean minority shareholders cannot outvote the controlling holder even collectively. Source: https://www.consob.it/web/area-pubblica/w/irce-spa-industria-romagnola-conduttori-elettrici-azionariato-2019-06-30. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Equita Group S.p.A. is a Milan-based independent investment bank, listed on Euronext Milan. Its main operating company is Equita SIM, which is authorised by Consob and since July 2025 can also offer services in Switzerland. It has three areas: Global Markets (equity and fixed-income brokerage, trading and research for institutional clients), Investment Banking (M&A advisory and debt and equity capital markets, focused on Italian mid-caps), and Alternative Asset Management (private debt and other alternative funds). FY2025 consolidated net revenues rose 41% to EUR 111.7m and net profit rose 73% to EUR 24.3m. Sources: https://www.equita.eu/en/investor-relations/press-release/FY-2025-and-strategic-partner.html ; https://www.equita.eu/static/upload/202/0001/2025_equita-group---informativa-al-pubblico-iii-pilastro-2025---def.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: Equita calls itself Italy's leading independent investment bank. Its niche is research coverage and advisory for Italian small and mid-caps, without the conflicts a commercial-bank parent would bring. FY2025 was its best year since the IPO: client revenues rose 35% to EUR 96.7m, and alternative asset management revenues rose 29% to EUR 11.2m, helped by performance fees. In March 2026 it agreed a strategic partnership with Gruppo BCC Iccrea to serve Iccrea's network of SME clients, with Iccrea taking about 15% of the capital. This search did not find independent market-share rankings against other Italian brokers and advisers. Sources: https://www.equita.eu/en/investor-relations/press-release/FY-2025-and-strategic-partner.html ; https://alternativecreditinvestor.com/2026/03/13/equita-grows-revenues-in-alternatives-business-to-e11m/ ; https://www.aziendabanca.it/notizie/banche/iccrea-entra-in-equita
thesis.main_shareholders: Management and professionals are the largest block. Equita's shareholder page (updated July 2026, before the Iccrea deal closed) showed them with about 41% of capital and 51% of votes; loyalty shares carry double votes. Fenera Holding held 2.0m shares, about 3.8% of capital and about 5.8-6.0% of votes. The two July 2026 company documents round these slightly differently. In September 2026 Iccrea Banca completed its entry with about 15% of capital, about 12% of votes per press reports. It subscribed about 3.4m new shares for about EUR 20m and bought 5.1m shares from some manager-shareholders, with a 3-year lock-up. Management should therefore now hold less than 41%, and an updated post-closing table was not found. Treasury shares were about 1.5m (about 3%) as of October 2025. Sources: https://www.equita.eu/en/corporate-governance/share-capital-and-shareholders.html ; https://www.equita.eu/static/upload/lis/list-increased-voting-rights--06072026-.pdf ; https://en.ilsole24ore.com/radiocor/nRC_21.09.2026_16.16_43010430 ; https://financecommunity.it/perfezionata-la-partnership-tra-equita-e-iccrea-banca/
thesis.red_flags: No Consob or Bank of Italy sanction against Equita was found in this search; press coverage (July 2026) of Consob's 2025 enforcement report did not name it. Structural risks: (1) revenues are cyclical and depend on Italian equity-market volumes and M&A/ECM activity, and 2025 included performance fees that may not recur; (2) double voting rights let management's voting power exceed its economic stake; (3) the Iccrea entry diluted existing holders and partly cashed out managers, and the commercial benefits are not yet proven. An old press report on a Guardia di Finanza/Consob visit during the 2016 RCS bid had no reported outcome. Otherwise none identified from official sources; standard caveat: this is not an exhaustive legal review. Sources: https://www.teleborsa.it/AMP/News/2026/07/13/consob-sanzioni-dimezzate-a-5-8-milioni-di-euro-nel-2025-77.html ; https://www.finanzaonline.com/?p=199439 ; https://www.equita.eu/en/corporate-governance/share-capital-and-shareholders.html
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is high. Before the Iccrea deal, managers and professionals held about 41% of capital (51% of votes), partly bound by a shareholders' agreement. The pact signed in 2022 expired on 31 March 2025, covering about 35.1% of capital and 46.0% of votes at expiry, and a new pact took effect on 1 April 2025. In March 2026, Chairman Andrea Vismara and Vice-Chairman Matteo Ghilotti together held about 7.0%. An October 2025 company page showed Vismara with 2,101,734 shares (4.0% of capital, 5.9% of votes); he no longer appears in the July 2026 list of holders above the threshold. The percentage held by the current pact and the effect of the September 2026 share sale to Iccrea on named managers were not located. Sources: https://www.equita.eu/en/corporate-governance/shareholders-agreement.html ; https://www.emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2026-03/20260309_178437.pdf ; https://emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2025-04/20250401_164036.pdf

thesis.business_description: Victrex plc is a UK-based manufacturer of high-performance polymers, primarily PEEK (polyetheretherketone) and related PAEK-based materials, serving aerospace, automotive, energy, electronics and healthcare (via its Invibio medical subsidiary) end markets.
thesis.competitive_position: Victrex owns a substantial share of global PEEK manufacturing capacity, making it a global leader in this high-performance polymer niche; it originated from a 1995 management buyout of ICI's PEEK business and listed on the London Stock Exchange, and remains widely held with a free float of roughly 99% and no controlling shareholder. [Interactive Investor - Victrex analysis](https://ii.co.uk/analysis-commentary/victrex-why-uk-star-stock-worth-owning-ii510162)
thesis.main_shareholders: No controlling shareholder; largest institutional holders per aggregator data (undated) are Threadneedle Asset Management (~11.67%), FIL Investment Advisors/Fidelity (~9.76%) and Norges Bank Investment Management (~9.18%), with further holdings above 3% from Jupiter, Schroder, Brown Capital, M&G, Janus Henderson, Royal London and Vanguard ([MarketScreener shareholder table](https://in.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/VICTREX-PLC-9590145/company-shareholders/)).
thesis.insider_ownership: No significant named founder/management insider stake was identified; ownership is essentially fully institutional/public float (~99.14% free float per MarketScreener data), consistent with its origin as a management buyout that subsequently listed and diluted founding management's stake over three decades. [MarketScreener](https://in.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/VICTREX-PLC-9590145/company-shareholders/)
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Zotefoams plc, founded in 1921 (as Onazote Limited) and headquartered near Croydon, UK (listed on LSE since 1995 following a 1992 demerger from BP), is the world's largest manufacturer of lightweight crosslinked polyolefin block foams (AZOTE brand), also selling/licensing high-performance products (ZOTEK, T-FIT) and microcellular materials technology (MuCell, via MuCell Extrusion LLC), serving automotive, aerospace, packaging, marine, construction, military, medical and sports/leisure markets. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zotefoams
thesis.competitive_position: Global leader in its core crosslinked polyolefin foam niche, reporting across three segments (Polyolefin Foams, High-Performance Products, MuCell Extrusion LLC) with manufacturing in Croydon (UK) and Kentucky (US), a conversion site in Jiangsu, China (T-FIT insulation) and an Asia sales joint venture in Hong Kong; FY2025 revenue reported at £158.5m with operating income of £21.6m. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zotefoams
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Zotefoams' own regulatory 'Holding(s) in Company' RNS disclosures (official DTR5 filings, via Investegate/ticker.app): Schroders Plc, through Schroders Investment Management Limited, has been the largest disclosed holder, with its voting-rights stake at 16.085911% (prior), decreasing to 15.994532% (notified 13 December 2024, following a transaction on 12 December 2024, representing 7,812,727 votes), and further decreasing to 14.979326% (notified 27 January 2025, following a threshold crossing on 24 January 2025, representing 7,316,837 votes). Other third-party (non-RNS) aggregator figures — not independently confirmed as current official filings — cite Tyndall Investment Management at roughly 9.9-10.3% and Business Growth Fund/1st Port Asset Management at roughly 6.6-10.9%, with top-5 holders together estimated around 51.8% (StocksGuide) or top-25 at 87.1% (Simply Wall St), though these two aggregators disagree materially with each other and should be verified against the company's own 2024/2025 Annual Report shareholder table or further RNS 'Holding(s) in Company' notices. Source: https://www.ticker.app/lse/ZTF/rns/2025-01-27/holdings-in-company/8133U ; https://www.ticker.app/lse/ZTF/rns/2024-12-13/holdings-in-company/0998Q
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; Schroders' declining but still-large stake (~16% to ~15%) reflects routine institutional portfolio adjustment disclosed via standard DTR5 filings, not a governance concern. Third-party aggregator shareholder percentages for other holders (Tyndall, Business Growth Fund/1st Port) conflict materially between sources and were not independently verified against an official RNS filing in this search, so should be treated as approximate pending confirmation.

thesis.business_description: Eurotel S.A., headquartered in Gdańsk, Poland (founded 1996), operates a retail and dealer network selling electronics and telecommunications services, including an authorized Apple reseller business (11 iDream-branded Apple Premium Reseller stores plus 5 hardware repair centers) and historically as an authorized sales partner for mobile operators T-Mobile and Play (via subsidiary Viamind) and satellite TV platform nc+/ITI Neovision. Source: https://www.sii.org.pl/5462/aktualnosci/czat-inwestorski/czat-inwestorski-ze-spolka-eurotel-s-a-22-marca-2012r.html ; https://emis.cn/php/company-profile/PL/Eurotel_SA_en_2112786.html
thesis.competitive_position: Established Polish retail/distribution operator (~430-517 employees depending on source) with diversified revenue across Apple retail, mobile-operator dealer commissions and pay-TV distribution; listed on the main Warsaw Stock Exchange market since 2006 and known as a consistent dividend payer, including a record-high dividend of PLN 1.9/share (yield ~8.6%) per one Polish investor-relations news item. Source: https://www.sii.org.pl/11516/analizy/newsroom/eurotel-rekomenduje-rekordowa-dywidende-1-9-zl-dy-8-6.html ; https://www.sii.org.pl/11877/analizy/analizy-i-komentarze/eurotel-zwieksza-zyski-i-liczy-na-poprawe-w-drugiej-polowie-roku.html
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Bankier.pl's shareholder table (most recent entry dated 27 March 2017, so likely outdated), B&K Stepokura Fundacja Rodzinna (a family foundation) held 1,131,182 shares = 30.17%, Jacek Foltarz held 707,399 shares = 18.87%, and Eurotel SA itself held 590,180 shares = 15.74% (treasury stock), with free float at 50.95%. Source: https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/akcje/EUROTEL/akcjonariat. Krzysztof Stepokura signed the company's 2017 shareholder letter as Chairman, consistent with the Stepokura family foundation being the controlling/founding shareholder. Source: https://money2.wpcdn.pl/gielda/gpw/raporty/2017/03/20170327_234800_0563258756_List_Prezesa.pdf. The company reduced share capital via cancellation of Series B shares per a 2026-dated filing, which would change the share count/percentages above; we could not obtain an updated post-cancellation shareholder breakdown in this search. This should be checked against Eurotel's current ESPI/EBI shareholder notifications.
thesis.red_flags: The 2017-dated shareholder data (30.17% Stepokura family foundation, 18.87% Foltarz) is the most specific figure found but is now stale, and a subsequent share-capital reduction (cancellation of Series B shares, per a 2026 filing) means current percentages are likely materially different — this data-currency gap should be resolved before relying on these figures. Source: https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/akcje/EUROTEL/akcjonariat ; https://biznes.pap.pl/download/attachment/52352371/DOC.20250903.52352371.20250903_0954_ETL_PL_RI.pdf. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Promotica S.p.A. is an Italian loyalty and promotional-marketing company listed on Euronext Growth Milan since 27 November 2020, based in Desenzano del Garda. It designs and runs loyalty campaigns for large retail chains, mainly Italian grocery retailers such as Coop and Esselunga, and sources and supplies the reward goods. It also earns smaller consulting and services revenues and is growing abroad. In 2025 revenue was EUR 137.4m (up about 43%), with merchandise sales of about EUR 131m and services of about EUR 6.4m. EBITDA was EUR 10.3m and net profit about EUR 3.85m, across 199 campaigns for 106 active clients, 14 of them international. Sources: https://www.soldionline.it/?p=156381 ; https://en.ilsole24ore.com/art/egm-raggi-x-promotica-reports-a-sharp-rise-in-profit-margins-AJcq1j ; https://euroborsa.it/public/euroborsa/Comunicati_Stampa/Promotica/Promotica_6_agosto_2026.pdf
