thesis.competitive_position: Promotica calls itself one of Italy's leading loyalty-campaign companies, and its relationships with the main Italian grocery chains (Coop, Esselunga) are its core asset. Its main lever is sourcing: in H1 2026 it used 120 suppliers, 11 of them under exclusive contracts. Growth comes from international clients and acquisitions; it bought 80% of Grani & Partners from Giochi Preziosi in 2022. In H1 2026 revenue fell to EUR 61.7m from EUR 68.2m (preliminary, unaudited), with 79 clients, while foreign revenue rose to EUR 9.1m from about EUR 6.6m. Net profit rose to EUR 3.45m on lower operating costs. This search did not identify named competitors or market-share data. Sources: https://www.teleborsa.it/News/2026/08/06/promotica-fatturato-primo-semestre-cala-a-61-7-milioni-di-euro-in-crescita-l-estero-231.html ; https://distribuzionemoderna.info/en/businesses/promotica-revenue-slightly-down-in-the-first-half-2026-but-strongly-up-abroad ; https://www.finanzaonline.com/notizie/giochi-preziosi-entra-nel-capitale-di-promotica-acquisira-500000-azioni-ordinarie-da-dieci-sette-srl-per-eur15-milioni
thesis.main_shareholders: The company is controlled by its founder. Dieci.Sette S.r.l., wholly controlled by Diego Toscani, held 77.13% after buying back 533,000 shares from Giochi Preziosi in August 2024. A later Pozzi Milano related-party notice (29 June, apparently 2026) gives Toscani an indirect 77.54%. In January 2022 the stake was 84.63% before 500,000 shares went to Giochi Preziosi. The same Pozzi notice lists Guglielmo Di Silvio with 6.03%. Treasury shares were 42,000 (0.25%) as of September 2024. Aggregators conflict (Simply Wall St about 74.6%, TipRanks about 77.4%); prefer the company filings. Sources: https://borsaitaliana.it/borsa/notizie/price-sensitive/download/20198_145598_2024_oneinfo.html ; https://italia-informa.com/public/italiainforma/ComunicatiStampa/Pozzi_Milano/POZZI_29_GIUGNO_26.pdf ; https://italia-informa.com/public/italiainforma/ComunicatiStampa/Promotica/opo20198_106882_2022_oneinfo.pdf
thesis.red_flags: (1) Related-party supply: Promotica renewed a reward-goods supply contract with related party Pozzi Milano for 30 June 2026 to 30 June 2027, capped at EUR 4m plus VAT (EUR 3m a year in 2023). The board also approved a framework supply contract with another related party, IVV Italia S.r.l. The nature of the link with Toscani was not verified in this search. (2) The founder holds about 77%, leaving a small free float, limited minority protection and low liquidity on Euronext Growth Milan. (3) Revenue depends on a small number of large Italian grocery chains, and the share of the top clients was not found. (4) H1 2026 revenue fell about 9.5% on higher procurement costs and weaker consumer spending, and net debt rose to EUR 10.96m from EUR 8.65m because of working capital. (5) Margins are thin for a business mostly trading merchandise (2025 EBITDA margin about 7.5%, our calculation). No accounting or litigation issues were identified from official sources. Sources: https://euroborsa.it/public/euroborsa/Comunicati_Stampa/Promotica/Promotica_6_agosto_2026.pdf ; https://italia-informa.com/public/italiainforma/ComunicatiStampa/Pozzi_Milano/POZZI_29_GIUGNO_26.pdf ; https://www.teleborsa.it/News/2026/08/06/promotica-fatturato-primo-semestre-cala-a-61-7-milioni-di-euro-in-crescita-l-estero-231.html
thesis.website: https://www.promotica.it (referenced in company releases; IR page not directly retrieved). Source: https://euroborsa.it/public/euroborsa/Comunicati_Stampa/Promotica/Promotica_6_agosto_2026.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: Diego Toscani, founder, Chairman and CEO, holds about 77.1-77.5% indirectly through Dieci.Sette S.r.l. (2024 company filing; later figure from the Pozzi Milano notice). Holdings of other board members were not located; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://borsaitaliana.it/borsa/notizie/price-sensitive/download/20198_145598_2024_oneinfo.html ; https://italia-informa.com/public/italiainforma/ComunicatiStampa/Pozzi_Milano/POZZI_29_GIUGNO_26.pdf

thesis.business_description: Tire Company Dębica S.A. (Firma Oponiarska Dębica S.A.), founded in 1937 and headquartered in Dębica, Poland, manufactures car, van and truck tires under its own Dębica brand and other Goodyear-group brands (Goodyear, Dunlop, Fulda, Sava), supplying original equipment to major carmakers and exporting to Luxembourg, Germany, Turkey, the US, Canada and France; it also makes tire-curing membranes. Source: https://debica.com.pl/s/key_information ; https://www.auto-swiat.pl/debica-najwieksza-fabryka-goodyeara-w-europie/r02whx1
thesis.competitive_position: Goodyear's largest tire-manufacturing facility in Europe, with ~2,900-3,100 employees and FY2025 revenue of PLN 2.91bn (up 15.72% year-on-year); the plant suffered a fire in 2023 that cut capacity to ~70% (an estimated $40m sales impact) with full capacity not restored until Q4 2024, but has since recovered. Listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (DBC) and Frankfurt (FD8). Source: https://www.debica.com.pl/o_firmie/aktualnosci/debica_celebrates_its_75th_birthday ; https://european-rubber-journal.com/article/2094245/goodyear-expects-40m-sales-drop-after-fire-at-polish-tire-plant
thesis.main_shareholders: Dębica is majority-controlled by The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company. Per the company's own 2024 current reports, Goodyear S.A. is the (now direct, following a September 2024 intra-group share transfer from Goodyear Holdings S.à r.l. in Luxembourg) parent holding 87.251% of the company's shares; prior to the September 2024 transfer, the same 87.251% was held indirectly through Goodyear Holdings S.à r.l. Source: https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/DEBICA-Umowa-pozyczki-z-Goodyear-S-A-8706695.html ; https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art40386611-firma-oponiarska-debica-sa-umowa-pozyczki-z-goodyear-s-a. Goodyear first acquired a majority stake in 1995/1996, growing from an initial ~30%+ stake to over 80% by the late 1990s; historical (2017-2018) sources cite ~81.35%, since risen to the current 87.251%. We did not find a 2025/2026 update confirming the percentage remains unchanged.
thesis.red_flags: Dębica has entered multiple loan agreements with parent Goodyear S.A. (disclosed as ESPI current reports in 2024), a recurring related-party financing arrangement that is transparent but concentrates the company's financing relationship with its controlling shareholder. Source: https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art40865951-firma-oponiarska-debica-sa-umowy-pozyczek-z-goodyear-s-a. The 2023 plant fire caused a material, disclosed production disruption (full recovery took over a year). Very low free float (~12.7%) given Goodyear's 87.251% stake significantly limits minority-shareholder influence and stock liquidity. No going-concern issues identified from official sources.

name: NWF Group plc
gmSourceUrl: [NWF Group plc Results Presentation](https://www.nwf.co.uk/application/files/2717/5380/5027/NWF_Group_plc_Results_Presentation_29_July_2025.pdf), [NWF Group plc Full Year Results RNS](https://www.nwf.co.uk/application/files/4217/5377/0315/Full_Year_Results_RNS_July_2025.pdf)

thesis.business_description: NWF Group plc, headquartered in Wardle, Nantwich, Cheshire, UK, operates three divisions: Fuels (distribution of heating oil, diesel and petrol to households, farms and businesses across the UK, its largest revenue contributor), Food (warehousing and distribution of ambient/non-chilled groceries for supermarket and retail distribution centres), and Feeds (manufacture and sale of livestock nutrition products for dairy, sheep and beef herds). Source: https://www.morningstar.com.au/investments/security/LSE/NWF ; https://musaffa.com/stock/NWF.L/
thesis.competitive_position: UK-focused diversified distribution group (~1,400-1,489 employees depending on source) combining a fuel-distribution business with counter-cyclical/defensive grocery-warehousing and agricultural-feed operations, giving it diversification across three distinct end-markets within the UK only. Listed on AIM. Source: https://www.morningstar.com.au/investments/security/LSE/NWF
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Fidelity's factsheet (updated 16 June 2026, sourced from the register), the largest named holders are Marlborough International Management and Marlborough Multi-Cap Income (each ~1.57m shares), followed by LOYS AG, LOYS FCP-LOYS Premium Dividende (each ~435,000 shares) and Chelverton Asset Management (~350,000 shares). Source: https://fidelity.co.uk/factsheet-data/factsheet/GB0006523608-nwf-group/profile. A December 2023 major-holdings notice from Close Asset Management disclosed a stake reaching 2,489,377 shares = 5.04% of shares in issue. Source: https://www.ticker.app/lse/NWF/rns/2023-12-14/holdings-in-company/8981W. A Simply Wall St snapshot (undated) separately shows TrinityBridge Limited at 8.22% and Aberdeen Group Plc at 5.63%, with institutions overall holding ~63.4% and insiders under 1%. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/energy/aim-nwf/nwf-group-shares/ownership. We found no evidence of a controlling family stake or employee benefit trust; ownership appears institutionally dispersed with no single holder confirmed above ~8-10%.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; ownership is broadly dispersed among institutional fund managers (no controlling family or founder stake identified), which is a governance positive relative to many peers in this batch. Director share purchases are held via personal SIPPs (self-invested personal pensions) rather than an employee benefit trust, per a March 2024 disclosure regarding the CEO. Source: https://sharesmagazine.co.uk/news/market/LSE20240301105225_5088870/directorpdmr-shareholding. No litigation or going-concern issues identified.

thesis.business_description: XANO Industri AB (publ), headquartered in Jönköping, Sweden and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (XANO B), develops, acquires and runs manufacturing businesses with unique or market-leading products and systems. It reports three business units: Industrial Products (plastic components by rotational, injection and blow moulding), Industrial Solutions (automation solutions for packaging, e.g. conveyors) and Precision Technology (cutting-machined metal and plastic components and systems). The group operates in the Nordics, Estonia, the Netherlands, Poland, China, the USA and Australia. FY2025 net revenue was SEK 3,402m (2024: SEK 3,315m). Founding year conflicts across aggregators (1937 vs 1961); one Inderes profile misdescribes it as an industrial software developer, treated as an outlier. Sources: https://xano.se/en/investors/xano-s-annual-report-2025 ; https://xano.se/storage/0B054BBE43909C62751A7B1A9B224C287B61A5A4365DF759AFB6D86F5FC1C75E/e769a15e69494f148e075a0e8da6b626/pdf/media/72ccf0c39508441199148f42a9de978c/XANO%202026-02-05%201300%20ENG.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: A decentralised industrial group built on owning niche manufacturing companies (acquire-and-develop model). The year-end report says Precision Technology companies are gradually consolidating relationships with defence and security customers; Q4 2025 profit was lower on reduced volumes and a less favourable mix in Industrial Solutions and Precision Technology. Specific competitors, market shares and moat evidence could not be located in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://xano.se/storage/0B054BBE43909C62751A7B1A9B224C287B61A5A4365DF759AFB6D86F5FC1C75E/e769a15e69494f148e075a0e8da6b626/pdf/media/72ccf0c39508441199148f42a9de978c/XANO%202026-02-05%201300%20ENG.pdf ; https://www.inderes.dk/en/companies/Xano-Industri
thesis.main_shareholders: Company-published Euroclear list dated 31 March 2026: Pomona-gruppen AB 16,828,360 shares = 28.22% of capital / 29.19% of votes; Anna Benjamin and related parties 16,160,000 shares = 27.10% of capital / 56.84% of votes (class A shares carry 10 votes); Stig-Olof Simonsson and related parties about 6.99% of capital (about 2% of votes); Svolder AB about 6.67% (down from 8.28% at 31 Dec 2025). The 15 largest holders hold 84.73% of capital (as summarised from the list; individual rows beyond the top four not reviewed). Sources: https://xano.se/storage/24B250EDC4C3522695583C59587C438F1C8A4ECA801950AC4F80707DDAB39A17/5911e91a89034c0e8b6da1b1e8172c8e/pdf/media/51fe37a3c25d46f5ae0c66bd8158a9bf/XANO_largest_shareholders_2026-03-31.pdf ; https://xano.se/en/investors/the-share/shareholders
thesis.red_flags: Control concentration: the dual-class structure gives the two largest holders about 86% of votes combined (56.84% + 29.19%) while Anna Benjamin's vote share far exceeds her capital share, so minority holders have limited influence. Leverage: an aggregator (Simply Wall St) shows total debt about SEK 954m vs cash about SEK 366m and equity about SEK 1.9bn, interest cover about 3x (as-of date not stated; verify against the latest interim report). Cyclical industrial exposure and acquisition-integration risk are standard caveats; Q4 2025 volumes and mix were weaker. No litigation or accounting issues were identified in the sources reviewed. Sources: https://xano.se/storage/24B250EDC4C3522695583C59587C438F1C8A4ECA801950AC4F80707DDAB39A17/5911e91a89034c0e8b6da1b1e8172c8e/pdf/media/51fe37a3c25d46f5ae0c66bd8158a9bf/XANO_largest_shareholders_2026-03-31.pdf ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/capital-goods/sto-xano-b/xano-industri-shares/health
thesis.insider_ownership: Anna Benjamin (board member, Vice Chair per company site) together with related parties holds 27.10% of capital and 56.84% of votes (31 Mar 2026). New board member Magnus Söderlind holds 3,200 class B shares. Board after the 7 May 2026 AGM: Fredrik Rapp (Chair), Anna Benjamin, Pontus Cornelius, Vibeke Gyllenram, Eva Nilsagård, Magnus Söderlind; holdings of the other directors, of Pomona-gruppen's ownership links to the board, and of executives could not be located in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://xano.se/en/corporate-governance/board-of-directors/anna-benjamin ; https://xano.se/en/corporate-governance/board-of-directors/magnus-soderlind ; https://xano.se/storage/C4CB839342FC9C40E863AE099D35DF3A8227409C80EB4940310AE521495B7A67/211a8f1222344a61b3578cf62ff2dab9/pdf/media/6c51f5fa0ed448afba98a5684a1484ad/XANO%202026-05-07%202000%20ENG.pdf

thesis.business_description: Orion S.A. supplies carbon black worldwide. It is incorporated in Luxembourg, and its FY2025 10-K lists its principal executive office in Spring, Texas (Houston area). It reports two segments. Specialty Carbon Black serves polymers, coatings, printing inks and battery/conductive uses. Rubber Carbon Black serves tyres and mechanical rubber goods. FY2025 net sales were USD 1,806.7m (down 4%), with a net loss of USD 70.1m that included an USD 81m goodwill impairment, and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 248m. Sources: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260217402948/en/orion-s.a.-reports-full-year-2025-and-fourth-quarter-earnings/ ; https://www.boardroomalpha.com/sec/oec-10-k-2026-02-17-0001628280-26-008601
thesis.competitive_position: Orion is one of a handful of global carbon black producers. Its main competitors are Cabot, Birla Carbon, PCBL (Phillips Carbon Black), Continental Carbon and Tokai Carbon. One market-research vendor ranks it third worldwide with about 16.8% share in 2025, behind Birla at 17.2%; that figure comes from an aggregator and is not verified. The specialty segment is the higher-margin growth engine: its Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA rose 96% year on year to USD 39.0m. Rubber Adjusted EBITDA fell 61% to USD 19.2m on lower 2026 contract pricing. Management has cut growth capex to prioritise deleveraging, and it guides 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 170-210m. Sources: https://www.reportprime.com/carbon-black-r20005/company ; https://quartr.com/events/orion-s-a-oec-q2-2026_FkA5VTKC ; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001609804/000162828026031402/a2026q1earningsreleasev2.htm
thesis.main_shareholders: The stock is widely held by institutions and there is no controlling holder. Schedule 13G filings dated 26 Feb 2026 show Divisar Capital Management LLC / Steven Baughman with about 5.5% (3,087,263 shares) and Divisar Partners QP, L.P. with about 5.0%; these were taken from the aggregator blarkad.com, so verify on EDGAR. Q1 2026 13F data (aggregator) show BlackRock with about 3.96m shares, Dimensional about 2.06m and Vanguard about 1.88m. This search did not obtain their percentages or the beneficial-ownership table in the 24 Apr 2026 DEF 14A; treat as a partial research gap. Sources: https://blarkad.com/ticker/OEC/ownership ; https://www.boardroomalpha.com/sec/oec-def-14a-2026-04-24-0001308179-26-000347
thesis.red_flags: (1) Leverage is high: Q2 2026 net debt was USD 960.7m, net leverage 4.4x and liquidity USD 178m. (2) Earnings are falling: FY2025 net loss of USD 70.1m including an USD 81m goodwill impairment, and the rubber segment's EBITDA collapsed in 2026 on contract repricing. (3) The business is cyclical and exposed to tyre demand and to Asian competition. (4) The heavy industry carries environmental capex risk; this search did not retrieve the details of US EPA consent-decree obligations or the Evonik-related indemnity/arbitration items, so check the 10-K legal-proceedings note. (5) Director Michel Wurth said in April 2026 he would not stand for re-election, which is a routine governance change. Sources: https://quartr.com/events/orion-s-a-oec-q2-2026_FkA5VTKC ; https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260217402948/en/orion-s.a.-reports-full-year-2025-and-fourth-quarter-earnings/ ; https://www.quantisnow.com/insight/orion-sa-filed-sec-form-8-k-leadership-update-6496614
thesis.insider_ownership: Per Form 4 data (aggregator secform4.com), CEO Corning F. Painter held 1,303,043 shares directly as of 1 May 2026. That is about 2.3% of the roughly 56.3m shares outstanding reported in the FY2025 annual report (our calculation). CFO Jonathan Puckett held about 90.7k shares and SVPs Quinones, Riveros and Niewiem about 50-113k each. Director holdings in the aggregator data are partly stale; for example, Anthony Lynn Davis at about 936k shares dates from a 2023 filing. The proxy's directors-and-officers-as-a-group percentage was not located. There is no founding-family holder. Sources: https://www.secform4.com/insider-holders/1609804.html ; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001609804/000149315226019003/formars.pdf

thesis.business_description: Philippos Nakas S.A. (Nakas Music), founded in 1937 and headquartered in Paiania, Greece, sells and distributes musical instruments, professional audio, Hi-Fi, studio and DJ equipment in Greece and Cyprus. It also runs the Philippos Nakas Conservatory (music education, including a Berklee College of Music collaboration). Its fiscal year ends 30 June. In FY 2023/24 group turnover was about EUR 27.70m (+6.25%), net profit about EUR 1.74m and EBITDA about EUR 3.68m. Sources: https://athens.euronext.com/en/node/941564 ; https://m.uk.investing.com/equities/philippos-nakas-sa
thesis.competitive_position: A long-established, family-run specialist distributor and retailer in a small domestic niche (musical instruments/pro audio), with an education arm (conservatory) that supports its brand and customer funnel. Market-share data and named competitors were not found in this search. FY 2024/25 full-year figures were not retrieved; a half-year report to 31 Dec 2025 exists on ATHEX. Sources: https://athens.euronext.com/en/node/941564 ; https://www.athexgroup.gr/sites/default/files/hermes_3/2026-03/el/508677db-5fa7-4823-8677-db5fa7182313/%CE%9F%CE%B9%CE%BA%CE%BF%CE%BD%CE%BF%CE%BC%CE%B9%CE%BA%CE%AE%20%CE%AD%CE%BA%CE%B8%CE%B5%CF%83%CE%B7%20%CE%A6%CE%99%CE%9B%CE%99%CE%A0%CE%A0%CE%9F%CE%A3%20%CE%9D%CE%91%CE%9A%CE%91%CE%A3%20%CE%91.%CE%92.%CE%95.%CE%A4.%CE%95.%20%282026%2C%CE%95%CE%BE%CE%B1%CE%BC%CE%B7%CE%BD%CE%B9%CE%B1%CE%AF%CE%B1%2C%CE%95%CE%BD%CE%BF%CF%80%CE%BF%CE%B9%CE%B7%CE%BC%CE%AD%CE%BD%CE%B7%29.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: Per a Law 3556/2007 voting-rights notification on ATHEX following a transaction notified 23/12/2024, Georgios Ph. Nakas holds 37.307% and Konstantinos Ph. Nakas 37.296%, together about 74.6%. Holders of the remaining about 25% were not identified in this search. Share capital is EUR 3.804m over 6,340,000 shares (after a December 2023 reserves capitalisation). thesis.red_flags: No accounting or litigation issues were identified from official sources. Caveats: control is concentrated in two brothers (about 74.6%), the free float is small and illiquid (micro-cap of 6.34m shares), the company depends on Greek consumer discretionary spending and on third-party instrument brands, and EBITDA dipped slightly in FY 2023/24. Sources: https://www.athexgroup.gr/en/more-options/announcements/announcement-regulated-information-under-law-35562007-notification ; https://athens.euronext.com/en/node/941564
thesis.insider_ownership: Both main holders are executives: Konstantinos Ph. Nakas (Chairman of the Board) about 37.30%, and Georgios Ph. Nakas (Managing Director) about 37.31%, per the December 2024 regulatory notification. Combined founding-family insider stake is about 74.6%. thesis.business_description: Compagnie du Bois Sauvage is a Brussels-listed, family-controlled investment holding company organised in three pillars: chocolate (100% of Neuhaus and, since April 2026, 100% of Jeff de Bruges, ~480 shops in France and ~50 abroad), real estate (including a stake in Belgian developer Eaglestone), and fund-based/financial investments (e.g. Berenberg bank, Vinventions, a listed Umicore stake). FY2025 (published 5 Mar 2026): NAV up 10% to EUR 887m or EUR 553/share, net EPS EUR 23.57, proposed gross dividend EUR 8.60; intrinsic value reached EUR 576.53/share at H1 2026. Portfolio of ~EUR 890m is ~87% unlisted. Sources: https://webdisclosure.com/press-release/compagnie-bois-sauvage-ebr-comb-cie-du-bois-sauvage-results-2025-8iAtVSI2tUH ; https://www.test-achats.be/invest/investir/actions/articles/2026/07/bois-sauvage-chocolat-confirmation-objectifs ; https://finanzwire.com/press-release/compagnie-bois-sauvage-ebr-comb-cie-du-bois-sauvage-completion-of-the-acquisition-of-jeff-de-bruges-PvZW4Q920Be
thesis.competitive_position: A long-term family holding whose value is now ~57-60% in premium chocolate retail (Neuhaus in Belgian pralines, Jeff de Bruges as a leading French chocolate shop chain); management targets EUR 400m revenue and EUR 80m EBITDA (excl. IFRS 16) from chocolate by 2030, and buying out founder Philippe Jambon's 34% of Jeff de Bruges added ~22% to division revenue. Other holdings give diversification (Berenberg results +25% in H1 2025) but real estate is weak (Eaglestone stake written down another 17% in H1 2026). The shares have historically traded at a sizeable discount to intrinsic value (current discount % not verified here). Sources: https://www.lalibre.be/economie/entreprises-startup/2026/03/05/bois-sauvage-prend-le-controle-total-de-jeff-de-bruges-2EM62ULUWVDEJJEAMAFOZ245SE/ ; https://www.test-achats.be/invest/investir/actions/articles/2026/07/bois-sauvage-chocolat-confirmation-objectifs ; https://www.bois-sauvage.be/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/CBS_Rsultats_S1_2025__EN.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: Per the company's transparency notice dated 27 Nov 2024 (denominator 1,658,509 voting rights): the Paquot family group controlled by Mrs Guy Paquot (Nicole Thys) holds 51.33%, via Anchorage SA -> Fingaren SRL (5.55% directly) -> Entreprises et Chemins de Fer en Chine SA (ECFC, 45.00%), plus Nicole Thys 0.10% and treasury shares 0.68%. An undated Beursgenoten profile shows ECFC 46.66% and Fingaren 5.76% (52.42%), possibly reflecting a later lower share count after buybacks - treat as unverified. No other holder above disclosure thresholds was identified. Sources: https://www.bois-sauvage.be/en/detail/?id=1300663 ; https://www.beursgenoten.nl/koersen/euronext-brussel/bois-sauvage/profiel
thesis.red_flags: (1) Majority family control and low free float/liquidity (~1.66m shares, high nominal price); persistent holding-company discount. (2) Concentration and rising leverage: chocolate is ~60% of intrinsic value, and the 2026 Jeff de Bruges buyout was debt-financed, partly via a EUR 110m bond (holding net debt figure not found). (3) Valuation subjectivity: ~87% of the portfolio is unlisted and marked by the company; real-estate (Eaglestone) and Vinventions have been written down. (4) Earnings volatility from the listed Umicore stake (EUR -59.1m fair-value hit in 2024). No governance or litigation issues identified from official sources. Sources: https://www.test-achats.be/invest/investir/actions/articles/2026/07/bois-sauvage-chocolat-confirmation-objectifs ; https://www.lalibre.be/economie/entreprises-startup/2026/03/05/bois-sauvage-prend-le-controle-total-de-jeff-de-bruges-2EM62ULUWVDEJJEAMAFOZ245SE/ ; https://www.bois-sauvage.be/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/CBS2024EN.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: Founding-family control (~51% as of Nov 2024) through the Paquot vehicles; Nicole Thys (Mrs Guy Paquot) is the ultimate controller. Family members Valerie Paquot (Chair April 2020 - June 2023) and Marie-Noel Paquot have sat on the board; Hubert Olivier became Chairman in 2023 and Benoit Deckers is CEO. Personal holdings of non-family directors and the CEO were not found. Sources: https://www.bois-sauvage.be/en/detail/?id=1171211 ; https://www.bois-sauvage.be/en/detail/?id=1300663 ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/de/diversified-financials/fra-c5s/compagnie-du-bois-sauvage-shares/management

thesis.business_description: EgnsINVEST Ejendomme Tyskland A/S is a Danish-listed property company (Nasdaq Copenhagen, ticker EGNETY; HC Andersen Capital is its Certified Adviser) that owns, runs and develops a portfolio of mainly residential, plus some commercial, property in Berlin. The properties are concentrated in Charlottenburg, Friedrichshain, Prenzlauer Berg and Mitte. FY2025 revenue was DKK 60.2m and EBVAT (earnings before value adjustments and tax) was DKK 15.3m. In H1 2026 revenue was DKK 30.2m, EBVAT DKK 7.1m and pre-tax profit about DKK 18m; investment properties were carried at DKK 1,491m and equity was DKK 646m. Sources: https://storage.mfn.se/b3db80fa-2f2a-4d19-9289-afb9bce23784/egnsinvest-ejd-tyskland-forventer-fremgang-i-2026.pdf ; https://www.inderes.dk/releases/egnsinvest-ejendomme-tyskland-as-resultat-for-1-halvar-2026-18-mio-kr ; https://attachment.news.eu.nasdaq.com/a1de171b3a32aac769528bebd16c375ca
thesis.competitive_position: It is a small, single-city residential landlord in a supply-constrained Berlin market. Management describes that market as strictly regulated, and it raises rents where the law allows. Operations are improving: vacancy fell from 16 to 13 units in 2025, and the Q2 2026 revaluation gain of about DKK 9.3m was attributed to rent adjustments and fast re-letting rather than lower yields. 2026 guidance is EBVAT of DKK 15-17m and revenue of DKK 60-64m. Inderes shows a market cap of about DKK 332m against reported equity of DKK 646m. This implies the shares trade at roughly half of book value, based on our calculation and assuming about 2.31m shares after the 2026 cancellation; verify. Sources: https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/vaekstaktierdk-egnsinvest-ejd-tyskland-presents-preliminary-figures-for-the-second-quarter-of-the-year ; https://www.inderes.dk/companies/EgnsINVEST-Ejendomme-Tyskland ; https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/egnsinvest-ejendomme-tyskland-as-generalforsamlingens-forlob-4
thesis.main_shareholders: This search did not find official 5%-holder announcements or an annual-report shareholder list; treat as a research gap. Aggregator data only (Simply Wall St, last updated around 17 November 2025): EgnsINVEST Holding A/S about 16.1% (about 378,744 shares), Sparekassen Danmark about 8.29%, Sparekassen Kronjylland about 7.77%, and the top seven holders about 33%. A 2020 filing likewise showed EgnsINVEST Holding at 16.13%; that holding company is itself owned by Danish savings banks and Jyske Bank. The percentages will have moved slightly after 39,036 treasury shares (1.66%) were cancelled following the 27 May 2026 AGM and with the ongoing buyback. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/dk/real-estate-management-and-development/cph-egnety/egnsinvest-ejendomme-tyskland-shares/ownership ; https://sources.opencorporates.com/bots/dk_xbrl_parser/9/e/9/78239533_amNsb3VkczovLzAzLzJhLzNhL2I0LzU4LzMzNGYtNDM2My1iYzk4LTBkMmM4YzRiMGM5MA.pdf
thesis.red_flags: No governance, accounting or litigation issues were identified from official sources in this search. Structural risks: (1) all assets are in one city, Berlin, under strict rent regulation; (2) the gap between property value (DKK 1,491m) and equity (DKK 646m) implies substantial liabilities, but this search did not retrieve mortgage debt, LTV or refinancing terms, so treat this as a gap, particularly given interest-rate sensitivity; (3) the stock is very small and illiquid, and the persistent discount to book value suggests the market doubts the valuations or the capital allocation; (4) any management or administration arrangements with the EgnsINVEST group and their fees were not verified. A 2025 buyback was meant to provide shares as payment for properties, but this did not happen as intended and the shares were cancelled. Sources: https://www.inderes.dk/releases/egnsinvest-ejendomme-tyskland-as-resultat-for-1-halvar-2026-18-mio-kr ; https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/egnsinvest-ejendomme-tyskland-as-generalforsamlingens-forlob-4
thesis.website: Could not confirm the official website domain in this search (likely under the EgnsINVEST group site, egnsinvest.dk, but unverified); treat as a research gap. Company announcements are available via Inderes/MFN. Source: https://www.inderes.dk/companies/EgnsINVEST-Ejendomme-Tyskland
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is small, and these figures come from an aggregator only (Simply Wall St, around November 2025). Board chair Knud Lomborg holds about 0.77% and director (CEO) Maibritt Lindstrom about 0.10%. No official insider-holdings table was located. There is no founding-family or controlling insider. The board elected at the May 2026 AGM: Knud Lomborg (chair), Vagn Hansen (deputy chair, new) and Bo Holse (new). Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/dk/real-estate-management-and-development/cph-egnety/egnsinvest-ejendomme-tyskland-shares/ownership ; https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/egnsinvest-ejendomme-tyskland-as-generalforsamlingens-forlob-4

name: Caisse Régionale de Crédit Agricole Mutuel de la Touraine et du Poitou Société Coopérative

thesis.business_description: Caisse Régionale de Crédit Agricole Mutuel de la Touraine et du Poitou Société Coopérative, incorporated in 1995 and based in Tours/Poitiers, is a mutual/cooperative regional retail bank within the Crédit Agricole Group, serving individuals, farmers, professionals, businesses, associations and public/social-housing bodies in the Indre-et-Loire, Vienne and Deux-Sèvres departments via a network of 64 local banks (caisses locales) and ~142-143 branches, offering deposits, loans (including agricultural and real-estate financing), insurance, leasing and cash-management services. Source: https://live.euronext.com/en/product/equities/FR0000045304-XPAR/company-information ; https://pickthebank.eu/banks/france/caisse-regionale-de-credit-agricole-mutuel-de-la-touraine-et-du-poitou-agrifrpp894
thesis.competitive_position: Dominant mutual retail/agricultural bank in its home territory as part of the nationwide Crédit Agricole network; per Euronext's company profile, it held €17.7bn in deposits and €12.5bn in outstanding loans at end-2024, with reported equity of ~€2.5bn and 534,700+ customers (end-2023 figures, per Motherbase). Source: https://live.euronext.com/en/product/equities/FR0000045304-XPAR/company-information
thesis.main_shareholders: As a Crédit Agricole mutual regional bank, its capital is split across three instrument types per an Easybourse shareholder-structure profile: Parts sociales (mutual member shares, held by the caisses locales and sociétaires) 58.52%, Certificats Coopératifs d'Associés (CCA, non-voting investment certificates) 25.28%, and Certificats Coopératifs d'Investissement (CCI, the listed Euronext Paris tranche) 16.2%. Source: https://www.easybourse.com/action-societe/crcam-touraine-cci/profil/FR0000045304-25. The bank reported more than 250,000 member-shareholders (sociétaires) by end-2014, growing from 215,000 at end-2012, per its own financial notices; sociétaires govern the bank through 64 local Assemblées Générales de Caisse locale. Source: https://www.credit-agricole.fr/content/dam/assetsca/cr894/npc/documents/informations-reglementees/avis-financier/Avis_Financier_CATP_20130218.pdf. The bank also invested in SACAM Mutualisation as part of a 2016 Crédit Agricole Group restructuring, though we could not confirm SACAM's or the caisses locales' exact percentage of the Caisse Régionale's own capital from an official source in this search — this is a standard feature of the Crédit Agricole group structure (caisses locales/SACAM typically hold the controlling majority of parts sociales) but the precise current split should be verified against the bank's latest document de référence.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; the mutual/cooperative ownership structure (majority control by member-owned local caisses, with only CCI shares — 16.2% of capital — publicly tradable) limits the influence of public minority (CCI) holders over governance, but this is the standard, long-disclosed Crédit Agricole regional-bank structure rather than a specific red flag. Source: https://www.easybourse.com/action-societe/crcam-touraine-cci/profil/FR0000045304-25

thesis.business_description: IMPACT Developer & Contractor S.A. is a Romanian residential real-estate developer listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange. It is based in Bucharest and builds and sells apartment complexes. Projects include GREENFIELD Baneasa and GREENFIELD West in Bucharest, BOREAL Plus in Constanta and LOTUS in Oradea, and Luxuria Residence was delivered through its subsidiary Bergamot Developments. It is now building ARIA Verdi in Bucharest, a mixed-use project with 865 apartments and an estimated development value of EUR 431m. In 2025 group revenue rose 6% to RON 331m and consolidated net profit rose 34% to RON 82.5m, with 247 apartments sold for RON 177m (53% of revenue). Sources: https://www.thediplomat.ro/2026/03/02/2025-impact-financial-results-a-net-profit-of-ron-82-5-million-up-to-34-compared-to-2024/ ; https://bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/IMP_20260331074225_Annual-Report-2025-IMP.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: Impact describes itself as the first real-estate developer listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange. It is a mid-sized player in Romania's fragmented residential market and is expanding beyond Bucharest into Constanta, Oradea and Iasi. At end-2025 it held building permits for 2,828 units with an estimated gross development value of EUR 733m. As of 30 June 2026 it had 970 homes under construction (GDV RON 1.68bn), which it calls its largest development cycle, and fair-value NAV of EUR 263m. Its edge is a large owned land bank, especially at Greenfield Baneasa, and long-standing access to Bucharest equity and bond funding. This search did not find named competitors or market-share data. Sources: https://www.romania-insider.com/impact-developer-revenues-h1-2026 ; https://bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/IMP_20260819181430_Press-release-H1-2026-EN.pdf ; https://profit.ro/povesti-cu-profit/real-estate-constructii/impact-developer-contractor-continua-expansiunea-la-nivel-national-si-intra-pe-piata-imobiliara-din-iasi-19508348
thesis.main_shareholders: Founder Gheorghe Iaciu controls the company. A BVB shareholder-structure filing (published November 2025, data as of 18 August 2025) shows him with 69,077,528 shares (58.42%). The same filing shows SWISS CAPITAL SA BUCURESTI with about 10.10%, which is likely a brokerage or omnibus account (not verified), other individuals with about 20.07% and other legal entities with about 11.41%, out of 118,247,071 shares. Note: the filing is under the bond symbol IMP26E, so check the share count against the 2025 annual report. Press reports give stakes ranging from 49.48% to 59.97% at various undated points; one undated Economica.net piece shows Adrian Andrici with 15.92%, which may be stale. Sources: https://bvb.ro/infocont/infocont25/IMP26E_20251117144646_Shareholder-Structure.pdf ; https://www.economica.net/?p=529581 ; https://profit.ro/povesti-cu-profit/real-estate-constructii/impact-developer-contractor-continua-expansiunea-la-nivel-national-si-intra-pe-piata-imobiliara-din-iasi-19508348
thesis.red_flags: (1) Profitability has fallen sharply in 2026. H1 2026 consolidated net profit was only RON 5.98m on RON 112.1m revenue, and Q1 revenue and profit also fell. Management blamed a VAT increase on housing, fiscal tightening, political instability and inflation. (2) Unsold stock of completed units was valued at RON 308.6m at 30 June 2026, and management aims to sell it within 18 months. (3) 2025 profit relied partly on items beyond apartment sales: apartments were only 53% of revenue, and parent-level profit of RON 105.5m exceeded group profit. Check for revaluation or intra-group effects in the annual report. (4) A single controlling shareholder means minority-governance risk, and the company relies on repeated bond issues. (5) Pipeline execution is large relative to current sales. Leverage is modest: the debt ratio was 14% at mid-2026 and 13% at end-2025. No ASF sanctions or litigation were identified from official sources in this search; related-party transactions were not reviewed. Sources: https://www.romania-insider.com/impact-developer-revenues-h1-2026 ; https://www.zfenglish.com/capital-market/impact-developer-contractor-sees-revenue-and-profit-shrink-in-q1-23160933 ; https://www.thediplomat.ro/2026/03/02/2025-impact-financial-results-a-net-profit-of-ron-82-5-million-up-to-34-compared-to-2024/
thesis.insider_ownership: Gheorghe Iaciu (founder, controlling shareholder) holds about 58.42% (BVB filing, data as of 18 Aug 2025). This search did not establish his current board role; the CEO is Dan Sebastian Campeanu. Holdings of the CEO and other board members were not located; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://bvb.ro/infocont/infocont25/IMP26E_20251117144646_Shareholder-Structure.pdf ; https://www.romania-insider.com/impact-developer-revenues-h1-2026

thesis.business_description: Porvair plc (King's Lynn, UK) is a specialist filtration and environmental technology group with three divisions: Aerospace & Industrial (FY2025 revenue GBP 83.7m, 43% of group), Laboratory (GBP 66.9m, 35%) and Metal Melt Quality (ceramic filters for aluminium/foundry casting). The FY2025 (November year-end) annual report describes record revenue, profit and margin; key markets are the UK, Europe and the US. Sources: https://reports.ticker.app/213800ECKHS8LAQO3C45/2026-03-11/NI-000140498.pdf ; https://www.ii.co.uk/analysis-commentary/shares-future-upgrade-makes-top-five-stock-ii538533
thesis.competitive_position: A niche supplier of engineered filtration with high-specification, regulated end-markets (aerospace platforms, laboratory consumables, molten-metal filtration), supplemented by frequent bolt-on acquisitions: Ratiolab (2023), European Filter Corporation (early 2024), Drache Umwelttechnik (12 Jan 2026) and further deals reported in H1 2026. Interim 2026 commentary: Aerospace & Industrial revenue +~10%, Laboratory +1%, Metal Melt Quality -6% on weak foundry demand. Hooman Caman Javvi (ex-COO of Hill & Smith) succeeded long-serving CEO Ben Stocks at the April 2025 AGM. Sources: https://reports.ticker.app/213800ECKHS8LAQO3C45/2026-03-11/NI-000140498.pdf ; https://www.ii.co.uk/analysis-commentary/shares-future-upgrade-makes-top-five-stock-ii538533 ; https://sharecast.com/news/news-and-announcements/porvair-appoints-new-chief-executive-trades-as-expected--17537546.html
thesis.main_shareholders: From TR-1 holding notifications: G.G.G. S.p.A. (vehicle linked to Giorgio Girondi per search summary) 29.00% (13,488,329 voting rights) as of 22 Apr 2026, up from 28.05%; Long Path Partners LP 11.92% as of 19 May 2026 (down from 12.03%). Total voting rights 46,585,211 (31 Jul 2026). A further 'Holding(s) in Company' RNS dated 8 Jul 2026 exists but its contents were not retrieved - treat as a research gap. Aggregator Simply Wall St shows G.G.G. at a stale 19.1%. Sources: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/porvair--prv/holding-s-in-company/9537251 ; https://www.ticker.app/lse/PRV/rns/2026-05-22/Holding(s)-in-Company/4563F ; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/porvair--prv/total-voting-rights/9699339 ; https://financialfilings.com/companies/porvair-plc/
thesis.red_flags: Concentrated register: G.G.G. S.p.A. at 29.00% sits just below the UK Takeover Code 30% mandatory-offer threshold, giving it significant influence; in May 2026 activist Richard Bernstein (founder of Crystal Amber) reportedly wrote to chairman John Nicholas urging a sale/strategic review - no offer had been announced in the sources found. Metal Melt Quality is cyclical (foundry weakness) and aerospace sales fell 8% in the interim period. Acquisitive strategy carries integration risk. No accounting or legal issues identified from official sources. Sources: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/porvair--prv/holding-s-in-company/9537251 ; https://financialfilings.com/companies/porvair-plc/ ; https://www.ii.co.uk/analysis-commentary/shares-future-upgrade-makes-top-five-stock-ii538533
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider holdings are small: per a March 2026 PDMR notice, CEO Hooman Caman Javvi held ~0.06% and Group Finance Director James Mills ~0.16% of issued share capital. Holdings of the chairman (John Nicholas) and non-executives were not located. Former CEO Ben Stocks held ~0.4-0.9% per 2024 RNS notices (figures inconsistent between notices; no longer a director). Sources: https://www.ticker.app/lse/PRV ; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/porvair--prv/director-pdmr-shareholding/7269249

thesis.business_description: Eurocash is a Polish FMCG wholesale and franchise-retail group (HQ Komorniki near Poznan) supplying independent local grocery stores through cash & carry, delivery wholesale and franchise/partner formats (e.g. Delikatesy Centrum, Duzy Ben specialty alcohol stores), plus an e-grocery business it describes as No. 1 in Poland. FY2025 revenue was about PLN 30bn (-4.6% y/y) with recurring EBITDA of PLN 867m (PLN 904m in 2024) and reported EBITDA of PLN 543m after restructuring costs. Sources: https://www.grupaeurocash.pl/en/about-us/eurocash-group ; https://www.esmmagazine.com/retail/eurocash-2025-revenue-down-4-6-amidst-strategy-optimisation-310989
thesis.competitive_position: The group says it integrates around 15,000 local shops under franchise and partnership formats, positioning it as the main supplier/organiser of Poland's independent grocery channel against discount chains. Its 2026-27 strategy (adopted 9 Dec 2025, 'Building Poland's Number 1 Integrated Franchise Retailer') shifts the group toward a franchise model, cutting cash & carry sites and distribution centres (15 to 10) and targeting PLN 400m of annual savings and PLN 600m EBIT by 2027; PLN 279m of savings were reported secured by mid-2026. Independent market-share data versus rivals was not found in this search. Sources: https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art43479801-eurocash-sa-przyjecie-strategii-dla-grupy-eurocash-na-lata-2026-2027 ; https://www.esmmagazine.com/retail/restructuring-drives-h1-margin-gains-and-savings-for-eurocash-group-320336
thesis.main_shareholders: Per the company's ESPI filing listing holders with 5%+ of votes at the AGM of 10 June 2026: Politra S.a r.l. 60,614,240 votes = 43.56% of total votes; Generali OFE ~6.72%; Allianz Polska OFE ~5.11% (total votes 139,163,286). Note these are AGM attendance-based disclosures, not a full register. Source: https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art44608151-eurocash-sa-wykaz-akcjonariuszy-posiadajacych-co-najmniej-5-glosow-na-zwyczajnym-walnym-zgromadzeniu-eurocash-s-a
thesis.red_flags: Ongoing restructuring with shrinking revenue (FY2025 -4.6%), large one-off costs (reported EBITDA PLN 543m vs recurring PLN 867m) and store closures (65 Delikatesy Centrum company stores closed in 9M 2025); thin margins (~2.9% adj. EBITDA). Leverage is low pre-IFRS 16 (~0.6x at YE2025 per company) but much higher including leases (2.48x post-IFRS 16 at Q3 2025). Controlling-shareholder structure (~44% Amaral). A PLN 76m UOKiK fine (2021) over supplier fees was annulled by the courts and the matter reported closed by the Supreme Court. Sources: https://www.esmmagazine.com/retail/eurocash-2025-revenue-down-4-6-amidst-strategy-optimisation-310989 ; https://biznes.pap.pl/download/attachment/52990666/DOC.20251128.52990666.20251128_0916_EUR_EN_AW.pdf ; https://www.parkiet.com/handel-i-konsumpcja/art45096901-skarga-uokik-oderwana-od-realiow-sad-najwyzszy-zamyka-sprawe-eurocash
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder Luis Amaral (Chairman of the Supervisory Board) indirectly controls the Politra stake (43.56% of votes per the June 2026 AGM filing) via Amaral e Filhas Limited; aggregators (Simply Wall St) show ~44% attributed to him, and AidData cites ~44% held via two vehicles (likely an earlier date). Holdings of management board members were not located in this search. Sources: https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art44608151-eurocash-sa-wykaz-akcjonariuszy-posiadajacych-co-najmniej-5-glosow-na-zwyczajnym-walnym-zgromadzeniu-eurocash-s-a ; https://china.aiddata.org/projects/108923 ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/pl/consumer-retailing/wse-eur/eurocash-shares/ownership

thesis.business_description: Fair Value REIT-AG is a German listed REIT (ISIN DE000A0MW975) owning commercial property (retail and office) in German secondary locations; per its 2025 annual report the group held 19 properties at 31 Dec 2025 (20 a year earlier) with a market value of about EUR 248.5m (2024: EUR 258.3m), rental income of about EUR 19.1m (-3.0%) and FFO per share of EUR 0.67 (2024: EUR 0.57). Assets include the Galerie Rostocker Hof, whose lease was extended to 2040 in March 2025. The current headquarters address was not confirmed in this search. Sources: https://www.hauptversammlung.de/fileadmin/public/user_upload/FairValue_GB25.pdf ; https://www.boerse-online.de/dpa-afx/gnw-news-fair-value-reit-ag-verlaengert-langfristig-mit-parkhausbetreiber-in-rostock-434389.html
thesis.competitive_position: A small, externally-controlled property vehicle within the DEMIRE Deutsche Mittelstand Real Estate group, which took control via a 2015 share-exchange offer (2 DEMIRE shares per FVI share, ~71.6% tendered in the first acceptance period) as part of DEMIRE's secondary-location commercial property strategy. Scale is small (~EUR 250m portfolio) and it competes with many German regional commercial landlords; no distinctive moat was identified. The 2025 report shows an EPRA vacancy rate of 9.8% (2024: 14.3%), but a separate table in the same report shows 29.0% - the basis for the two figures could not be reconciled from search snippets, so treat vacancy as a data conflict. Sources: https://www.hauptversammlung.de/fileadmin/public/user_upload/FairValue_GB25.pdf ; https://www.demire.ag/en/corporate_news_en/shareholders-of-fair-value-reit-ag-vote-in-favour-of-merger-with-demire/
thesis.main_shareholders: Controlled indirectly by DEMIRE Deutsche Mittelstand Real Estate AG, which held 84.35% of voting rights per a July 2020 WpHG voting-rights notice (up from 77.70%) and was still described as the 84.35% indirect majority shareholder in a later ad-hoc notice; free float was ~14% per comdirect (2020-dated data). DEMIRE itself is ~90% owned by Apollo-managed fund AEPF III 15 S.a r.l. and Wecken & Cie.; Apollo and Klaus/Ina Wecken filed group voting-rights notices on FVI after a 5 Dec 2024 restructuring. On 8 June 2026 DEMIRE's main shareholders began a structured sale process for their ~90% DEMIRE stake, which would indirectly change FVI's controlling holder. Simply Wall St (aggregator, undated) shows Apollo ~59.9% and AEPF III 1 S.a r.l. ~19.9% - this attribution differs from the filings and is unverified. A 2025/2026 confirmation of the exact current DEMIRE percentage was not found. Sources: https://www.boerse-online.de/dpa-afx/dgap-stimmrechte-fair-value-reit-ag-deutsch-6481.html ; https://www.boerse-online.de/dpa-afx/dgap-adhoc-fair-value-reit-ag-grossaktionaerin-demire-steht-vor-moeglicher-veraenderung-im-aktionaerskreis-deutsch-138760.html ; https://www.boerse-online.de/dpa-afx/eqs-stimmrechte-fair-value-reit-ag-deutsch-415380.html ; https://www.onvista.de/news/2026/06-08-gnw-adhoc-demire-deutsche-mittelstand-real-estate-ag-hauptaktionaere-beginnen-strukturierten-verkaufsprozess-fuer-ihre-beteiligung-0-10-26519693 ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/de/real-estate/fra-fvi/fair-value-reit-ag-shares/ownership
thesis.red_flags: (1) Controlled company: ~84% held indirectly by DEMIRE, leaving a ~14-16% free float with low liquidity and little minority influence; DEMIRE's owners started a sale process in June 2026, creating change-of-control uncertainty (and possible squeeze-out/delisting scenarios, not announced). (2) In Feb 2026 an ad-hoc warned of a 2025 HGB net loss (~EUR 0.5m; final single-entity loss EUR 890,722) after a EUR 4.9m write-down on a Neumuenster property whose Sparkasse Suedholstein lease expired end-January 2026, and the 2026 dividend was suspended - a material issue for a REIT whose appeal is distributions. (3) Group net result 2025 about -EUR 1.3m; NAV per share fell to EUR 9.61 from EUR 9.97. (4) Conflicting EPRA vacancy figures (9.8% vs 29.0%) in the 2025 report snippets. Sources: https://www.boerse-online.de/dpa-afx/gnw-adhoc-fair-value-reit-ag-erwartet-jahresfehlbetrag-im-hgb-einzelabschluss-fuer-2025-in-hoehe-von-rund-eur-05-mio-und-setzt-dividendenzahlung-im-jahr-2026-aus-500295.html ; https://www.onvista.de/news/2026/04-13-eqs-hv-fair-value-reit-ag-bekanntmachung-der-einberufung-zur-hauptversammlung-am-21-05-2026-in-frankfurt-mit-dem-ziel-der-europaweiten-verbreitung-gemaess-121-aktg-0-37-26499925 ; https://www.hauptversammlung.de/fileadmin/public/user_upload/FairValue_GB25.pdf
thesis.website: https://www.fvreit.de (official domain; not surfaced directly in search results this session, so verify). Source: https://www.fvreit.de
thesis.insider_ownership: No direct holdings by named board members were found. The Wecken family (Klaus Wecken, Ina Wecken via Wecken & Cie.) holds an indirect interest through DEMIRE and filed voting-rights notices in December 2024, but their look-through percentage in FVI was not stated in the snippets. Current Management Board and Supervisory Board composition could not be confirmed (only 2022-era personnel news was found). Treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.boerse-online.de/dpa-afx/eqs-stimmrechte-fair-value-reit-ag-deutsch-415380.html ; https://www.boerse-online.de/dpa-afx/eqs-news-fair-value-reit-ag-veraenderungen-im-aufsichtsrat-deutsch-254784.html

thesis.business_description: GO p.l.c. is Malta's incumbent integrated telecoms operator (fixed, fibre, mobile, TV) and also owns majority stakes in BMIT Technologies plc (data centres/cloud, listed on the MSE) and Cablenet Communication Systems in Cyprus (51% control since 2016), plus Klikk electronics retail and cybersecurity/renewables/assisted-living services. FY2025 revenue was EUR 254.4m (+3.9%), EBITDA EUR 92m, net profit EUR 20.7m (+31.8%); non-telecom revenue EUR 68.2m (~27%). H1 2026 revenue EUR 134.7m (+9%) but EBITDA -3.7% to EUR 46m and pre-tax profit -10% to EUR 14.8m. Sources: https://www.go.com.mt/news/go-plc-marks-50-years-of-leadership-with-record-profit-growth-2025/ ; https://businessnow.mt/gos-growing-cash-flow-from-malta/ ; https://thebusinesspicture.com/2026/08/07/go-revenue-increases-as-pre-tax-profits-fall/ ; https://maltatoday.com.mt/business/business_news/43174/go_finalises_cablenet_acquisition
thesis.competitive_position: Incumbent with a nationwide 'True Fibre' FTTH network (EUR 100m programme completed in 2025, letting capex fall from EUR 36.5m to EUR 24.1m and free cash flow exceed EUR 23m) in a small, competitive three-player market (rivals include Melita and Epic per general market knowledge - not detailed in sources retrieved). Diversification into data centres (BMIT) and Cyprus cable/mobile (Cablenet) provides growth beyond the mature Maltese telecom market; the H1 2026 directors' report cites a 'highly competitive landscape'. Sources: https://businessnow.mt/gos-growing-cash-flow-from-malta/ ; https://www.go.com.mt/news/go-plc-crosses-quarter-billion-euro-revenue-milestone-as-group-charts-bold-course-beyond-telecoms ; https://thebusinesspicture.com/2026/08/07/go-revenue-increases-as-pre-tax-profits-fall/
thesis.main_shareholders: Tunisie Telecom (via subsidiary TT ML Limited) holds ~65.4% (66,281,050 shares transferred in August 2016; GO's company-structure page rounds to 66%); the remainder is held by the investing public on the Malta Stock Exchange. No other 5%+ holder was identified in this search; a current named shareholder table from the annual report was not retrieved. Sources: https://www.go.com.mt/investor-centre/company-structure/ ; https://cdn.borzamalta.com.mt/download/announcements/GO385.pdf ; https://businessnow.mt/gos-growing-cash-flow-from-malta/
thesis.red_flags: Controlling shareholder (~65%) is Tunisie Telecom, which is linked to the Tunisian state - minority holders depend on its dividend/strategy decisions and related-party dealings (e.g. intra-group transactions between BMIT and Cablenet such as the Arsinoe cable IRU of ~EUR 6.9m). H1 2026 showed falling EBITDA and pre-tax profit despite revenue growth. Exposure to a small, competitive domestic market. No accounting or litigation issues identified from official sources. Sources: https://www.go.com.mt/investor-centre/company-structure/ ; https://cdn.borzamalta.com.mt/download/announcements/CCS45.pdf ; https://thebusinesspicture.com/2026/08/07/go-revenue-increases-as-pre-tax-profits-fall/
thesis.insider_ownership: Could not locate directors' or executives' personal shareholdings in this search; control rests with Tunisie Telecom (itself majority state-owned by Tunisia) rather than with management or a founding family. Treat director holdings as a research gap (check the annual report's directors' interests section). Source: https://www.go.com.mt/investor-centre/company-structure/

thesis.business_description: Cemat A/S is a Copenhagen-listed holding company whose assets are real estate in the Bielany district of Warsaw, Poland, operated through two segments: Property Management (letting premises and land) and Property Development (residential projects such as 'Moje Bielany', 105 flats). FY2025 revenue rose to DKK 164.7m (2024: DKK 39.4m), driven by sale of 93 apartments (DKK 125.3m), with leasing revenue DKK 39.3m and EBITDA DKK 40.0m (2024: DKK 7.3m). Sources: https://filings.xbrl.org/213800899MWAZT9KQZ78/2025-12-31/ESEF/DK/0/cemat-2025-12-31-en/reports/cemat-2025-12-31-en.xhtml ; https://filings.xbrl.org/213800899MWAZT9KQZ78/2025-06-30/ESEF/DK/0/cemat-2025-06-30-en/reports/cemat-2025-06-30-en.xhtml
thesis.competitive_position: A micro-cap single-location land bank/developer rather than a scaled competitor: value rests on converting its Warsaw Bielany industrial/rental land into residential development. Warsaw property was carried as investment property at DKK 191.8m at end-2024 (2025 valuation not retrieved). A binding zoning decision in H1 2025 opened a next phase on a 4,795 sqm plot with potential for 127 residential units plus retail; it has also acquired perpetual usufruct rights to road-designated plots (May 2025, March 2026). Sources: https://filings.xbrl.org/213800899MWAZT9KQZ78/2024-12-31/ESEF/DK/0/cemat-2024-12-31-en/reports/cemat-2024-12-31-en.xhtml ; https://filings.xbrl.org/213800899MWAZT9KQZ78/2025-06-30/ESEF/DK/0/cemat-2025-06-30-en/reports/cemat-2025-06-30-en.xhtml ; https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/no-62026-cemat-as-acquires-right-of-perpetual-usufruct-to-land-plot-in-bielany-warsaw
thesis.main_shareholders: Aggregator data only (Simply Wall St / S&P Global, updated ~Apr-May 2025): EDJ Group / Eivind (Dam) Jensen ~32.5% (81,234,585 shares, listed twice for the same stake - not additive), Gist Holding ApS ~10%, Frede Clausen 4.83%. Official company announcement of 9 Sep 2025: Frede Clausen holds 12,578,091 shares = 5.034% of capital and votes (conflicts with/updates the aggregator figure). The shareholder section of the 2025 annual report was not retrieved - verify there. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/dk/real-estate-management-and-development/cph-cemat/cemat-shares/ownership ; https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/no-192025-major-shareholders-announcement
thesis.red_flags: Very small, illiquid company with a single-asset, single-city concentration (Warsaw Bielany); earnings are lumpy and depend on apartment handovers (2025 jump driven by one project), and investment property values rely on valuation reports. Concentrated board-linked ownership (~top 8 holders ~82% per aggregator). Board recommended no dividend at a recent AGM. No accounting or litigation issues identified from official sources in this search. Sources: https://filings.xbrl.org/213800899MWAZT9KQZ78/2025-12-31/ESEF/DK/0/cemat-2025-12-31-en/reports/cemat-2025-12-31-en.xhtml ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/dk/real-estate-management-and-development/cph-cemat/cemat-shares/ownership ; https://investorshangout.com/cemat-as-holds-annual-general-meeting-amid-key-resolutions-252462-/
thesis.insider_ownership: Board members are among the largest holders: Deputy Chairman Eivind Jensen (~32.5% via EDJ, aggregator figure) and Chairman Frede Clausen (5.034% per 9 Sep 2025 company announcement). CEO Jaroslaw Lipinski reportedly ~0.94-1.03% (aggregator, figures differ by date). Board composition per aggregator snapshot May 2025; verify against the annual report. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/dk/real-estate-management-and-development/cph-cemat/cemat-shares/management ; https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/no-192025-major-shareholders-announcement

thesis.business_description: NOTE AB (publ) is a Swedish electronics manufacturing services (EMS) provider (founded 1990; HQ Stockholm per most sources, TradingView lists Kista; Nasdaq Stockholm) covering component selection, test-equipment development, prototyping, serial production of circuit-board assemblies and box-build, and after-sales; main end markets are medtech, greentech, industrial and communications, with sites in Sweden, Finland, the UK, Estonia, China and elsewhere. FY2025: sales SEK 3,814m (2024: 3,901m), organic growth 0%, operating profit SEK 381m (352m), profit after tax SEK 281m, EPS SEK 9.89. A profile figure of roughly SEK 4.2bn revenue conflicts with the reported 2025 figure and is likely trailing/stale. Sources: https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/notes-year-end-report-2025 ; https://finchat.io/company/OM-NOTE
thesis.competitive_position: A mid-sized Nordic/European EMS player that grows largely through acquisitions: Q2 2026 sales rose 20% to SEK 1,175m but organic growth was only 1%; five companies were acquired in the quarter (Axotan, Phacotec, Createc, Valveco, Autek) and two add-ons after quarter-end (Dorte Egelund, Albiox, via Labema). Order backlog for the current year was 11% higher like-for-like. Market share and named competitors were not found in this search (research gap). Sources: https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/note-notes-interim-report-q2-2026-20260715 ; https://www.inderes.se/releases/notes-interim-report-q2-2026
thesis.main_shareholders: Aggregator data (Affarsvarlden, Millistream; undated, possibly stale): Johan Hagberg about 19.3%; Egil Christen Dahl 6.0%; Cervantes Capital 4.2%; Swedbank Robur Fonder 3.8%; Varner Equities AS 3.8%; Avanza Pension 3.7%; Fredrik Hagberg 3.5%; AAT Invest AS 2.6%; La Financiere de l'Echiquier 2.0%; Fondsfinans 1.8%. Could not locate the company's own Modular Finance/Euroclear list or a dated annual-report table; treat as a research gap. Source: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/note
thesis.red_flags: Acquisition-driven growth with weak organic growth (0% in 2025; 1% in Q2 2026) creates integration and goodwill risk; operating profit fell to SEK 90m in Q2 2026 (101m prior year) and operating cash flow was SEK -34m on inventory build. The board proposed no dividend for 2025. Net debt level was not found in this search (research gap). A single large holder-director (about 19%) has influence. Customer concentration and litigation were not located. Sources: https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/note-notes-interim-report-q2-2026-20260715 ; https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/notes-year-end-report-2025
thesis.insider_ownership: Johan Hagberg (board member, ex-chair; about 19% per Affarsvarlden/analysis) is the largest holder. The 2026 nomination-committee proposal re-elects Hagberg and Egil Dahl (Egil Christen Dahl holds 6.0% per Millistream; identity match not verified), Anna Belfrage (chair), Charlotte Stjerngren, with Jan Engelberg (0 shares) and Sir Michael Wigston proposed as new. CEO Johannes Lind-Widestam owns about 1.1% per one analysis (secondary source). Fredrik Hagberg 3.5% (relationship unverified). Sources: https://www.inderes.se/releases/valberedningens-reviderade-forslag-till-styrelse-infor-arsstamman-2026 ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/note-aterhamtning-2025

thesis.business_description: CLIQ Digital AG (Dusseldorf, Germany; founded by CEO Luc Voncken per TradingView) sells bundled and single-content subscription streaming products (licensed movies, music, games, audiobooks etc.) to consumers worldwide, acquiring customers mainly via performance marketing. FY2025 sales fell ~46% to about EUR 132m (2024: EUR 243.0m) with negative EBITDA (~EUR -6m) and a net loss reported at ~EUR 12-13.6m (figures/currency inconsistent across secondary sources); paying customers fell to 0.6m by 30 June 2025. Sources: https://www.edisongroup.com/research/managing-cash/BM-2391/ ; https://finder.techleap.nl/news/feed/cliq-digital-sales-plunge-46-to-149m-posts-13-6m-loss-in-turbulent-2025 ; https://in.tradingview.com/symbols/SWB-CLIQ/financials-overview
thesis.competitive_position: Small player in a crowded digital-subscription market dominated by large streaming platforms; its model depends on licensed (not proprietary) content and on paid customer acquisition plus card-payment processing. Disruptions in the global digital-payments ecosystem and card-scheme policy changes on cancellations/refunds sharply restricted customer acquisition in 2025; the 2025 outlook was withdrawn and quarterly reporting dropped (half-year/annual only). No durable moat identified. Sources: https://www.edisongroup.com/research/managing-cash/BM-2391/ ; https://daytraders.com/news/2025/11/06/cliq-announces-third-quarter-2025-results
thesis.main_shareholders: Dylan Media B.V. (Netherlands vehicle created to facilitate a delisting, reportedly alongside members of management) held ~19.1% plus agreements for 21.2% = ~40.3% in June 2025. In 2026 it requisitioned an EGM (24 Apr 2026) approving a company partial repurchase offer for up to ~51% of shares at EUR 3.85, which Dylan Media did not tender into; acceptance period extended to 8 Jul 2026. A July 2026 headline states Dylan Media is above 60% after the buyback, but the article body did not confirm the final percentage and no voting-rights notification was located - treat the current stake as unverified (research gap). Remaining holders are small; aggregator institutional data (Simply Wall St) appears stale. Sources: https://finder.techleap.nl/news/feed/dylan-media-acquires-40-3-of-cliq ; https://www.onenewspage.com/n/Press+Releases/1ztf28oo34/Cliq-Digital-AG-decides-to-conduct-public.htm ; https://www.boerse-express.com/news/articles/cliq-digital-aktie-dylan-media-ueber-60-prozent-nach-rueckkauf-926896

Controlling/near-controlling shareholder with management links using company cash for large partial buybacks (up to ~51% at EUR 3.85 in 2026), and the board has said a delisting could be considered if Dylan Media reaches 60%+ - minority holders face delisting/illiquidity risk. Conflicting reports on whether delisting is still being considered, and an unverified search snippet about a further October 2026 10% repurchase offer at EUR 6.07 - check company ad-hoc releases. Reduced disclosure (quarterly reporting dropped). Sources: https://briefglance.com/companies/cliq-digital-ag/pulses/39338 ; https://pro.stockalarm.io/quote/CLQDF/news ; https://www.generation-nt.com/communiques-presse/cliq-digital-ag-decides-to-conduct-public-partial-share-repurchase-2082403 ; https://www.edisongroup.com/research/managing-cash/BM-2391/
thesis.insider_ownership: Edison states Dylan Media holds its stake 'alongside some of the management team', but the individual holdings of CEO Luc Voncken or other board members, and the ultimate owners of Dylan Media, were not identified in this search (Simply Wall St lists Voncken's ownership as n/a).
