thesis.business_description: Anpario plc (UK, AIM-listed) produces and distributes natural animal-feed additives for animal health, nutrition and biosecurity (e.g. Orego-Stim oregano-oil products, Optomega algae omega-3, plus the Bio-Vet range acquired in the US), selling to livestock producers and feed mills globally. FY2025 (Dec year-end, reported 31 Mar 2026): revenue +24% to GBP 47.2m (GBP 40.5m like-for-like excluding Bio-Vet, +12%), gross margin 50.9%, adjusted EBITDA GBP 9.6m (+38%), PBT GBP 8.0m (+54%), basic EPS 40.20p, year-end cash GBP 12.4m; total dividend 12.50p. Sources: https://www.ticker.app/lse/ANP/rns/2026-03-31/Final-Results/7232Y ; https://joshthompson.co.uk/investing/anpario-54-profit-surge-record-revenue-2025-final-results/
thesis.competitive_position: A small, niche player in the global feed-additive market focused on natural, patented products (benefiting from UK Patent Box tax relief) with premium gross margins (~51%); growth strategy combines organic expansion with bolt-ons such as Bio-Vet (final earn-out paid in 2025). It competes against much larger diversified animal-nutrition groups; specific market-share data was not found in this search. Debt-free with net cash. Sources: https://www.ticker.app/lse/ANP/rns/2026-03-31/Final-Results/7232Y ; https://joshthompson.co.uk/investing/anpario-54-profit-surge-record-revenue-2025-final-results/
thesis.main_shareholders: Aggregator (Simply Wall St, undated): Unicorn Asset Management 9.12%, Aberdeen Group 7.65%, Gresham House Asset Management 6.84%; top 25 holders ~65%; institutions >50% (Feb 2026). Official TR-1s: Downing LLP 3.12% (638,232 shares) as of 26 Feb 2026 (down from 4.09%, partly via transfer of a 2.59% holding to Foresight Group); older notices include Amati Global Investors 5.56% and Investec 9.98% (Apr 2022) - stale. The company's AIM Rule 26 significant-shareholder page was not retrieved. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/food-beverage-tobacco/aim-anp/anpario-shares/ownership ; https://www.ticker.app/lse/ANP/rns/2026-03-03/Holding(s)-in-Company/0177V ; https://www.ticker.app/lse/ANP/rns/2022-04-20/holdings-in-company/7834I
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources. Standard caveats: small-cap AIM stock with limited liquidity; earnings depend on agricultural/livestock cycles and export markets, and on the integration of the Bio-Vet acquisition; part of the 2025 EPS growth came from a lower tax rate (15.4% vs 20.6%) aided by Patent Box. Sources: https://joshthompson.co.uk/investing/anpario-54-profit-surge-record-revenue-2025-final-results/ ; https://www.ticker.app/lse/ANP/rns/2026-03-31/Final-Results/7232Y
thesis.insider_ownership: CEO Richard Edwards held 245,796 shares (~1.2%) after exercising EMI options on 16 Dec 2024 (latest PDMR notice found); holdings of Group Finance Director Marc Wilson and non-executives (chair Kate Allum since 2021) were not quantified in this search. Former non-executive chairman Peter Lawrence retired in June 2021 with ~0.1%. No controlling insider. Sources: https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/directorpdmr-shareholding-dsfaogmfsj2l8jk.html ; https://www.sharesmagazine.co.uk/news/market/LSE20210422160544_3951695/directorpdmr-shareholding

thesis.business_description: The Bank of Greece is Greece's central bank (Athens), a member of the Eurosystem responsible for implementing ECB monetary policy in Greece, banking supervision, payment systems and reserve management; unusually, its shares (19,864,886) are listed on Euronext Athens. 2025 profit was EUR 257.7m after a EUR 169.2m increase in provisions; net result of pooling of monetary income was EUR 1,340.3m (2024: EUR 3,348.8m). Of the profit, EUR 13.3m was distributed as dividend (EUR 0.6720/share gross, paid 30 Apr 2026) and EUR 244.4m transferred to the Greek State. Sources: https://www.athexgroup.gr/sites/default/files/hermes_3/2026-03/en/2e0196e3-5cb0-463f-8196-e35cb0963f61/53_1088_2026_English_2.pdf ; https://www.athexgroup.gr/sites/default/files/hermes_3/2026-03/en/3ad3f0aa-ebae-4b0d-93f0-aaebae9b0d97/Financial%20statement%20BANK%20OF%20GREECE%20S.A.%20%282025%2CAnnual%20report%2CParent%29.pdf ; https://athens.euronext.com/en/more-options/announcements/bank-greece-cash-distribution-23-04-2026
thesis.competitive_position: Not a competitive business: it is a statutory monopoly central bank whose earnings derive from Eurosystem monetary income and its own portfolios, set by monetary policy rather than commercial competition. For equity holders it behaves like a fixed-income instrument - the dividend has been EUR 0.67/share, described in notices as 12% of the Bank's capital, across many years (2008, 2011 and 2025 notices), with residual profit going to the State. Sources: https://athens.euronext.com/en/node/564670 ; https://www.athexgroup.gr/sites/default/files/hermes_3/2026-04/en/090e4be7-81fc-482a-8e4b-e781fc082a20/53_1922_2026_English_2.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Wikipedia (as of early 2024, secondary source): Greek government interests ~21%, of which ~8.9% held directly by the State and ~12.4% via the National Social Security Fund (e-EFKA); the rest is widely dispersed with no single holder known above 1%. A 2011 Bank of Greece regulatory notice confirms the State's direct holding of 1,774,088 shares = 8.93%. A current official shareholder table was not located - research gap. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Greece ; https://www.athexgroup.gr/en/more-options/announcements/notification-34
thesis.red_flags: Shareholders have very limited rights: one vote per 75 shares (total 264,865 voting rights) and, since a 2012 Statute amendment (ratified by Law 4099/2012), all financial rights including dividends are suspended for shareholders supervised by the Bank of Greece; dividend is effectively capped at 12% of capital, so earnings growth does not accrue to shareholders. Profit is volatile and depends on ECB interest-rate policy and provisioning for financial risks. Not a typical 'value stock' - the shares behave like a perpetual fixed-coupon instrument. Sources: https://athens.euronext.com/en/node/564670 ; https://www.athexgroup.gr/documents/10180/43440/53_9012_2012_Greek_1.doc/d88bee7c-1b28-4ade-aab8-b4933ff27a6b ; https://www.athexgroup.gr/sites/default/files/hermes_3/2026-03/en/2e0196e3-5cb0-463f-8196-e35cb0963f61/53_1088_2026_English_2.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: Not applicable in a meaningful sense: governance is by the Governor and General Council appointed under the Bank's Statute/Greek law, not by shareholders; no holdings by board members/executives were identified. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Greece ; https://athens.euronext.com/en/node/564670

thesis.business_description: Introl S.A. is a Katowice-based holding of more than ten companies operating mainly in power/energy engineering, environmental protection and industrial automation (subsidiaries include Introl-Energomontaż, INtrol Pro-ZAP, RAControls, IB Systems and Introl Automatyka). It has been listed on the WSE since 2007. 2024 consolidated revenue was PLN 643.57m; H1 2025 revenue fell to PLN 255.85m from 305.95m, with EBITDA of PLN 21.05m (from 30.7m). Sources: https://inwestycje.pl/gielda/introl-mial-442-mln-zl-zysku-netto-2105-mln-zl-zysku-ebitda-w-i-pol-2025-r/ ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/wiadomosci/INL
thesis.competitive_position: A mid-sized Polish engineering and automation contractor whose diversification across energy, environmental and automation niches is presented by management as a safety buffer. It has historically grown by acquiring smaller engineering firms and has said it is interested in acquisitions in the Polish energy sector. It is exposed to Polish industrial and energy capex cycles; named competitors and market shares were not found in this search. Sources: https://www.parkiet.com/budownictwo/art21037871-introl-buforem-bezpieczenstwa-jest-dywersyfikacja-dzialalnosci ; https://www.money.pl/gielda/wiadomosci/artykul/introl-zapowiada-przejecie-w-polskim-sektorze,94,0,2031198.html
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Stockwatch (aggregator, based on ESPI notifications): Wiesław Józef Kapral together with Weka Investments sp. z o.o. holds 12,023,979 shares (46.78%), last change 27 Sep 2022, and Józef Bodziony together with Svanser Prosta sp. z o.o. holds 8,854,288 shares (34.45%), last change 21 Dec 2023. Together they hold about 81%. Kapral's 2022 ESPI notice confirms a move from 44.81% to 46.78% of votes. These figures may be stale; no 2025-2026 official shareholder table was located. Sources: https://www.stockwatch.pl/gpw/introl,akcjonariat,dane-finansowe.aspx ; https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art37127571-introl-s-a
thesis.red_flags: No accounting or litigation issues were identified from official sources. Caveats: about 81% is held by two insiders, so free float and liquidity are low. Results deteriorated in H1 2025 (revenue -16%, EBIT down from PLN 21.15m to 12.12m). As a contractor it is exposed to project margins and Polish energy-sector capex. An EGM was called for 14 September 2026, and this search did not reveal the content of its resolutions. Payouts have been generous, including an extraordinary dividend of PLN 0.41/share approved January 2026, and the company has a history of buybacks. Sources: https://inwestycje.pl/gielda/introl-mial-442-mln-zl-zysku-netto-2105-mln-zl-zysku-ebitda-w-i-pol-2025-r/ ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/142833,dywidendowe-podsumowanie-dwoch-pierwszych-tygodni-2026-r
thesis.insider_ownership: Both major holders are insiders: Józef Bodziony is President of the Management Board (about 34.45% with Svanser Prosta), and Wiesław Józef Kapral is Deputy Chairman of the Supervisory Board (about 46.78% with Weka Investments). Insiders therefore control about 81% (aggregator data, last updated 2022/2023). Sources: https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/akcje/INTROL/wladze-zatrudnienie ; https://www.stockwatch.pl/gpw/introl,akcjonariat,dane-finansowe.aspx

thesis.business_description: Tharisa plc (Cyprus-domiciled; primary JSE listing, also LSE) is an integrated resource group producing platinum group metals (PGMs) and chrome concentrates from the open-pit Tharisa Mine in South Africa's Bushveld Complex, with an underground extension under development and the Karo Platinum project in Zimbabwe. FY2026 (year to 30 Sep 2026) PGM output rose ~11% to 153,700 oz and chrome to ~1.56Mt, within guidance; Q4 PGM 41,000 oz. Sources: https://miningmx.com/news/2026-10-13-tharisa-lifts-q4-production-keeps-karo-on-track/ ; https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/tharisa-annual-platinum-group-metal-and-chrome-output-meets-guidance
thesis.competitive_position: A mid-tier, low-cost co-product producer whose chrome revenue diversifies PGM price exposure (unlike pure PGM miners); growth hinges on the Tharisa underground project (450m developed and 52kt mined in Q3 FY2026, on budget) and Karo Platinum (25-year special mining lease signed with Zimbabwe in Aug 2026; phase-one capex ~USD 240m of ~USD 516-545m total; first ore targeted Q4 2027; concentrate offtake with Valterra Platinum), funded by a USD 300m 5-year senior secured Nordic bond priced Sept 2026 at 98% with an 11.00% coupon. Sources: https://www.miningweekly.com/article/tharisa-reports-project-development-progress-steady-third-quarter-production-2026-07-14 ; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/tharisa-di---ths/successful-pricing-us-300m-senior-sec-nordic-bond/9766631 ; https://www.businessday.co.za/companies/company-strategy/2026-09-11-tharisa-prices-300m-bond-to-advance-karo-platinum-project-in-zimbabwe/
thesis.main_shareholders: Official >5% table (Corporate Governance report, FY2025 annual report) was not retrieved. Aggregator data (MarketScreener, date unclear): holder attributed to Adonis Pouroulis 40.75% (likely the Pouroulis family-linked Medway Developments vehicle, which Moneyweb lists as a major shareholder - unconfirmed), Rance Holdings Ltd 12.73% (38,526,509 shares; an earlier snapshot shows 9.163%), Fujian Wuhang Stainless Steel Products 8.836% (26,737,540 shares). Simply Wall St separately lists Chow Tai Fook Capital at 9.36% - conflicting/unreconciled. Treat as aggregator-only and verify. Sources: https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/THARISA-PLC-16933108/company-shareholders/ ; https://www.moneyweb.co.za/tools-and-data/click-a-company/THA/ ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/materials/otc-tihr.f/tharisa/ownership ; https://www.tharisa.com/pdf/investors/annual-results/2025/afs-2025.pdf
thesis.red_flags: Related-party exposure: Karo was originally controlled by the Pouroulis family (Tharisa bought into Karo Holdings from family-linked parties; Medway Settlements holds part of Karo Mining per the annual report). Jurisdiction risk in Zimbabwe and construction risk on a USD 500m+ project; expensive 11% secured bond reduces balance-sheet flexibility - net cash fell to USD 10.7m at 30 Jun 2026 from USD 54.7m at 31 Mar 2026, before the bond. Commodity price exposure to PGMs and chrome. Sources: https://businesstimes.co.zw/tharisa-acquires-27pc-stake-in-karo-holdings/ ; https://www.tharisa.com/pdf/investors/annual-results/2025/afs-2025.pdf ; https://www.businessday.co.za/companies/company-strategy/2026-09-11-tharisa-prices-300m-bond-to-advance-karo-platinum-project-in-zimbabwe/ ; https://businessreport.co.za/companies/2026-07-14-tharisas-new-projects-gathered-pace-while-third-quarter-pgm-production-increased/
thesis.insider_ownership: The founding Pouroulis family is the dominant holder (see ~40.75% aggregator figure). CEO Phoevos Pouroulis ~2.83% (8,324,656 shares, Simply Wall St). Founder Loucas Pouroulis held shares via LTIP vestings (e.g. 385,372 shares under LTIP 2022) and stepped down as chairman effective 1 Oct 2026 after 15+ years, becoming Founding Chairman Emeritus; lead independent director Carol Bell takes the chair. Exact family percentages need confirmation from the annual report. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/materials/lse-ths/tharisa-shares/ownership ; https://miningmx.com/2026-09-30-loucas-pouroulis-bows-out-15-year-stint-at-tharisa/ ; https://investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/tharisa-di---ths/director-pdmr-shareholding/5390085

thesis.business_description: Profile Systems & Software SA, established in 1990 and headquartered in Athens, Greece, develops software for the global banking, investment and wealth-management industries, with named products including Axia, IMSplus, FMS.next (and FMS.next Payments), RiskAvert, a Native Wealth Management mobile app, GS Market Suite, Plexus and Registry, serving clients such as National Bank of Greece, EFG Eurobank, ING and ABN AMRO. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Profile_Systems_and_Software ; https://musaffa.com/stock/PROF.AT/
thesis.competitive_position: Internationally oriented Greek fintech/wealth-management software vendor, with international activity representing roughly 70% of total sales in 2023; grew via acquisitions including Thessaloniki-based Profile Technologies (2020 regional development hub), a 100% stake in Nordic asset/fund-management software provider Euronext Centevo (2021), and a majority stake in Algosystems. Reported 2021 group turnover of €20.12m, up from €15.04m in 2020. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Profile_Systems_and_Software
thesis.main_shareholders: A Simply Wall St ownership page (undated) names Charalambos Stasinopoulos as the largest shareholder with approximately 41.4%, followed by Norges Bank Investment Management at ~4.25% and Spyridon Barbatos at ~2.31% (top 21 shareholders holding 58.02% in total). Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/software/lse-0n1c/profile-systems-software-shares/ownership. This is corroborated by official Athens Exchange flagging notices: in November 2024, Norges Bank crossed the 5% voting-rights threshold with 1,250,932 shares (5.08%), then a later November 2024 notice showed its holding reduced to 1,205,932 shares (4.90%). Source: https://athens.euronext.com/en/node/962913 ; https://athens.euronext.com/en/node/963744. We could not independently confirm Stasinopoulos's exact current percentage from an official Athens Exchange Law 3556/2007 notification in this search, though his large stake is consistent across the aggregator data; this should be checked against Profile's current major-shareholder disclosure.
thesis.red_flags: Significant founder/insider concentration (Charalambos Stasinopoulos reportedly ~41% per aggregator data) gives one individual substantial control, a disclosed structure typical of Greek tech small-caps rather than a hidden issue. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/software/lse-0n1c/profile-systems-software-shares/ownership

thesis.business_description: Zagreb-based crude oil transport, storage and reloading operator (established 1974) running the JANAF system, the Croatian part of the Adria pipeline, which carries crude from the Omisalj terminal on Krk (Adriatic) to refineries in Central and Eastern Europe; domestic terminals include Sisak, Virje, Zitnjak and Slavonski Brod. Customers include MOL/Slovnaft and INA. Pipeline length is inconsistent across sources (about 759 km vs 622 km in a 2015 report). Secondary-source figures: 2024 revenue EUR 136.1m, net income EUR 48.3m, about 441-454 employees (Wikipedia/Marketscreener, aggregators). Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jadranski_naftovod ; https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/JADRANSKI-NAFTOVOD-D-D-20702341/
thesis.competitive_position: Quasi-monopoly strategic infrastructure: the main route for seaborne crude into Hungary, Slovakia and (historically) Serbia, a role that grew as Druzhba flows became unreliable. MOL says it relies more on the Adriatic pipeline since a Druzhba outage began in late January 2026. Revenue is tariff/storage based with a state-controlled regulatory and political overlay. Detailed throughput (tonnes), capacity utilisation and 2025 full-year financials were not located in this search; the 2025 annual reports were published on ZSE on 28 Apr 2026 but their content was not read. Sources: https://pgjonline.com/news/2026/march/druzhba-outage-spurs-eu-complaint-over-russian-crude-transit-via-croatia-pipeline ; https://eho.zse.hr/en/financial-reports/view/31668
thesis.main_shareholders: No official current register located in this search; treat as a research gap. Press reports of 2022 (Lider) gave: Croatian state ministry of state assets ~52%, CERP (state restructuring agency) ~26%, INA ~12%; a 2019 SeeNews report gave similar figures with the remainder in small holders. A later Lider article says the state holds about 84% - CONFLICTING with the 52/26/12 split (which sums to 90%); unresolved. Lider also reported unofficial talk of MOL acquiring a JANAF share package via exchange for INA shares (unconfirmed, from 24sata); the Prime Minister said in Oct 2025 JANAF is not for sale. Sources: https://en.lider.media/?p=207997 ; https://glashrvatske.hrt.hr/en/politics/plenkovic-janaf-is-not-for-sale-it-is-and-will-remain-croatian-12372846 ; https://seenews.com/news/croatias-janaf-to-pay-859-kuna-116-euroshare-dividend-for-2018-667061
thesis.red_flags: State-controlled company (political/governance risk; dividend and tariff policy follow state interests). Geopolitical/regulatory: MOL and Slovnaft filed a complaint with the EU competition authorities (March 2026) alleging JANAF charges 3-4x fair price for Russian seaborne-oil transit and refuses such transit; JANAF denies it. Oct 2025 dispute with Slovnaft over reduced non-Russian crude deliveries (JANAF denies breach of contract). JANAF halted deliveries to Serbia's NIS in 2022 and later after US sanctions on NIS. Dividend per share is volatile: EUR 28.81 in 2025 and EUR 20.21 proposed for 31 Jul 2026 (per ZSE announcements). Ownership percentages in public sources conflict. Sources: https://ceenergynews.com/oil-gas/mol-eu-complaint-janaf-russian-oil/ ; https://hydrocarbonprocessing.com/news/2025/10/slovak-refiner-slovnaft-says-croatias-janaf-cuts-supply-of-non-russian-crude/ ; https://eho.zse.hr/en/issuer-announcements/view/67420
thesis.website: https://www.janaf.hr (company domain; not independently verified by search in this run)
thesis.insider_ownership: Could not locate named board or management holdings with percentages in this search; treat as a research gap. Board/management appointments are state-influenced given the Republic of Croatia's controlling stake (unconfirmed %, see main_shareholders). Source: https://eho.zse.hr/en/financial-reports/view/31668

thesis.business_description: Nichols plc (Newton-le-Willows, UK) is a soft-drinks group best known as owner of the Vimto brand, operating a Packaged segment (UK and International, incl. Middle East and Africa, increasingly via a higher-margin concentrate/local-production model) and an Out of Home segment (dispense drinks to hospitality/leisure). FY2025 revenue +1.3% to ~GBP 175m, PBT +22% to GBP 29.2m, adjusted EBITDA GBP 33.8m, year-end cash GBP 55.8m; H1 2026 revenue +4.7% to GBP 89.5m and adjusted operating profit +3.7% to GBP 14.1m, with Africa sales +17.2%. Sources: https://www.esmmagazine.com/a-brands/vimto-maker-nichols-posts-1-3-revenue-growth-in-fy-2025-304389 ; https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/nichols-ups-dividend-annual-pretax-profit-jumps-outlook-optimistic ; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/nichols--nicl/2026-interim-results-/9692319
thesis.competitive_position: A small branded player against global soft-drink majors, relying on the heritage Vimto brand (strong in the UK and with Ramadan-linked demand in the Middle East) and an asset-light outsourced manufacturing model; strategy is UK Packaged growth, shifting Africa to concentrate supply and production closer to consumers, and improving Out of Home profitability after exiting low-margin Starslush. Cash-rich with no debt cited in sources. CEO: Andrew Milne. Sources: https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/stock-market-news/aim-and-small-cap-news/aim-bulletin/archive/nichols-fy25-revenues-tick-up,-confident-in-fy26-outlook ; https://www.foodanddrinktechnology.com/news/69004/nichols-mixes-growth-across-markets/
thesis.main_shareholders: Per a 'Holdings in Company' RNS (1 Dec 2025): the Nichols family Concert Party holds 13,122,925 shares = 35.89% of voting rights. Octopus Investments increased to 9.04% as of 24 Mar 2025 (TR-1). Aggregator lists (Simply Wall St) show other individual family figures (e.g. Nichols Family Trust 8.53%) that conflict with the Dec 2025 filing - likely stale. Sources: https://www.ticker.app/lse/NICL/rns/2025-12-01/Holdings-in-Company/7563J ; https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/octopus-investments-increases-stake-in-nichols-plc ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/food-beverage-tobacco/aim-nicl/nichols-shares/ownership
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources. Caveats: significant family concert party (~36%) influences control; exposure to Middle East geopolitics (company 'closely monitoring' disruption, April 2026) and shipment-timing volatility around Ramadan; slow FY2025 top-line growth (+1.3%) and no special dividend in 2025 versus 2024. Sources: https://www.ticker.app/lse/NICL/rns/2026-04-21/AGM-Trading-Update/2082B ; https://www.esmmagazine.com/a-brands/vimto-maker-nichols-posts-1-3-revenue-growth-in-fy-2025-304389 ; https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/stock-market-news/aim-and-small-cap-news/aim-bulletin/archive/nichols-fy25-revenues-tick-up,-confident-in-fy26-outlook
thesis.insider_ownership: Founding Nichols family (concert party 35.89%) per Dec 2025 filing: after John Nichols transferred 500,000 shares to each of his three children on 25 Nov 2025, Matthew Nichols 4.33%, James Nichols 4.32%, Katharine Kropp 4.27%, John Nichols 1.37% (from 5.47%); remaining concert-party shares held by other family members/trusts not itemised in the summary. Holdings of non-family executives (e.g. CEO Andrew Milne) not located. Source: https://www.ticker.app/lse/NICL/rns/2025-12-01/Holdings-in-Company/7563J

thesis.business_description: Thermador Groupe (Saint-Quentin-Fallavier, near Lyon, France) is a holding of specialised wholesale distribution subsidiaries (e.g. Thermador, Isocel, Aello, Axelair, Odrea, DPI) selling central-heating and domestic-hot-water accessories, heating pumps, plumbing equipment, taps, building valves, ventilation and industrial/water-cycle products mainly to professional distributors in France and Europe. 2025 consolidated turnover was ~EUR 501.7m (slightly down; sources differ between -0.4% reported and -2.9% like-for-like); H1 2026 turnover reached ~EUR 288.0m, +11.3% (+5.6% at constant scope). Sources: https://www.sustainabilityreports.com/thermador-groupe/2025/universal-registration-document ; https://quartr.com/events/thermador-groupe-sa-thep-q2-2026-tu_FeoYlIyM ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/fr/capital-goods/epa-thep/thermador-groupe-shares/news/thermador-groupe-first-half-2025-earnings-eps-243-vs-275-in
thesis.competitive_position: A decentralised group of niche, stock-holding specialist distributors with strong logistics, positioned between manufacturers and builders' merchants; growth comes from organic expansion and regular bolt-on acquisitions - most recently C2AI (France, consolidated from 1 Jul 2025) and Quilinox (Spain, from 1 Oct 2025) in industrial and water-cycle distribution. Revenue fell in 2024 (~-13%) amid the French housing/renovation downturn before recovering in H1 2026. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/fr/capital-goods/epa-thep/thermador-groupe-shares/news/thermador-groupe-first-half-2025-earnings-eps-243-vs-275-in ; https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/fr:thep/revenue ; https://quartr.com/events/thermador-groupe-sa-thep-q2-2026-tu_FeoYlIyM
thesis.main_shareholders: No controlling holder. Aggregators (ABC Bourse/Zonebourse, 2026 snapshots): Investmentaktiengesellschaft fur langfristige Investoren TGV (Norman Rentrop) ~9.0%, FMR LLC ~7.6%, Credit Mutuel Equity ~6.8-6.9%, FCP Thermador Groupe (employee fund) ~3.8%, Mr & Mrs de Sereys ~3.5%, treasury ~0.3%. A Dutreil pact signed 2 Oct 2024 for two years (initiated by heirs of founder Guy Vincent) covers 2,313,461 shares = 25.14% of capital / 25.23% of votes, including TGV 9%, de Sereys 3.47%, Guy Vincent estate 2.97% and CEO Guillaume Robin 0.76%; the parties state it is not concerted action. Official URD shareholder table not retrieved. Sources: https://www.abcbourse.com/analyses/chiffres/THEPp ; https://www.zonebourse.com/cours/action/THERMADOR-GROUPE-43328026/societe-actionnaires/ ; https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/ECO/2024/10/FCECO076237_20241002.pdf ; https://www.finanzwire.com/article/thermador-groupe-epa-thep-thermador-groupe-announces-dutreil-pact-to-safeguard-shares-E4jwMVBmeNb
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources. Caveats: cyclical exposure to French residential construction/renovation (2024 revenue ~-13%, H1 2025 EPS EUR 2.43 vs 2.75); several subsidiaries saw double-digit declines in H1 2025 (Odrea -14.9%, DPI -19.6%, Thermador -12.0%); the two-year Dutreil pact (Oct 2024) comes up for renewal around Oct 2026. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/fr/capital-goods/epa-thep/thermador-groupe-shares/news/thermador-groupe-first-half-2025-earnings-eps-243-vs-275-in ; https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/ECO/2024/10/FCECO076237_20241002.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: Directors and officers ~5.9% as a group (ABC Bourse, aggregator). Chairman & CEO Guillaume Robin holds at least 0.76% within the Dutreil pact (total holding not located) and made small open-market purchases in March 2026 (e.g. 145 shares at EUR 68.80). Founder Guy Vincent's estate/heirs hold ~2.97% within the pact. Sources: https://www.finanzwire.com/article/thermador-groupe-epa-thep-thermador-groupe-announces-dutreil-pact-to-safeguard-shares-E4jwMVBmeNb ; https://www.abcbourse.com/marches/transactions_dirigeants/FR0013333432p

thesis.business_description: Brunel International N.V., headquartered in Amsterdam, is a global staffing and workforce-solutions company providing contract staffing, recruitment, payroll/employer-of-record, HR consultancy, project management, immigration and relocation services across energy, engineering, automotive, finance, IT, legal and pharma sectors, with its largest revenue segment (Energy) supplying engineers, project managers and consultants to oil & gas companies in over 40 countries. Source: https://www.globaldata.com/company-profile/brunel-international-nv/ ; https://morningstar.com.au/investments/security/fra/3BY3
thesis.competitive_position: Internationally diversified technical/engineering staffing group (~12,200-12,900 employees/contractors depending on source) with reporting segments spanning DACH, the Netherlands, the Americas, Australasia and Asia, giving it geographic and sector diversification beyond pure oil & gas exposure. Listed on Euronext Amsterdam. Source: https://www.globaldata.com/company-profile/brunel-international-nv/
thesis.main_shareholders: Brunel is majority-controlled by founder Jan Brand via his holding vehicle Noverhead Holding S.à r.l. Per the Dutch AFM substantial-holdings register, Noverhead Holding's most recent notification (transaction date 14 May 2025, last updated December 2025) reports 30,459,592 shares = 60.23% of total holding; prior AFM filings show 60.05% in 2020 and 58.56% in 2018, indicating a long-stable, slightly increasing majority stake. Source: https://www.afm.nl/en/sector/registers/meldingenregisters/substantiele-deelnemingen/details?id=175002 ; https://www.afm.nl/en/sector/registers/meldingenregisters/substantiele-deelnemingen/details?id=68850. CEO Jan Arie van Barneveld succeeded founder Jan Brand in 2000 but his personal shareholding was not identified in this search.
thesis.red_flags: Majority founder control (Jan Brand, ~60% via Noverhead Holding, per official AFM filings) concentrates governance power with one individual, a long-disclosed structure rather than a hidden issue, but a standard minority-shareholder consideration. Source: https://www.afm.nl/en/sector/registers/meldingenregisters/substantiele-deelnemingen/details?id=175002. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Global Dominion Access S.A. (Dominion) is a Bilbao-based multi-technology services and engineering group, founded in 1999 and listed in Spain since 2016. Its 2025 reporting simplification uses two units: GDT (energy and digital transition, i.e. renewables, grids, telecoms, hospital infrastructure) and GDE (industrial transition, circular economy, waste and water treatment). It serves industry, telecoms, energy and infrastructure clients in about 30-35 countries, with annual turnover of about EUR 1.1bn. H1 2025 sales were EUR 537.6m and EBITDA was EUR 73.8m (13.7% margin). Sources: https://www.bolsasymercados.es/en/bme-exchange/prices-and-markets/shares/detail.global-dominion-access-es0105130001.html ; https://www.estrategiasdeinversion.com/actualidad/noticias/bolsa-espana/dominion-aumenta-un-10-su-ebitda-y-obtiene-un-n-833591
thesis.competitive_position: A mid-sized Spanish outsourcing/engineering integrator spun out of CIE Automotive (CIE distributed about 50% of Dominion to its shareholders in 2018). It has grown historically through serial acquisitions across services and '360' turnkey projects. It is now pruning the portfolio (Dominican Republic assets sale for EUR 87m cash, French activities sold) and pursuing a 2026-2029 strategic plan. It competes with larger Spanish and European engineering/services groups; named peers and market share were not found in this search. Sources: https://www.bolsamania.com/noticias/ultimas/economiamotor--los-accionistas-de-cie-automotive-aprueban-la-salida-de-dominion-y-recibir-el-50-de-su-capital--3259397.html ; https://www.estrategiasdeinversion.com/actualidad/noticias/empresas/domnion-presenta-su-plan-estrategico-2026-2029-n-911823 ; https://www.estrategiasdeinversion.com/actualidad/noticias/bolsa-espana/dominion-aumenta-un-10-su-ebitda-y-obtiene-un-n-833591
thesis.main_shareholders: Per an undated Bolsamania report citing CNMV records: Acek Desarrollo y Gestión Industrial (Riberas family holding, also the reference holder of CIE Automotive) 17.288%, CEO Mikel Barandiaran Landín 5.093%, Cartera e Inversiones Blaster (linked to Barandiaran) 5.078%, Indumenta Pueri (Domínguez de la Maza/Mayoral family) about 5.009%, Cobas Asset Management (García Paramés) 5.001%, and Corporación Financiera Alba at a similar level (exact % not given). Stakes near the 5% threshold may have changed, so verify against the CNMV register; no dated official table was retrieved. Sources: https://www.bolsamania.com/noticias/empresas/parames-aumenta-participacion-global-dominion-hasta-5-valorada-23-millones--22733850.html
thesis.red_flags: No restatement or formal profit warning was found. Caveats: earnings quality is diluted by valuation charges on Dominican Republic solar assets (EUR 14m in H1 2025; a EUR 18.5m extraordinary effect cited on the Feb 2026 call), and attributable net profit is thin (EUR 5m in H1 2025; EUR 7.1m in H1 2026). The projects segment is weak because of macro and geopolitical factors. Net debt was EUR 207m at H1 2025 before divestment proceeds, versus a 1x net debt/EBITDA target. The share price fell about 21% over the past year per TradingView (undated snapshot). M&A-driven complexity adds risk. Sources: https://quartr.com/events/global-dominion-access-s-a-dom-q2-2026_ojjNv85J ; https://www.estrategiasdeinversion.com/actualidad/noticias/bolsa-espana/dominion-aumenta-un-10-su-ebitda-y-obtiene-un-n-833591 ; https://vn.tradingview.com/symbols/BME-DOM/
thesis.insider_ownership: CEO Mikel Barandiaran Landín (CEO since 2004) holds 5.093% directly, plus 5.078% through linked Cartera e Inversiones Blaster, about 10.2% combined per the CNMV-based report. The Riberas family (Acek, 17.288%) is linked to the board via its CIE Automotive heritage, but named Riberas directors' percentages were not confirmed in this search. Sources: https://www.bolsamania.com/noticias/empresas/parames-aumenta-participacion-global-dominion-hasta-5-valorada-23-millones--22733850.html ; https://www.globaldata.com/company-profile/global-dominion-access-sa/executives/

thesis.business_description: Hexatronic Group AB, headquartered in Gothenburg, Sweden, manufactures fiber-optic and copper communication cables, microducts, connectivity/network accessories, prefabricated optical distribution frames, wireless/5G and powered-fiber systems, and harsh-environment/sensor cable solutions, serving telecom operators, network owners and installers across Sweden, the rest of Europe, North America and APAC through roughly 40 subsidiaries. Source: https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/CHIX:HTROs/summary ; https://tracenable.com/company/hexatronic-group/group-entities
thesis.competitive_position: Growth-oriented Nordic fiber-infrastructure equipment maker serving the global broadband/fiber-to-the-home buildout, with ~1,900-2,000+ employees across its subsidiary network and primary revenue concentration in Europe and North America; listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. Source: https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/CHIX:HTROs/summary
thesis.main_shareholders: A November 2022 company press release on insider share sales indicates then-CEO Henrik Larsson Lyon held approximately 4,057,180-4,139,592 shares (figures vary slightly between the release and the company's executive-management page), and that deputy CEO Martin Åberg held a large stake (8,929,360 shares) via his holding company Chirp AB; both were stated to remain long-term shareholders after the disclosed sales. Source: https://hexatronic.com/hubfs/pressmeddelanden/2022-11-29-Hexatronics-VD-vice-VD-och-tv%C3%A5-ledande-befattningshavare-s%C3%A4ljer-aktier-Kvarst%C3%A5r-som-l%C3%A5ngsiktiga-aktie%C3%A4gare.pdf. Historically (2016 flagging notices), founder Gert Nordin held ~13.9% and chairman Göran Nordlund ~10.4%, while Accendo Capital held 4,720,109 shares = 13.7% of capital/votes. Source: https://www.hexatronic.com/hubfs/hexatronic.com/Press%20releases/SV/2016/2016-10-31-flaggningsmeddelande-accendo-capital.pdf. In September 2024, Henrik Larsson Lyon announced he would step down as CEO (after holding the role since 2014) but stated his intention to remain a shareholder. Source: https://mfn.se/one/a/hexatronic-group/president-and-ceo-henrik-larsson-lyon-has-decided-to-leave-hexatronic-83f5a985. We could not confirm a current (2025/2026), complete largest-shareholders percentage table from the company's investor-relations page in this search; the figures above are dated (2016-2022) and ownership has likely shifted since, especially following the September 2024 CEO change.
thesis.red_flags: Management/insider share sales were disclosed in November 2022 (CEO, deputy CEO and two other senior executives sold shares), and the long-time CEO departed in September 2024 — both disclosed, orderly events rather than governance red flags, but worth noting as a leadership-transition point. Source: https://mfn.se/one/a/hexatronic-group/president-and-ceo-henrik-larsson-lyon-has-decided-to-leave-hexatronic-83f5a985. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Grupo Empresarial San Jose (SANJOSE) is a construction-led group founded in 1962 in Pontevedra, Galicia, by the Rey family and still headquartered there. Construction (buildings, hospitals, industrial/energy plants and infrastructure) generated 91.6% of 2025 revenue and ~83% of the EUR 3,631m backlog at 31 Dec 2025 (+14%); other activities include energy/environment, concessions and services. FY2025: revenue EUR 1,588m (+1.9%), EBITDA EUR 89m (+20%), net profit about EUR 41m (+26%; an aggregator shows ~EUR 39.9m), dividend EUR 0.18. Spain is the core market (~81% of 9M 2025 activity); international work includes Chile (e.g. the Copiapo prison build-and-operate award, est. EUR 510m). Sources: https://www.estrategiasdeinversion.com/actualidad/noticias/bolsa-espana/san-jose-gana-41-millones-en-2025-un-26-mas-y-n-894131 ; https://iberian.property/news/market-updates/sanjose-earns-nearly-eur1-15-billion-through-september/ ; https://www.merca2.es/2026/03/05/san-jose-cartera-fichajes-2357581/
thesis.competitive_position: A mid-sized Spanish contractor, far smaller than ACS, Ferrovial, Acciona or Sacyr, with a niche in building construction (including the Santiago Bernabeu stadium refurbishment) and selective international projects (Latin America). It has rebuilt after a 2015-era debt restructuring and is positioned for Madrid's Operacion Chamartin / Madrid Nuevo Norte urban project, which has driven share-price speculation. Backlog growth (+14% in 2025) and a March 2026 board refresh with independent directors are recent positives. Sources: https://www.merca2.es/2024/10/24/san-jose-chamartin-2045580/ ; https://www.merca2.es/2026/03/05/san-jose-cartera-fichajes-2357581/ ; https://valenciaplaza.com/valenciaplaza/bolsas/grupo-san-jose-vuelve-a-superar-el-euro-en-bolsa-por-la-operacion-chamartin
thesis.main_shareholders: Chairman/CEO Jacinto Rey Gonzalez controls about 48.2-48.3% (48.29% per a 2021 Vozpopuli report and CNMV-declared figure cited in press; ~48.2% per a 2025 Estrategias de Inversion article). The Sanchez Avalos family is reported as the second-largest group at about 13% (press figure, date unclear). Former Telefonica chairman Juan Villalonga crossed 2% on 16 May 2025 (CNMV notification), making him roughly the fourth-largest holder; he has also declared 2.18% at one point. Figures come from press reports of CNMV filings rather than the IAGC directly; verify against CNMV's significant-holdings register. Sources: https://www.estrategiasdeinversion.com/actualidad/noticias/empresas/juan-villalonga-supera-el-2-de-participacion-en-n-815645 ; https://valenciaplaza.com/juan-villalonga-declara-tener-el-2-18-de-una-san-jose-en-stand-by-en-bolsa ; https://www.vozpopuli.com/economia/popular-san_jose-jacinto_rey_0_732526775.html
thesis.red_flags: (1) Near-majority family control with the Chairman also CEO (combined roles since a July 2015 CNMV filing) and his son as Vice-Chairman - limited minority protection. (2) History of financial distress: a mid-2010s liability restructuring cut debt sharply but ceded control of the real-estate arm to creditor banks, after earlier refinancing of a EUR 1.1bn syndicated loan. (3) Thin construction margins (2025 EBITDA ~5.6% of revenue) and fixed-price contract risk; heavy Spain concentration. (4) Share price sensitivity to the speculative Operacion Chamartin theme. No current litigation or accounting issues were identified in this search. Sources: https://www.ttrdata.com/en/radar/aggregated/Grupo-San-Jose-modifies-governance-structure/227683 ; https://www.vozpopuli.com/economia/popular-san_jose-jacinto_rey_0_732526775.html ; https://www.estrategiasdeinversion.com/actualidad/noticias/bolsa-espana/san-jose-gana-41-millones-en-2025-un-26-mas-y-n-894131
thesis.insider_ownership: Founding-family control: Jacinto Rey Gonzalez (Executive Chairman and CEO) holds ~48.2-48.3%; his son Jacinto Rey Laredo is Vice-Chairman (individual holding not found). Holdings of other directors were not located in this search; the company's IAGC section A.3 would confirm. Sources: https://www.estrategiasdeinversion.com/actualidad/noticias/empresas/juan-villalonga-supera-el-2-de-participacion-en-n-815645 ; https://www.merca2.es/2026/03/05/san-jose-cartera-fichajes-2357581/

name: Constantinou Bros Hotels Public Company Limited

thesis.business_description: Cyprus Stock Exchange-listed owner-operator of hotels in Paphos, Cyprus (headquartered in Paphos). Portfolio per third-party sources: Athena Beach Hotel, Athena Royal Beach Hotel, Pioneer Beach Hotel (4-star, 255 rooms) and Asimina Suites Hotel (5-star, 121 rooms); about 525 rooms in total per Cyprus Mail. FY2025: revenue EUR30.06m (+12%), average occupancy 79% (75% in 2024), net profit EUR8.43m (EUR7.68m in 2024), total assets about EUR162.7m, net assets about EUR107.6m; board proposed no dividend. Conflict: Stockopedia shows a different 2025 revenue figure (EUR66.64m), so scope/currency of that aggregator figure is unverified. Sources: https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/04/30/constantinou-bros-hotels-reports-e8-4-million-profit-for-2025 ; https://www.tradingview.com/symbols/CSECY-CBH ; https://www.stockopedia.com/share-prices/constantinou-bros-hotels-pcl-CSE:CBH/
thesis.competitive_position: Small, single-destination (Paphos, Cyprus) beach-resort hotel owner with a mix of 4- and 5-star assets; performance is tied to Cyprus tourism volumes and occupancy. Could not locate market-share data, competitor list or management strategy statements in this search; research gap. Latest guidance conflicts: the April 2026 results release expected 2026 revenue and profit roughly flat vs 2025, but a June 2026 announcement said H1 2026 results will be below 2025, that occupancy is expected below 2025 and that full-year results cannot safely be predicted. Sources: https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/06/18/constantinou-bros-hotels-warns-of-weaker-first-half-2026-results ; https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/04/30/constantinou-bros-hotels-reports-e8-4-million-profit-for-2025
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Cyprus Business News (CBN) shareholder rosters (2023, 2024 and a latest roundup referencing 30 June 2026): Andreas Constantinou, Chairman, 86.87%; free float about 12.85% (earlier lists 12.82-12.84%). No other 5%+ holder identified. This is a secondary press source built from exchange disclosures; the annual report shareholder table was not located in this search. Sources: https://www.cbn.com.cy/article/132145/major-shareholders-in-30-cypriot-companies-changes-in-the-share-capital-of-listed-firms ; https://www.cbn.com.cy/article/113087/the-major-shareholders-of-35-listed-companies-in-cyprus
thesis.red_flags: Control concentration: a single holder owns about 87%, leaving roughly 13% free float (very low liquidity, minimal minority influence). Single-region tourism exposure, and a June 2026 profit-warning-style announcement (H1 2026 below H1 2025, occupancy below 2025), which contradicts the April 2026 flat outlook; board cites Ukraine war and Middle East tensions. No hedging instruments were used in 2025 (interest-rate risk disclosed); an aggregator lists net debt of about USD78.8m, which is unverified and no loan terms or maturities were found. No dividend paid or proposed. Auditor is reported as Ernst & Young Cyprus (Stockopedia). No litigation or governance issues were found in this search, which was not an exhaustive legal check. Sources: https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/06/18/constantinou-bros-hotels-warns-of-weaker-first-half-2026-results ; https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/04/30/constantinou-bros-hotels-reports-e8-4-million-profit-for-2025 ; https://www.stockopedia.com/share-prices/constantinou-bros-hotels-pcl-CSE:CBH/
thesis.website: https://www.cbh-cyprus.com (domain taken from a search-tool reference to the company's website; not independently verified in this search)
thesis.insider_ownership: Chairman Andreas Constantinou holds 86.87% (CBN, as above). The company was reportedly founded by Andreas Konstantinou and Agathoclis Constantinou (TradingView profile; Simply Wall St gives a different founding date, 1979); holdings of Agathoclis Constantinou, other directors or executives, and whether the 86.87% is direct or indirect, were not located; research gap. Sources: https://www.cbn.com.cy/article/132145/major-shareholders-in-30-cypriot-companies-changes-in-the-share-capital-of-listed-firms ; https://www.tradingview.com/symbols/CSECY-CBH

thesis.business_description: Northern Bear PLC is a Newcastle upon Tyne-based specialist building and support services group listed on AIM, operating three segments: Roofing (slating, tiling, leadwork, refurbishment and maintenance for domestic, commercial and public-sector buildings), Materials Handling (supply, hire, service and maintenance of forklift trucks and warehouse equipment) and Specialist Building Services (smaller businesses in maintenance, electrical contracting, fire protection - e.g. Isoler - and sound insulation). Customers include local authorities, housing associations, NHS trusts, universities, contractors and national housebuilders, mainly in Northern England. FY to 31 Mar 2026 (prelims 16 Jul 2026): revenue GBP 86.1m (+10.2%), operating profit GBP 5.1m (FY25: GBP 3.4m), net cash GBP 6.2m. Sources: https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/NTBR/preliminary-results-cir0obnexoiqisa.html ; https://hl.co.uk/shares/shares-search-results/n/northern-bear-plc-ord-gbp0.01/company-information ; https://sharesmagazine.co.uk/news/market/LSE20250715070003_5737465/preliminary-results
thesis.competitive_position: A regional buy-and-build group of small trade businesses rather than a national player; its edge is local relationships and contract selectivity in the North of England (management attributed FY25 gross margin improvement to 24.6% from 23.1% to sales mix and careful contract selection). Competes with many local roofing/building contractors and forklift dealers; no reliable named competitor list was found (aggregator suggestions were poor matches). Growth drivers cited include fire protection (Isoler) and public-sector/social-housing maintenance demand; FY25 revenue was GBP 78.1m with pretax profit about GBP 3.1m. Sources: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/northern-bear-profit-rises-50-touts-strong-forward-order-book ; https://sharesmagazine.co.uk/news/market/LSE20250715070003_5737465/preliminary-results
thesis.main_shareholders: Most recent official holdings notice found (RNS, 13 Dec 2023, after a tender-offer buyback): Nicholas Beaumont-Dark 3,626,500 shares (26.42%), Steven Roberts 813,300 (5.93%), David Jay 561,510 (4.09%). Beaumont-Dark had been at 19.03% in April 2023 and ~13% in 2021. An undated summary associated Non-Executive Chairman Jeff Baryshnik's Cedarvale Holdings with ~25.6%, but this could not be verified in any filing found and may be stale. No 2024-2026 register was found; Fidelity lists top holders as 'no data'. Treat current figures as a research gap. Sources: https://sharesmagazine.co.uk/news/market/LSE20231213070019_5000999/holdings-in-company ; https://sharesmagazine.co.uk/news/market/LSE20230427070008_4751436/notification-of-holdings ; https://talent4boards.com/northern-bear-appoints-jeff-baryshnik-to-its-board-as-non-executive-director/
thesis.red_flags: No accounting or governance scandals identified from official sources. Risks: concentrated register (one holder ~26% as of Dec 2023, plus directors) and thin AIM liquidity; cyclical exposure to construction/maintenance and public-sector budgets; weather sensitivity in roofing; FY26 results mention an onerous lease provision at the Jennings site and a prior-year exceptional item relating to H Peel & Sons Ltd (details not found); frequent board changes in 2023-2024. Shareholder data is stale (2023). Sources: https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/NTBR/preliminary-results-cir0obnexoiqisa.html ; https://sharesmagazine.co.uk/news/market/LSE20231213070019_5000999/holdings-in-company
thesis.website: https://www.northernbearplc.com (official domain; not surfaced directly in search results, verify). Source: https://www.northernbearplc.com
thesis.insider_ownership: Executive Director Steve Roberts held 813,300 shares (5.93% per the Dec 2023 notice; holding reconfirmed on his reappointment in Jan 2024). John Davies became Group CEO in 2024; his holding was not found. Jeff Baryshnik was Non-Executive Chairman as of April 2023 (possible Cedarvale stake unverified); Hargreaves Lansdown currently lists Simon Carr as Non-Executive Chairman, suggesting a later change that was not confirmed via RNS. Nicholas Beaumont-Dark (26.42%) is a major outside holder; no evidence he sits on the board. Sources: https://www.ticker.app/lse/NTBR/rns/2024-01-18/Board-Changes/1391A ; https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/shares-search-results/n/northern-bear-plc-ord-gbp0.01/company-information ; https://sharesmagazine.co.uk/news/market/LSE20231213070019_5000999/holdings-in-company

thesis.business_description: Banka Intesa Sanpaolo d.d. (trading as Intesa Sanpaolo Bank Slovenia; formerly Banka Koper d.d., renamed in December 2016) is a universal commercial bank headquartered in Koper, Slovenia, serving retail, small-business and corporate clients mainly in Slovenia. Intesa Sanpaolo group reported 2025 figures for the bank of about EUR 60m net result, EUR 3.7bn direct customer deposits, EUR 2.7bn loans and roughly EUR 4.3bn total assets. Sources: https://group.intesasanpaolo.com/it/newsroom/tutte-le-news/news/2026/cambiamenti-leadership-international-banks ; https://sloveniatimes.com/11413/banka-koper-changing-its-name
thesis.competitive_position: Intesa Sanpaolo group describes it as the third-largest bank in Slovenia (group source only). Slovenian press reported 2023 market shares of about 9% in non-bank lending (EUR 2.47bn) and 8.3% in deposits (EUR 3.42bn), with record 2023 net profit of EUR 71.5m. 2024 profit of about EUR 68.5m and assets of about EUR 4.06bn come from aggregators (SeeNews, Simply Wall St). Its main strength is being part of the Intesa Sanpaolo international banks network. Mojca Kovac became CEO in March 2026, replacing Luigi Fuzio. Sources: https://group.intesasanpaolo.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026/03/intesa-sanpaolo-bank-slovenia-appoints-mojca-kova-as-ceo- ; https://www.sloveniabusiness.eu/business-news/intesa-sanpaolo-profit-up-more-than-300-in-2023 ; https://english.sta.si/2728966/intesa-san-paolo-net-profit-more-than-doubles ; https://seenews.com/companies/banka-intesa-sanpaolo-d-d-3682
thesis.main_shareholders: The bank is controlled by the Intesa Sanpaolo group. At 30 Sep 2016 Intesa Sanpaolo S.p.A. held 98.84% (525,218 shares). It then announced it would transfer 51% to its Croatian subsidiary Privredna banka Zagreb (PBZ) and keep about 48%. Press reports say the 51% sale to PBZ closed on 20 July (apparently 2017) for EUR 144.4m. SeeNews and Simply Wall St now list PBZ as the owner/parent. Current exact percentages (likely about 51% PBZ / about 48% Intesa Sanpaolo S.p.A. / about 1% minorities) could not be confirmed from a current annual report or LJSE filing in this search; treat them as a research gap. Sources: https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/migrated/news/PBZ-nSzdP02i4sm1Tjcy3jeQRQ__.pdf ; https://en.lider.media/?p=126485 ; https://seenews.com/companies/banka-intesa-sanpaolo-d-d-3682
thesis.red_flags: No accounting or litigation issues found in official sources. Structural risks: (1) about 99% group control (2016 figures) leaves a very small free float and thin LJSE liquidity. Dividend policy, capital allocation and any future squeeze-out or delisting are decided by the parent; no squeeze-out was found in this search. (2) Earnings are sensitive to rates: profit fell from EUR 71.5m (2023) to about EUR 68.5m (2024, aggregator) and about EUR 60m (2025, group source). (3) Aggregator profiles (e.g. Stockopedia) carry stale Banka Koper-era data, so verify figures against the bank's own reports. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/si/banks/ljse-bkp/banka-intesa-sanpaolo-d-d-shares/information ; https://stockopedia.com/share-prices/banka-intesa-sanpaolo-dd-LJE:BKP ; https://group.intesasanpaolo.com/it/newsroom/tutte-le-news/news/2026/cambiamenti-leadership-international-banks
thesis.insider_ownership: Could not locate any board or management shareholdings in this search; treat this as a research gap. Insider holdings are likely immaterial, because the Intesa Sanpaolo group (via PBZ and the parent) holds roughly 99% of the shares according to the 2016 figures. Source: https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/migrated/news/PBZ-nSzdP02i4sm1Tjcy3jeQRQ__.pdf

thesis.business_description: AGRANA Beteiligungs-AG (Vienna) is an Austrian agri-industrial processor with about 8,400 employees and ~50 production sites, organised into Food & Beverage Solutions (fruit preparations for dairy/food, apple and berry juice concentrates) and Agricultural Commodities & Specialities (ACS - Sugar, mainly Central/Eastern Europe; ACS - Starch, potato/corn/wheat starch and bioethanol). FY2025|26 (to 28 Feb 2026): revenue EUR 3.24bn (-7.9%), operating profit before exceptionals and JVs EUR 81.2m (+6.2%), reported EBIT EUR 3.2m after EUR 74.1m exceptional items; FY2026|27 guidance is EBIT EUR 70-90m with slight revenue growth. Sources: https://www.ots.at/presseaussendung/EQS_20260512_EQS0002/eqs-news-agrana-achieves-solid-202526-operating-profit-of-812-million-before-exceptionals-and-joint-ventures ; https://igrownews.com/agrana-latest-news/ ; https://reports.agrana.com/fileadmin/inhalte/2026/AGRANA_Annual_Report_2025_26_EN_web.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: Describes itself as the global market leader in fruit preparations and the world's leading producer of apple and berry juice concentrates, with a fruit footprint of roughly 26-28 plants worldwide (count varies by date/source); also the leading sugar producer in Central and Eastern Europe and a major European starch/bioethanol producer. The FBS segment is now the main earnings driver, while sugar suffers from low EU sugar prices and tariff-free Ukrainian imports, and starch from weaker ethanol/saccharification margins. Strategy includes restructuring sugar (closing Leopoldsdorf, Austria, and Hrusovany, Czech Republic) and bolt-ons such as Mercator-Emba in Slovenia. Named competitor data was not found in this search. Sources: https://live.deutsche-boerse.com/news/7bc5a078-9f78-4aec-bcd8-3e9aaaab2df4 ; https://igrownews.com/agrana-latest-news/ ; https://live.deutsche-boerse.com/news/EQS-News-AGRANA-launch-in-Slovenia-acquisition-of-the-food-company-Mercator-Emba-successfully-concluded-43686222-304b-41eb-b3cd-bda88b721f82
thesis.main_shareholders: AGRANA Zucker, Staerke und Frucht Holding AG (formerly Z&S Zucker und Staerke Holding) holds 48,955,088 shares (78.34%) plus a call option over 800,000 shares (1.28%); this holding is jointly owned by Suedzucker AG and an Austrian syndicate (Raiffeisen Holding NOe-Wien/RLB NOe-Wien and beet-grower and agricultural entities such as Zucker-Beteiligungsgesellschaft, Almara Holding, Leipnik-Lundenburger Invest, Marchfelder Zuckerfabriken). Per an 11 Aug 2026 voting-rights notice, the syndicate's attributable total is 82.36% (81.08% adjusted), triggered by a 6 Aug 2026 split-and-takeover agreement under which RLB NOe-Wien takes over Raiffeisen-Holding NOe-Wien's AGRANA interest (an intra-Raiffeisen reorganisation, not a bid for minorities). Suedzucker also held ~2.74% directly and free float was ~18.9% per a 2023-dated profile (aggregator); Suedzucker can exercise majority voting control in the holding company. Sources: https://www.boerse-online.de/dpa-afx/eqs-stimmrechte-agrana-beteiligungs-aktiengesellschaft-deutsch-544321.html ; https://boerse-express.com/boerse/aktie/agrana-beteiligungs-ag+tts-147056705/firmenprofil ; https://www.suedzucker.de/en/press/sudzucker-successful-agrana-share-placement
thesis.red_flags: (1) Controlled company: ~78-82% held via the Suedzucker/Raiffeisen holding structure, leaving a small free float; minority interests are subordinate to group parent Suedzucker (itself controlled), creating potential parent-vs-minority conflicts of interest (no specific related-party issue was identified in this search). (2) Sugar segment losses: ACS-Sugar revenue fell 32% to EUR 570.6m with an operating loss of EUR 106.5m in FY2025|26, including a EUR 46.0m impairment and EUR 13.7m closure costs; dividend proposal halved to EUR 0.35 (from EUR 0.70). (3) Leverage: net debt EUR 421.0m, gearing 39.2% (up from 35.5%), equity ratio 44.1%; free cash flow fell to EUR 127.2m from EUR 259.1m. (4) Exposure to EU sugar price cycle and Ukrainian import competition. No accounting or litigation issues identified. Sources: https://www.ots.at/presseaussendung/EQS_20260512_EQS0002/eqs-news-agrana-achieves-solid-202526-operating-profit-of-812-million-before-exceptionals-and-joint-ventures ; https://reports.agrana.com/fileadmin/inhalte/2026/AGRANA_Annual_Report_2025_26_EN_web.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: No meaningful personal holdings by Management Board (CEO Stephan Buettner) or Supervisory Board members were found; control sits with institutional/cooperative owners (Suedzucker and the Raiffeisen/beet-grower syndicate), which are represented on the Supervisory Board. Individual director shareholdings could not be located in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://live.deutsche-boerse.com/news/7bc5a078-9f78-4aec-bcd8-3e9aaaab2df4 ; https://www.boerse-online.de/dpa-afx/eqs-stimmrechte-agrana-beteiligungs-aktiengesellschaft-deutsch-544321.html

thesis.business_description: AS Ekspress Grupp is a Tallinn-based Baltic media group whose core activities are web media content production and publishing of newspapers, magazines and books across Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania; it also runs an electronic ticket-sales platform and ticket offices in Latvia and Estonia, a digital outdoor screen network in Estonia and Latvia, and event/conference/training businesses mainly in Estonia and Lithuania. 2025 audited revenue was EUR 80.2m (+5%) with net profit of EUR 1.0m; digital revenues were 86% of the total. Sources: https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/audited-annual-report-2025-1 ; https://nasdaqbaltic.com/market/upload/reports/eeg/2025_ar_en_eur_con.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: Describes itself as the leading Baltic media group, with a digital subscription base reported at about 256,000 in 2025 (+7%); it has been extending into adjacent niches such as digital outdoor screens (about 160 screens in 2025) and bolt-ons like the traffic-training platform Liikluslab. Named competitors and market-share figures were not found in this search. Sources: https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/audited-annual-report-2025-1 ; https://www.sustainabilityreports.com/as-ekspress-grupp/2025/annual-report
thesis.main_shareholders: Controlled by HHL Rühm OÜ (controlled by Hans H. Luik). A November 2025 stock-exchange notice put HHL Rühm at 22,775,442 shares (73.57%) after buying 7,963,307 shares from Hans Luik. HHL Rühm then made a voluntary takeover bid at EUR 1.25/share (Nov-Dec 2025); about 22.55% of shares were tendered, taking it to about 96.12% after settlement. Sources: https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/changes-in-substantial-shareholding ; https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/the-results-of-the-voluntary-takeover-bid-made-of-the-shares-of-aktsiaselts-ekspress-grupp
thesis.red_flags: TAKE-PRIVATE IN PROGRESS: on 1 June 2026 the AGM approved a squeeze-out of minority shareholders by HHL Rühm OÜ at EUR 1.26 per share and voted to end trading on the Nasdaq Tallinn Baltic main list. On 10 July 2026 the company stopped publishing digital-subscription data because of the delisting. This search did not confirm the final settlement or delisting date, so the listing may already be gone or about to be. Free float is minimal (under about 4%), and profitability is thin (2025 net profit EUR 1.0m on EUR 80.2m revenue). Sources: https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/resolutions-of-the-annual-general-meeting-of-shareholders-of-as-ekspress-grupp-held-on-1-june-2026 ; https://www.inderes.se/releases/as-ekspress-grupp-stops-publishing-information-about-digital-subscriptions
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder Hans H. Luik is the ultimate beneficiary of HHL Rühm OÜ, which held about 96.12% after the December 2025 bid. He moved his directly held shares (7,963,307) into HHL Rühm in November 2025; his personal direct stake after that transfer was not stated in the sources found. Holdings of other board or management members were not located in this search, so treat that as a research gap. Sources: https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/changes-in-substantial-shareholding ; https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/the-results-of-the-voluntary-takeover-bid-made-of-the-shares-of-aktsiaselts-ekspress-grupp

thesis.business_description: Orzel Bialy S.A. is a lead recycler and producer based in Piekary Slaskie (Silesia, Poland): it recycles spent lead-acid (mainly automotive) batteries and other lead-bearing materials and sells refined soft lead and lead-antimony/lead-calcium alloys to battery manufacturers and lead-oxide producers. Standalone 2025 results (annual report published 14 Apr 2026): net revenue about PLN 574.9m (2024: PLN 699.1m) and net profit PLN 70.8m (2024: PLN 98.0m); consolidated net profit about PLN 72.9m (partially seen). Sources: https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/ORZEL-BIALY-S-A-Wyniki-finansowe-RR-2025-9113297.html ; https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/ORZEL-BIALY-S-A-Wyniki-finansowe-SRR-2025-9113298.html ; https://simplywall.st/stock/wse/obl
thesis.competitive_position: Described (in an EMIS profile using 2023 data) as Poland's leading refined-lead producer and largest recycler of used lead-acid batteries; the smelter site has operated for about 150 years. It sits inside the ZAP Sznajder Batterien battery group, which provides a captive/strategic outlet for lead. Earnings track lead prices, recycling margins (battery scrap cost) and European automotive battery demand; revenue fell ~18% in 2025 on lower sales. No verified market-share figure or named competitor list was found. Sources: https://emis.cn/php/company-profile/PL/Orzel_Bialy_SA_en_1454698.html ; https://resolve.cambridge.org/core/journals/mineralogical-magazine/article/composition-and-element-mobilization-in-pyrometallurgical-slags-from-the-orzel-bialy-smelting-plant-in-the-bytompiekary-slaskie-area-poland/6B0EF8159C9157313F90C25EB3483A7E ; https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/ORZEL-BIALY-S-A-Wyniki-finansowe-RR-2025-9113297.html
thesis.main_shareholders: ZAP Sznajder Batterien S.A. (controlled by Lech Sznajder) holds 12,343,456 shares (74.13%; register entry last changed 25 Nov 2021) following its 2019 tender offer (PLN 10.44/share, aiming for 100%); PZU OFE Zlota Jesien together with DFE PZU holds 2,656,891 shares (15.95%, as of 4 Jun 2025); others ~9.9% of 16,650,649 shares. Figures are from Bankier/Stockwatch summaries of company filings; confirm in latest ESPI reports. Sources: https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/akcje/ORZBIALY/akcjonariat ; https://www.stockwatch.pl/gpw/ORZBIALY,akcjonariat,dane-finansowe.aspx ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/84241,wezwanie-rowniez-na-akcje-orzel-bialy
thesis.red_flags: (1) Controlled company: ~74% owned by ZAP Sznajder Batterien (which sought 100% in 2019), with free float only ~10% beyond PZU's ~16% - illiquid stock and squeeze-out/delisting risk; potential related-party dealings with the parent battery group (not quantified here). (2) Commodity exposure: profits fell in 2025 (net profit -28%) with lower lead revenue. (3) Environmental: a 150-year-old lead smelting site with slag heaps studied for heavy-metal contamination; no specific fines or proceedings were found in this search, but environmental liability is an inherent risk. (4) Supervisory board composition on aggregator sites may be stale. Sources: https://www.stockwatch.pl/gpw/ORZBIALY,akcjonariat,dane-finansowe.aspx ; https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/ORZEL-BIALY-S-A-Wyniki-finansowe-RR-2025-9113297.html ; https://resolve.cambridge.org/core/journals/mineralogical-magazine/article/composition-and-element-mobilization-in-pyrometallurgical-slags-from-the-orzel-bialy-smelting-plant-in-the-bytompiekary-slaskie-area-poland/6B0EF8159C9157313F90C25EB3483A7E
thesis.website: https://www.orzel-bialy.com.pl (likely official domain; not surfaced directly in search results, verify). Source: https://www.orzel-bialy.com.pl
thesis.insider_ownership: Indirect control: Lech Sznajder controls ZAP Sznajder Batterien (74.13%). Management Board for the 12th term (appointed 10 Jun 2025): President Konrad Sznajder, Vice-Presidents Slawomir Czeszak and Tomasz Lewicki; any personal shareholdings by them were not found, and the family relationship between Konrad and Lech Sznajder was not confirmed in this search. Sources: https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art42507331-orzel-bialy-spolka-akcyjna-powolanie-zarzadu-spolki-orzel-bialy-s-a-na-nowa-kadencje ; https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/akcje/ORZBIALY/akcjonariat

thesis.business_description: KME Group S.p.A. (formerly Intek Group, renamed September 2022) is a Milan-based holding company whose main asset is KME SE, a European producer of copper and copper-alloy semi-finished products (laminates, special products, wire). H1 2025 revenue was EUR 1,022.9m (+29%, largely from the Sundwiger acquisition), with EBITDA of EUR 53.3m. Sources: https://quartr.com/events/kme-group-kme-h1-2025_F9IjI08o ; https://uk.finance.yahoo.com/quote/0MB2.L/profile?p=0MB2.L
thesis.competitive_position: An established European copper-semis processor, growing by acquisition (Sundwiger) and portfolio deals. In December 2025 it agreed with Paragon to buy back control of Cunova (KME held 45%), backed by a EUR 300m financing package and a partnership with an Apollo Global Management affiliate; the closing is reported as 10 July 2026, with a possible Frankfurt IPO of the combined Cunova entity. Management also says it may sell non-core copper holdings to cut debt. Named competitors and market shares were not found in this search. Sources: https://www.emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2025-12/20251223_175920.pdf ; https://www.emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2026-04/20260402_181222.pdf ; https://quartr.com/events/kme-group-s-p-a-kme-h1-2026_F9Ijigwx
thesis.main_shareholders: Controlled by Quattroduedue S.p.A. (led by Vincenzo Manes), which held 47.46% of ordinary shares and 63.59% of voting rights (increased voting rights) when the 2023 delisting tender offers were announced; Milano Finanza separately cited 59.4% control. After the reopened 2023 offer, a secondary source reported the offeror side at 277,416,637 ordinary shares (89.66% of the class, 85.45% of total capital). That source is ambiguous about whether the figure includes treasury shares or the concert party, so verify it against official notices. A July 2026 filing shows a shareholder pact at the Quattroduedue level, with Hanseatic transferring its Quattroduedue stake to Hanseatic Americas Ltd. No current post-2023 official shareholder table was located, so treat this as a research gap. Sources: https://www.soldionline.it/?p=17553 ; https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/kme-vola-dopo-aver-alzato-il-prezzo-di-opa-e-averla-trasformata-100-cash-grazie-a-jp-morgan-202303291149305135 ; https://www.emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2026-07/20260709_186746.pdf
thesis.red_flags: Control and delisting overhang: the 2023 tender offers (financed partly by a JP Morgan-managed fund/Lynstone) did not meet squeeze-out conditions, and the company said it would pursue delisting by reverse merger into subsidiary KMH. Whether that merger was completed was not confirmed in this search, so check listing status. Leverage is high and figures conflict: net debt was EUR 324.4m at 30 June 2025 on one definition and EUR 517.5m on another (incl. leases), and about EUR 321m at 30 June 2026. There was a H1 2025 net loss of EUR 28.9m, and the H1 2026 profit of EUR 91.4m is 'net management' (likely boosted by one-offs). The holding structure is complex, with copper-price/cyclical exposure. Sources: https://www.soldionline.it/?p=17553 ; https://quartr.com/events/kme-group-kme-h1-2025_F9IjI08o ; https://www.soldionline.it/notizie/azioni-italia/conti-kme-group-primo-semestre-2026
thesis.insider_ownership: Executive Chairman/CEO Vincenzo Manes leads controlling holder Quattroduedue; his personal look-through percentage was not found. Diva Moriani (Executive President) is a long-standing executive; no personal holding was found. Aggregators list both as 'n/a'. Treat named insider percentages as a research gap. Sources: https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/kme-vola-dopo-aver-alzato-il-prezzo-di-opa-e-averla-trasformata-100-cash-grazie-a-jp-morgan-202303291149305135 ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/it/materials/bit-kme/kme-group-shares/management

thesis.business_description: STRATEC SE (Birkenfeld, Germany; Frankfurt Prime Standard) designs and manufactures fully automated analyzer systems, software, service parts and consumables for clinical in-vitro diagnostics and life sciences, acting as an OEM partner whose systems are typically marketed by partners together with their own test reagents; it builds around 10,000 analyzer systems a year. FY2025: sales EUR 250.9m (-2.6% nominal, -1.1% cc), adjusted EBIT EUR 25.2m (-24.8%), adjusted EBIT margin 10.0%; Service Parts & Consumables EUR 103.6m, Development & Services EUR 58.9m. Sources: https://www.stratec.com/news/detail/stratec-reports-final-results-for-2025-financial-year ; https://www.hauptversammlung.de/fileadmin/public/user_upload/STRATEC_JA25.pdf ; https://ir.stratec.com/download/companies/stratec/CompanyPresentation/STRATEC_IR_Presentation_202412.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: A specialised outsourced design-and-manufacturing partner for large diagnostics companies (secondary sources name Abbott, Siemens, Bio-Rad, DiaSorin and Hologic as partners; not confirmed from company revenue disclosures). Moat: regulatory co-approval with partners' reagents and long instrument lifecycles create sticky, multi-year partnerships and recurring service/consumables revenue. The main alternative for customers is in-house instrument development; named direct competitors were not found in this search. Targets an adjusted EBIT margin of 15.0% by 2030; 2026 guidance is a margin around 10.0% with growth weighted to H2 (H1 2026 adjusted EBIT margin 6.9%, Q2 11.9%). Sources: https://www.hauptversammlung.de/fileadmin/public/user_upload/STRATEC_JA25.pdf ; https://intuitionlabs.ai/companies/medtech/stratec-se ; https://live.deutsche-boerse.com/news/EQS-News-STRATEC-POSTS-RESULTS-FOR-FIRST-HALF-OF-2026-bd003891-c036-4d95-b01c-827dd6024ec4
thesis.main_shareholders: Per STRATEC's IR shareholder-structure page (date not shown): founder Hermann Leistner's family and their investment companies 40.36%, free float 59.62%, treasury 0.02%. Ralf Leistner notified >25% of voting rights via attribution (2025 AGM invitation). Recent institutional notices (total 12,157,841 voting rights): Union Investment Privatfonds 3.82% (27 Mar 2025, after 5.84% on 28 Jan 2025); J.P. Morgan Securities plc 3.79% (3 Mar 2025); Invesco fund 1.48% (22 Jan 2025). No 2026 voting-rights notices were found. Sources: https://ir.stratec.com/websites/stratec/English/1300/shareholder-structure.html ; https://www.hauptversammlung.de/fileadmin/public/user_upload/STRATEC_TO25.pdf ; https://ir.stratec.com/websites/stratec/English/1350/notification-of-voting-rights.html
thesis.red_flags: (1) Earnings momentum: an ad hoc on 30 Oct 2025 cut 2025 sales guidance due to supply-chain production delays; adjusted EBIT fell ~25% in 2025, with EUR 10.5m impairments on intangibles and inventories, and H1 2026 margin was only 6.9%. A 2024 sales-guidance adjustment preceded this. (2) Customer concentration inherent to the OEM model (few large diagnostics partners; exact share not verified - an ~80% multinational-customer figure comes only from a low-quality blog). (3) Family block of ~40% gives the Leistners significant influence and a family member now sits on the Supervisory Board. No accounting or litigation issues identified from official sources. Sources: https://www.stratec.com/news/detail/stratec-reports-supply-chain-related-production-delays-adjustment-to-2025-sales-guidance-and-preliminary-results-for-9m-2025 ; https://app.boersengefluester.de/en/newswire/DE000STRA555/stratec-se/stratec-posts-impairments-reports-preliminary-results-for-2025-and-offers-guidance-for-2026-2297992 ; https://app.boersengefluester.de/en/newswire/DE000STRA555/stratec-se/target-corridor-for-adjusted-ebit-margin-confirmed-with-adjustment-to-2024-sales-guidance-2010991
thesis.insider_ownership: Founding Leistner family ~40.4% (family plus investment companies); Ralf Leistner was elected to the Supervisory Board at the 2025 AGM (board enlarged from four to five) and is attributed >25% of voting rights while holding no more than 10% directly. CEO Marcus Wolfinger (CEO since April 2011) bought shares in March 2023 at ~EUR 66-70; his total holding percentage was not found. Sources: https://www.hauptversammlung.de/fileadmin/public/user_upload/STRATEC_TO25.pdf ; https://ir.stratec.com/websites/stratec/English/6300/directors-dealings.html ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/healthcare/otc-stse.y/stratec/management

thesis.business_description: Bursa de Valori Bucuresti SA operates the Bucharest Stock Exchange, Romania's regulated and multilateral trading venues. It consolidates Depozitarul Central (central securities depository) and CCP.RO Bucharest (a central counterparty in which BVB held about 54.93%), so revenues come from trading, post-trading, issuer and data services. Preliminary 2025 group net profit was about RON 9m, with operating profit of RON 5.66m (2024: 10.21m). H1 2026 was described as a record half. Sources: https://m.bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/BVB_20260218182421_BVB-Preliminary-Report-4Q2025-EN.pdf ; https://www.bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/BVB_20260812183703_BVB-Half-Year-Report-1H2026-EN.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: The domestic monopoly exchange and depository in Romania. It benefits from rising market capitalisation (above EUR 100bn for the first time in 2025) and turnover, and from building local clearing (CCP.RO received ASF authorisation on 1 July 2026). Post-trading is the most profitable segment (about 40% operating margin in 9M 2025). It competes with larger regional/EU venues for listings and liquidity. thesis.business_description: Farmaceutica Remedia S.A. (Deva, Romania; established 1991 as a state-owned company) is a Romanian pharmaceutical distribution and logistics group: wholesale distribution through the wholly owned subsidiary Farmaceutica Remedia Distribution & Logistics S.R.L., plus a hospital and private-clinic supply business; it also holds 50% of Pharma Expertspedition S.R.L. (equity-accounted). FY2025 consolidated turnover was about RON 759.8m (about RON 500.5m distribution, about RON 234.9m hospital/clinic) with net profit about RON 8.0m (per a Profit.ro report on the company's results; exact segment split not verified against the annual report itself). Share capital is 95,480,820 shares of RON 0.10 nominal. Sources: https://www.bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/RMAH_20260327172358_REMEDIA---annual-report-2025.pdf ; https://www.profit.ro/povesti-cu-profit/financiar/piata-de-capital/farmaceutica-remedia-si-a-majorat-profitul-net-22360128
thesis.competitive_position: A medium-sized Romanian pharma wholesaler with regional strength in the west and centre of the country; a 2019 third-party analysis put its share of the pharma market below 3%, and a 2010 Cegedim-based analysis showed a fragmented market dominated by Mediplus (A&D Pharma), Farmexpert and Fildas, so these shares are dated and no current market-share figure was found in this search. Competitors include Phoenix-owned Farmexim/Help Net. Remedia exited much of retail (sold pharmacies, with a 52-pharmacy sale to Phoenix reported; date and final terms not confirmed in this search) and refocused on wholesale/logistics and the hospital channel. Sources: https://www.brd.ro/_files/pdf/pharma.pdf ; https://www.romania-insider.com/Phoenix-takeover-pharmacies-remedia-deva ; https://bvb.ro/infocont/infocont24/RMAH_20240425170137_REMEDIA---annual-report-2023-EN.pdf

Company filings confirm V. Tarus RoAgencies S.R.L. acquired 55.802% from the state-linked fund (FPS) in October 2000 and merged into the company on 1 Jan 2006. AGM of 29 Apr 2026: 77,126,388 votes present = 82.3091% of voting shares; 1,777,433 shares (1.8615% of capital) are suspended from voting. thesis.red_flags: Controlling founder-type shareholder (apparently above 80%, aggregator-sourced) implies a very small free float (about 17-18%), low liquidity and minority-shareholder risk; shares suspended from voting (1.86%) noted in AGM filing. Thin economics: FY2025 net profit about RON 8.0m on RON 759.8m turnover (about 1% margin) and equity of about RON 79.6m vs assets of about RON 383.2m (high leverage/working-capital dependence typical of distribution, per company results summary). Affiliated-party transaction audit reports are filed regularly (e.g. Jan 2024), a standard governance item to review. Exposure to Romanian drug-price regulation/claw-back and public-hospital payment delays was not checked in this search; treat as a research gap.
