thesis.insider_ownership: Conpet is state-controlled (Ministry of Energy, 58.7162% at end-2022); holdings of board members and executives could not be located in this search; treat as a research gap. Source: https://bvb.ro/infocont/infocont23/COTE_20230227174906_Raport-anual-preliminar-2022-CONPET-ASF-si-BVB-ENG.pdf

thesis.business_description: Robinson plc, tracing its origins to 1839 and headquartered in Chesterfield, UK, manufactures custom rigid plastic (injection/blow-moulded bottles, pots, tubs, containers, caps, closures, jars) and paperboard packaging (boxes, lids, book jackets, clam packs, rigid trays, folding cartons) for the food, personal care, homecare and luxury-gift sectors, with plants in the UK, Poland and Denmark. Source: https://robinsonpackaging.com/investors ; https://www.packagingbirmingham.com/exhibitors/robinson-plc-241165/
thesis.competitive_position: Small AIM-listed rigid-packaging manufacturer (~400 employees) with a blue-chip consumer-goods customer base including McBride, Procter & Gamble, Reckitt Benckiser, SC Johnson and Unilever, giving it exposure to defensive, repeat-order FMCG demand. Source: https://www.packagingbirmingham.com/exhibitors/robinson-plc-241165/
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Barclays' share factsheet (defining major shareholders as holders of >3% per the annual accounts, data as at 31/12/2024), and a Simply Wall St ownership snapshot, Charles Robinson (likely a member of the founding Robinson family) holds approximately 8.19%, with Peter Gyllenhammar AB at ~4.03% and Rebecca Hartley at ~4.02%; the top 25 shareholders together hold about 60.23% of the company. Source: https://research-centre.barclays.co.uk/shares/robinson/company-information ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/materials/aim-rbn/robinson-shares/ownership. Share-count figures differ between sources (17.69m per Barclays vs. 16.75m per a Frankfurt-listing Simply Wall St page), so percentages should be treated as approximate pending direct verification against Robinson's current annual report substantial-shareholdings section.
thesis.red_flags: Peter Gyllenhammar AB, a known activist/value investor, holds a disclosed stake (~4%), which can signal either constructive engagement or potential boardroom friction — not inherently a red flag but worth monitoring. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/materials/aim-rbn/robinson-shares/ownership. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources; ownership is relatively dispersed (no single holder above ~8%) compared to many of the other small-caps in this batch.

thesis.business_description: Operator of Malta International Airport (MLA/LMML) in Luqa, the only international airport serving the Maltese Islands, listed on the Malta Stock Exchange. Revenue is split into aviation (68.0% of 2025 revenue; EUR106.7m) and non-aviation (retail, property, car parking etc.; EUR50.3m). 2025: record 10.06 million passengers (+12.3%), 65,470 flight movements, revenue EUR157.0m (+9.9%), EBITDA EUR95.0m, record net profit EUR49.8m (+7.6%); top five markets UK, Italy, Poland, Germany, France. A EUR345m investment programme is planned for 2025-2029. Sources: https://maltairport.com/app/uploads/2026/04/MIA26-AR-OnlineExport-MP-v1-compressed.pdf ; https://thebusinesspicture.com/?p=6748 ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malta_International_Airport
thesis.competitive_position: Natural monopoly: sole commercial airport for Malta, operating under a 65-year concession effective July 2002 per the company's annual reports (an end date around 2067 is my arithmetic, not stated in the results). Strong traffic momentum continues in 2026: H1 2026 revenue EUR82.5m (+14.8%), passengers 5.2m (+15.6%), net profit EUR29.0m (+18.5%), interim dividend EUR0.06 net per share. Ryanair (Malta Air) has a base there, but the ranking of airlines by traffic share was not found. Total 2025 net dividend EUR0.1196 per share (60% payout). Net debt, tariff-regulation details and peer comparisons were not located in this search; research gap. Sources: https://maltairport.com/app/uploads/2026/07/Malta-International-Airport-Approves-H1-Financial-Results-and-the-Payment-of-an-Interim-Dividend.pdf ; https://thebusinesspicture.com/?p=6748 ; https://filings.xbrl.org/2138008EKXNMKZRXCT63/2022-12-31/ESEF/MT/0/MIAP_20221231_CON_AFR_2138008EKXNMKZRXCT63/reports/2138008EKXNMKZRXCT63-2022-12-31-en.html
thesis.main_shareholders: Per company announcements (2025-2026, repeated in the 34th AGM notice): Malta Mediterranean Link Consortium (MMLC) 40% (Flughafen Wien AG owns about 96% of MMLC), Government of Malta 20%, general public 29.9%, VIE (Malta) Limited 10.1% (VIE Malta is a Flughafen Wien subsidiary), so Flughafen Wien's consolidated stake is above 48% (2016 deal announcement). The percentages are the same as in 2016 announcements, so the exact as-of date of the current register was not confirmed; the 5%+ holder table in the 2025 annual report was not read in this search. A January 2025 buyback of up to 1% of share capital (1,353,000 shares, to be cancelled) was proposed, which may have slightly changed percentages. Sources: https://maltairport.com/app/uploads/2026/05/34th-AGM.pdf ; https://cdn.borzamalta.com.mt/download/announcements/MIA299.pdf ; https://www.airport-technology.com/?p=13289
thesis.red_flags: Concentration: single-airport, single-country exposure heavily tied to tourism and a few airline customers; controlling strategic holder (Flughafen Wien, over 48%) plus the State (20%) leaves roughly 30% public float. Concession and regulated-charges terms, leverage/net debt and the large capex programme were not verified in this search. No litigation, accounting or governance problems found, but this search did not specifically examine the audit report or legal notes; standard caveat applies. Sources: https://maltairport.com/app/uploads/2026/05/34th-AGM.pdf ; https://thebusinesspicture.com/?p=6748
thesis.insider_ownership: Could not locate directors' or executives' individual shareholdings (directors' report interests) in this search; treat as a research gap. Insider-type control is institutional rather than personal: Flughafen Wien AG (via MMLC and VIE Malta) controls more than 48% and the Government of Malta holds 20%. Sources: https://cdn.borzamalta.com.mt/download/announcements/MIA299.pdf ; https://maltairport.com/app/uploads/2026/04/MIA26-AR-OnlineExport-MP-v1-compressed.pdf

thesis.business_description: Dometic describes itself as a global outdoor technology company making mobile living easy: installed products for land vehicles (RVs, trucks) and boats, and standalone products (e.g. mobile cooling) for outdoor enthusiasts. Segments named in the Q1 2026 report: Marine, Mobile Cooling Solutions, Land Vehicles and Global Verticals. 2025 net sales about SEK 21bn (USD 2.3bn), sales in over 100 countries, about 7,000 employees. Headquarters: current site says Stockholm, a 2019 release said Solna (conflict). Sources: https://www.dometicgroup.com/en/our-company ; https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/dometic-group-interim-report-first-quarter-2026 ; https://dometicgroup.com/en-us/our-brands/dometic
thesis.competitive_position: Branded OEM and aftermarket supplier to major RV and leisure-boat manufacturers (Thor Industries and Winnebago named as OEM customers in a profile), with global scale across 100+ countries. Strategy in 2026: global restructuring program (extended in Q2 2026 to save a further SEK 150m a year by mid-2027), deleveraging toward about 2.5x net debt/EBITDA. Competitors (e.g. in RV climate/sanitation) and market-share figures were not found in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.dometicgroup.com/en/our-company ; https://mb.cision.com/Main/10773/4374233/4191781.pdf ; https://quartr.com/events/dometic-group-dom-q2-2026_3sfjuk00
thesis.main_shareholders: Aggregator data (Simply Wall St, appears to reflect late-2025 filings, no single as-of date): NN Group about 7.6% (24.2m shares), Incentive AS about 7.0% (22.4m), Carnegie Fonder about 6.4%, Forsta AP-fonden about 6.1%, Nordea Investment Management about 5.5%, AP4 about 5.1%, 1832 Asset Management about 5%, Alecta about 4.5%, Vanguard about 3.8%; institutions about 76%. No controlling holder. Official register (Euroclear/Modular Finance) or annual report table not located; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/automobiles/sto-dom/dometic-group-shares/ownership ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/automobiles/lse-0rco/dometic-group-shares/ownership
thesis.insider_ownership: CEO Juan Vargues (CEO since Jan 2018) directly owns about 0.27% (Simply Wall St aggregator, date unclear). Fredrik Cappelen was re-elected chairman at the 14 Apr 2025 AGM (board then: Cappelen, Vibbleus, Hoogerbrugge, Du, Sjolander, Schmuckle, Frisk); the 2026 AGM set a board of eight (names and chair not confirmed here). Board member holdings not located. Incentive AS (about 7%) is a large holder but its link to the board was not verified. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/automobiles/otc-dtcg.f/dometic-group/management ; https://news.cision.com/dometic-group/r/bulletin-from-the-annual-shareholders--meeting-of-dometic-group-ab--publ-,c4136517
thesis.red_flags: Leverage: net debt/EBITDA 3.3x at Q2 2026 (flat), net debt about SEK 9.3bn vs a target of about 2.5x. Weak demand: Q2 2026 EBITA before items SEK 739m (12.4% margin) vs 877m a year earlier; free cash flow SEK 806m vs 1,302m; inventory build tied to restructuring. SEK 52m bad-debt charge from West Marine's Chapter 11 filing (credit loss, not goodwill impairment). Restructuring extension cost about SEK 100m; tariff volatility (new US Section 232 tariffs, partly offset by refunds). No dividend for FY2025 (2026 AGM). A Quartr entry mentioning a SEK 2,000m goodwill impairment in Q3 2024 is of unclear date and was not verified. Sources: https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/dometic-group-interim-report-second-quarter-2026-20260714 ; https://quartr.com/events/dometic-group-dom-q2-2026_3sfjuk00 ; https://rv-pro.com/news/dometic-q2-2026-sees-stable-sales-in-a-volatile-market/ ; https://news.cision.com/dometic-group/r/bulletin-from-the-annual-shareholders--meeting-of-dometic-group-ab--publ-,c4136517

thesis.business_description: Seko S.A., headquartered in Chojnice, Poland, is one of Poland's leading producers of preserved fish products, manufacturing fish marinades, salted-herring products, fish salads and fish pastes at its production plant in Chojnice. (Note: this is a distinct company from the similarly-named global logistics group SEKO Logistics, which is unrelated.) Source: https://strefainwestorow.pl/notowania/spolki/PLSEKO000014 ; https://www.parkiet.com/firmy/240461-seko
thesis.competitive_position: Established Polish branded fish-preserves producer listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (ticker SEK, ISIN PLSEKO000014), with a market capitalization of roughly PLN 86.1m as of August 2026; the Kustra family holds senior management roles, with Tomasz Kustra becoming Management Board President effective 1 January 2026, indicating long-running family operational leadership. Source: https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/116382,wyniki-finansowe-seko-w-2022-r-oraz-list-do-akcjonariuszy ; https://www.parkiet.com/firmy/240461-seko
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Seko's own 2024 quarterly financial report, the company's parent, Złota Rybka sp. z o.o. (based in Straszyn), owns 4,155,688 shares = 62.49% of share capital and voting rights at the General Meeting. Source: (Seko S.A. 2024 quarterly report, as referenced via company filings index) https://bossa.pl/sites/b30/files/2023-09/document_gpw_editor/Seko_32_GPW_76_2023_DM_BO%C5%9A_PL_0.pdf. A more recent shareholder notice exists — 'Akcjonariusze posiadający co najmniej 5% liczby głosów na ZWZ SEKO S.A. w dniu 17 czerwca 2026 r.' — but its contents (confirming whether Złota Rybka's 62.49% stake is unchanged) were not retrievable in this search. Source: https://www.money.pl/gielda/spolki-gpw/plseko000014,emitent,1.html. We could not confirm the individual(s) who ultimately control Złota Rybka sp. z o.o. (likely the Kustra family, given their board roles) from an official filing in this search.
thesis.red_flags: High ownership concentration via parent company Złota Rybka sp. z o.o. (~62.5% of votes per the 2024 filing) limits free float and minority-shareholder influence, though this is a disclosed holding-company structure rather than evidence of misconduct. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources. Source: https://bossa.pl/sites/b30/files/2023-09/document_gpw_editor/Seko_32_GPW_76_2023_DM_BO%C5%9A_PL_0.pdf

thesis.business_description: Holding company headquartered in Pliezhausen, Germany, that operates IT infrastructures and provides IT services, technology consulting and IT solutions, mainly for medium and large German enterprises and public authorities (workplace and cloud services, managed/private/public cloud, SAP outsourcing, network, security, service desk; CORBOX full-service workplace offering). Third-party profiles list a Services segment (largest) and a Solutions & Consulting segment; the current segment structure should be verified in the latest annual report. About 3,500 employees at sites across Germany. H1 FY2024/25 revenue EUR279.8m (+12.5%), EBITDA EUR41.4m; fiscal year ends 30 September. Sources: https://www.datagroup.de/en/news/datagroup-posts-revenue-growth-in-the-second-quarter-and-first-half-of-2024-2025 ; https://www.datagroup.de/en/?p=57310
thesis.competitive_position: Describes itself as one of the leading German IT service companies; ranked top in a German IT-outsourcing study (Whitelane/Navisco) per a 2023 company release, with customer satisfaction of 78%. Strategy is organic growth plus acquisitions, with ongoing investment in AI, cyber security and cloud; company described the market as challenging and EBIT margin was 8.0% for the first nine months of FY2024/25. Could not locate independent market-share data or a competitor list in this search; research gap. Sources: https://www.datagroup.de/en/news/datagroup-posts-revenue-growth-in-the-second-quarter-and-first-half-of-2024-2025 ; https://app.boersengefluester.de/en/newswire/DE000A0JC8S7/datagroup-se/datagroup-posts-revenue-growth-in-the-third-quarter-and-first-nine-months-of-20242025-2182320
thesis.main_shareholders: Takeover context: in April 2025 KKR-advised funds, via Dante Beteiligungen SE, launched a public cash offer at EUR54.00 per share (c.33% premium); the founder-family holding HHS (Max H.-H. Schaber), which held an indirect 54.4%, agreed to transfer its stake to the bidder, giving KKR and HHS 50:50 joint control of the bidder. The bidder said it had secured about 59.4% by 1 June 2025, and an aggregator headline (mainsights.io) says KKR ended at roughly 67% with free-float holders largely not tendering; the official final result, and the current shareholder register, could not be located in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.datagroup.de/en/news/datagroup-enters-into-an-investment-agreement-with-and-supports-a-public-purchase-offer-of-kkr-at-a-price-of-eur-54-00-per-share-in-cash ; https://www.mainsights.io/ma-news/kkr-gets-rejected-by-free-float-shareholders-and-increases-its-stake-in-datagroup-publ-to-only-67-still-plans-delisting
thesis.red_flags: LISTING STATUS: the company is subject to a KKR-led takeover with a planned delisting and no delisting offer. Confirmed from company/exchange notices: DATAGROUP initiated delisting from the Munich Stock Exchange (m:access, Freiverkehr), with trading there ending 27 Feb 2026 per a Munich exchange notice and the inclusion revocation effective at end of 30 June 2026 per the company news item dated 27 Jan 2026. Could NOT confirm whether the Xetra/Frankfurt listing (D6H) is still active, was revoked, or when; check Deutsche Boerse notices before treating this as an investable listed stock. Remaining minority holders face low liquidity and no exit offer once delisted. Net debt was EUR166.1m at end of H1 FY2024/25 (2.0x EBITDA), up from EUR139.1m at 30 Sep 2024; post-LBO leverage is unknown. Sources: https://www.datagroup.de/en/news/datagroup-initiates-delisting-procedure-on-the-munich-stock-exchange ; https://www.datagroup.de/en/news/munich-stock-exchange-announces-dates-for-delisting-of-datagroup-shares ; https://www.datagroup.de/en/news/datagroup-posts-revenue-growth-in-the-second-quarter-and-first-half-of-2024-2025
thesis.insider_ownership: Pre-offer, the Schaber family holding HHS (Max H.-H. Schaber) held an indirect 54.4% and agreed to roll it into the bidder (joint 50:50 control with KKR). Post-settlement insider holdings, and holdings of other board members/executives, could not be located in this search; research gap. Source: https://www.datagroup.de/en/news/datagroup-enters-into-an-investment-agreement-with-and-supports-a-public-purchase-offer-of-kkr-at-a-price-of-eur-54-00-per-share-in-cash

thesis.business_description: Swedish investment bank / securities firm headquartered in Stockholm (offices in Stockholm and Malmo). Operates through the wholly owned Mangold Fondkommission AB, supervised by Finansinspektionen, in two segments: Investment Banking (services to companies on smaller marketplaces such as NGM, Spotlight and Nasdaq First North) and Private Banking. Founded 2000; moved from First North Premier (listed 2012) to Nasdaq Stockholm Main Market in February 2022. The company described about 90 employees in an older document (date not confirmed). FY2025: total income SEK 195.9m (2024: 182.8m, +7.2%), total comprehensive income SEK 32.5m (2024: loss of SEK 4.5m). Source: https://www.inderes.se/releases/mangold-ab-bokslutskommunike-2025 ; https://www.inderes.se/releases/mangold-ab-kallar-till-arsstamma-den-29-april-2026 ; https://cdn.bequoted.com/media/1/d42adba2-a9cf-4fc3-b82c-ed0d52f0216f/Mangold_Arsredovisning_2022.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: Self-described as one of the larger providers of financial services for companies on Sweden's smaller marketplaces; no third-party market-share data or named competitor set found (research gap). Business is cyclical: Q2 2026 total income fell to SEK 50.2m from 62.2m with EPS of -23.3 SEK (vs 3.3); Affarsvarlden reports an operating result of -10.9 MSEK vs +4.1 MSEK, not confirmed in the report text. Q4 2025 net interest income was a record SEK 9.6m. Source: https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/mangold-ab-delarsrapport-q2-2026 ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/mangold ; https://www.inderes.se/releases/mangold-ab-bokslutskommunike-2025
thesis.main_shareholders: Sources conflict and are undated or secondary; no Euroclear register was retrieved. Affarsvarlden (undated): Gomobile NU AB 29.6%, Alandsbanken (nominee) 17.2%, Tammerlov Invest AB 16.9%, Futur Pension 15.5%, Charles Wilken 2.6%, Nordnet Pension 1.8% (capital and votes). Realtid (July 2026): chairman Per Ahlgren 28.44% and CEO Per-Anders Tammerlov 15.88% (including related parties/companies). Whether Gomobile NU is Ahlgren-related was not confirmed. Registered share count was 479,193 on 29 May 2026 after 8,352 new shares were issued for the Finserve acquisition. The nomination committee is appointed by the three largest shareholders per Euroclear. Source: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/mangold ; https://www.realtid.se/bors-finans/mangolds-vd-okar-sitt-agande/ ; https://www.inderes.se/releases/mangolds-valberedning-infor-arsstamman-2026
thesis.red_flags: (1) Concentration: chairman and CEO together hold roughly 44% per Realtid, and chairman is the only non-independent director. (2) Deteriorating results: Q2 2026 loss and revenue down about 19% y/y. (3) Litigation and counterparty risk: I.V. Numen Adest claimed about SEK 182m; district court awarded Mangold SEK 27.0m, appeal withdrawn May 2026, and a settlement of SEK 1m instalments agreed; a SEK 43.2m dispute settled Dec 2025 with no payment by Mangold; July 2026 settlement with Trention and 22 bridge lenders (terms not read); Evox Fund Management did not fulfil a settlement and Mangold filed a further bankruptcy petition against it (Realtid, Sept 2026). (4) Regulatory: management noted in 2023 that it followed FI sanction decisions closely; no 2025-26 sanction found. (5) Dilution: shares issued for the Finserve acquisition. Source: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/artikel/mangold-ingar-forlikning-i-tvist-om-43-miljoner ; https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/mangold-aktiebolaget-i-v-numen-adest-aterkallar-overklagande-i-hovratten-20260527 ; https://www.realtid.se/bors-finans/trention-har-ingatt-forlikningsavtal-med-mangold/ ; https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/mangold-ab-delarsrapport-q2-2026
thesis.website: https://www.mangold.se (domain named in search results; verify)
thesis.insider_ownership: Chairman Per Ahlgren (board since 2003): 28.44% per Realtid (July 2026, including related parties) and bought further shares in May-July 2026 per insider-register coverage. CEO Per-Anders Tammerlov: 71,454 shares = 15.88% per Realtid; an older Borsvarlden article gave 117,118 shares = 24.87%, and 71,454/479,193 shares computes to about 14.9%, so the holding or the percentage basis changed or the reports use different bases (flagged conflict). Other directors proposed for re-election: Katarina Liden, Sofia Isaksson, Quoc Duong; their holdings were not found. Source: https://www.realtid.se/bors-finans/mangolds-vd-okar-sitt-agande/ ; https://borsvarlden.com/artiklar/mangolds-vd-och-storagare-per-anders-tammerlov-okar-sitt-aktieinnehav ; https://borsvarlden.com/artiklar/mangolds-styrelseordforande-per-ahlgren-okar-aktieinnehavet ; https://www.inderes.se/releases/mangolds-valberedning-infor-arsstamman-2026

thesis.business_description: Heba Fastighets AB (publ), incorporated 1952 and based in Stockholm, develops, owns and manages housing and community properties (residential and social-infrastructure) in the Stockholm region and the Mälardalen valley; B shares are listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. It has been a co-owner of the shared-housing company Colive since 2021 (company consultation response, 2023). H1 2026: property portfolio SEK 10,490.7m, rental income SEK 193.5m (H1 2025: 198.7m), NAV SEK 82.21 per share (74.88). Realtid reports a target of SEK 20bn property value (date and basis not verified). Sources: https://extraetf.com/ch/stock-profile/SE0017911480 ; https://boverket.se/contentassets/52240cd5077e4c4494b87e1a76c58b2d/heba-fastighets-ab.pdf ; https://www.realtid.se/bors-finans/heba-tar-sikte-pa-20-miljarder-i-fastighetsvarde/
thesis.competitive_position: A mid-sized Stockholm-region residential and community-property owner; strategy is growth in property value and in housing/social-infrastructure assets. Peers and market-share data were not located in this search; treat as a research gap. An aggregator (TradingView) lists Patrik Emanuelsson as CEO (not verified from the company site). Heba started a share buyback on 21 Aug 2026 (up to 1,651,200 B shares / SEK 50m; 245,000 B shares repurchased 5-9 Oct 2026). Sources: https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/heba-fastighets-aterkop-av-egna-aktier-i-heba-under-perioden-5-9-oktober-2026-vecka-41-20261012 ; https://in.tradingview.com/symbols/FWB-V7Y
thesis.main_shareholders: Aggregator only (Simply Wall St, undated, may be stale): AB Industricentralen 13.6%, Johan Vogel 12.4%, Christina Holmbergh 11.7%, Charlotte Ericsson 6.46%, Anna Vogel 6.11%, Anders Ericsson 5.12%, Birgitta Härnblad 4.92%. History: SBB bought B shares to hold 20.6% of capital / 11.0% of votes, then reportedly sold nearly all (leaving 0.74%) in mid-2023 per Affärsvärlden/Börsvärlden; Realtid pages show 2026 dates for the purchase story, which looks like a page-date artifact (unverified). An official Euroclear/company shareholder list was not retrieved; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/real-estate-management-and-development/sto-heba-b/heba-fastighets-shares/ownership ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/artikel/sbb-har-salt-nastan-hela-innehavet-i-heba ; https://www.realtid.se/bors-finans/sbb-ny-storagare-i-heba/
thesis.red_flags: Property company with a portfolio of SEK 10.5bn against an aggregator-reported market cap of about SEK 4.2bn (1 May 2026), implying material leverage and interest-rate/refinancing sensitivity; debt and loan-to-value were not retrieved (research gap). Rental income slipped year on year in H1 2026. Past ownership volatility (SBB entry and exit) may recur as a share-overhang risk. Concentrated family and holding-company ownership and the dual share structure limit minority influence. A quoted share price of SEK 24.35 (11 Jun 2026) on one aggregator conflicts with NAV of SEK 82.21 per share and is not relied upon. No litigation or accounting issues were identified in the sources reviewed. Sources: https://www.realtid.se/bors-finans/heba-tar-sikte-pa-20-miljarder-i-fastighetsvarde/ ; https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/HEBA-B.ST
thesis.insider_ownership: Family-linked holders (Vogel, Holmbergh, Ericsson families and AB Industricentralen) appear to account for a large share of capital per the aggregator, but whether they sit on the board or in management was not confirmed, and no official board/executive holding table was found; treat as a research gap. The company is buying back its own B shares (see competitive_position). Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/real-estate-management-and-development/sto-heba-b/heba-fastighets-shares/ownership ; https://www.inderes.fi/sv/releases/valberedningens-forslag-till-styrelse-infor-hebas-arsstamma-2026

thesis.business_description: AB Amber Grid is Lithuania's natural-gas transmission system operator (Vilnius; Nasdaq Vilnius Baltic Secondary List), operating about 2,288 km of transmission pipelines, 64 gas distribution stations, 4 metering stations and 2 compressor stations (Quartr/third-party summary), and connected to the Polish market via the GIPL interconnector. 2025: revenue EUR 69.6m, net profit EUR 1.3m (company release; a GlobeNewswire version gives EUR 1.4m, so the final figure is unclear) versus EUR 8.3m in 2024; EBITDA EUR 17.3m, adjusted EBITDA EUR 27.4m. Sources: https://ambergrid.lt/en/for-media/news/amber-grids-2025-results-revenue-reached-eur-69.6-million-net-profit-eur-1.3-million/1261 ; https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-02/67816965-ab-amber-grid-operating-results-for-the-year-2025-399.htm ; https://quartr.com/events/ab-amber-grid-amg1l-q2-2026_FeNf4ZjU
thesis.competitive_position: Regulated monopoly operator: earnings are set by the national energy regulator's allowed return and revenue cap rather than competition. The company says the 2025 profit fall reflected lower revenue, higher costs and a Cross-Border Cost Allocation payment to Poland for GIPL; adjusted net profit was roughly flat at about EUR 10.0m. Quartr (AI summary) reports 2027 average transmission price to fall 15.8% to EUR 1.28/MWh on a lower revenue cap and higher capacity bookings, and H1 2026 revenue of EUR 49.4m (+41%); both unverified against filings. Strategic focus on hydrogen and CO2 networks with major projects after 2033. Sources: https://ambergrid.lt/en/for-media/news/amber-grids-2025-results-revenue-reached-eur-69.6-million-net-profit-eur-1.3-million/1261 ; https://quartr.com/events/ab-amber-grid-amg1l-q2-2026_FeNf4ZjU
thesis.main_shareholders: Aggregator data (Investing.com, MarketScreener): UAB EPSO-G 96.58% (about 172.28m shares); free float 3.42%. EPSO-G is 100% owned by the Lithuanian Ministry of Energy (governance.lt), i.e. indirect state ownership of about 96.6%. The 96.58% figure is undated and not confirmed against the 2025 annual report (MarketScreener also cites an older 56.6% EPSO-G stake from 2014, which is stale); treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.investing.com/equities/amber-grid ; https://governance.lt/en/vvi/amber-grid ; https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/AMBER-GRID-44154872/
thesis.red_flags: Dominant state-controlled holder (about 96.6%) with a very thin free float (3.42%), so liquidity is limited and minority holders have little influence. Earnings depend on regulatory decisions (2025 net profit fell about 84% on regulatory timing and a GIPL cost-allocation payment; a lower 2027 revenue cap is reported by Quartr, unverified). Reported net profit differs between sources (EUR 1.3m vs 1.4m). Dividend for 2025 about EUR 0.056/share (about EUR 9.99m, Quartr; other aggregators say about 0.06). Gas-demand, transit and litigation risks were not located in this search. Sources: https://ambergrid.lt/en/for-media/news/amber-grids-2025-results-revenue-reached-eur-69.6-million-net-profit-eur-1.3-million/1261 ; https://quartr.com/events/ab-amber-grid-amg1l-q2-2026_FeNf4ZjU
thesis.insider_ownership: Could not locate board or management shareholdings in this search; treat as a research gap. As a state-controlled company, no founder/family holder exists; control sits with EPSO-G/Ministry of Energy. The 2025 integrated management report (https://ambergrid.lt/data/public/uploads/2026/03/integrated_management_report_2025.pdf) should contain the governance tables but its contents were not readable here.

thesis.business_description: Danish company (listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen) that innovates, designs and manufactures wireless communication solutions in three segments: Enterprise, Healthcare and ProAudio; stated growth areas include scaling the ProAudio modules business and new markets such as Defence and First Responders. 300+ employees at locations in Denmark, Hong Kong, Romania and the USA. FY2024/25 (to 30 Sep 2025; report published 27 Nov 2025): revenue DKK 547.1m, EBIT DKK 8.7m, equity DKK 334m (68% equity ratio), net liquidity DKK 153m. FY2025/26 guidance: revenue DKK 575-625m, EBITDA DKK 35-65m, EBIT DKK 0-30m. Sources: https://www.sustainabilityreports.com/rtx-as/2025/annual-report ; https://www.inderes.dk/releases/annual-report-202425-1
thesis.competitive_position: Niche design-and-manufacture partner for wireless (DECT-type and related) communication in enterprise, healthcare and professional audio; growth has relied on large framework-agreement customers and a few big ProAudio product customers. Long-term ambition: DKK 1bn revenue and EBITDA margin above 16% (company says the 2025/26 timing is no longer realistic), and a 2030 aim of double-digit annual growth and EBITDA margin above 15% (the two ambitions are stated in different reports; not reconciled). A 2023 healthcare agreement was expected to lift Healthcare revenue by 100-200% by 2025/26. H1 2025/26 (report 13 May 2026): revenue and EBITDA above prior year with improving gross margins; CEO flags uncertainty around RAM/memory pricing and lead times and a weak USD. Named competitors were not located in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://cdn.rtx.dk/media/uhrlbdjg/2024-25_q1_rtx_investor_presentation-v20250131.pdf ; https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/interim-report-for-q2-and-h1-202526-the-period-01102025-31032026
thesis.main_shareholders: No consolidated top-holder table with percentages was located in this search; treat as a research gap. From major-shareholder announcements: Polaris PPU Master Fund ICAV 7% (592,435 shares, as of 5 Mar 2025); Michael Voss / Fundamental Fondsmaeglerselskab A/S above 5% (as of 5 Jan 2026); ATP 5.95% (514,605 shares, Feb 2022 - stale, current status unknown); Danske Bank fell below 5% on 7 Feb 2024. RTX itself held more than 5% in treasury shares after a buyback (May 2024). These are individual threshold notices of differing dates and not a current register. Sources: https://inderes.dk/releases/major-shareholder-announcement-339 ; https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/major-shareholder-announcement-384 ; https://www.mfn.se/nir/a/rtx/major-shareholder-announcement-391e585d.iframe ; https://cdn.rtx.dk/media/bovfwvft/rtx-ca-no-26-2024-150524-major-shareholder-announcement.pdf
thesis.red_flags: Customer concentration (a few large ProAudio product customers and framework-agreement Enterprise customers); revenue is volatile (H1 2023/24 revenue DKK 207.1m vs DKK 387.5m a year earlier; customer inventory destocking). Previous revenue/margin targets (DKK 1bn, EBITDA above 16% in 2025/26) have been missed or deferred. Thin profitability (EBIT DKK 8.7m on DKK 547.1m in 2024/25). Exposure to USD weakness and memory/component pricing. Several mid-size (5-7%) holders mean ownership is concentrated among a few funds/individuals. No litigation or accounting concerns identified in this search, but no audit report was reviewed. Sources: https://cdn.rtx.dk/media/ac5pmwaa/rtx-ca-no-45-2024-281124-annual-report-2023_24.pdf ; https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/interim-report-for-q2-and-h1-202526-the-period-01102025-31032026
thesis.insider_ownership: Could not locate current share counts or percentages for board and executives in this search; treat as a research gap (the annual report lists them). Named: CEO Peter Ropke (CEO since 20 Sep 2016 per Simply Wall St, ownership shown as n/a); board chair is Henrik Schimmell per RTX's 2025 insider-trade announcements, while Simply Wall St (aggregator) names Peter Thostrup as chairman - CONFLICT, the company announcements are likelier current. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/tech/bats-chixe-rtxc/rtx-shares/management ; https://app.researchpool.com/provider/globenewswire/rtx-as-rtx-major-shareholder-announcement-3

thesis.business_description: Munich-based real-estate company (Marsstrasse 46-48, Munich per the AGM contact data), a legacy of the Sedlmayr brewing family after the separation of the brewing business. Acquires, manages and exploits real estate, owning residential and commercial buildings in Munich and, via a majority stake in Dinkelacker AG, property in the Stuttgart region. Fiscal year runs 1 October to 30 September. Dinkelacker's 2024/25 report cites 80 properties, 105 buildings and 101,409 sqm lettable area, annual net profit of EUR10.4m (AG) and EUR11.2m (group); a balance-sheet total of EUR168.9m (2023/24: EUR170.5m) was shown but it is unclear whether it relates to the AG or group. Sources disagree on the legal form (AG vs KGaA); AGM invitations use AG. Source: https://www.boerse.de/unternehmensprofil/Sedlmayr-Grund-und-Immobilien-Aktie/DE0007224008 ; https://www.hauptversammlung.de/fileadmin/public/user_upload/DIA_GB25.pdf ; https://www.hauptversammlung.de/fileadmin/public/user_upload/Sedl_TO25.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: Could not locate market-position data, portfolio size or valuation for Sedlmayr itself (research gap). Small private-landlord style property holder in Munich with a majority-held, separately listed Dinkelacker AG (exact stake percentage not located; no source gave it). Source: https://www.finanzen.net/unternehmensprofil/sedlmayr_grund_und_immobilien ; https://www.hauptversammlung.de/fileadmin/public/user_upload/DIA_GB25.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: Aggregator only (dates not shown): boerse.de lists Sedlmayr Treuhandgesellschaft mbH 87.25% with free float 12.75%; finanzen.net lists the Sedlmayr family about 87.26% and free float about 12.74%. Official voting-rights notices or annual-report shareholder note not located. Source: https://www.boerse.de/unternehmensprofil/Sedlmayr-Grund-und-Immobilien-Aktie/DE0007224008 ; https://www.finanzen.net/unternehmensprofil/sedlmayr_grund_und_immobilien
thesis.red_flags: Controlled company: about 87% held by one trust/family vehicle, leaving about 13% free float (thin liquidity). Governance: the management board opened a status procedure (Statusverfahren, section 97 ff. AktG) on 27 Feb 2026 on the composition of the supervisory board, with a related articles amendment on the 8 May 2026 AGM agenda; the outcome was not found. A precautionary second AGM was convened for 18 July 2025 in case resolutions of the 13 May 2025 AGM were successfully challenged (whether a challenge was filed is unknown). The May 2025 AGM also covered a domination and profit-transfer agreement with the subsidiary 'Schwabinger Brau' Grundbesitz GmbH (no outside shareholders, so no compensation due). Dinkelacker stake percentage and Sedlmayr's own 2024/25 accounts were not located. Source: https://www.hauptversammlung.de/fileadmin/public/user_upload/Sedlmayr_TO26.pdf ; https://www.hauptversammlung.de/fileadmin/public/user_upload/Sedl_2TO2025.pdf ; https://www.hauptversammlung.de/fileadmin/public/user_upload/Sedl_TO25.pdf
thesis.website: Could not confirm an official website in this search (an AGM contact address uses the domain sedlmayr-ag.de; the site URL itself was not verified).
thesis.insider_ownership: Family/trust ownership of about 87% via Sedlmayr Treuhandgesellschaft mbH (aggregator; not confirmed from a filing). Management board per boerse.de (date unclear, possibly stale): Dr. Hermann Brandstetter (chair), Martin Schumacher, Alexander Adam, Enno Braune; individual holdings not located. Source: https://www.boerse.de/unternehmensprofil/Sedlmayr-Grund-und-Immobilien-Aktie/DE0007224008

thesis.business_description: Artea SA is a French integrated real-estate-led group: development of service parks, landmark projects, urban office buildings, eco-districts, hotels and residential projects, hospitality (hotels; 2026 programmes Paros and Sant'Orsola), and renewable energy via Dream Energy (deconsolidated in 2025). Chairman and CEO Philippe Baudry (since 2013). FY2025: revenue about EUR 58.2m (-41.8%), current operating result -EUR 9.8m, net loss group share EUR 16.7m after a EUR 13.2m gain on deconsolidating Dream Energy; recurring real-estate revenue about EUR 20m (+2%). Revenue conflicts across sources (Parqet shows EUR 31.9m). HQ conflicts (Paris 16e vs Le Vesinet in company notices). Sources: https://www.boursedirect.fr/fr/actualites/categorie/actualites-financieres/artea-realise-un-resultat-net-part-du-groupe-de-16-7-meur-en-2025-zone-bourse-fb836424fc099d472a347706e6d4512cc6b77e88 ; https://www.ideal-investisseur.fr/en/stock-news/artea-net-loss-of-eur16-7m-in-2025-revenue-down-by-41-8/20102.html ; https://www.abcbourse.com/marches/artea-creuse-sa-perte-en-2025-sur-fond-de-chute-du-chiffre-daffaires_697572
thesis.competitive_position: Micro-cap developer/investor in French (and Italian/Greek hotel) real estate with a diversified, project-driven model; no evidence found of a dominant niche, market share or named competitors. Management says it will refocus resources on high-value programmes to restore profitability and cash flow in 2026. Market-position data not located; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.ideal-investisseur.fr/en/stock-news/artea-net-loss-of-eur16-7m-in-2025-revenue-down-by-41-8/20102.html ; https://in.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ARTEA-18578993/
thesis.main_shareholders: Controlled by Arteme1, a vehicle of chairman Philippe Baudry: a 2019 AMF threshold filing reports Arteme1 crossing 90%, with 93.75% of capital and 85.93% of voting rights (stale, 2019). Share data: 4,968,952 shares / 9,374,563 voting rights at the June 2024 AGM (double voting rights); 5,014,302 shares of which 4,790,230 entitled to vote at the 2026 AGM, with 95.89% quorum. Idéal Investisseur shows insiders at 96.4% but says thresholds are not integrated (indicative, unverified). No current official shareholder table located; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/307/8888/01/FC307294645_20190802.pdf ; https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/MKW/2024/06/FCMKW138481_20240626.pdf ; https://www.abcbourse.com/marches/artea-valide-toutes-les-resolutions-lors-de-son-assemblee-generale-2026_699368 ; https://www.ideal-investisseur.fr/actions/artea-FR0012185536-societe.html
thesis.insider_ownership: Philippe Baudry (chairman/CEO) controls the company through Arteme1 (93.75% of capital in 2019 per AMF filing; current percentage not confirmed). Aggregator shows insiders at about 96.4% (unverified). Other board members' holdings not located. Sources: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/307/8888/01/FC307294645_20190802.pdf ; https://www.ideal-investisseur.fr/actions/artea-FR0012185536-societe.html
thesis.red_flags: (1) Extreme ownership concentration (controller around 90%+ in 2019) means a very thin free float and minimal minority influence; the company said in 2019 it intended to widen the public float, but no follow-through was found. (2) Deteriorating financials: FY2025 revenue -41.8%, operating loss EUR 9.8m, net loss EUR 16.7m, equity down to EUR 62.1m from EUR 79.6m, net debt EUR 128.4m (stable vs EUR 129.9m), current net cash flow -EUR 3.4m; the net result was cushioned by a one-off EUR 13.2m deconsolidation gain. (3) Listing status unclear: the June 2025 AGM approved transferring the listing from Euronext Paris to Euronext Growth Paris (lighter regime), but a MarketScreener page still showed Euronext Paris in Aug 2026; completion not confirmed. (4) Source conflicts on revenue (EUR 31.9m vs 58.2m) and HQ. Sources: https://www.boursedirect.fr/fr/actualites/categorie/divers/artea-l-ag-approuve-le-projet-de-transfert-de-la-cotation-des-titres-sur-le-marche-euronext-growth-paris-boursier-5e36554314e9494b2ff909e1e0c609d728fa7985 ; https://www.ideal-investisseur.fr/en/stock-news/artea-net-loss-of-eur16-7m-in-2025-revenue-down-by-41-8/20102.html ; https://www.marketscreener.com/ARTEA-18578993/company/
thesis.website: Official website not confirmed in the searches run; research gap (verify before publishing).

thesis.business_description: Mineralbrunnen Überkingen-Teinach GmbH & Co. KGaA is a southern German (Baden-Württemberg) mineral-water and soft-drinks producer with regional brands including Teinacher and Krumbach and bottling sites such as Bad Teinach-Zavelstein and Kißlegg. 2025 gross revenue was EUR 193.3m (+3.8%), net revenue after deductions and excise was EUR 162.4m (+4.0%), and EBITDA was EUR 20.0m (2024: 21.1m). Sources: https://www.mynewsdesk.com/de/karlsberg/pressreleases/mineralbrunnen-ueberkingen-teinach-waechst-im-fuenften-jahr-in-folge-umsatz-2025-erneut-gesteigert-3444398 ; https://www.meininger.de/alkoholfreie-getraenke/hersteller/ueberkingen-teinach-umsatzplus-aber-ertragsminus
thesis.competitive_position: A regional premium mineral-water player growing for five consecutive years, led by the Teinacher brand (+7.9% in 2025) and Krumbach (+1.7%). It is managed within the Karlsberg beverage group, whose Karlsberg International Getränkemanagement GmbH is the general partner. It invested EUR 18.4m in 2025 in bottling lines and guides to slight revenue growth and EBITDA moderately above 2025 in 2026. It competes in a fragmented German mineral-water market with many regional springs and national brands; market shares were not found in this search. Sources: https://www.mynewsdesk.com/de/karlsberg/pressreleases/mineralbrunnen-ueberkingen-teinach-waechst-im-fuenften-jahr-in-folge-umsatz-2025-erneut-gesteigert-3444398 ; https://www.about-drinks.com/mineralbrunnen-ueberkingen-teinach-erwartet-leichten-anstieg-der-umsatzerloese/
thesis.main_shareholders: Could not confirm a current official shareholder table. finanzen.net (aggregator, undated, page for the preference share class) lists Förderverein des Württ.-Hohenz. Gaststättengewerbes 38.55%, Weber Richard Family 1.85% and free float 59.60%; the figures are likely around 2021 and may refer to one share class only. The company has ordinary and preference shares (about 8m shares in total per an aggregator). A 2018/19 buyback left it holding 285,000 treasury shares (about 3.52% of capital / 4.81% of ordinary shares). The Karlsberg group's capital stake was not verified in this search; at the conversion to KGaA, the general partner was intended to hold no capital. Treat as a research gap and verify in the annual report. Sources: https://www.finanzen.net/unternehmensprofil/mineralbrunnen_ueberkingen-teinach_vz ; https://www.about-drinks.com/mineralbrunnen-ueberkingen-teinach-gmbh-co-kgaa-beschliesst-oeffentliches-aktienrueckkaufangebot/ ; https://lebensmittelpraxis.de/industrie-aktuell/13653-ueberkingen-teinach-formwechsel.html
thesis.red_flags: No accounting or litigation issues were identified from official sources. Caveats: the KGaA structure means outside shareholders have limited influence over the general partner (Karlsberg-controlled management), with potential related-party exposure to the Karlsberg group. It is traded on the less-regulated Freiverkehr segment, with limited disclosure and liquidity. The 2025 EBITDA guidance was slightly missed because of higher costs, and net income reportedly fell sharply ('brach ein') amid heavy capex. Sources: https://lebensmittelpraxis.de/industrie-aktuell/48416-getraenkeindustrie-mineralbrunnen-ueberkingen-teinach-waechst-verdient-aber-deutlich-weniger.html ; https://www.mynewsdesk.com/de/karlsberg/pressreleases/mineralbrunnen-ueberkingen-teinach-waechst-im-fuenften-jahr-in-folge-umsatz-2025-erneut-gesteigert-3444398
thesis.insider_ownership: Management is provided by the general partner Karlsberg International Getränkemanagement GmbH (managing directors named as Martin Adam, Andreas Gaupp and Gerd Gründahl). No personal shareholdings of these managers or of supervisory board members were located. Treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.boerse-stuttgart.de/-/media/files/geschaeftspartner/listing/freiverkehr-plus/mineralbrunnen-ueberkingen-teinach-gmbh/unternehmensdarstellung/20210330_unternehmensdarstellung-mineralbrunnen-ueberkingen-teinach-de.ashx ; https://www.meininger.de/alkoholfreie-getraenke/hersteller/ueberkingen-teinach-gruppe-erfolgreiche-hauptversammlung

thesis.business_description: McBride plc is a UK-headquartered (Manchester) manufacturer of private-label/contract household cleaning and laundry products (liquids, unit dosing, powders, aerosols) sold mainly to European retailers, with a smaller Asia-Pacific business. FY to 30 June 2026 revenue was GBP 934.2m (+0.8% reported, -1.8% at constant currency) and adjusted EBITDA was GBP 80.0m. Sources: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/mcbride--mcb/results-for-the-year-ended-30-june-2026/9771587 ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McBride_plc
thesis.competitive_position: A leading European private-label household-products supplier. It benefits from structural private-label share gains (European private-label volume share was 36.7% in the 12 months to June 2026, up about one point per the earnings call) but competes against branded giants and other private-label makers on price. After year-end it announced the Eurotab acquisition and a Vestacy contract-manufacturing agreement, which management/analysts estimate could add about GBP 170m of revenue by H2 FY2028. Sources: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-mcbride-h2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-09-16/ ; https://quartr.com/events/mcbride-plc-mcb-h2-2026_FgjxEgOw
thesis.main_shareholders: From the company's significant-shareholders page (shareholdings as at 5 August 2026): Teleios Capital Partners 21.37% (38,150,906 shares, per notice of 24 Nov 2025), Zama Capital 12.07%, Stichting Pieter Bastiaan 5.17%, Aberforth Partners 4.99%, Premier Miton 4.80%, and the McBride Employee Benefit Trust 4.15%. Teleios has been reducing its stake (23.76% to 22.51% in Oct 2025, then 21.37%). Sources: https://www.mcbride.co.uk/fr/investisseurs/share-price-centre/significant-shareholders/ ; https://www.ticker.app/lse/MCB/rns/2025-11-25/holdings-in-company/8125I
thesis.red_flags: Margins are thin and volatile because of raw-material and energy costs: FY2026 profit fell on a Q4 margin-recovery lag after Middle East-driven inflation, and management expects continued margin pressure. Net debt rose to GBP 122.8m (1.5x adj. EBITDA, from 1.2x). Customer concentration in European grocery retail and price-competitive private-label tenders are structural risks. The company has a concentrated activist/hedge-fund register (Teleios plus Zama about 33%). No competition investigation or fine involving McBride was found in this search; it was not exhaustive. Sources: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/mcbride--mcb/results-for-the-year-ended-30-june-2026/9771587 ; https://quartr.com/events/mcbride-plc-mcb-h2-2026_FgjxEgOw
thesis.insider_ownership: Per the company's directors/PDMR table as at 30 June 2026, CEO Chris Smith beneficially holds 2,021,640 shares (1,810,141 in his own name, 211,499 held by his wife). That is about 1% of the company (Simply Wall St estimates 0.99%). He sold 842,654 shares in October 2025 to cover tax on LTIP/RSU vesting. Holdings of other directors were not captured in this search. The EBT holds 4.15%. Sources: https://www.mcbride.co.uk/de/investoren/share-price-centre/significant-shareholders/ ; https://www.ticker.app/lse/MCB/rns/2025-10-17/DirectorPDMR-Shareholding/9200D

thesis.business_description: Portuguese gaming and real-estate group (incorporated 1958, HQ Estoril) that holds casino concessions: Casino Estoril and Casino Lisboa (new concessions secured in 2023 per Macau Business) and, until its exit, Casino da Povoa (via subsidiary Varzim Sol), plus online casino and sports-betting activity. The Povoa concession ended after Estoril Sol did not bid in the new tender (deadline 29 Dec 2025; awarded to Barriere per one report; one outlet gives an end date of 30 Apr 2026 - not reconciled). Controlled by Finansol - Sociedade de Controlo, SGPS, S.A.; also linked in press to Macau's STDM. Sources: https://macaubusiness.com/stdms-estoril-sol-posts-e25-million-loss-in-2025/ ; https://agbrief.com/news/05/01/2026/estoril-sol-portugals-casino-leader-abandons-concession-for-povoa-de-varzim/ ; https://simplywall.st/stock/enxtls/eson
thesis.competitive_position: Largest Portuguese casino operator historically (Estoril and Lisbon casinos plus Povoa); competitors in concession tenders include Solverde (Espinho and Algarve) and Barriere (Povoa). Its position is concession-based (licensed, regulated gaming zones), so the moat depends on retaining concessions; exit from Povoa reduces scale to two casinos (Estoril, Lisbon). Management plans cost reductions: a EUR 3.3m restructuring provision and permanent operating-cost cuts (Observador, workers' meeting reported Aug 2026). Market share and operating KPIs (GGR, visits) were not located in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://agbrief.com/news/05/01/2026/estoril-sol-portugals-casino-leader-abandons-concession-for-povoa-de-varzim/ ; https://observador.pt/2026/08/05/trabalhadores-da-estoril-sol-em-plenario-apos-prejuizo-subir-para-179-milhoes-e-provisao-para-reestruturacao/
thesis.main_shareholders: Per an Estoril-Sol CMVM notice reported by Executive Digest (stated 'as of 15 September'; year not clear in the snippet, so potentially stale): Finansol 6,930,604 shares = 57.79% of capital and 58.09% of votes; Fozpatrimonio directly 3,917,793 shares = 32.67% of capital and 32.84% of votes; 62,565 treasury shares; about 11.99 million shares in total. A 2022 report attributes a 32.7% stake to the Amorim Turismo group (via Sociedade Figueira Praia) and about 9% to small holders - the holding entity (Fozpatrimonio vs Amorim Turismo) should be checked against the CMVM filing. No reported free float located. Sources: https://executivedigest.sapo.pt/?p=813716 ; https://infotrustgo.pt/en/companies/estoril-sol-sgps-sa
thesis.red_flags: Heavy losses: 2025 loss attributable to shareholders EUR 25.3m (vs EUR 12.1m in 2024) and consolidated net loss EUR 17.9m, with EUR 13.2m impairment on concession-related assets (outlets differ; one headline cites a USD 28.8m attributable loss - unreconciled). Accounts flag a need to reinforce equity by about EUR 35m to meet Gaming Law requirements (Observador), and one Macau Business headline cites a EUR 36.9m tax-penalty risk (body not read). Delayed accounts (published 20 Jul 2026) due to complexity of Povoa exit. Loss of Povoa concession; union concerns on viability. Controlled by Finansol (57.79%) with Amorim-linked holder at ~32.7%: tiny free float (research gap on exact figure), related-party and minority-investor risk. Concession/regulatory dependence (state licensing; a 2023 court suspension of the Lisbon/Estoril tender was reported). Sources: https://macaubusiness.com/stdms-estoril-sol-posts-e25-million-loss-in-2025/ ; https://agbrief.com/news/macau/23/07/2026/stdm-controlled-estoril-sol-posts-28-8m-attributable-loss-in-2025/ ; https://observador.pt/2026/08/05/trabalhadores-da-estoril-sol-em-plenario-apos-prejuizo-subir-para-179-milhoes-e-provisao-para-reestruturacao/
thesis.website: Could not verify the official website in this search; likely https://www.estoril-sol.com - treat as unverified.
thesis.insider_ownership: Controlling holder Finansol (57.79%) is described in press as held by the descendants of Stanley Ho (snippet, unverified against a filing). Press/aggregator profiles name Pansy Ho (board member, chairs the executive committee) and list Dr Stanley Ho as chairman and Wing Chann Ka as vice-chairman from 2025 (MarketScreener); the Stanley Ho chairman listing looks stale and the current board was not confirmed. Individual director holdings with percentages could not be located; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://executivedigest.sapo.pt/?p=813716 ; https://it.marketscreener.com/insider/WING-CHANN-KA-A1OJES/

thesis.business_description: ScandBook Holding AB (HQ Falun, Sweden) manufactures and sells hardcover and softcover books to publishers, with plants in Sweden, Lithuania and, since the Norhaven Book A/S acquisition (reported Sep 2025), Denmark. FY2025 (annual report): net sales SEK 489.3m (416.8m), EBITDA SEK 67.7m (49.7m), profit SEK 40.7m, proposed dividend SEK 2.75 per share, net debt SEK 74.5m (net cash the year before); Norhaven contributed two months. Shares were renamed B-shares from 17 Jun 2026 (new ISIN/ticker; the input ticker may need checking). Sources: https://storage.mfn.se/93998f53-1c86-4df6-baea-b42be822bcf0/arsredovisning-scandbook-holding-2025.pdf ; https://inderes.dk/en/companies/ScandBook-Holding ; https://financialfilings.com/companies/scandbook-holding-ab/ ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/scandbook-holding
thesis.competitive_position: A 2022 LINC research note called it the largest Swedish book producer, supplying fiction to 300+ publishers, with market-leading digital printing and a push into markets beyond the Nordics; the Nordic market had shrunk 4.9% in 2018-20 (dated). The Norhaven deal adds Danish capacity. Named competitors, current market share and the acquisition price were not found; treat as a research gap. The earlier screen notes lower additional consideration (earn-out) in the Q2 2026 report, not re-verified here. Sources: https://linclund.com/scandbook ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/scandbook-nu-med-danskar-i-bockerna ; https://storage.mfn.se/93998f53-1c86-4df6-baea-b42be822bcf0/arsredovisning-scandbook-holding-2025.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: Affarsvarlden/Inderes (Millistream data; Inderes shows a 2024-era listing, both undated): Auris Holding 49.3% of capital / 28.9% of votes; Bronsstadet (Peter Gyllenhammar's holding company) 21.3% of capital / 29.9% of votes; Avanza Pension 5.6-6.2%; SIP 203 / Touplus Assurance 5.4-6.5%; Par Nilsson 3.9%. In June 2026 Bronsstadet bought just over 1.01m shares from Accent Equity, reported as 29.9% (just under the mandatory-bid threshold; unclear if capital or votes, not reconciled with the 21.3% figure); Accent's remaining 9.75% was reportedly sold the same day to an undisclosed buyer. Simply Wall St (S&P data May/Sep 2025) shows conflicting figures (Auris 25.6%, Peter Gyllenhammar AB 31.3%). Current official register not located. Sources: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/scandbook-holding ; https://inderes.dk/en/companies/ScandBook-Holding/ownership ; https://www.realtid.se/bors-finans/bronsstadet-tar-over-accents-roll/ ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/commercial-services/sto-sbok/scandbook-holding-shares/ownership
thesis.insider_ownership: Founding/anchor owner family: Auris Holding is the Odd Rune Austgulen vehicle (49.3% capital); Austgulen chaired the company 2015-2024 and his son Henrik is a board member. Peter Gyllenhammar's Bronsstadet (21.3% capital) has Carina Heilborn on the board. Current chairman Havard Grjotheim (holding not found). CEO Paulius Juska (CEO since 2022) held no shares per an Affarsvarlden piece (date uncertain, possibly 2024). Sources: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/scandbook-nu-med-danskar-i-bockerna ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/scandbook-holding ; https://www.realtid.se/bors-finans/bronsstadet-tar-over-accents-roll/
thesis.red_flags: Known event (sanity-checked): ScandBook is the ACQUIRER of Norhaven Book (announced Sep 2025; the annual report shows only two months of contribution in FY2025, so the closing date should be verified); no bid for ScandBook found. Risks: (1) two blocks (Auris about 49%, Bronsstadet about 21%+) hold about 70% of capital, leaving a thin float, and Bronsstadet's June 2026 purchase sits just below the 30% mandatory-bid line, so a control contest or bid is a possibility; (2) acquisition took the company from net cash to SEK 74.5m net debt and an earn-out is outstanding; (3) shrinking Nordic book market (dated figure) and dependence on publisher customers (concentration not quantified); (4) share-class change in 2026 (B-share) and conflicting ownership data across providers. Sources: https://storage.mfn.se/93998f53-1c86-4df6-baea-b42be822bcf0/arsredovisning-scandbook-holding-2025.pdf ; https://www.realtid.se/bors-finans/bronsstadet-tar-over-accents-roll/ ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/scandbook-holding
thesis.website: https://www.scandbook.se (not confirmed by the searches run; verify before publishing)

thesis.business_description: AS Tallinna Vesi is the regulated water supply and sewerage utility for Tallinn and surrounding municipalities (Maardu, Saue, Harku, Saku): about 25,000 private and business customers, about 500,000 end-consumers, 360 employees at end-2025, over 1,210 km of water pipes and over 1,200 km of wastewater pipes. Subsidiaries Watercom OU and ASTV Green Energy OU (in liquidation). Listed on Nasdaq Baltic Main List; HQ Tallinn. FY2025 net profit EUR 14.2m, dividend EUR 0.57 per share approved at the 23 Apr 2026 AGM. Sources: https://www.aastaaruanne-2025.tallinnavesi.ee/company ; https://aastaaruanne-2022.tallinnavesi.ee/en ; https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/resolutions-adopted-by-the-annual-general-meeting-of-shareholders-of-aktsiaselts-tallinna-vesi-on-23-april-2026
thesis.competitive_position: Natural regional monopoly under regulation: designated water undertaker for the main Tallinn service area until 30 Nov 2032 and administrative contract with the city for 1 Dec 2022 to 30 Jan 2032; prices set by the Competition Authority (from 1 May 2025 EUR 2.10/m3 private and EUR 3.33/m3 business, excl. VAT; pricing principles to be harmonised by July 2026). Regulated model gives stable cash flow; dividend policy 50-80% of profit. Investment plan about EUR 60m for 2025 (secondary source). Sources: https://www.aastaaruanne-2022.tallinnavesi.ee/en ; https://tallinnavesi.ee/en/investor/ ; https://tallinnavesi.ee/en/?p=39107
thesis.main_shareholders: After the 31 Mar 2021 purchase of United Utilities' stake, the City of Tallinn held 10,469,565 A-shares plus 1 B-share = 52.35% and OU Utilitas 3,530,435 A-shares = 17.65% (company/Utilitas announcements; implies about 20m shares and, by my arithmetic, about 30% free float). The 2022 annual report confirms only Utilitas and the City as direct holders above 5%. No 2025/2026 shareholder table was located, so these percentages are from 2021 and not reconfirmed. Sources: https://utilitas.ee/en/utilitas-and-the-city-of-tallinn-acquires-shares-in-as-tallinna-vesi/ ; https://news.err.ee/1608096088/united-utilities-to-sell-stake-in-tallinna-vesi-to-tallinn-utilitas ; https://aastaaruanne-2022.tallinnavesi.ee/en
thesis.insider_ownership: Supervisory Council (2025) mainly represents the two controlling holders: Utilitas - Priit Koit (chair), Robert Kitt, Niall Patrick Mills; City of Tallinn - Karoline Ebba Anna Ullman, Silver Tamm, Mart Magi, Priit Lello; independents Priit Rohumaa and Gerli Kivisoo. At the 23 Apr 2026 AGM shareholders voted to remove Mart Magi, with Priit Lello proposed for election. Personal shareholdings of Council and Management Board members were not located; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://tallinnavesi.ee/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Council-Report-on-activities-2025.pdf ; https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/resolutions-adopted-by-the-annual-general-meeting-of-shareholders-of-aktsiaselts-tallinna-vesi-on-23-april-2026
thesis.red_flags: (1) Operational: on 31 Dec 2025 frazil ice blocked the Lake Ulemiste intake and, with high New Year's Eve demand, pressure fell in several Tallinn districts; supply was restored by the morning of 1 Jan 2026; the company is reviewing crisis plans and resilience investment and faced media criticism (company statement of 9 Jan 2026). (2) Regulatory/political: prices set by the Competition Authority, the city is the majority owner and counterparty to the administrative contract (to Jan 2032), and pricing harmonisation due by July 2026. (3) About 70% held by two related-purpose owners (city and Utilitas), leaving limited float (2021 data). (4) Financing/capex needs (Nordic Investment Bank loan signed 2025). Sources: https://tallinnavesi.ee/en/?p=40564 ; https://www.err.ee/1609898695/terik-tallinna-veekatkestusest-see-on-ajutine-suur-ebamugavus ; https://tallinnavesi.ee/en/?p=39107 ; https://tallinnavesi.ee/en/2025

thesis.business_description: Forterra plc is a UK manufacturer of building products, mainly clay bricks and concrete products (the Bison precast business was acquired in 2017 for GBP20m). Search results reference the Desford brick factory and the Accrington facility (Omnia extruded brick slips); its brick range is weighted to extruded bricks and exposed to UK new-build housing. FY2025 (published 25 March 2026): revenue up 12.1% to GBP386m, adjusted EBITDA GBP61.6m. Registered HQ town was not confirmed in the search results. Sources: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/forterra-backs-guidance-revenue-rises-amid-strong-new-build-demand ; https://finance.yahoo.com/news/forterra-h2-earnings-call-highlights-115046072.html ; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/forterra--fort/acquisition-of-bison-manufacturing-ltd/4724493
thesis.competitive_position: Listed UK brick and concrete-products maker with roughly GBP386m FY2025 revenue; management said it outperformed the wider market helped by its extruded-brick/new-build exposure, and guided 2026 to be slightly ahead of 2025 with price rises to cover cost inflation. Market-share figures, named competitors and moat details were not located in this search (research gap). Listing status verification: Forterra plc was still publishing RNS announcements via Investegate/LSE as of 12 October 2026 (a 'Transaction in Own Shares' buyback notice), it announced a GBP20m buyback with FY2025 results, and the London Stock Exchange company page for FORT is live. No Rule 2.7 firm offer, scheme or cancellation of admission was found, so it appears still listed, but this was not confirmed against an official delisting register. Sources: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/forterra--fort/transaction-in-own-shares/9654843 ; https://www.londonstockexchange.com/stock/FORT/forterra-plc/company-page ; https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/forterra-backs-guidance-revenue-rises-amid-strong-new-build-demand
thesis.main_shareholders: Could not locate the current substantial-shareholder table (Directors' Report of the 2025 Annual Report, published 25 March 2026, or 'Holding(s) in Company' RNS contents) in this search; treat as a research gap. History only: Lone Star Funds floated Forterra in 2016 (35% sold at 180p) and later sold a 53% stake for about GBP206m (date not shown), so Lone Star is not presumed to be a current holder. Fintel (aggregator) lists funds such as Dimensional and State Street-linked vehicles, without verified percentages. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forterra_plc ; https://www.unquote.com/uk/official-record/3004634/lone-star-sells-53-of-forterra-for-gbp206m ; https://fintel.io/so/de/f0t ; https://www.sustainabilityreports.com/forterra/2025/annual-report-and-accounts
thesis.insider_ownership: Only one data point found: Chair Nigel Lingwood bought 50,000 shares at GBP1.798 (RNS dated 23 October 2025), giving a total beneficial interest of 50,000 ordinary shares (a very small holding). Executive directors' and other holdings were not located; research gap. Source: https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/FORT/directorpdmr-shareholding-hyrjgn7rilabl7p.html
thesis.red_flags: FY2025 results mention exceptional costs of GBP2.7m for an aborted corporate transaction announced at the earlier interim results (bidder not named in the results; the year of that filing should be checked). Net debt before leases GBP55.7m at FY2025 (moderate). Cyclical dependence on UK new-build housing and energy-cost inflation. Listing status is not confirmed by an official register, only by continued RNS activity to 12 Oct 2026. No litigation or accounting issues found in these results. Sources: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/forterra--fort/full-year-results/8774564 ; https://finance.yahoo.com/news/forterra-h2-earnings-call-highlights-115046072.html
thesis.website: Not confirmed in search results (a search summary mentioned forterra.co.uk/investors as the report location, but the page itself was not returned).

thesis.business_description: Neobo Fastigheter AB is a Swedish real estate company (Nasdaq Stockholm: NEOBO) that manages and refines residential properties long term in municipalities with strong demand for rental apartments. FY2025: net operating income SEK 513m, profit from property management SEK 201m, property portfolio SEK 13,562m at year-end. H1 2026: property value SEK 13,601m, rental income SEK 469m. Headquarters location was not stated in the sources retrieved (only that the 2026 AGM was held in Stockholm); treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.neobo.se/en/neobo-publishes-annual-report-for-2025/ ; https://www.neobo.se/en/neobo-fastigheter-ab-publ-year-end-report-january-december-2025/ ; https://www.neobo.se/en/neobo-fastigheter-ab-publ-interim-report-january-june-2026/
thesis.competitive_position: Niche is residential rental portfolios in Swedish municipalities with strong rental demand; H1 2026 like-for-like rental income grew 3.8%, and the company has been divesting properties (lower net operating income from sold assets) and refinancing (two loans totaling SEK 1.2bn extended in the quarter at lower margins than its average). Net asset value per share was SEK 48.02 at 30 June 2026. Named competitors, apartment count and market-share data were not found in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.neobo.se/en/neobo-fastigheter-ab-publ-interim-report-january-june-2026/ ; https://www.neobo.se/en/neobo-publishes-annual-report-for-2025/
thesis.main_shareholders: No controlling holder; ownership is fragmented and sources conflict and are undated. Neobo's own release says Bjorn Danckwardt-Lillieström holds about 9.5% (mostly via an Avanza investment insurance policy). Inderes (Millistream data, undated, aggregator): ICA-handlarnas Forbund 11.0%, Danckwardt-Lillieström 9.4%, Martin Larsen 6.9%, Lansforsakringar Fonder 5.0%, Avanza Pension 5.0%. Simply Wall St (aggregator, c.2025): Avanza Fonder ~13.2%, ICA-handlarnas Forbund ~10.3%, Martin Larsen ~7.5%; top 25 holders 51.7%. The 2026 nomination committee (ICA retailers' association, Martin Larsen, Lansforsakringar Fondforvaltning, plus chair) represents ~23.3% of shares and votes. Total 146,030,803 shares and votes, of which 5,520,737 (3.78%) are treasury shares (May 2026). Official Euroclear holder list not located. Sources: https://www.neobo.se/en/neobos-nomination-committee-proposes-bjorn-danckwardt-lilliestrom-as-new-board-member/ ; https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/nomination-committee-for-neobos-annual-general-meeting-2026 ; https://www.inderes.dk/en/companies/Neobo-Fastigheter/ownership ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/real-estate-management-and-development/sto-neobo/neobo-fastigheter-shares/ownership ; https://www.neobo.se/en/increased-number-of-shares-and-votes-in-neobo-due-to-exercise-of-warrants/
thesis.insider_ownership: Chair Jan-Erik Hojvall bought 500,000 shares on 11 March 2025 (Simply Wall St, aggregator); his total holding was not located. Martin Larsen (about 7-7.5% per aggregators) sits on the nomination committee. Bjorn Danckwardt-Lillieström (~9.5%) was proposed by the nomination committee as a new board member for the 2026 AGM; whether he was elected was not confirmed in this search. CEO Ylva Sarby Westman and CFO Maria Strandberg are named as contacts; their holdings were not found. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/real-estate-management-and-development/lse-0xcy/neobo-fastigheter-shares/management ; https://www.neobo.se/en/neobos-nomination-committee-proposes-bjorn-danckwardt-lilliestrom-as-new-board-member/ ; https://www.neobo.se/en/neobo-publishes-annual-report-for-2025/
thesis.red_flags: Thin earnings: H1 2026 net loss SEK 2m and profit from property management down to SEK 87m from SEK 102m (divestments, higher costs, cold Q1); FY2024 net loss was SEK 193m (FY2025 net profit SEK 78m). Property values slightly negative (H1 2026 value change SEK -39m). Leverage metrics (loan-to-value, interest coverage, debt maturities) were not retrieved in this search - a key gap for a levered property company; check the annual report. Fragmented, partly nominee/insurance-wrapped ownership makes the true holder list hard to verify; outstanding warrants and treasury shares affect the share count. Sources: https://www.neobo.se/en/neobo-fastigheter-ab-publ-interim-report-january-june-2026/ ; https://www.neobo.se/en/neobo-fastigheter-ab-publ-year-end-report-january-december-2025/

thesis.business_description: AB Vilkyskiu pienine, operating as VILVI Group, is a Lithuanian dairy processor based in Vilkyskiai. It reports in segments for cheese and cheese products, cream, dry milk products and fresh milk products; in Q3 2024 cheese was about 40% of revenue, cream 30% and dry milk 17%. Group companies include Modest, Kelmes piene and Latvia's SIA Baltic Dairy Board (100% owned since 2025), and it took 100% of UAB Marijampoles pieno konservai on 16 Jan 2026. In 2023 the EU took 49% of sales, Lithuania 17%, and Asia, the Middle East and the Americas 34%. Preliminary unaudited 2025 revenue was EUR 286.9m (+16.9%). Sources: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/02/27/3246561/0/en/Unaudited-financial-results-of-VILVI-Group-for-the-12-months-of-2025.html ; https://nasdaqbaltic.com/market/upload/reports/vlp/2024_q3_en_eur_00.pdf ; https://just-food.com/news/lithuanias-vilvi-group-takes-full-ownership-of-peer-sia-baltic-dairy-board ; https://www.nasdaqbaltic.com/market/upload/reports/vlp/2025_q4_en.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: Trade press describes VILVI as one of Lithuania's largest cheese makers and dairy processors, mainly an exporter selling to dozens of countries. Its main domestic listed peers would be Rokiskio suris and Pieno zvaigzdes, but no market-share ranking was found in this search. Its strategy is consolidation and scale in cheese: buying Baltic Dairy Board and Marijampoles pieno konservai (after first buying claims against it from Siauliu bankas in Feb 2025) and investing about EUR 50m in new cheese capacity at Bauska, Latvia, due by 2027. The company says the new plant targets up to 18,000 tonnes of cheese a year. Milk intake rose 19.6% in 9M 2025. Sources: https://www.dairyreporter.com/Article/2020/09/21/Vilkyskiu-Pienine-changes-name-to-Vilvi-Group/ ; https://www.just-food.com/news/vilvi-group-makes-multi-million-investment-new-cheese-production-capacity ; https://finanzen.ch/nachrichten/aktien/addition-ab-vilky-ki-pienin-acquired-the-right-to-claim-1034474766 ; https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/11/28/3196033/0/en/Unaudited-consolidated-financial-results-of-VILVI-Group-for-9-months-of-2025.html
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Nasdaq Baltic (as of 31 Dec 2024, updated yearly from the audited report), holders above 5% are Swisspartners Versicherung AG Zweigniederlassung Osterreich with 60.4% (7,213,680 of 11,943,000 shares) and Multi Asset Selection Fund with 17%. The Swisspartners block is held under a joint life-insurance policy for chairman Gintaras Bertasius, who exercises its voting rights (H1 2024 report). The company had 1,670 shareholders at 30 Jun 2024. 2025 year-end figures were not checked. Sources: https://www.nasdaqbaltic.com/statistics/en/ir/ff950f3986/security ; https://nasdaqbaltic.com/market/upload/reports/vlp/2024_q2_en_eur_00.pdf
thesis.red_flags: No accounting or litigation issues found in official sources. Points to watch: (1) the controlling 60.4% stake sits in an insurance-policy wrapper with Swisspartners, which makes beneficial ownership less transparent; with Multi Asset Selection Fund at 17%, free float is only about 23%. (2) Profit has fallen sharply: preliminary 2025 net profit of about EUR 10.4m is down 59.9% from EUR 25.7m in 2024 despite higher sales, and 9M 2025 EBITDA fell 29%. An aggregator shows EUR 10.94m, which conflicts with the company release. (3) Leverage is rising: net financial debt was EUR 64.9m at Q3 2025 against EUR 17.5m a year earlier, driven by acquisitions and the Latvian capex. (4) As a commodity processor, earnings depend on milk-price and dairy-commodity cycles. Sources: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/02/27/3246561/0/en/Unaudited-financial-results-of-VILVI-Group-for-the-12-months-of-2025.html ; https://ml-eu.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/56a8d65c-ecd3-4670-9a96-1a3fa9eb2878 ; https://stockanalysis.com/quote/fra/UDW/
thesis.website: https://www.vilvi.eu (company domain not confirmed in this search; Nasdaq Baltic IR profile: https://nasdaqbaltic.com/statistics/en/ir/ff950f3986/company)
thesis.insider_ownership: Gintaras Bertasius (Chairman of the Management Board and head of the group) effectively controls 60.4% of voting rights. He holds no shares directly; the shares are owned by Swisspartners under a joint life-insurance policy, and the insurer has irrevocably authorised him and related persons to exercise non-property rights. Older reports (2014-2015) showed him holding 51% directly. Other board members' holdings were not found in this search. Sources: https://nasdaqbaltic.com/market/upload/reports/vlp/2024_q2_en_eur_00.pdf ; https://www.nasdaqbaltic.com/market/upload/reports/vlp/2015_q1_en_eur_00_00_00.pdf

thesis.business_description: Novita S.A. is a Zielona Gora (Poland) manufacturer and distributor of nonwovens - household, commercial, medical/sanitary, clothing, footwear and technical - using spunlace (hydroentangling) technology; a 2020 Andritz spunlace line took total installed capacity to nearly 3,000 kg/h and opened hygiene and medical markets. Part of the Vaporjet group since 2016; a third-party profile says sales are mostly export (aggregator; unverified). Sources: https://textilemedia.com/about-us/latest-news/polish-nonwovens-firm-starts-up-new-spunlace-line/ ; https://www.nonwovensnews.com/2020/01/28/polish-nonwovens-firm-starts-up-new-andritz-line/ ; https://www.bankier.pl/static/att/emitent/2025-04/NOVITA-SA-SZD-2024-12-31-0-pl_202504040549910618.xhtml
thesis.competitive_position: Mid-size spunlace nonwovens producer in a niche supplied largely through export; named competitors, market share and 2025 financials (revenue, margins, debt) were not found in this search - research gap (see the FY2024 board report on Bankier). Strategic review (known event, verified): on 30 July 2026 the management board started a review of strategic options aimed at maximising shareholder value, which may include bringing in a financial or strategic investor or another transaction changing the shareholder structure; the supervisory board gave a positive opinion the same day; no decision has been taken and timing is uncertain. Sources: https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art44915461-novita-sa-rozpoczecie-przegladu-opcji-strategicznych ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/149739,novita-rozpoczyna-przeglad-opcji-strategicznych
thesis.main_shareholders: Tebesa Sp. z o.o. 64.11% (H1 2025 report: structure unchanged from 7 May 2025 to publication), 100% owned by Vaporjet Ltd (Israel). Sept 2023 breakdown: Finveco ~27.64%, others 8.25%. Tebesa originally bought 63.32% on 3 Aug 2016. Lists of 5%+ holders for the 3 Dec 2025 EGM and 24 June 2026 AGM exist but their contents were not retrieved, so the 2026 percentages are unverified.
