name: Humana AB
gmSourceUrl: [Humana Annual and Sustainability Report 2024](https://www.humanagroup.se/download/18.54270f75195b251bf5ec410/1743419556942/Humana_Annual%20and%20Sustainability%20Report%202024.pdf), [Year-end Report Q4 and Full Year 2024](https://www.humanagroup.se/download/18.b9989d1194d84ba40a205/1738825653361/Interim%20report%20Q4%20and%20full-year%202024.pdf)

thesis.business_description: Stockholm-headquartered Nordic care company providing individual and family care (specialised services, e.g. foster/family and institutional care), personal assistance, elderly care and special service housing. Individual and family care operates in Sweden, Norway, Finland and Denmark; elderly care in Sweden and Finland (per the 2023 annual report as relayed by search results). Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. A press release (undated in the search results) cites about 16,000 employees and 9,000 clients; 2020 operating revenue was SEK 7,797m - both figures are dated, current figures not located in this search. Source: https://news.cision.com/humana-ab/r/humana-acquires-individual-and-family-company-kalliola-oy,c3480751
thesis.competitive_position: Mid-sized Nordic provider in publicly funded social care (individual & family care, disability/personal assistance, elderly care), a market served by private operators and municipalities. Ambea (the bidder) says the combination would create a leading Nordic care platform with broader services and geographic presence; Ambea intends to divest Humana's Personal Assistance business in Sweden. Competitor lists, market shares and margins were not located in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://news.cision.com/ambea/r/ambea-ab---publ---announces-a-recommended-public-offer-to-the-shareholders-of-humana-ab-to-tender-al,c4368326
thesis.main_shareholders: Pre-offer (third-party Simply Wall St / S&P Global data, ~May 2025, aggregator only): Impilo Care AB ~26.6%, Incentive AS ~12.7%; top 25 holders ~73.4%. At the 29 June 2026 offer announcement, Impilo Care AB, Incentive AS and Per Granath together held ~41.9% of shares and votes and committed to accept; Evli, PriorNilsson Fonder and Cicero Fonder (~3.4%) also viewed the offer favourably. JPMorgan Chase crossed 5% per a July 2026 major-holding notice (per a financial-data site; filing not checked). Humana held 2,611,036 own shares (5%) of 51,826,058 at 28 Oct 2025. NOTE: the offer is now unconditional with 90.84% accepted (1 Oct 2026); Ambea is the effective majority owner and the pre-offer register is stale. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/healthcare/sto-hum/humana-shares ; https://www.inderes.dk/releases/notification-regarding-humanas-holding-of-its-own-shares ; https://news.cision.com/ambea/r/ambea-ab---publ---announces-a-recommended-public-offer-to-the-shareholders-of-humana-ab-to-tender-al,c4368326 ; https://www.placera.se/telegram/ambea-ambea-fullfoljer-budet-pa-humana-accept-pa-knappt-91-procent-av-aktierna-20261001
thesis.red_flags: TAKEOVER: Ambea's offer (SEK 20 cash + 0.305 Ambea shares plus a contingent value right; SEK 62.30 per share excl. CVR) was accepted by 90.84% of capital and votes and declared unconditional on 1 Oct 2026; Ambea intends compulsory redemption of the remaining shares and delisting from Nasdaq Stockholm (Humana applied for delisting on ~6 Oct 2026). The stock is therefore effectively not an independent investable value idea; an extended acceptance period to 14 Oct was reported, final acceptance level after extension not located. LITIGATION: Stockholm District Court dismissed Humana's damages claim against the Swedish state (up to ~SEK 259.1m plus ~SEK 46m legal costs) on 17 June 2026; appeal requires leave from Svea Court of Appeal. CONCENTRATION: controlling holder group (~41.9%) pre-offer. Other leverage/accounting risks not assessed in this search. Sources: https://www.placera.se/telegram/ambea-ambea-fullfoljer-budet-pa-humana-accept-pa-knappt-91-procent-av-aktierna-20261001 ; https://www.placera.se/telegram/humana-humana-ansoker-om-avnotering-fran-nasdaq-stockholm-20261006 ; https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/statement-by-the-board-of-directors-of-humana-regarding-ambeas-public-takeover-offer
thesis.website: https://www.humanagroup.se (named in search results but not independently verified; confirm before use)
thesis.insider_ownership: Board members Fredrik Stromholm and Carolina Oscarius Dahl are linked to Impilo Care AB (largest holder, ~26.6% pre-offer, aggregator data) and recused themselves from the board's offer decision; Per Granath is named among the holders committed to accept (stake size not stated in the results). Individual director/executive holdings with percentages were not located in this search; treat as a research gap (see annual report corporate governance section). Source: https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/statement-by-the-board-of-directors-of-humana-regarding-ambeas-public-takeover-offer

thesis.business_description: Pihlajalinna Oyj is a Finnish healthcare services provider listed on Nasdaq Helsinki, with a Private Healthcare Services segment (FY2025 revenue EUR 465.2m, +3.0%) and a Public Services segment (EUR 199.2m) that delivers outsourced services to Finnish public-sector customers (e.g. selected as provider for outsourcing of services in Northern Pirkanmaa). FY2025 group revenue was EUR 652.3m (2024: EUR 704.4m, -7.4%, due to changes in outsourcing agreements and divestment of residential care units, together EUR 49.4m); adjusted EBITA EUR 65.3m (+18.3%); EPS EUR 1.58; proposed dividend EUR 0.53. Source: https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/pihlajalinna-financial-statements-release-1-january-31-december-2025-strong-profitability-development-continued-in-2025
thesis.competitive_position: One of Finland's larger private healthcare and public-outsourcing providers; strategy is a shift towards higher-margin private services and fewer low-margin public contracts. 2026 guidance: revenue about EUR 570-600m and adjusted EBITA margin 9-10%; medium-term targets are revenue of at least EUR 700m and net debt/adj. EBITDA below 2.5x (2.5x at end-2025, 2.9x a year earlier; excl. IFRS 16 leases net debt was EUR 81.4m, 1.0x). Market share and named competitors (e.g. Terveystalo, Mehiläinen) were not confirmed in this search; treat as a research gap. Source: https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/pihlajalinna-financial-statements-release-1-january-31-december-2025-strong-profitability-development-continued-in-2025
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Inderes (Euroclear Finland register, updated 30 April 2026; third-party aggregator, not the company page): LocalTapiola (Lähitapiola Keskinäinen Vakuutusyhtiö) 16.84% and Fennia Mutual Insurance 10.42%. The company's own largest-shareholders page exists but its table was not readable in this search; other holders and the combined LocalTapiola entities' totals were not confirmed. Sources: https://www.inderes.fi/en/companies/Pihlajalinna/ownership ; https://www.pihlajalinna.fi/en/investors/share-information/largest-shareholders
thesis.red_flags: Revenue is shrinking (2026 guidance EUR 570-600m vs EUR 652.3m in 2025) as public contracts roll off; reliance on public-sector outsourcing contracts and Finnish healthcare policy/regulation; leverage still material with net debt EUR 271.7m incl. leases (2.5x adj. EBITDA, at the top of the target ceiling). Two insurer holders own about 27% combined (influence over governance). The FY2025 release is unaudited. No litigation or accounting issues were identified in the sources reviewed. Source: https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/pihlajalinna-financial-statements-release-1-january-31-december-2025-strong-profitability-development-continued-in-2025
thesis.insider_ownership: Board members receive about 40% of their annual fees in company shares (AGM 31 March 2026); on 5 May 2026 the company transferred 9,072 treasury shares to board members, leaving 130,978 treasury shares. Board members holding over EUR 1m of shares may take fees fully in cash. Named insiders in managers' transaction notices include Jukka Leinonen (2,367 shares received at EUR 0) and Kim Ignatius. Aggregate board/management ownership percentages and named large insider holdings could not be located in this search; treat as a research gap. LocalTapiola and Fennia are represented on the shareholders' nomination board. Sources: https://www.inderes.fi/releases/transfer-of-pihlajalinnas-own-shares ; https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/composition-of-pihlajalinnas-shareholders-nomination-board

thesis.business_description: Officina Stellare S.p.A. (Sarcedo/Vicenza, Italy; Euronext Growth Milan) designs and manufactures opto-mechanical and optical systems for ground-based telescopes and space applications, including adaptive optics and laser-communication/QKD terminals; optics are made in-house (lab in Occhiobello). On 1 Jun 2026 it completed a merger by incorporation of Global Aerospace Technologies Group (GATG), issuing 11,340,488 new shares, and now positions itself as a multi-domain supplier (space, aviation, defence, maritime, cybersecurity). Standalone 2025 production value EUR 26.6m, EBITDA EUR 8.1m; pro-forma combined group 2025 production value EUR 98.8m, adjusted EBITDA EUR 17.8m (company/Teleborsa figures; bases differ). Sources: https://www.teleborsa.it/AMP/News/2026/06/01/officina-stellare-perfezionata-la-fusione-di-global-aerospace-technologies-group-203.html ; https://www.teleborsa.it/AMP/News/2026/06/24/gruppo-officina-stellare-backlog-record-di-192-milioni-di-euro-a-fine-maggio-211.html ; https://dfd.dr.morningstar.com.au/investments/security/MIL/OS
thesis.competitive_position: Vertically integrated European supplier of space-qualified optics; Intesa Sanpaolo calls its capabilities rare and hard to replicate in Europe. Pro-forma backlog was EUR 191.9m at end-May 2026 (EUR 163.1m end-2025). Strategy: become an aggregator in selected high-tech niches (M&A), and plan to move from Euronext Growth Milan to Euronext Milan within about 12 months (needs IFRS and free float raised from about 15% to 35%, per Equita). Only competitor named in sources is Planewave Instruments (PitchBook); no broader competitive analysis found. Sources: https://www.officinastellare.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Officina-Stellare_Capital-Markets-Day-2026.pdf ; https://www.teleborsa.it/News/2026/07/29/officina-stellare-intesa-avvia-copertura-con-buy-nonostante-rally-da-inizio-anno-45.html ; https://www.borsaitaliana.it/borsa/notizie/teleborsa/finanza/officina-stellare-equita-avvia-copertura-con-hold-multipli-richiedono-verifica-della-capacita-di-esecuzione-69_2026-09-21_TLB.html?lang=it
thesis.main_shareholders: Post-merger (Teleborsa reporting a regulatory notification of 4 Jun 2026): Global Aerospace Technologies Investments 59.38% (10,323,974 shares; indirectly held by investment vehicles of Investindustrial Growth III); Virgilio Holding 13.06%; Mirak Enterprise 5.28%; Astro Alliance 5.28%. This supersedes the pre-closing projection of about 57.5% (other relevant holders about 25.4%, free float about 17.1%, per Milano Finanza/Start Magazine). Sources: https://www.teleborsa.it/News/2026/06/04/officina-stellare-global-aerospace-technologies-investments-sale-al-59-38percent-79.html ; https://www.startmag.it/spazio-e-difesa/investindustrial-di-bonomi-accelera-sullaerospazio-con-officina-stellare/
thesis.red_flags: Controlled by Investindustrial vehicle (59.4%); free float only about 15% (thin liquidity, and Equita notes a possible long-term Investindustrial exit subject to Golden Power rules). Reverse-takeover integration risk: financials are pro-forma, share count and market cap changed sharply, and the 2025 figures mix standalone and combined bases. Valuation multiples require execution proof (Equita Hold). Lock-up terms were not found. Planned listing move needs IFRS adoption. Net financial debt standalone EUR 8.9m end-2025; pro-forma net cash EUR 30m (company). Sources: https://www.borsaitaliana.it/borsa/notizie/teleborsa/finanza/officina-stellare-equita-avvia-copertura-con-hold-multipli-richiedono-verifica-della-capacita-di-esecuzione-69_2026-09-21_TLB.html?lang=it ; https://www.teleborsa.it/AMP/News/2026/06/24/gruppo-officina-stellare-backlog-record-di-192-milioni-di-euro-a-fine-maggio-211.html
thesis.insider_ownership: Could not locate named board/executive holdings with percentages in this search; treat as a research gap. Chairman is Giovanni Dal Lago and CEO Alessandro Franzoni (CMD June 2026 deck); historic holders Virgilio Holding, Mirak Enterprise and Astro Alliance are founder/early-investor vehicles but their individual beneficial owners were not verified here. Source: https://www.officinastellare.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Officina-Stellare_Capital-Markets-Day-2026.pdf

thesis.business_description: Thrace Plastics Holding Company S.A., founded in 1977 in Xanthi, Greece (restructured in 2017 into its current holding form, with 14 operating companies), is an international producer of Technical Fabrics (including geosynthetics — woven/nonwoven geotextiles, geogrids, geocomposites, geosynthetic clay liners, drainage geonets, erosion-control products — via its Thrace NG unit) and Packaging (rigid plastic containers, lids, cups, bottles, and flexible films/big bags for food, consumer and industrial use), with a 2023 expansion into paper packaging via a new line in Ioannina. Source: https://m.uk.investing.com/equities/thrace-plastic-company-profile ; https://www.thracegroup.com/uploads_file/2024/05/09/p1htf16u9m1pkkbv8j0f1usn1akk33.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: Established international (though Greek-headquartered) producer with Technical Fabrics historically the larger segment (~73% of FY2018 gross revenue vs. ~23% for Packaging, mix may have since shifted); listed on the Athens Exchange, with an active share-buyback program per a recent company announcement. Source: https://www.edisongroup.com/research/improving-returns-to-drive-re-rating/24410/ ; https://www.newmoney.gr/roh/palmos-oikonomias/epixeiriseis/plastika-thrakis-elixe-to-programma-agoras-idion-metochon/
thesis.main_shareholders: A June 2026 Athens Exchange regulated-information disclosure (official company filing) shows the Loukakos family as significant shareholders: Athanasios Loukakos and Stavros Loukakos (the elder generation) each transferred 212,071 common registered voting shares (0.485% of total voting rights each) from individual accounts into a new joint account held together with their children (also named Athanasios Loukakos and Stavros Loukakos) — confirming the Loukakos family as long-standing, named shareholders, though this particular filing concerns only an intra-family transfer, not their total combined stake. Source: https://www.newmoney.gr/roh/palmos-oikonomias/epixeiriseis/plastika-thrakis-elixe-to-programma-agoras-idion-metochon/ (referencing the 10 June 2026 disclosure). A 2017 EGM record shows 33,727,386 voting shares present, representing 74.792% of share capital, but did not name the underlying holders in the retrieved excerpt. We could not determine the Loukakos family's aggregate percentage of total share capital, nor identify any other major shareholder, from an official source in this search; this should be verified against Thrace Plastics' current annual report shareholder-structure section or Hellenic Capital Market Commission notifications.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources regarding litigation or going-concern. The Loukakos family's intra-family share transfer (June 2026) into a joint account with the next generation is a succession-planning move disclosed transparently rather than a red flag. The company's active treasury-share buyback program is a disclosed capital-allocation choice. Source: https://www.newmoney.gr/roh/palmos-oikonomias/epixeiriseis/plastika-thrakis-elixe-to-programma-agoras-idion-metochon/

name: Aeroporto Guglielmo Marconi di Bologna S.p.A.

thesis.business_description: Aeroporto Guglielmo Marconi di Bologna S.p.A. (AdB) manages and develops Bologna Marconi airport in northern Italy (aviation and non-aviation revenue, cargo). FY2025: about 11.1m passengers (+3.4%), consolidated revenues EUR 181.4m (+9.2%), EBITDA EUR 54.5m, consolidated profit EUR 24.8m; 7th-largest Italian passenger airport and 4th for cargo. Sources: https://media.bologna-airport.it/System/3283848/2026-03-16-CS-ADB-Bilancio-2025-EN.pdf ; https://www.teleborsa.it/AMP/News/2026/03/16/aeroporto-di-bologna-nel-2025-ricavi-a-181-4-milioni-9-2percent-traffico-passeggeri-in-crescita-205.html
thesis.competitive_position: Regional hub with a strong low-cost component: Ryanair projected about 6m passengers a year at Bologna and listed 44 routes and 11 based aircraft for winter 2025 (airline statements, not airport data); Q1 2026 low-cost traffic +7.9%. Traffic H1 2026 5.49m passengers (+3.6%), 8M 2026 7.77m (+3.5%). More than EUR 50m of infrastructure works in 2025. Ryanair's actual share of traffic/revenue and the concession expiry were not found; research gap. Sources: https://corporate.ryanair.com/novita/ryanair-lancia-la-winter-2025-per-bologna/ ; https://www.teleborsa.it/AMP/News/2026/05/15/aeroporto-di-bologna-nel-primo-trimestre-ricavi-ed-ebitda-in-crescita-183.html ; https://www.soldionline.it/notizie/azioni-italia/aeroporto-bologna-andamento-operativo-agosto-2026
thesis.main_shareholders: Bologna Chamber of Commerce ~44% and Mundys S.p.A. ~29% (company presentation), other public shareholders ~15%, free float ~12% (the presentation excerpt was seen in search snippets; exact document not verified). Il Sole 24 Ore (aggregator, page dated 28 June 2026): Camera di Commercio di Bologna 44.06%, Modena 5.80%, Edizione Holding 29.38%, market 20.76%; AdB's 2025 communication attributes the 29.38% to Mundys, not Edizione - likely a labelling difference (Edizione is Mundys' parent per my background knowledge; sources did not state it). Consob register page (dated 2021) not used. thesis.insider_ownership: No insider or management shareholding was located; CEO Nazareno Ventola is named in the FY2025 results release, but his holdings were not found. The register is dominated by public bodies and an institutional investor, not individuals - research gap on director holdings. Sources: https://www.teleborsa.it/AMP/News/2026/03/16/aeroporto-di-bologna-nel-2025-ricavi-a-181-4-milioni-9-2percent-traffico-passeggeri-in-crescita-205.html ; https://media.bologna-airport.it/System/2937296/08-04-2025-CS-Deposito-liste.pdf
thesis.red_flags: Rising leverage: net financial position was +EUR 5.4m at end-2024, -EUR 17.2m at 30 June 2025, -EUR 26.3m at end-2025 and -EUR 46.8m at 31 March 2026 (Q1 2026 net profit EUR 2.6m vs 3.1m on higher financial charges tied to an EIB loan, EUR 12.7m quarterly capex). Dividend cut: FY2025 gross dividend EUR 0.35/share vs EUR 0.471 for FY2024. Airline-cost pressure: Ryanair said it could not add significant growth in summer 2025 after the municipal passenger surcharge rose EUR 0.50 from 1 April 2025. Concession term, regulatory (tariff) risk and airline concentration were not located; public-body control (~44% Chamber of Commerce + other public holders). Sources: https://www.teleborsa.it/AMP/News/2026/05/15/aeroporto-di-bologna-nel-primo-trimestre-ricavi-ed-ebitda-in-crescita-183.html ; https://media.bologna-airport.it/System/3312928/AdB-Shareholders-Meeting-PR-23-04-26.pdf ; https://corporate.ryanair.com/?p=26762

thesis.business_description: Sligro Food Group N.V. (Veghel, Netherlands) is a foodservice wholesaler supplying caterers, company restaurants and similar customers in the Netherlands and Belgium via home delivery (63% of revenue) and cash-and-carry (37%). FY2025 revenue EUR 2,668m (+1.7% excl. tobacco), net profit EUR 30m (+26%); Netherlands EUR 2.28bn (+2.6%), Belgium EUR 384m (-3.2%). It sold its EMTE supermarket chain in 2018. Sources: https://www.sligrofoodgroup.nl/en/news/revenue-2025 ; https://www.esmmagazine.com/retail/sligro-food-group-sees-1-7-revenue-growth-in-fy-2025-303604 ; https://www.sligrofoodgroup.nl/sites/default/files/pdf/Capital%20Markets%20Day%2C%205%20March%202026%2C%20EN.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: Self-described foodservice leader with roughly 26% share in the Netherlands and about 4% in Belgium (March 2026 Capital Markets Day); gained share in both countries in H1 2026. Margins are under pressure from 'cost price plus' contracts in an inflationary period and growth skewed to lower-margin national chains; 2026-2030 plan focuses on a healthier Dutch revenue mix, improved Belgian profitability and fundamental cost reduction. Acquirer event: Sligro agreed on 4 June 2025 to buy Gepu (Utrecht cash-and-carry/delivery wholesaler, ~EUR 15m expected turnover, 40 staff; price undisclosed); Gepu contributed EUR 6m of 2025 revenue per the annual-report coverage, implying it was consolidated in 2025, but the formal completion date was not confirmed. Competitor names (e.g. Bidfood) were not found in these sources. Sources: https://www.sligrofoodgroup.nl/sites/default/files/pdf/Capital%20Markets%20Day%2C%205%20March%202026%2C%20EN.pdf ; https://www.esmmagazine.com/retail/sligro-sees-market-share-growth-in-h1-despite-flat-revenue-317275 ; https://www.esmmagazine.com/retail/sligro-food-group-acquires-dutch-cash-carry-wholesaler-gepu-289957
thesis.main_shareholders: Sligro's IR page lists Stichting Administratiekantoor Slippens 33.95% (figure rests on a 2006 disclosure, so dated), Van Lanschot Kempen Investment Management 5.05% (17 July 2024) and Stichting Werknemersaandelen Sligro Food Group 3.06% (16 May 2025). Conflict: the AFM register shows the employee foundation at 3.94% (last updated 23 June 2026). Simply Wall St (aggregator) adds NN Group ~10.2% and ABP ~10%, not confirmed in official sources. Sources: https://www.sligrofoodgroup.nl/en/investor-relations/shares/major-shareholders ; https://www.afm.nl/en/sector/registers/meldingenregisters/substantiele-deelnemingen/details?id=15531 ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/nl/consumer-retailing/ams-sligr/sligro-food-group-shares/ownership
thesis.insider_ownership: AFM register for K.M. (Koen) Slippens: 107,402 ordinary shares and 21,100 personnel options before a March 2023 transaction (stale; current holding and current role not verified; he was CEO in 2015 and on the management board in 2017/2018). Rob van der Sluijs' holdings were not found. The Slippens-named foundation holds 33.95% but its beneficial owners are not identified in these sources. Employee foundation holds ~3-4%. Sources: https://www.afm.nl/en/sector/registers/meldingenregisters/bestuurders-commissarissen/details?id=3151 ; https://www.sligrofoodgroup.nl/en/investor-relations/shares/major-shareholders
thesis.red_flags: Profit squeeze: H1 2026 revenue flat at EUR 1.27bn but EBIT fell from EUR 9m to EUR 2m; Belgium sub-scale (about 4% share, revenue -3.2%); cost-plus contract pressure. Control: a ~34% foundation stake limits takeover prospects (no bid for Sligro found; the Gepu deal is a bolt-on with Sligro as acquirer). Net debt/leverage figures were not retrieved - research gap. Sources: https://www.esmmagazine.com/retail/sligro-sees-market-share-growth-in-h1-despite-flat-revenue-317275 ; https://www.sligrofoodgroup.nl/sites/default/files/pdf/Capital%20Markets%20Day%2C%205%20March%202026%2C%20EN.pdf

thesis.business_description: PharmaNutra S.p.A. (Pisa, Italy) develops and sells nutraceutical supplements and medical devices built on its patented Sucrosomial delivery technology. Its main lines are SiderAL (oral iron), Cetilar (joint/muscle), Apportal and Sidevit B12. Its subsidiary Akern makes bioimpedance devices. FY2025 net revenues were EUR 131.7m (FY2024: EUR 115.4m), EBITDA EUR 34.2m and net profit EUR 20.0m. SiderAL alone contributed EUR 91.8m. Foreign revenues grew 23.6%, against 8.6% at home. Sources: https://www.emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2026-03/20260317_179110.pdf ; https://www.teleborsa.it/AMP/News/2026/03/17/pharmanutra-l-utile-2025-sale-a-20-milioni-dividendo-di-1-20-euro-213.html ; https://pharmanutra.it/en/sucrosomial-technology
thesis.competitive_position: A 2022 Midcap Partners broker report calls PharmaNutra the Italian leader in nutraceuticals. It puts SiderAL above 55% of the Italian oral-iron supplement market, against 4.7% for the nearest competitor. The company's own IQVIA-based releases show a lower share of about 43-45.5% (2019-2020). These figures are dated and use different measures; no post-2022 independent share data was found. The moat is the patented Sucrosomial technology (protection said to run to at least 2032) plus a direct sales force; expansion abroad (China, US) is the growth lever. The company is listed on the STAR segment of Euronext Milan. Q1 2026 revenue rose 24.5% to EUR 33.4m. In June 2026 the CEO said no M&A was on the horizon. Sources: https://www.pharmanutra.it/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/PHARMANUTRA-ricerca-Midcap-22-3-2022.pdf ; https://www.pharmanutra.it/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/PR-PHN-market-figures-1S-27082020-ENG.pdf ; https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/il-ferro-di-sideral-trascina-i-conti-pharmanutra-86-in-un-anno-in-borsa-202606120656526814
thesis.main_shareholders: CONSOB major-holding data at 31 Dec 2023 (voting rights): Andrea Lacorte via ALH S.r.l. about 31.4%; Roberto Lacorte via RLH S.r.l. about 22.98% plus 0.145% direct (about 23.1% total); Carlo Volpi via Beda S.r.l. about 10.48%. ALH, RLH and Beda are bound by a shareholders' agreement (updated December 2021), which together controls roughly 65%. These figures are 2023 data; a newer CONSOB snapshot exists but its values could not be read in this search, so treat current percentages as possibly stale. Sources: https://www.consob.it/web/consob-and-its-activities/w/pharmanutra-spa-azionariato-2023-12-31 ; https://www.pharmanutra.it/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/Aggiornamento-patti-parasociali-Informazioni-essenziali-23-12-2021.pdf
thesis.red_flags: No accounting, regulatory or litigation issues found in official sources. Risks: (1) heavy reliance on one product line, with SiderAL about 70% of FY2025 revenue; the broker report also flags single-product dependence and rising competition. (2) A founder/insider pact controls about 65% of votes, which limits minority influence and makes an outside takeover unlikely. (3) Market-share claims come mainly from company releases or broker research. (4) After an approximately 86% one-year share price rise (MF, June 2026), the valuation may already price in growth. Sources: https://www.pharmanutra.it/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/PHARMANUTRA-ricerca-Midcap-22-3-2022.pdf ; https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/il-ferro-di-sideral-trascina-i-conti-pharmanutra-86-in-un-anno-in-borsa-202606120656526814
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is high. The controlling holders sit on the board: Andrea Lacorte (Chairman, about 31.4% via ALH), Roberto Lacorte (Vice Chairman and CEO, about 23.1% via RLH and directly) and director Carlo Volpi (about 10.48% via Beda), as of the 31 Dec 2023 CONSOB data. Volpi bought a further 850 shares in June 2024. Holdings of other directors were not found. Sources: https://www.consob.it/web/consob-and-its-activities/w/pharmanutra-spa-azionariato-2023-12-31 ; https://www.emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2026-03/20260327_180319.pdf ; https://www.websim.it/azioni/small-mid-cap/notizie/pharmanutra-carlo-volpi-acquista-850-azioni-20240624051512/

thesis.business_description: Norway-headquartered retail technology company (about 500 employees) serving grocery and other retail with solutions such as electronic shelf labels (ESL) and in-store productivity, e-commerce/order-picking logistics, payment and checkout solutions, and shop fitting; operates in Norway, Sweden, the Baltics, the UK, Ireland, Spain and elsewhere. Segment labelling differs across sources (six legacy segments vs a newer Retail Technology / Labels description) - structure may have changed. H1 2026 revenue NOK 685m (697m), Q2 2026 NOK 342m (350m), H1 EBITDA NOK 15m (18m); net interest-bearing debt NOK 57m; disposable funds NOK 98m. Sources: https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/strongpoint-strongpoint-asa-second-quarter-and-first-half-2026-20260710 ; https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/strongpoint-asa-reports-q1-2025-financial-results-and-strategic-focus
thesis.competitive_position: Regional integrator/reseller in grocery-retail technology; long-time ESL reseller and installer in Norway, Sweden, the Baltics (and UK/Ireland/Spain after a 2022 extension). The ESL partnership with its former partner (not named in the 2026 release; earlier sources show it was Pricer - link not confirmed in the same document) ended, with full effect from the start of 2026, and StrongPoint now works with Vusion; the company says it will take time to build recurring revenue with the new partner. Rolling-12-month recurring revenue fell 2% to NOK 372m; Nordics revenue down 22% in H1 2026, International up 15%. No short-term guidance; full effect of large Order Picking projects expected in H1 2027. Notable wins: ESL deal with Coop Estonia and a US order-picking agreement with Meijer. Competitor and market-share data were not located in this search. Sources: https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/strongpoint-strongpoint-asa-second-quarter-and-first-half-2026-20260710 ; https://live.euronext.com/en/products/equities/company-news/2022-11-15-strongpoint-and-pricer-deepen-and-broaden-strategic
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Simply Wall St (aggregator, 2026 data, not the company's own list): Stromstangen AS 3,933,092 shares (8.79%), Muen Invest AS 2,698,205 shares (6.03%); earlier snapshot also lists Tohatt AS ~5.0%, Sole Active AS ~5.0%, Quaero Capital SA ~4.4%; top 25 ~64%. The company publishes monthly top-50 shareholder lists (top 50 held ~74% of about 44.9m shares in early 2025); the current list was not read. One other site (growthsharematrix.com) names Vensafe AS at 10.5% - not corroborated, treat as unreliable. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/no/tech/ob-stro/strongpoint-shares/ownership ; https://www.strongpoint.com/app/uploads/2025/07/top-50-shareholders-30.06.25.pdf ; https://www.strongpoint.com/investor/share-information/shareholders/
thesis.red_flags: Loss of recurring ESL partner revenue (partnership ended, full effect from start of 2026) with uncertain ramp-up of the new Vusion relationship; H1 2026 EBITDA down (NOK 15m vs 18m), Q2 included NOK 4m one-offs; revenue declining slightly. Dependence on reseller/distribution agreements with third-party technology suppliers. Net debt NOK 57m is moderate. Ownership is fragmented across several 4-9% holders; no controlling holder identified. No litigation or accounting concerns identified in this search, but no audit report or annual report was reviewed. Sources: https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/strongpoint-strongpoint-asa-second-quarter-and-first-half-2026-20260710 ; https://www.inderes.se/releases/strongpoint-asa-second-quarter-and-first-half-2026
thesis.insider_ownership: Per the company's primary-insider page (possibly dated, versions differ): CEO Jacob Tveraabak 250,146 shares (0.6%); Chair Morthen Johannessen incl. owned companies 147,584 shares (0.3%; an April 2025 notice gave 153,989 after a purchase of 3,495 - the figures differ, reason unclear); directors Ingeborg Molden Hegstad 30,826, Cathrine Laksfoss 10,435, Audun Nordtveit 28,296, Pal Wibe 3,868 shares. Board members must use 20% of gross remuneration to buy shares until holdings equal one year's fee. Whether Stromstangen/Muen Invest are linked to any board member was not established. Sources: https://strongpoint.com/investor/share-information/primary-insiders ; https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/strongpoint-asa-board-members-increase-shareholdings

thesis.business_description: Loulis Food Ingredients S.A. (formerly Loulis Mills S.A.; headquartered in Almyros, Greece; listed on Athens Exchange as KYLO) produces and supplies raw materials for nutrition: flour and semolina (Loulis Mills brand, St. George Mills), premium artisanal baking mixes (Kaizen), mixes for bakers and confectioners (Kenfood), consumer mixes (Easy Bake) and cereals trading. It sells in Greece, Bulgaria, other EU markets and internationally and acquired a mill in General Toshevo, Bulgaria via subsidiary Loulis MEL-Bulgaria EAD (price conflicts: EUR 2.25m in the exchange filing vs EUR 2.5m plus EUR 3.5m renovation per World Grain). FY2024 turnover was EUR 206.7m with net profit EUR 7.1m (press report); the EUR 199.7m FY2025 revenue and about 425 employees figures come only from the aggregator Simply Wall St. Segment count differs by provider (3 vs 4). Sources: https://simplywall.st/stock/atse/kylo ; https://www.world-grain.com/articles/13911-loulis-mills-still-growing-after-238-years ; https://millermagazine.com/magazine/issue-192/84-85/ ; https://www.powergame.gr/epichirisis/924875/loulis-food-merisma-0285-evro-ana-metochi-gia-to-2024/
thesis.competitive_position: Per the company's own statements in a Miller Magazine interview (not independently verified), Loulis is the market leader in Greek milling and a growing regional player in the Balkans: third mill by size in Bulgaria and a milling group with daily wheat grinding capacity above 1,500 tonnes. Strategy combines branded flour/mixes with Balkan expansion (Bulgaria, targeting Bulgaria and Romania). Named competitors and independently sourced market shares were not found in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://millermagazine.com/magazine/issue-192/84-85/ ; https://www.world-grain.com/articles/13911-loulis-mills-still-growing-after-238-years
thesis.main_shareholders: Aggregator only (Simply Wall St, data appears to date from around May 2025 and should be verified): Nikolaos Loulis 48.5% as largest holder; individual insiders about 55.6%; top 9 holders 75.91%. An official shareholder table from the annual report or Athens Exchange filings was not located in this search; treat as a research gap. Dividend context: EUR 0.30 per share (total EUR 5,136,084) approved by the AGM of 21 May 2025 for FY2024, implying about 17.12m shares (derived by division, not stated in the source). Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gr/food-beverage-tobacco/ath-kylo/loulis-food-ingredients-shares/ownership ; https://www.powergame.gr/epichirisis/924875/loulis-food-merisma-0285-evro-ana-metochi-gia-to-2024/
thesis.red_flags: Founder/family control (about half of capital per aggregator) limits minority influence and free float. Margin risk from wheat, energy and currency volatility (company commentary on 2025 cites heightened uncertainty and raw-material/energy cost volatility). Expansion in Bulgaria adds integration and execution risk. The company runs a share buyback programme authorised until 21 May 2027. The 2025 annual report (scheduled 27 April 2026 per financial calendar) was not located, so leverage and audit opinion were not checked; treat as a research gap. No litigation or accounting issues were identified in the sources reviewed. Sources: https://athexgroup.gr/en/more-options/announcements/financial-calendar-2025-27 ; https://simplywall.st/stock/atse/kylo
thesis.insider_ownership: Nikolaos Loulis (Chairman of the Board) is the leading shareholder, about 48.5% per Simply Wall St (aggregator, approx. May 2025); aggregate insider holding about 55.6% per the same source. Nikolaos Fotopoulos is CEO and Spyridon Theodoropoulos attended the 28 May 2026 extraordinary board meeting; their holdings could not be located. Official holdings disclosure not found; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gr/food-beverage-tobacco/ath-kylo/loulis-food-ingredients-shares/ownership ; https://www.naftemporiki.gr/business/1950164/loylis-pos-foyskose-to-zymari-tis-loulis-food/

thesis.business_description: bpost NV/SA is the Belgian postal and logistics group (mail, parcels, retail network) that has been repositioning towards parcel-sized logistics in Europe, North America and Asia (2025 annual report calls the transformation 'Bnode'), with Paxon (Europe, North America), Radial (US) and Staci (Europe/Americas) businesses. Q2 2026 operating income EUR 1,046.4m (-4.2%), adjusted EBIT EUR 29.4m. HQ city was not stated in the sources retrieved. Sources: https://www.sustainabilityreports.com/bpost/2025/annual-report ; https://quartr.com/events/bpost-nv-sa-bpost-q2-2026_F3HkTqLO
thesis.competitive_position: Incumbent in Belgian mail (domestic letter volumes -14% in Q1 and about -17% in Q2 2026) and a major Belgian parcel player, pushing growth via parcels, lockers and retail partnerships; Paxon Europe grew 6.5% in Q2 2026 while Radial US, Staci Americas and Paxon North America (Fast Track) weakened. Management expects parcel volumes to return to low-single-digit growth in H2 2026. Competitor names, market shares and universal-service-obligation terms were not found in this search; research gap. Sources: https://quartr.com/events/bpost-nv-sa-bpost-q2-2026_F3HkTqLO ; https://www.belganewsagency.eu/bpost-estimates-strike-impact-at-at-least-15-million-euros
thesis.main_shareholders: SFPIM/FPIM (Belgian federal holding company, wholly owned by the Belgian State) 51.04% of voting rights = 102,075,649 of 200,000,944 votes, after the State contributed its shares on 22 May 2024 (transparency notification; FSMA overview dated 16 May 2025). Next-largest holders are far smaller (~1.9% and ~1.2%, Simply Wall St, aggregator). One aggregator (altss) shows 44.94% via a 'Sovereign Fund', which conflicts with official filings and is disregarded. No 2026 notification found. Sources: https://press.bpost.be/disclosure-of-a-transparency-notification ; https://www.fsma.be/sites/default/files/issuers/files/0214596464_fr.pdf ; https://press.bpost.be/shareholdings ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/transportation/otc-bpos.y/bpost-sa/ownership
thesis.insider_ownership: No director or executive shareholdings were found (aggregator tables show 'no data'). CEO Chris Peeters (CEO since late 2023; start date given as 23 Nov or 11 Dec 2023 by different sources); Chair Francoise Roels (Belgian-government nominee, since 14 May 2025). Insider holdings are immaterial relative to the 51% State-owned stake - research gap on exact figures. Sources: https://press.bpost.be/changes-in-bpostgroup-board-of-directors ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/be/transportation/ebr-bpost/bpost-sa-shares/management
thesis.red_flags: Controlled by the Belgian State (51.04%) - political/governance influence on strategy, dividend and public-service duties. Operational: a five-week nationwide strike in April 2026 cost EUR 25.5m of Q2 EBIT; FY2026 adjusted EBIT guidance cut to ~EUR 140m from EUR 165-195m; Q2 mail volume -17%, parcel volume -9%; Q2 free cash flow EUR -17.4m; shares fell ~10% on the news. Leverage: net debt EUR 1,720.0m at 30 June 2026 (aggregator summary); FY2025 balance-sheet aggregator data show current portion of long-term debt EUR 700.9m vs cash EUR 1,256m. Dividend status and pension liabilities not confirmed. Aggregator Q1 2026 revenue/volume figures conflict with the Q2 trend and should be checked against bpost filings. Sources: https://quartr.com/events/bpost-nv-sa-bpost-q2-2026_F3HkTqLO ; https://www.belganewsagency.eu/bpost-estimates-strike-impact-at-at-least-15-million-euros ; https://stockanalysis.com/quote/ebr/BPOST/financials/balance-sheet/
thesis.website: https://www.bpostgroup.com (not directly shown in search results; press site: https://press.bpost.be)

thesis.business_description: Geodrill Limited is a mineral-exploration drilling contractor (incorporated 1998; registered office Ragnall House, 18 Peel Road, Douglas, Isle of Man; TSX: GEO) serving senior, intermediate and junior mining companies in West Africa (Ghana, Cote d'Ivoire, Senegal, Burkina Faso, Mali per earlier releases), Egypt, and South America (Chile, Peru). Fleet ~100-104 rigs (sources differ; Seeking Alpha says 102). Q2 2026 revenue USD 55.1m (company record), Q1 2026 USD 48.4m. Sources: https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/q/pr?s=GEO.TO ; https://www.miningstockeducation.com/2026/05/geodrill-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial-results/ ; https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/geodrill-q2-earnings-call-highlights ; https://seekingalpha.com/article/4801014-geodrill-stock-mineral-drilling-contractor-with-core-focus-on-west-african-markets-hold
thesis.competitive_position: Company states it has a leading market position in Ghana and Cote d'Ivoire (April 2024 release); a Seeking Alpha opinion piece calls it one of the world's largest third-party drilling contractors (unverified). One source cites ~USD 150m of new long-term contracts entering 2026; a 2022 USD 31m Endeavour Mining contract (350,000 m) was reported. Utilisation averaged 76% in Q1 2026. Named competitors, customer concentration and a formal backlog were not found; research gap. Sources: https://www.newswire.ca/en/releases/archive/April2024/16/c2222.html ; https://www.miningstockeducation.com/2026/05/geodrill-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial-results/ ; https://miningfocusafrica.com/?p=4425

Ronald Sellwood (director): 262,170 shares, 0.59% (MarketScreener). Directors elected 11 May 2026: Harper (~99.9% for), John Bingham (~99.4%), Sellwood, Peter Prattas. Other officers: Gregory Borsk (CFO), Terry Burling (COO); their holdings not found. Sources: https://ca.marketscreener.com/insider/DAVE-HARPER-A166WP/ ; https://www.marketscreener.com/insider/RON-SELLWOOD-A0PQAB/ ; https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/geodrill-geodrill-announces-annual-and-special-meeting-voting-results-20260512
thesis.red_flags: Deteriorating profitability: Q2 2026 gross margin 16% (24% a year earlier), EBITDA USD 7.9m (14% margin vs 28%), net loss ~USD 0.2m; Q1 2026 net loss USD 0.1m; Q3 2025 net loss USD 1.5m. thesis.business_description: Polskie Towarzystwo Wspierania Przedsiebiorczosci S.A. (Grupa PTWP) is a Polish business-media and events group. It organises the European Economic Congress (EEC) in Katowice; the 2025 edition had about 18,000 in-person and online guests and over 1,300 speakers. It also runs digital business portals (e.g. wnp.pl). In late 2025 it took a 56.82% capital stake (60.62% of votes) in Gremi Media, publisher of Rzeczpospolita and Parkiet, and in early 2026 it bought 100% of Elamed Media Group, a trade-press publisher. Preliminary FY2025 revenue was PLN 132.5m (FY2024: PLN 103.3m) and EBITDA PLN 26.7m. Q1 2026 revenue was PLN 52m (+118%), the first quarter consolidating Gremi and Elamed. The head-office city was not confirmed in this search. Sources: https://www.parkiet.com/wyniki-spolek/art44099551-rekordowy-rok-ptwp-przychody-i-ebitda-mocno-w-gore ; https://www.parkiet.com/firmy/art43531341-ptwp-sfinalizowala-transakcje-z-pluralis-b-v-i-obejmuje-wiekszosciowy-pakiet-akcji-gremi-media ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/148015,wyniki-ptwp-pod-wplywem-zmian-organizacyjnych-i-procesow-optymalizacyjnych
thesis.competitive_position: The flagship EEC is one of Poland's largest business conferences, giving PTWP a strong niche in B2B events, sponsorship and industry media. The Gremi Media deal adds a leading national daily (Rzeczpospolita) and the main financial daily (Parkiet), turning PTWP into a much larger publisher with cross-selling potential between events and media. The deal was paid in shares (369,590 Series C shares at PLN 122.43, about PLN 45.25m). H1 2025 was a record (revenue PLN 71.9m, net profit PLN 16.2m). Q1 2026 had a net loss of PLN 2.9m because of reorganisation and integration costs. Sources: https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/PTWP-przejmie-wiekszosciowy-pakiet-w-Gremi-Media-9044034.html ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/138882,ptwp-szacuje-blisko-trzykrotny-wzrost-zysku-netto-w-pierwszym-polroczu ; https://www.parkiet.com/wyniki-spolek/art44507901-rekordowe-przychody-ptwp-kwartal-pod-znakiem-inwestycji
thesis.main_shareholders: As disclosed when the Gremi Media deal closed (late 2025): Wojciech Kuspik about 55.14% and Pluralis B.V. about 23%. Pluralis took newly issued Series C shares in exchange for its Gremi Media stake, and share capital rose from PLN 618,660 to PLN 803,455. Before the deal Kuspik held 874,236 shares (70.61%) per a late-2022 notice. No post-registration 2026 shareholder table was found. A 2026-2027 incentive programme (up to 5% new shares) could dilute these percentages; treat current figures as needing verification. Sources: https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/142311,ptwp-obejmuje-wiekszosciowy-pakiet-akcji-gremi-media ; https://www.parkiet.com/firmy/art43531341-ptwp-sfinalizowala-transakcje-z-pluralis-b-v-i-obejmuje-wiekszosciowy-pakiet-akcji-gremi-media ; https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art37700501-ptwp-s-a-zawiadomienie-akcjonariusza-o-zmianie-udzialu-w-ogolnej-liczbie-glosow
thesis.red_flags: No accounting or litigation issues found in official sources. Risks: (1) a controlling CEO-shareholder (about 55%) plus a second block (Pluralis about 23%) leaves a small free float and limits minority influence. (2) Integration and execution risk from two acquisitions, with Q1 2026 moving to an operating loss of PLN 3.2m. Owning Rzeczpospolita adds exposure to the structurally declining print and news-advertising market and to political or reputational sensitivity. (3) Earnings depend heavily on the seasonal, single large event (EEC in Q2). (4) Reported FY2025 net profit differs between sources (PLN 19.1m, 19.3m, 20.2m), so check the audited report. A Comparic article cites an 'operating loss' of PLN 108m, which appears to be a misreading of operating costs; do not rely on it. Debt and acquisition financing were not found; year-end 2025 cash was PLN 44.7m. thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is very high. Co-founder and CEO (prezes) Wojciech Kuspik is the controlling shareholder with about 55.14% after the Pluralis share issue (late 2025), down from 70.61% in late 2022. Press noted he receives most of the PLN 9.5m (about PLN 5.89/share) dividend for 2025. Holdings of other management or supervisory board members were not found in this search. thesis.business_description: IT Link is a French digital-services/engineering group headquartered in Le Kremlin-Bicetre, listed on Euronext Growth Paris (moved from the regulated market by direct listing on 1 September 2020). It sells consulting, technical assistance and expertise, development contracts and service centres across the study, build and run phases, with roots (founded around 1986) in automotive embedded systems and defence critical systems; clients span automotive, energy, defence, aerospace, telecom, transport and healthcare. One aggregator (Boursedirect, undated) splits revenue ~87% services / ~13% simulation software and ~83% France / ~12% Canada / ~5% Belgium. FY2025 revenue was EUR 82.57m (EUR 82.68m in 2024); Q1 2026 revenue fell 3.7% to EUR 21.03m with 898 employees at 31 March 2026. Sources: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/MKW/2024/10/FCMKW135166_20241001.pdf ; https://www.optionfinance.fr/info-financiere-en-continu/d/2026-05-20-it-link-confirme-ses-objectifs-annuels-malgre-un-debut-dannee-difficile.html ; https://live.euronext.com/sites/default/files/2020-08/IT%20Link%20-%20Document%20d%27admission%20Euronext%20Growth%20VDEF.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: Mid-sized French engineering-services specialist (about 880-900 employees) focused on connected/embedded systems; growth has partly come from bolt-ons: RADeS (banking/finance/insurance consulting, closed Dec 2022), Ciao Technologies (Canada, Jan 2024) and Mi CONCEPT (rail signalling, Sep 2024). Strategic plan 'Synergies 2028' targets more than EUR 100m revenue in 2028 and profitability above 7%. Named competitors and market-share data were not located in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.boursedirect.fr/fr/actualites/categorie/divers/it-link-lance-son-nouveau-plan-strategique-boursier-d7a6851e62aff32ebbc9b1b05704db45e50ebccd ; https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/MKW/2024/10/FCMKW135166_20241001.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: Aggregator figures only (abcbourse, undated table): Robert Zribi family ~14.35%, Michel Zribi ~7.29%, Claude Zribi ~5.55%, free float ~67.74%, treasury ~2.20%. thesis.red_flags: Earnings are falling: FY2025 net income EUR 2.7m (-33% from EUR 4.03m), EBITDA EUR 6.28m; H1 2026 net income reported down 59.1% and Q1 2026 revenue -3.7% (management cited a gap between order intake and project starts). Net cash was EUR 3.8m at 31 Dec 2025 (EUR 5.2m a year earlier, excluding IFRS 16 lease debt), with the decline attributed to a major client's late payment (EUR 1.7m settled early 2026), which hints at client concentration; gross debt not located. thesis.business_description: Azkoyen S.A. is a Navarra (Spain)-based industrial technology group founded more than 80 years ago. It makes coffee and vending machines, payment technologies (coin/note handling and cashless systems) and security/access-control systems, the last including a German business. 2025 net turnover was a record of just over EUR 211m (+6.0%), with EBITDA of about EUR 38m (+7.8%), profit after tax of EUR 17.5m, and no net debt at year-end. Sources: https://www.azkoyen.com/en/prensa/azkoyen-group-increases-its-turnover-by-6-reaching-211-million-euros/ ; https://investinnavarra.com/en/grupo-azkoyen-maintains-its-momentum-in-2025-with-strong-results-and-stock-market-revaluation/
thesis.competitive_position: A niche industrial-technology player with international sales across vending/coffee, payments and security. Its EBITDA margin was about 17.9% in 2025, and recurring maintenance/SaaS revenue was about EUR 19.9m. The balance sheet is net-cash, supporting large payouts (dividends of up to EUR 24.5m approved at the 2026 AGM). Named competitors and segment market shares were not found in this search. Sources: https://www.azkoyen.com/en/prensa/azkoyen-group-increases-its-turnover-by-6-reaching-211-million-euros/ ; https://www.eldebate.com/economia/20260609/grupo-azkoyen-factura-211-millones-cifra-alta-historia_426903.html
thesis.main_shareholders: The company's shareholding-structure page lists Inverlasa S.L. at 29.65% of voting rights (indirect; an older table attributes this 29.65% to Ana Ruiz Lafita), Carolina Masaveu Herrero at 12.66% (an earlier version shows 11.45%), and Ignacio Suárez-Zuloaga Gáldiz at 7.91% (an older version shows about 8.51%). Masaveu Finanzas, Santander Asset Management and La Previsión Mallorquina de Seguros are also listed. CONFLICT: Simply Wall St shows Berkelium S.L. at 21.5%, which does not match the company table, although Berkelium is described in a May 2026 board report as a significant shareholder nominating proprietary directors. thesis.red_flags: TAKEOVER BID IN PROGRESS: in July 2026 Ohmnia Electronics (vehicle of the Basque consortium led by Jainaga's Clerbil, with BBK and Indar Kartera, financed by CaixaBank and Sabadell) launched a voluntary cash offer at EUR 10/share (about EUR 244.5m), below the prior close of EUR 11.40. The board called it 'friendly' but reserved its formal opinion, and the CNMV admitted it for processing on 4 Sept 2026. The bidder plans to keep Azkoyen listed. thesis.business_description: Valsoia is a Bologna-based Italian listed food company, a leader in Italy in health-oriented, mainly soy and plant-based foods: beverages, ice cream, yogurt alternatives, desserts, biscuits, ready meals and dressings, produced mainly at Serravalle Sesia. Brands include Valsoia Bonta e Salute, Vitasoya (soy drinks), Santa Rosa (jams/sorbets) and Diete.Tic (liquid sweetener); sales are mostly through Italian large-scale retail. FY2025 parent-company revenue was ~EUR 116.8m (stable), net profit EUR 8.04m (8.28m in 2024); H1 2026 revenue rose 4.4% to EUR 62.4m. Sources: https://mercati.ilsole24ore.com/azioni/borsa-italiana/dettaglio-completo/VLS.MI/analisi-fondamentale ; https://www.teleborsa.it/DettaglioNews/109_2026-09-07_TLB/Valsoia-ricavi-semestre-salgono-a-624-milioni-Investimenti-per-stabilimento-pesano-su-margini.html ; https://mercati.ilsole24ore.com/azioni/borsa-italiana/dettaglio-completo/VLS.MI/analisi-fondamentale/bilancio
thesis.competitive_position: Niche leader in Italian plant-based foods: a Jan 2025 company release cites ~35% volume share in plant-based ice cream and a stable #2 position in plant-based beverages (no precise beverage share located). Strategy includes bolt-on M&A: in Dec 2025 Valsoia bought 70% of Slovenian kefir maker Kele & Kele (brand Krepko, ~30% of Slovenia's kefir market by value, 2024 revenue ~EUR 4.9m) for ~EUR 3m (implying EUR 5.4m for 100%), funded from existing resources, with a put/call on the remaining 30% after three years; it is being consolidated in H1 2026. Differentiators cited by management: proprietary ERP system and AI capabilities; strategy targets for 2027-2029 are to be updated by year-end 2026, focused on gross margin and efficiency. thesis.business_description: AFC Ajax N.V. is the listed company (Euronext Amsterdam since 17 May 1998; Amsterdam Zuidoost) behind the Dutch football club Ajax: revenue comes from matchday/season tickets, sponsorship, media/broadcasting rights, merchandise and player transfers, plus operation of the De Toekomst youth academy. FY2025/26 (to 30 Jun 2026): net profit EUR 2.0m versus a EUR 37.3m loss in 2024/25, with net revenue up 6% to EUR 188.3m, transfer income EUR 65.5m and an operating loss of EUR 18.2m (the revenue/operating figures are from an AI-generated Quartr digest; verify against the annual report). thesis.competitive_position: One of the Netherlands' biggest football brands and the only Dutch club with a stock-market listing; it competes domestically with PSV and Feyenoord and depends on European competition (UEFA Champions League prize money drove the 2025/26 revenue increase) and on player-trading. Profitability is volatile: 2024/25 loss of EUR 37.3m on EUR 178.1m revenue (financialfilings.com, from the ESEF filing), then a small profit in 2025/26 helped by transfers. Multi-segment conglomerate with a changing perimeter (Benrubi acquisition, solar disposal, a reported share-capital reduction and return to shareholders per a Stockopedia brief), so year-on-year comparisons are affected. No fines, litigation, tax disputes or qualified audit opinions turned up in a targeted search, but that search was not exhaustive; standard caveat: check the audit report and notes in the annual report. thesis.business_description: Amica S.A. is a Polish household-appliance manufacturer headquartered and producing in Wronki, making freestanding cookers, ovens and built-in hobs plus washing machines, fridges, microwaves, dishwashers, extractor hoods and small appliances, sold through a network of distribution companies in Europe. Over 70% of revenue comes from more than 40 foreign markets. Nine-month 2025 revenue was PLN 1,785.5m (PLN 1,895.1m a year earlier); an aggregator lists FY2025 revenue ~PLN 2.41bn (2024: PLN 2.57bn). Sources: https://biznes.pap.pl/download/attachment/52942786/DOC.20251121.52942786.zal02_Zal.02_AMICA_3Q2025_SzD.pdf ; https://www.sii.org.pl/19005/analizy/analizy-i-komentarze/amica-4-kw-2025-z-poprawa-operacyjna-ale-przychody-topnieja-a-marza-netto-nadal-skromna-analiza.html ; https://financialfilings.com/companies/amica/
thesis.competitive_position: Self-described largest Polish household-appliance maker with a 15.8% domestic market share (Q3 2025 report) and among Europe's larger appliance firms; per SII it slightly gained share in Poland while foreign sales fell with the market. Group is restructuring foreign subsidiaries (e.g. Spain, UK) and targeting lower inventories and selling/logistics costs. Brand portfolio (e.g. Hansa, Gram) and named competitors were not confirmed in this search (research gap). Sources: https://biznes.pap.pl/download/attachment/52942786/DOC.20251121.52942786.zal02_Zal.02_AMICA_3Q2025_SzD.pdf ; https://www.sii.org.pl/19005/analizy/analizy-i-komentarze/amica-4-kw-2025-z-poprawa-operacyjna-ale-przychody-topnieja-a-marza-netto-nadal-skromna-analiza.html ; https://biznes.pap.pl/wiadomosci/firmy/amica-white-goods-wants-lower-inventory-levels-and-sales-costs
thesis.main_shareholders: Aggregator data (strefainwestorow.pl, dated 14.08.2026): Holding Wronki sp. z o.o. 2,715,771 shares = 34.93% of capital and 51.76% of votes; Allianz Polska OFE 9.14% (6.77% of votes); Amica treasury 250,000 shares = 3.22%; total 7,775,273 shares; free float 55.93%. Conflicts: Stockwatch (Sept 2025) shows Nationale-Nederlanden OFE at 9.58% (update 16.06.2025) and dates the Holding Wronki entry to 6 Dec 2021; older SII analysis had Holding at 41.1% of capital / 57% of votes plus Noble TFI and ING OFE above 5%. Verify against Amica's ESPI/EBI reports. Sources: https://strefainwestorow.pl/notowania/spolki/PLAMICA00010/akcjonariat ; https://www.stockwatch.pl/gpw/amica,akcjonariat,dane-finansowe.aspx ; https://www.sii.org.pl/6661/analizy/analizy-i-komentarze/amica-jeden-z-najwiekszych-producentow-sprzetu-agd-w-europie.html
thesis.insider_ownership: Jacek Rutkowski, long-time president (22 years, handed over in June 2025 to become strategic adviser to the management board), controls Holding Wronki through Invesco sp. z o.o. per a Comparic analysis (undated), i.e. effective control of ~35% of capital / ~52% of votes; his personal percentage was not located. Current management board per Bankier (from June 2025): Robert Stobinski (President), Maja Rutkowska, Michal Rakowski, Pawel Biel (VPs). Supervisory board includes Tomasz Rynarzewski (Chairman) and Piotr Rutkowski (nominated by Holding Wronki, June 2025); family relationships among the Rutkowskis are not stated in the sources. Sources: https://amica-group.com/news/succession-in-the-amica-group-management-board ; https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/akcje/AMICA/wladze-zatrudnienie ; https://comparic.pl/amica-silna-marka-na-wymagajacym-rynku-analiza-fundamentalna/ ; https://biznes.pap.pl/download/attachment/51715990/DOC.20250603.51715990.zal01_Raport_biezacy_12-2025.pdf
thesis.red_flags: Controlling holder: Holding Wronki has ~52% of votes on ~35% of capital (voting-rights wedge). Leverage and cash flow: net debt PLN 187.2m at 30 June 2025 with operating cash flow of PLN -44.0m in H1 2025; the company states it monitors financial covenants and confirms going concern and sufficient liquidity (covenant terms not located). Cyclical weakness: revenue down ~6% over nine months 2025 and 2024 revenue PLN 2.57bn vs 2.84bn; Q1 2025 net loss PLN 6.7m; ongoing restructuring of foreign subsidiaries; thin margins (9M 2025 EBITDA margin 5.1%). Sources: https://quartr.com/events/amica-sa-amc-q2-2025_FVOrb51h ; https://biznes.pap.pl/wiadomosci/firmy/amica-white-goods-posts-pln-67-mln-net-loss-q1-2025-against-pln-15-mln-profit ; https://biznes.pap.pl/download/attachment/52942786/DOC.20251121.52942786.zal02_Zal.02_AMICA_3Q2025_SzD.pdf

thesis.business_description: Spanish IT consultancy founded in 1994 and headquartered in Oleiros (A Coruna), Galicia; a generalist technology consultancy offering end-to-end services from consulting to application development and maintenance. Listed on BME Growth since 1 Dec 2010. H1 2025 revenue was reported at EUR 150.5m (+17.2%) with net profit EUR 7.99m, and headcount of more than 4,030 at mid-2025 (press figures; inconsistent with older articles citing about 1,000 staff). Growth is acquisition-led (Noesis in Portugal, Bilbomatica, IN2, Ednon). Sources: https://www.altiacompany.com/en/insights/news/tenth-anniversary-bme-growth-bme ; https://www.estrategiasdeinversion.com/analisis/bolsa-y-mercados/el-experto-opina/altia-apuesta-por-la-internacionalizacion-y-la-n-829871 ; https://www.bmegrowth.es/docs/documentos/OtraInfRelevante/2026/03/13312_OtraInfRelev_20260326.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: Mid-sized Spanish/Iberian IT services group; one analyst piece names large integrators such as NTT Data and Indra as competitors. Strategy is serial bolt-on M&A: Ednon (Santiago de Compostela; 100% closed 21 Jul 2026 for EUR 9.85m fixed plus up to EUR 2.795m earn-out tied to 2026-27 plans; about 140 staff; Ednon 2025 turnover EUR 18.2m and EBITDA EUR 1.8m, as reported by press, unaudited; strengths in healthcare, retail, justice, banking, cybersecurity), plus Noesis (Portugal), IN2 (Dec 2024) and a Verne data/AI unit (EUR 4.15m, Mar 2025 - from earlier screen). No market-share data located in this search. Sources: https://www.altiacompany.com/sites/default/files/hechos-relevantes/2026-07/20260721%20IP%20adquisici%C3%B3n%20Ednon.pdf ; https://www.democrata.es/en/economy/altia-closes-the-purchase-of-ednon-for-9-85-million-and-integrates-140-technology-specialists/ ; https://www.estrategiasdeinversion.com/analisis/bolsa-y-mercados/el-experto-opina/altia-apuesta-por-la-internacionalizacion-y-la-n-829871
thesis.main_shareholders: At 31 Dec 2025 (company filing to BME Growth, 8 Jan 2026): Boxleo TIC, S.L.U. and related parties 80.9075% (55,649,670 shares); vehicles controlled by Ramchand Bhavnani and related persons 6.8573% (was about 12.47% at end-2022, so falling); Incio Inversiones S.L. 5.6627%. The company states it knows of no other holder at or above 5%. Boxleo has held roughly 80.9% since at least 2017. Source: https://www.bmegrowth.es/docs/documentos/OtraInfRelevante/2026/01/13312_OtraInfRelev_20260108.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: Press reports (Estrategias de Inversion / Finect) describe Constantino 'Tino' Fernandez Pico as chairman and top shareholder controlling 80.91% of capital, i.e. via the Boxleo vehicle; the BME Growth filing itself names Boxleo TIC and related parties (80.9075%) and signs Mr Fernandez Pico as Consejero Delegado, so the personal look-through is from press only. A Bhavnani-vehicle proprietary director (Carlos Bercedo Toledo) was reported in a Jan 2022 filing - possibly out of date. Current board-level holdings otherwise not located; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.bmegrowth.es/docs/documentos/OtraInfRelevante/2026/01/13312_OtraInfRelev_20260108.pdf ; https://www.finect.com/usuario/Gonzalo26/articulos/valoracion-altia-consultores ; https://www.bmegrowth.es/docs/documentos/OtraInfRelevante/2022/01/13312_OtraInfRelev_20220107.pdf
thesis.red_flags: Controlling holder: Boxleo and related parties hold about 81%, and two further holders hold 12.5% combined, so free float is thin (roughly 6-7% outside the three named blocks, by subtraction) and liquidity is limited; the company is on BME Growth (lighter disclosure regime than the main market). Serial acquirer: integration and earn-out risk (Ednon EUR 9.85m + up to EUR 2.795m; closed 21 Jul 2026, confirmed in company release). No takeover bid for Altia found in this search (a search result on an OPA/delisting concerned a different company, AGIL). Related-party/controller risk is generic for a 81% holder. 2025 audited accounts published 23 Apr 2026 but figures were not retrieved; auditor opinion not checked. Sources: https://www.bmegrowth.es/docs/documentos/OtraInfRelevante/2026/01/13312_OtraInfRelev_20260108.pdf ; https://www.altiacompany.com/sites/default/files/hechos-relevantes/2026-07/20260721%20IP%20adquisici%C3%B3n%20Ednon.pdf ; https://beta.bmegrowth.es/docs/documentos/OtraInfRelevante/2026/04/13312_OtraInfRelev_20260423_2.pdf

thesis.business_description: Festi hf. is an Icelandic retail/services group listed on Nasdaq Iceland, with operating units N1 (fuel and road services), Krónan (grocery), ELKO (electronics) and Lyfja (pharmacy/health), plus logistics support such as the Bakkinn refrigerated warehouse (planned for Q1 2026). FY2025 EBITDA was ~ISK 16.0bn, Q4 2025 sales ISK 44,956m (+7.2%), equity ratio 41.2% (37.9% before); 2026 EBITDA guidance ISK 16.5-17.0bn. Headquarters city not confirmed in this search. Sources: https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-02/67628133-festi-hf-2025-annual-report-399.htm ; https://www.mfn.se/one/a/festi/festi-hf-financial-results-for-q1-2025-ae1d0edf ; https://mfn.se/one/a/festi/festi-hf-financial-results-for-q3-2025-2766e76c
thesis.competitive_position: One of Iceland's largest listed consumer-facing groups, combining leading positions across fuel, grocery, electronics and pharmacy (the 2018 Festi/N1 merger was cleared with remedies including store divestitures in southern Iceland, citing Festi's market strength). Krónan is performing strongly and ELKO's online sales are growing fast (Q2 2026 release); N1 faces a headwind from higher global fuel prices. Exact market shares by segment and named competitors were not located in this search (research gap). Sources: https://mfn.se/one/a/festi/festi-hf-financial-results-for-q2-2026-dd171021 ; https://www.samkeppni.is/en/release/news/regarding-a-possible-sale-of-land-in-the-south/
thesis.main_shareholders: No official top-20 list located. Aggregator (Simply Wall St article, undated): Lífeyrissjóður verslunarmanna (pension fund) is the largest holder at ~11% with the next two holders at ~10% each (not named in the extract); Vanguard ~3.84% and Íslandssjóðir ~1.35% per the SWS ownership page. Festi's own treasury stock was ~0.88% (late 2025) and ~1.83% (Sept 2026) under a buyback programme. A major-shareholder notice from Stefnir hf. (July 2024) exists on Nasdaq Iceland but its percentage was not extracted. Treat the holder list as a research gap and verify on festi.is or Nasdaq Iceland. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/is/retail/icse-festi/festi-hf-shares/news/what-type-of-shareholders-own-the-most-number-of-festi-hf-ic ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/is/retail/icse-festi/festi-hf-shares/ownership ; https://www.mfn.se/one/a/festi/festi-hf-transactions-in-relation-to-a-share-repurchase-programme-week-36-b1f233ef ; https://mfn.se/one/a/festi/festi-hf-major-shareholder-announcement-from-stefnir-hf-017b6954
thesis.insider_ownership: Could not locate board/executive holdings or named founding-family stakes in this search; Festi is a widely held, pension-fund-owned company without a known controlling family. Treat as a research gap (check Nasdaq Iceland insider notifications / the 2025 annual report). Source: https://mfn.se/one/a/festi/festi-hf-2025-annual-report-36402db9
thesis.red_flags: Regulatory: the Icelandic Competition Authority was investigating possible breaches by Festi of conditions from the 2018 N1/Festi merger agreement; in October 2024 Festi requested settlement talks and the Authority agreed to begin discussions. The outcome was not found in this search. Sector-wide scrutiny of Icelandic food and fuel prices (2026 Authority papers) is context, not a Festi-specific finding. Other: fuel-price headwind at N1, concentration in a small domestic market, and a ~1.8% buyback (capital allocation, not a risk per se). Sources: https://www.samkeppni.is/en/release/news/festioskar-after-sattavidraedum/ ; https://mfn.se/one/a/festi/festi-hf-financial-results-for-q2-2026-dd171021
thesis.website: https://www.festi.is (standard company domain; not confirmed by a search result in this run - verify). Source: none located in this search.

thesis.business_description: 2G Energy AG, founded in 1995 and headquartered in Heek, Germany, manufactures gas-engine-driven combined heat and power (CHP/cogeneration) systems (20 kW to 4.5 MW electrical output) running on natural gas, biomethane, biogas, sewage gas, landfill gas, propane/LPG and hydrogen, and provides planning, installation and service, serving industrial, utility, municipal, commercial, real-estate and farming customers, with a secondary production/sales site in St. Augustine, Florida, USA. Source: https://www.morningstar.com.au/investments/security/fra/2GB/summary ; https://eqs-news.com/company/2g-energy-ag/info/5b86047f-ea7c-11e8-902f-2c44fd856d8c
thesis.competitive_position: Specialist decentralized-energy/CHP manufacturer with total system efficiency reported between 85% and 90%+; has delivered a reported 6,500-8,500+ systems across 60+ countries (figures vary by source/date), with most revenue derived from German operations, positioning it to benefit from distributed-generation and biogas/hydrogen-ready energy-transition trends. Source: https://www.morningstar.com.au/investments/security/fra/2GB/summary
thesis.main_shareholders: 2G Energy is controlled by co-founder and CEO Christian Grotholt, described in company/press material as 'CEO und größter Aktionär' (CEO and largest shareholder). A First Berlin research report (March 2018) put Grotholt's stake at 30.0% and co-founder Ludger Gausling's at 23.1%, with free float at 46.9%; a comdirect profile (undated, more recent) shows 'Christian Gro...' (truncated, presumably Grotholt) at 29.60%. Source: https://2-g.com/downloads/de/IR/Analystenberichte%20%26%20Studien/2025/2GB_GR-2025-02-28_DE.pdf ; https://www.comdirect.de/inf/aktien/DE000A0HL8N9. A Boerse-Express article reports Grotholt moved his shares into a private asset-management vehicle while retaining his position as largest shareholder (exact date/percentage not given). An iTiger summary separately states insiders hold about 45% of the company in aggregate. Source: https://www.boerse-express.com/news/articles/2g-energy-aktie-ceo-manoever-und-technische-warnsignale-801647 ; https://www.itiger.com/hans/news/2529577452. We could not confirm Grotholt's or Gausling's exact current percentages from a 2024/2025 Stimmrechtsmitteilung (voting-rights notification) in this search; the figures above (29.6-30.0%) are the most recent reasonably specific data points found.
thesis.red_flags: CEO Grotholt moving his shareholding into a private asset-management vehicle is a governance/structural change worth monitoring, though it does not by itself indicate wrongdoing and was reported without further detail in this search. Source: https://www.boerse-express.com/news/articles/2g-energy-aktie-ceo-manoever-und-technische-warnsignale-801647. Founder/insider control (~45% combined per aggregator data) concentrates governance influence, a disclosed structure typical of German founder-led industrials. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Cyprus-based international IT group (established 1987), listed on the Main Market of the Cyprus Stock Exchange (FTSE/CySE 20 and FTSE-Med member). Main business is regional wholesale distribution of technology products and services, with subsidiaries in Cyprus, Greece, Italy, Germany, Romania, Turkey, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Lebanon, Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar and Oman (group page also lists Egypt and Morocco); more than 800 staff and over 8,000 customers per company page. FY2025 gross sales EUR 1,235.8m (-4.6% vs EUR 1,294.8m); net sales after IFRS 15 adjustment EUR 871.7m vs EUR 1,091.0m. H1 2025 sales fell 14.6% to about EUR 490m while profit after tax nearly doubled to EUR 29.7m. Full-year profit before tax was not retrieved. Sources: https://www.logicom.net/about-us/ ; https://www.logicom.net/media/20060/logicom-public-cfs-ye2025-final-full-set.pdf ; https://cyprus-mail.com/2025/09/26/logicom-posts-after-tax-profit-of-e29-67m-in-first-half-of-2025
thesis.competitive_position: Regional (Mediterranean/Middle East/Africa) IT distributor; vendor list on company page includes Cisco, HP Inc., HPE, IBM, Lenovo, Microsoft, NetApp, Kingston and others. Gross-to-net sales gap indicates a large agency/IFRS 15 component. No market-share or competitor data located in this search. Strategy includes building a stake in Demetra Holdings Plc: Logicom Services bought Eurobank's 8.576% (17,152,353 shares at EUR 1.55, about EUR 27m, completed 16 Jan 2025), then ran a CySEC-approved public offer (EUR 1.55 cash, 5 Mar - 14 Apr 2025); direct holding was about 38.5% (77,000,909 shares) as of 7 Apr 2025 and the company page states 38.50%; the final offer result was not found. In July 2026 CySEC exempted Logicom Services from a further mandatory bid that Demetra's own buy-backs would trigger. Sources: https://www.logicom.net/about-us/ ; https://cyprus-mail.com/2025/04/08/logicom-increases-stake-in-demetra-to-38-5-per-cent ; https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/07/01/logicom-granted-exemption-from-demetra-holdings-takeover ; https://cbn.com.cy/article/2025/1/17/816361/eurobank-sells-858-stake-in-demetra-holdings-plc-to-logicom-services-for-eur27m
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Logicom's dispersion statements: Varnavas Irinarchos (Vice-Chairman and Managing Director) 38,186,848 shares = 51.548%; Demetra Holdings Plc 7,615,937 shares = 10.281% (both unchanged at 30 Sep 2025, 31 Dec 2025 and 31 Mar 2026); Iliana Theofanous 3,709,315 shares = 5.007% appeared in the 31 Dec 2025 statement (not confirmed for 31 Mar 2026). Free float to public about 30.6% at 31 Dec 2025 (line hard to match exactly; verify in PDF). Sources: https://www.logicom.net/media/20020/dispersion-announcement-311225-eng-full.pdf ; https://www.logicom.net/media/19907/dispersion-statement-31-03-2026-digitally-signed.pdf ; https://www.logicom.net/media/19379/dispersion-report-300925-eng-full.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: Varnavas Irinarchos, Vice-Chairman and Managing Director, 51.548% (38,186,848 shares) at 31 Mar 2026 per Logicom's dispersion statement (direct vs indirect split not shown in the excerpt). Other directors' holdings not located in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.logicom.net/media/19907/dispersion-statement-31-03-2026-digitally-signed.pdf ; https://www.logicom.net/media/20020/dispersion-announcement-311225-eng-full.pdf
thesis.red_flags: Controlled by one individual (about 51.5%). Cross-holding loop: Logicom owns about 38.5% of Demetra while Demetra holds 10.28% of Logicom; Logicom's reported profit depends on Demetra's results (the Dec 2025 profit warning said final after-tax profit could not be estimated because Demetra's results were unavailable). Mandatory-bid exposure from Demetra buy-backs was exempted by CySEC (July 2026) - a regulatory/governance sensitivity. 31 Dec 2025 profit warning: lower turnover and higher admin costs expected to cut operating profit; sales fell in the Gulf, Italy, Romania and Greece in H1 2025. Low-margin distribution business with Middle East exposure (generic caveat). Sources: https://www.logicom.net/media/19762/profit-warning-for-2025-eng.pdf ; https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/07/01/logicom-granted-exemption-from-demetra-holdings-takeover ; https://cyprus-mail.com/2025/09/26/logicom-posts-after-tax-profit-of-e29-67m-in-first-half-of-2025 ; https://www.logicom.net/media/19907/dispersion-statement-31-03-2026-digitally-signed.pdf

thesis.business_description: Logwin AG is a global logistics group listed in the Prime Standard of Deutsche Boerse, with two segments: Air + Ocean (international freight forwarding; FY2025 revenue EUR 1,108.7m, EBITA margin 5.8%) and Solutions (contract logistics; revenue EUR 255.8m, EBITA margin 10.8%). Group FY2025 revenue EUR 1,362.0m (-5.6% vs EUR 1,442.4m), net result EUR 61.6m (2024: EUR 65.6m), about 3,690 employees at 31 Dec 2025 and around 190 locations on six continents. Incorporated in Luxembourg; the exact HQ/operating-centre location was not confirmed in this search. A Q1 2026 release described conditions as challenging. Sources: https://ir-api.eqs.com/storage/ir/85ed8a/documents/18459e1d-ff6d-437c-8c72-57c39513ddff/LU1618151879-JA-2025-EQ-E-00.pdf ; https://app.boersengefluester.de/en/newswire/LU1618151879/logwin-ag/logwin-utilizes-stable-financial-and-earnings-position-in-fiscal-year-2025-to-further-expand-its-global-activities-2288054 ; https://app.boersengefluester.de/en/newswire/LU1618151879/logwin-ag/logwins-first-quarter-of-2026-characterized-by-challenging-conditions-2317840
thesis.competitive_position: Mid-sized global forwarder/contract logistician; the company describes itself as one of the leading companies in its market, but no market-share or competitor data were located. Revenue is dominated by Air + Ocean (about 81% of group revenue by the segment figures above, derived), which is lower-margin and cyclical; Solutions carries roughly double the EBITA margin. The board intends to propose a EUR 12.80 per share distribution for FY2025 (reason for the size - e.g. any special component - not verified). Sources: https://app.boersengefluester.de/en/newswire/LU1618151879/logwin-ag/logwin-utilizes-stable-financial-and-earnings-position-in-fiscal-year-2025-to-further-expand-its-global-activities-2288054 ; https://ir-api.eqs.com/storage/ir/85ed8a/documents/18459e1d-ff6d-437c-8c72-57c39513ddff/LU1618151879-JA-2025-EQ-E-00.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: Majority shareholder is DELTON Logistics S.a r.l., Grevenmacher, Luxembourg (named in the company's FY2025 and Q1 2026 releases); a 2018 voting-rights notice reports DELTON Vermoegensverwaltung AG transferring shares to this entity. The current percentage was not found in this search. Older press (undated) said Delton held 53.71% at the time of a takeover offer, which is stale; MarketScreener (aggregator) lists a free float of 12.71%, which would imply a very large controlling stake but is unverified. Delton is described in press as the holding of the Quandt family (Stefan Quandt). thesis.business_description: ForFarmers N.V. (Lochem, Netherlands) is a European producer of compound feed and nutrition for livestock farmers. FY2025: 10.6 million tonnes of feed, underlying net profit EUR 61.9m (+52.5%), ROACE 17.4% (2024: 13.0%), dividend EUR 0.30 per share. The Netherlands is the core market (about half of volume); the UK (2025 volume 2.51m tonnes, +5.2%; revenue EUR 729.5m, underlying EBIT EUR 15.4m vs 8.1m) and Germany (JV with team agrar launched March 2025, new organic feed plant) are the other main markets. Belgium was not confirmed in this search. Sources: https://www.forfarmersgroup.eu/en/results/forfarmers-2025-results ; https://agritradenews.co.uk/news/2026/02/23/profit-rise-for-forfarmers-in-2025/ ; https://en.boerenbusiness.nl/artikel/10915434/topresultaat-forfarmers-in-jaar-dat-het-tij-meezat
thesis.competitive_position: Management says it is gaining share in a shrinking Dutch compound-feed market (industry body Nevedi estimated Dutch production down 3-5% in 2024). Strategy: bolt-ons and specialisation (Beukelaar Diervoeders acquisition late 2025, about 80,000 tonnes; organic feed in Germany) and UK restructuring (two feed mills sold to 2Agriculture). Scale is a feed-volume business with thin per-tonne margins; no named competitor or market-share figures were located in this search. Outlook flagged as less favourable for 2026 (raw-material prices rising, milk prices sharply lower). Sources: https://en.boerenbusiness.nl/varkens/artikel/10912770/forfarmers-groeit-verder-in-krimpende-markt ; https://en.boerenbusiness.nl/artikel/10915434/topresultaat-forfarmers-in-jaar-dat-het-tij-meezat ; https://www.forfarmersgroup.eu/en/results/forfarmers-2025-results

thesis.business_description: German maker of special machinery and automated production lines, mainly for electromobility (segment E-Mobility, about 82.8% of FY2024 revenue per a secondary source) plus segment Next Automation (aerospace, rail, consumer goods, agriculture, clean tech and other markets). thesis.business_description: Kulmbacher Brauerei Aktien-Gesellschaft (Kulmbach, Bavaria) is the parent of the Kulmbacher Gruppe, a German brewer with beer brands including Kulmbacher, Mönchshof, EKU and Kapuziner; Wikipedia's history also lists Sternquell, Braustolz and a majority in the Bad Brambacher mineral spring (history, may be dated).
