thesis.business_description: Integrated Diagnostics Holdings plc (Jersey-registered, listed in London since May 2015) runs a network of medical laboratory and radiology branches in Egypt, Jordan, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia and Sudan, with 767 branches at 31 Dec 2025 (FY2025 results, 17 Apr 2026) and 794 at Q1 2026. H1 2026 (to 30 Jun 2026): revenue about EGP4.9bn (+37%), EBITDA about EGP1.6bn (33.9% margin), net profit EGP839m (+47%; EGP802m excluding FX effects); Egypt is about 86% of revenue (aggregator). HQ city was not confirmed in this search. thesis.competitive_position: Large multi-country private diagnostics network, with growth from branch roll-out (Saudi Arabia: nine branches planned for 2026 and a three-year target of 50, per earnings-call coverage; Nigeria Echo-Lab local-currency revenue +12%) and a stated acquisition strategy across the Middle East, Africa and East Asia. Market-share figures and named competitors were not found in this search (research gap). Sources: https://www.dailypolitical.com/?p=10504489 ; https://www.ticker.app/lse/IDHC/rns/2026-05-20/Replacement-1st-Quarter-Results/1408F ; https://www.boerse-stuttgart.de/en/products/equities/stuttgart/a2qjtq-intergrated-dia-h-dl-0-25/
thesis.main_shareholders: Hena Holdings (vehicle owned by CEO Hend El Sherbini and her mother) held about 56.67% per the H1 2026 report (329,423,666 shares, about 56.66%, as of 5 Aug 2026); free float about 43.3%. Sequence: on 23 Jun 2026 Hena bought 126,000,000 shares (21.67%) from Actis IDH Limited (Elliott-controlled) at US$0.50, reaching 288,445,383 shares (49.62%) and triggering a Rule 9 mandatory cash offer at US$0.50 (about US$290.7m total, about 11% below the prior close); acceptances were 7.04% by day 28; the offer became unconditional 28 Jul and a final extension ran to 12 Aug 2026. Final settlement after 12 Aug was not confirmed. An aggregator (Simply Wall St, undated) lists El Sherbini 27.6% and a 21.7% block (126m shares) under the name General Atlantic, which conflicts with the filings naming Actis IDH Limited as seller; treat as stale. Other institutional holders not located. thesis.insider_ownership: CEO Hend El Sherbini controls Hena Holdings together with her mother, so effective insider control is about 56.7% (see above); pre-offer aggregator data showed her at 27.6% directly (unverified). Holdings of other directors were not located (research gap). Sources: https://www.perivan.com/resources/news/unrecommended-mandatory-final-cash-offer-document-published-for-the-us290-7-million-offer-by-hena-holdings-for-integrated-diagnostics-holdings/ ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/healthcare/lse-idhc/integrated-diagnostics-holdings-shares/ownership
thesis.red_flags: Change-of-control situation (from screen, checked against sources): Hena, owned by the CEO and her mother, acquired 21.67% from Actis/Elliott, triggered an unrecommended mandatory final offer at US$0.50, and now holds about 56.7%; the independent directors (advised by Shoosmiths) recommended rejection, reportedly saying the price undervalued the company. IDH is the offer target and remains listed in London; the earlier screen says Hena would seek cancellation of the listing if it reaches 75% (not confirmed in my searches), so delisting/minority-squeeze risk exists. The CEO-controlled bidder is a conflict-of-interest situation for minorities. About 86% of revenue is Egyptian, so EGP/FX and macro risk is high; reported H1 profit includes FX effects (EGP839m reported vs EGP802m adjusted). thesis.business_description: The Alumasc Group plc is a UK-based supplier of building products (fiscal year to 30 June) organised in three divisions: Building Envelope (Alumasc Roofing, Roof-Pro, Blackdown roof and podium landscaping), Water Management (Alumasc Water Management Solutions: Skyline architectural aluminium, rainwater, Harmer/Wade drainage, Gatic access covers, aluminium roofline) and Housebuilding Products (Timloc). FY26 (year to 30 June 2026, announced 15 Sep 2026): revenue GBP107.1m (down 6%), underlying profit before tax GBP10.0m (FY25: GBP14.2m). Principal market is UK construction/housebuilding; HQ location was not confirmed in this search (research gap). Sources: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/alumasc-group--alu/full-year-results-/9771548 ; https://www.alumascwms.co.uk/about
thesis.competitive_position: Per the FY26 results: Housebuilding Products revenue grew about 16% in a weak UK housebuilding market, which the company attributes to market-share gains from product innovation and service; Building Envelope held revenue at record levels; Water Management revenue fell about 16% (about 3% excluding a prior-year Chek Lap Kok project). Stated medium-term operating margin target is 15-20%; net bank debt GBP6.9m (0.5x leverage); order book up 56% at end Aug 2026. The company claims more than 80% of revenue comes from environmental/sustainable building solutions (company claim, undated). Named competitors and a current UK market-share figure were not found in this search (research gap). Sources: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/alumasc-group--alu/full-year-results-/9771548 ; https://www.alumascwms.co.uk/about

thesis.business_description: UK-based designer and supplier of housewares and small domestic appliances, with own brands including Salter and Beldray sold mainly to UK retailers (supermarkets, discounters) and others. FY2025 (year to 31 Jul 2025): revenue GBP 150.1m (-3%), adjusted EBITDA GBP 12.5m (-31%), net bank debt GBP 14.1m (1.1x adj. EBITDA vs 1.0x target), dividend 3.70p (FY24: 7.38p). Air-fryer sales fell 32% and third-party close-out parcels 60%. HQ location not confirmed in this search. Moved from the LSE Main Market to AIM on 15 Jan 2026 (86,330,132 voting shares). Sources: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/ultimate-products--ultp/audited-results-for-the-year-ended-31-july-2025/9197676 ; https://joshthompson.co.uk/investing/ultimate-products-fy25-profit-decline-aim-listing-consideration/ ; https://www.ticker.app/lse/ULTP/rns/2026-01-15/Admission-to-AIM/8983O
thesis.competitive_position: Mid-sized UK housewares/small-appliance brand owner and sourcer (Salter, Beldray); gross margin fell to 23.2% on mix and an extra GBP 3.1m of shipping costs. One analysis says supermarket sales rose 18% (to about GBP 40.4m) while UK discounter sales fell 34% after a customer shifted to own-label, illustrating retailer concentration and private-label risk. No market-share data or named competitors located; the customer names Tesco/Aldi/Home Bargains were not confirmed, and a Russell Hobbs licence was not found in these results. At AIM admission about 59.5% of shares were 'not in public hands' (AIM Schedule One). The AIM Rule 26 page on upplc.com should list significant shareholders but was not readable here. Moved from the Main Market to AIM in Jan 2026 (smaller market cap about GBP 50m expected at the time; lower liquidity and lighter regulatory regime than the Main Market); about 59.5% of shares not in public hands at admission. name: Gielda Papierów Wartosciowych w Warszawie S.A.

thesis.business_description: Operator of the Warsaw Stock Exchange (Warsaw, Poland) and parent of a group covering the financial market (equities, bonds, derivatives), the commodity market via wholly owned Towarowa Gielda Energii (TGE; power and gas trading), market data, and benchmark administration (GPW Benchmark, wholly owned); BondSpot is held at 97.23% (June 2024 fact sheet). Per the same fact sheet revenue was split roughly financial market 48%, commodity market 34%, information services 14%. Depository and clearing sit outside the group in associate KDPW and KDPW_CCP. FY2025 (Quartr summary of results): revenue PLN551.9m (+18.7%), adjusted net profit PLN204.7m (+30.2%), cost/income 66.1%; dividend policy targets 60-80% of consolidated net profit. Sources: https://www.gpw.pl/pub/GPW/files/PDF/RI/GPW_Fact_Sheet_June_2024.pdf ; https://quartr.com/events/gielda-papier-w-wartosciowych-w-warszawie-sa-gpw-q4-2025_3ep4h18E ; https://gpw.pl/capital-group
thesis.competitive_position: Describes itself as the largest national stock exchange in Central and Eastern Europe; a 2023 investor presentation states Main Market share turnover in 2022 was 54% of total CEE share turnover. TGE gives it one of the more liquid electricity markets in Europe. Group development plan covers 2023-2027 and targets a 50% EBITDA margin in 2027 (per search summary of company materials; 2025-26 updates not verified). LTM ROE was reported at 17.8% (bank.pl) vs 18.1% to September (PAP), so sources differ slightly. Sources: https://www.gpw.pl/pub/GPW/files/PDF/RI/2023_12_GPW_IR_presentation.pdf ; https://bank.pl/gpw-wypracowala-w-2025-roku-rekordowe-wyniki-finansowe-i-rynkowe/ ; https://biznes.pap.pl/wiadomosci/firmy/wse-operator-gpw-posts-pln-492-mln-net-profit-q3-2025-above-expectations
thesis.main_shareholders: State Treasury is the dominant holder: about 35% of share capital with two votes per share, which gave it 51.80% of total votes per the June 2022 KNF-filed current report (16/2022); NN OFE then held about 3.70% of total votes (about 5% of shares per one search summary; the sources appear inconsistent). 2015 annual report also showed the Treasury at about 35% of shares and 51.8% of votes as the only 5%+ holder. These are 2022 and older figures; a current 2025-26 shareholder table could not be located in this search; treat as a research gap. Search results for PKO BP (not GPW) show different numbers and should not be used here. Sources: https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art36563371-gpw ; https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/GPW-Wykaz-akcjonariuszy-posiadajacych-co-najmniej-5-liczby-glosow-na-Nadzwyczajnym-Walnym-Zgromadzeniu-Gieldy-Papierow-Wartosciowych-w-Warszawie-w-dniu-15-czerwca-2022-r-8357915.html ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/4797,akcjonariusze-gpw-zadecyduja-22-vi-o-zmianach-w-rn-na-wniosek-skarbu-panstwa
thesis.red_flags: State control: the Treasury's double-vote shares give it a majority of votes with about a third of capital, so board composition and strategy are exposed to political decisions (a Polish press item reported the Treasury seeking to remove the previous president before the February 2024 change; date and details not verified). Earnings are sensitive to market turnover and to regulatory fee treatment (Q1 2025 profit was partly lifted by a change in how KNF fees are recognised). No litigation, accounting or audit concerns were found in this search, which was not an exhaustive legal check; standard caveat applies. Sources: https://comparic.pl/gpw-czekaja-powazne-zmiany-skarb-panstwa-chce-odwolac-prezesa-warszawskiej-gieldy/ ; https://biznes.pap.pl/wiadomosci/firmy/wse-operator-gpw-posts-pln-505-mln-net-profit-q1-2025-above-expectations
thesis.insider_ownership: Management board per Bankier/ESPI: President Tomasz Bardziłowski (appointed 5 Feb 2024 after KNF approval), Vice President Slawomir Panasiuk, with Dominika Niewiadomska-Siniecka, Marcin Rulnicki and Michal Kobza also listed. Their GPW share holdings were not found; research gap (check the annual report and MAR notifications). The State Treasury (about 35% of shares) is the relevant controlling holder. thesis.business_description: Henry Boot PLC is a UK property investment, development and land-promotion group; the Property Investment and Development segment generates the most revenue. Land promotion is run through Hallam Land (e.g. sale of a Queniborough, Leicestershire site with consent for 160 homes in October 2025) and house building through Stonebridge Homes. thesis.competitive_position: Strategy under outgoing CEO Tim Roberts has been a portfolio shake-up: acquisition of Stonebridge Homes, disposal of the lower-margin construction contracting business, and a refocus on land promotion, development and investment. thesis.business_description: NEUCA S.A. is a Polish pharmaceutical wholesale distributor; pharmacy wholesale accounts for more than 90% of group revenue (2023 analyst report, may be dated). H1 2025 consolidated revenue was PLN5,471.5m (H1 2024: PLN4,630.5m); full-year 2025 results and HQ details were not located in this search (research gap). Sources: https://www.sii.org.pl/7684/analizy/analizy-i-komentarze/raport-specjalny-neuca-pelion-porownanie-dwoch-gigantow-w-branzy-farmaceutycznej.html ; https://www.stockwatch.pl/gpw/neuca,analiza-techniczna,dane-finansowe.aspx
thesis.competitive_position: One of the three main pharmaceutical wholesalers in Poland alongside Pelion and Farmacol, which together account for about 70% of sales to pharmacies, with Neuca above 30% (2023 analysis, dated). Reported market share was 31.1% in Q2 2025 and 38.1% among independent pharmacies, its strategic segment (from search summaries of Stockwatch/Comparic pages; exact page not pinned down). Sources: https://www.sii.org.pl/7684/analizy/analizy-i-komentarze/raport-specjalny-neuca-pelion-porownanie-dwoch-gigantow-w-branzy-farmaceutycznej.html ; https://www.stockwatch.pl/gpw/neuca,analiza-techniczna,dane-finansowe.aspx ; https://comparic.pl/neuca-z-reakcja-rynku-w-rejonie-700-zl-zapiski-gieldowego-spekulanta/
thesis.main_shareholders: From the company's ESPI list of holders with at least 5% of votes at the Dec 2025 extraordinary meeting (report dated 16 Dec 2025; percentages shown of total votes): Altea Alternatywna Spolka Inwestycyjna Sp. z o.o. 1,007,413 votes = 22.12%; Wiesława Herba 1,005,240 = 22.07%; Allianz Polska OFE 170,352 = 3.74%; Nationale-Nederlanden OFE 132,000 = 2.90% (the latter two passed 5% only of votes present at the meeting). Conflict: Simply Wall St (undated aggregator) shows Kazimierz Herba 27.4% and Wiesława Herba 25%; this does not match the ESPI list. The relationship between Altea and the Herba family was not established in this search. Sources: https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art43516791-neuca-sa-akcjonariusze-posiadajacy-co-najmniej-5-glosow-na-nwza ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/pl/healthcare/wse-neu/neuca-shares/ownership
thesis.insider_ownership: Wiesława Herba holds 22.07% of total votes (ESPI, Dec 2025). Piotr Sucharski, long-time president, shows about 1.46% (65,244 shares) on Simply Wall St (undated aggregator figure); search results report he would step down as president at end-2025 with Grzegorz Dzik, currently a vice-president, as successor (not confirmed from a company filing). Holdings of the supervisory board and of Altea's owners were not located (research gap). Sources: https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art43516791-neuca-sa-akcjonariusze-posiadajacy-co-najmniej-5-glosow-na-nwza ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/pl/healthcare/wse-neu/neuca-shares/ownership ; https://www.sii.org.pl/17964/analizy/analizy-i-komentarze/5-spolek-z-gpw-do-obserwacji-w-marcu-neuca-i-inne-pod-lupa-analityka.html
thesis.red_flags: Ownership is concentrated in two roughly 22% holders, and the shareholder data conflict between sources (see above). Management transition at end-2025 (president Sucharski stepping down per secondary sources). Low-margin wholesale model in a regulated, concentrated Polish pharma market (three wholesalers hold about 70%) is exposed to pricing/reimbursement and customer-consolidation risk (general caveat, not a company-specific finding). No litigation or accounting issue was identified in this search, but audit reports and the risk section of the annual report were not reviewed. Sources: https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art43516791-neuca-sa-akcjonariusze-posiadajacy-co-najmniej-5-glosow-na-nwza ; https://www.sii.org.pl/7684/analizy/analizy-i-komentarze/raport-specjalny-neuca-pelion-porownanie-dwoch-gigantow-w-branzy-farmaceutycznej.html
thesis.website: https://www.neuca.pl (domain from prior knowledge, not confirmed by the search results)

thesis.business_description: Hagar hf is an Icelandic retail group with operations in Iceland, the Faroe Islands and the Netherlands, primarily in grocery and fuel. Subsidiaries include Bonus, Hagkaup and Hysing; the Icelandic footprint cited is 40 grocery stores, 22 Olis service stations and 45 OB self-service stations, plus warehouses and an online store. Financial year ends in February; FY2025/26 audited statements were approved by the board on 29 April 2026, with a proposed dividend of 50% of profit after tax. Q1 2026/27 revenue was ISK 50.8bn (+5.5% y/y). Sources: https://www.hagar.is/media/jxhftypt/2026-05-samþykktir-haga.pdf ; https://www.streetinsider.com/Press+Releases/Hagar+hf%3A+Financial+Statements+202526/26391531.html ; https://www.esmmagazine.com/retail/icelands-hagar-reports-revenue-and-profit-growth-in-q1-2026-27-315576
thesis.competitive_position: Low-price grocery positioning via Bonus (a trade guide describes Bonus as the cheapest supermarket and Hagkaup as the biggest retail channel in Iceland; weak source, undated). Strategy items: purchasing alliance with Salling Group (over 350 new products across Bonus and Hagkaup in Q1 2026/27) and the Takk loyalty programme launched 14 Jan 2026 (nearly 60,000 members). In Sept 2024 Hagar and co-owners began a formal sales process for their stakes in fuel distributor Olidreifing; outcome not found. Could not locate market-share percentages or competitor figures; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.esmmagazine.com/retail/icelands-hagar-reports-revenue-and-profit-growth-in-q1-2026-27-315576 ; https://www.bankofscotlandtrade.co.uk/en/market-potential/iceland/distribution
thesis.main_shareholders: Aggregator only (Simply Wall St, S&P Global data, undated): Lifeyrissjodur verslunarmanna about 23.2%, Gildi lifeyrissjodur about 16.9%, an Icelandic municipal-employees pension fund about 11.3%, Kaldbakur ehf. about 8.1%. Hagar's own top-20 list was not located; check Nasdaq Iceland or the annual report. Share capital ISK 1,106,428,863 (nominal ISK 1 each, May 2026 articles); 1,081 shareholders at the AGM of 21 May 2026, when 40 holders representing 76.46% of outstanding shares were present. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/is/consumer-retailing/icse-haga/hagar-hf-shares/ownership ; https://www.hagar.is/media/w5hehesn/fundargerð-aðalfundar-21-05-2026_signed.pdf ; https://www.hagar.is/media/jxhftypt/2026-05-samþykktir-haga.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: Could not locate board or executive holdings in this search; treat as a research gap (the annual report or Nasdaq Iceland insider notices would carry them). No named founding-family or insider holder was seen among the top holders in the aggregator data, which are mainly pension funds and an investment company.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in this search (no litigation, restatement or governance issue surfaced). Caveats: ownership is concentrated in Icelandic pension funds (aggregator data, unverified); dominant domestic exposure to a small, competitive Icelandic grocery and fuel market; potential competition-authority scrutiny is a standard risk for market leaders (not verified here); Olidreifing stake sale outcome unknown. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/is/consumer-retailing/icse-haga/hagar-hf-shares/ownership ; https://www.streetinsider.com/Press+Releases/Hagar+hf%3A+Financial+Statements+202526/26391531.html

thesis.business_description: RTC Group plc is an AIM-listed engineering and technical recruitment group headquartered in Derby, UK, supplying temporary and permanent white- and blue-collar staff in domestic and international markets. UK brands include Ganymede (technical/engineering talent for rail, energy, construction, highways) and ATA Recruitment; GSS serves international clients. FY2025: revenue from continuing operations GBP 95.5m (2024: GBP 96.8m), operating profit GBP 2.5m, operating cash inflow GBP 5.2m, no term debt; H1 2026 revenue GBP 45.2m vs GBP 48.3m a year earlier. Sources: https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/interim-results-4j33fucuqpec253.html ; https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/rtc-group-raises-final-dividend-says-earnings-extremely-robust ; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/rtc-group--rtc/final-results-for-the-year-ended-31-december-2020/6401439
thesis.competitive_position: Niche small-cap contract recruiter focused on UK rail/infrastructure and engineering labour supply, with an international arm; operates in a fragmented market against larger staffing groups. Could not locate market-share data or named competitors in this search; treat moat as a research gap. Strategy visible from filings: capital-light, debt-free balance sheet, rising dividend (FY2025 total proposed 6.71p incl. 5.5p final) and share buybacks (e.g. 1,063,699 shares bought in April 2025, about 7.81% of issued shares per RNS). Sources: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/rtc-group-raises-final-dividend-says-earnings-extremely-robust ; https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/RTC/transaction-in-own-shares-oi6z5779qyow99s.html
thesis.main_shareholders: Aggregator only (Simply Wall St, S&P Global data, updated March 2026): Mary Douie about 20.5% (2,575,728 shares), Gerard Mason about 7.57% (table layout garbled, attribution not certain); top 25 holders about 75.2%. RNS items: Northern Venture Trust 3.05% (383,330 shares) after 14 Apr 2025; Chelverton Asset Management reported above 10% of voting rights in a notice tied to Oct 2024 data (possibly stale). Older conflicting/stale: June 2016 RNS showed Alison Chapman at about 8.9%. The annual report's substantial-shareholder table was not located; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/commercial-services/aim-rtc/rtc-group-shares/ownership ; https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/rtc-group-sees-major-shareholding-shift ; https://www.ticker.app/lse/RTC/rns/2025-05-14/tr-1-notification-of-major-holdings/6414I
thesis.insider_ownership: Andy Pendlebury is Chairman and Chief Executive and Sarah Dye is Group Finance Director. Current percentages from the annual report not located. Stale RNS (June 2016): Pendlebury about 5.5% and Dye about 0.3% after sales. Simply Wall St (aggregator) shows Dye with 43,000 shares and estimates insiders collectively at about 54% (undated; unverified). Director Nick Spoliar bought 5,072 shares at 97.2p in December 2025 (0.04% of issued capital per RNS). Sources: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/rtc-group--rtc/director-shareholding/9304021 ; https://financialfilings.com/filings/rtc-group-plc/directors-dealing/2016/3654824/ ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/commercial-services/aim-rtc/rtc-group-shares/ownership
thesis.red_flags: Combined Chairman and Chief Executive role (Andy Pendlebury) is a governance caveat under UK Corporate Governance norms. Non-executive director Wayne Thornhill resigned effective 28 Nov 2025 (board changes also announced Oct 2025), thinning the board. Concentrated register (top 25 about 75%) and AIM small-cap illiquidity. H1 2026 revenue down about 6% year on year (GBP 45.2m vs GBP 48.3m). Dependence on UK rail/infrastructure project cycles (standard caveat, not quantified here). No litigation or accounting issues found in this search. Sources: https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/interim-results-4j33fucuqpec253.html ; https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/RTC/replacement-board-change-0xfqtrul6v260d1.html

thesis.business_description: Polski Holding Nieruchomości S.A. (PHN) is a Polish state-controlled property group listed on the WSE since its 2013 IPO. Its 2025-2030 'Nowy Start' strategy rests on four pillars: Development, Rental, Construction and PRS (institutional residential rental). At 31 Mar 2026 the portfolio was about PLN3.5bn across 149 properties, 480k sqm of managed space and 600 ha of land (the strategy cites asset value PLN4.6bn rising to PLN6.1bn; different measures). 2025 net profit PLN204.4m vs a PLN184.4m loss in 2024, helped by a one-off VAT refund (via media summaries of the annual report). Sources: https://bank.pl/polski-holding-nieruchomosci-w-swojej-strategii-stawia-m-in-na-prs/ ; https://www.phnsa.pl/sites/default/files/prezentacje/phn_prezentacja_wynikowa_za_i_kwartal_2026_roku_-_26.05.2026.pdf ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/136863,zwrot-vat-wyniosl-zysk-netto-phn-na-historyczny-poziom
thesis.competitive_position: Large Polish landholder with a legacy portfolio of over 150 properties that the strategy aims to cut to under 90 (about PLN300m of disposals) while investing over PLN4.4bn. 2030 targets: net revenue above PLN1.6bn, EBITDA above PLN400m, and over PLN180m of dividends across 2025-2030. PHN also seeks cooperation with other State Treasury companies. Market share and named competitors were not found in this search (research gap). Sources: https://bank.pl/polski-holding-nieruchomosci-w-swojej-strategii-stawia-m-in-na-prs/ ; https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/PHN-chce-rozwijac-wspolprace-ze-spolkami-Skarbu-Panstwa-8906399.html
thesis.main_shareholders: State Treasury about 71.93% (PAP Biznes item, March 2025). Allianz Polska OFE 5,102,442 shares = 9.96% (notice reported Jan 2023; stale). Nationale-Nederlanden PTE about 5.62% (money.pl aggregator, updated 2018; stale and unverified). Share capital 51,217,313 shares, one vote each. No 2026 shareholder list was found; treat the minority holders as a research gap. Sources: https://biznes.pap.pl/download/attachment/51887467/DOC.20250625.51887467.zal01_PHN_-_Odpowiedzi_na_pytania_akcjonariusza.pdf ; https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/PHN-S-A-Zawiadomienie-o-zmianie-stanu-posiadania-8541607.html ; https://www.money.pl/gielda/spolki-gpw/PLPHN0000014,o_firmie.html
thesis.insider_ownership: No personal shareholdings of board members were located (research gap). Money.pl/Bankier list Wiesław Malicki as president of the management board (appointed 24 Apr 2024), Jacek Krawczykowski as vice-president and Sławomir Frąckowiak as supervisory board chair (appointed Mar 2024); these are aggregator listings that may be out of date. The State Treasury is the dominant holder. Sources: https://www.money.pl/gielda/spolki-gpw/PLPHN0000014,o_firmie.html ; https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/akcje/PHN/podstawowe-dane
thesis.red_flags: State control (about 72%) means strategy can be influenced by government policy; the 2025 debate over PHN's role in housing policy is reflected in an rp.pl piece. Earnings are volatile and partly non-recurring (2024 loss PLN184.4m; 2025 profit boosted by a VAT refund; Q2 2025 was a loss). Leverage and funding: group liabilities PLN1,847.8m at 31 Mar 2026 (no overdue liabilities), parent debt securities PLN640.3m, and a decision in Sept 2026 to issue up to PLN250m of series F2 bonds, alongside a capex plan above PLN4.4bn. Net debt/LTV, covenants and H1 2026 results were not found (research gap). Sources: https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/154705,phn-sa-13-2026-decyzja-w-sprawie-emisji-obligacji-serii-f2 ; https://www.rp.pl/nieruchomosci/art42100101-phn-to-nie-instrument-polityki-mieszkaniowej-panstwa ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/141393,zysk-netto-phn-po-trzech-kwartalach-wyniosl-179-2-mln-zl

thesis.business_description: Aspocomp Group Oyj is a Finnish printed circuit board (PCB) maker headquartered in Espoo with its plant in Oulu; main technologies are HDI, multilayer (up to 28 layers), heat-sink and Teflon/ceramic-based boards (2012 trade press, may be dated). Customers design telecom equipment, automotive and industrial electronics and semiconductor test systems for security technology; most sales are exports. 2025: net sales EUR38.2m (+38%), operating result EUR0.9m (2024: -EUR4.0m), equity ratio 65.0%, dividend proposal EUR0.00. H1 2026: net sales EUR20.3m, operating result EUR0.6m (H1 2025: EUR1.0m), orders EUR25.2m (+24%), record order book. Sources: https://www.inderes.fi/releases/aspocomps-half-year-report-january-june-2026-order-book-at-a-record-high-and-revenue-grew ; https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/aspocomps-financial-statement-release-2025-net-sales-increased-significantly-and-the-operating-result-turned-profitable ; https://evertiq.com/news/22795
thesis.competitive_position: Niche high-end PCB supplier focused on demanding HDI/multilayer boards for defence, semiconductor test, telecom and industrial customers; management expects demand from defence and semiconductors to stay good. An undated profile quotes the CEO calling it Europe's second-largest PCB producer concentrating on the high end (treat as dated). It is expanding Oulu capacity by about 50%: EUR1.75m EU Just Transition Fund support within a EUR10m project (completion expected by 2027), plus EUR5.5m of long-term loans from LähiTapiola and Nordea. Current competitor comparison not found (research gap). Sources: https://finder.techleap.nl/news/feed/aspocomp-gets-eur-1-75m-eu-funding ; https://finder.techleap.nl/news/feed/aspocomp-secures-5-5m-for-growth ; https://www.inderes.fi/releases/aspocomps-half-year-report-january-june-2026-order-book-at-a-record-high-and-revenue-grew
thesis.main_shareholders: Simply Wall St (aggregator, data as of Nov 2025): Joensuun Kauppa ja Kone Oy about 18.1%; Etola Oy about 15.4%; Mandatum Asset Management about 4.9%; Erkki Etola personally about 4.7%; Nordea Investment Management about 3.7%; Mikko Montonen about 3.6%; top 25 holders 69.9%. The company's Sept 2026 nomination-board release confirms the three largest holders' representatives (Kyösti Kakkonen for Joensuun Kauppa ja Kone; Ville Vuori for Etola Group and Erkki Etola) and Mikko Montonen as sixth-largest holder, but gives no percentages in the snippet seen. Official shareholder register figures were not retrieved (research gap). Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/fi/tech/hel-acg1v/aspocomp-group-oyj-shares/ownership ; https://www.inderes.fi/releases/aspocomp-group-plc-composition-of-shareholders-nomination-board-3
thesis.insider_ownership: Erkki Etola personally about 4.7% and the associated Etola Oy/Etola Group about 15.4% (aggregator, Nov 2025; the family/entity link is implied by the nomination-board release, not stated as a percentage there). Mikko Montonen about 3.6% (his role was not confirmed). CEO Manu Skyttä about 0.13% (Simply Wall St, undated). 2026 board proposed by the nomination board: Jenni Enroth, Kaisa Kokkonen, Anssi Korhonen and Ville Vuori (AGM 29 Apr 2026; outcome not confirmed); their personal holdings were not located. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/fi/tech/hel-acg1v/aspocomp-group-oyj-shares/ownership ; https://www.inderes.fi/sv/releases/aspocomps-shareholders-nomination-boards-proposals-to-the-annual-general-meeting-2026
thesis.red_flags: Small company (2025 sales EUR38m) that only returned to an operating profit in 2025 after a EUR4.0m operating loss in 2024; H1 2026 operating result was below the prior year. The company warns planned investments could cause temporary production disruptions and longer material lead times will raise inventory and working capital. Growth is debt- and equity-funded (EUR5.5m loans; Oct 2025 directed issue of 673,682 shares, EUR3.2m, 8.96% dilution). Ownership is concentrated (top two holders about 33%). No dividend. Customer concentration and governance issues were not assessed in this search. Sources: https://www.inderes.fi/releases/aspocomps-half-year-report-january-june-2026-order-book-at-a-record-high-and-revenue-grew ; https://finder.techleap.nl/news/feed/aspocomp-secures-5-5m-for-growth
thesis.website: https://www.aspocomp.com (domain from prior knowledge, not confirmed by the search results)

gmSourceUrl: [MFO S.A. Investor Relations](https://www.mfo.pl/pl/relacje-inwestorskie), [MFO S.A. Raporty](https://www.mfo.pl/pl/raporty), [GPW.pl ESPI Reports](https://www.gpw.pl/komunikat?geru_id=483798), [MFO 2023 Annual Report PDF](https://www.mfo.pl/sites/default/files/2024-03/RR_2023.pdf)

thesis.business_description: MFO S.A. (registered office Kozuszki Parcela 70A, Sochaczew, Poland; KRS 0000399598) manufactures and distributes cold-formed steel profiles; its main segment is reinforcement profiles for PVC windows, which generate most revenue. Range also includes PV, GK and special profiles and welded square/rectangular tubes. H1 2025 sales PLN 340.3m (+9% y/y), net profit PLN 7.82m; 9M 2025 sales about PLN 517.8m; preliminary Q1 2026 revenue PLN 173.4m. Sources: https://www.parkiet.com/spolka/mfo ; https://www.money.pl/gielda/spolki-gpw/PLMFO0000013,o_firmie.html ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/139977,wybrane-wyniki-mfo-za-pierwsza-polowe-2025-r-oraz-list-prezesa-zarzadu ; https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/MFO-S-A-Wstepne-dane-finansowe-MFO-S-A-za-trzy-kwartaly-2025-roku-9038082.html
thesis.competitive_position: Niche steel-profile producer for the window-fabrication supply chain. A new plant in Boryszew (Sochaczew district) was due to start production from Q2 2025 and lift capacity from about 175k to 280k tonnes of steel per year (Parkiet article; later ramp-up status not confirmed). Welded profile sales grew 31% in H1 2025 partly due to the new plant. Could not locate market-share data, named competitors or margin comparisons; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.parkiet.com/firmy/art41474321-mfo-jest-coraz-blizej-uruchomienia-nowego-zakladu ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/139977,wybrane-wyniki-mfo-za-pierwsza-polowe-2025-r-oraz-list-prezesa-zarzadu
thesis.main_shareholders: Bankier.pl (6,607,490 shares in total; free float about 18.31%): AZT Fundacja Rodzinna 31.68% of shares / 34.31% of votes and MBM Fundacja Rodzinna 30.37% / 32.84% (both changes dated 2025-10-01); Goldenco Investments Ltd via Bouders Ltd 13.62% (last change 2017, likely stale); Erste TFI 5.99% (2019, likely stale). Conflict: Simply Wall St (aggregator) lists individuals Tomasz Mirski 31.7% and Marek Mirski 30.4% plus Santander TFI 10.5%, so it differs on the minor lines. The 5%+ holder list from the AGM of 28 May 2026 exists on GPW but its contents were not visible; check it for current figures. Sources: https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/akcje/MFO/akcjonariat ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/pl/materials/wse-mfo/mfo-shares/ownership ; https://www.money.pl/gielda/spolki-gpw/plmfo0000013,emitent,1.html
thesis.insider_ownership: The two largest holders are family foundations, which Simply Wall St maps to Tomasz Mirski (31.7%) and Marek Mirski (30.4%); Forsal/ISBnews describes Tomasz Mirski, president of the management board, as the largest shareholder. Together the Mirski family foundations hold about 62% of shares (about 67% of votes) per Bankier. Foundation-to-individual mapping comes from an aggregator and was not verified against a filing. Sources: https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/akcje/MFO/akcjonariat ; https://forsal.pl/artykuly/765501,cena-emisyjna-mfo-ustalona-na-1130-zl-za-akcje.html ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/pl/materials/wse-mfo/mfo-shares/ownership
thesis.red_flags: Controlling shareholder block (family foundations about 62% of shares, about 67% of votes) with a thin free float of about 18%, so minority holders have limited influence and liquidity may be low. Revenue concentrated in PVC-window reinforcement profiles (construction-cycle and steel-price exposure; standard caveat, not quantified here). Capex for the Boryszew plant and any associated debt were not examined in this search. Some shareholder entries (2017, 2019) are stale. No litigation or accounting issues found in this search. Sources: https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/akcje/MFO/akcjonariat ; https://www.parkiet.com/firmy/art41474321-mfo-jest-coraz-blizej-uruchomienia-nowego-zakladu

thesis.business_description: Syn hf. is an Icelandic telecommunications and media company listed on Nasdaq Iceland (ticker SYN). Offerings include 4G/5G mobile services, the news site Visir.is and radio stations such as Bylgjan; it formerly operated the Stod 2 and Vodafone Iceland brands (Wikipedia). 2026 earnings guidance was reportedly unaffected by its Q2 2026 report (search summary; not independently verified). Could not locate segment revenue figures or the annual report in this search. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%BDn_(media_corporation) ; https://ruv.is/utvarp/spila/hadegisfrettir/25243/bhs7qn
thesis.competitive_position: Competes in Icelandic telecom and media; Siminn is a rival Icelandic telecom and is also the counterparty to the asset sale below. Known event sanity-checked: Syn is the SELLER of its web and radio media (Visir.is, Bylgjan, FM957) to Siminn under a term sheet reported 12 March 2026, valuing the unit at ISK 5,250m with about ISK 3,000m annual revenue; the parties commit to work toward a purchase agreement, subject to due diligence. No signing, completion or competition-authority approval was found. If completed, Syn would be a narrower telecom-focused company. Could not locate market-share data. Sources: https://ruv.is/utvarp/spila/hadegisfrettir/25243/bhs7qn/siminn-ad-kaupa-midla-synar ; https://mfn.se/one/a/siminn/siminn-hf-afkoma-fyrsta-arsfjordungs-2026-e67c99fa
thesis.main_shareholders: Aggregator only (Simply Wall St, undated; official top-20 list not located): Gavia Invest ehf about 18.2%, Gildi lifeyrissjodur about 16%, Skel fjarfestingafelag about 10.1%, Reir ehf. about 8.3%, Lifeyrissjodur verslunarmanna about 5.6%; top 15 holders about 93%; institutions about 55%, private companies about 38%, public about 7%. thesis.business_description: KGL S.A. (Korporacja KGL; registered in Moscisko per its ESPI filings) distributes plastic granules (polymers; the business started in 1992) and produces plastic packaging by thermoforming, in two segments (production and distribution). Distribution serves markets including the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary and the Baltics. Preliminary H1 2026 (Biznesradar): revenue about PLN 296m vs PLN 259m, EBITDA about PLN 28m vs PLN 18m, operating profit about PLN 14m vs PLN 3m; production revenue +15%, distribution +11%. Conflict: a Parkiet-based summary instead cites H1 revenue -6.8% and net profit -79.3%, which could refer to a different period; unresolved. Known event sanity-checked: the board has been running a review of strategic options (started per report 21/2024; update of 25 Feb 2026) alongside a business optimisation plan with identified cost reductions (announced 24 Apr 2026). The new strategy was first due in Q2 2026 and Biznesradar's headline now points to Q3 2026; no outcome, bid or transaction was found as of this search. Could not locate market share or named competitors; treat as a research gap. thesis.business_description: Madrid-based mid-market investment bank and asset manager (formerly Nmás1 Dinamia; renamed Alantra Partners in January 2017). Investment banking covers M&A, debt advisory, portfolio advisory, financial restructuring and capital markets, plus equity research/brokerage; asset management acts as general partner for private equity/credit vehicles for institutional and wealthy-family investors. Offices across Europe, the US and Asia (aggregator description; headcount and founding-year figures conflict between aggregators, so not relied on). FY2025: net revenues EUR 211.3m (+17.6%), of which Investment Banking EUR 167.7m and Asset Management EUR 37.9m; net profit attributable EUR 20.2m. Sources: https://craft.co/alantra ; https://www.alantra.com/alantra-generates-revenues-of-e211-3mn-17-6-and-a-net-profit-of-e20-2mn-186-2-in-2025/
thesis.competitive_position: Independent mid-market advisory boutique with an asset-management arm; reports 110 M&A transactions in 9M 2025 (vs 100 a year earlier), a 30% higher average M&A fee, and over 1,000 transactions in the last five years (company press release). Mutua Madrileña is a strategic partner with a 20% stake in the asset-management division (sources dated; current level not re-confirmed), and a report links a EUR 10bn AUM target by 2028 to proceeds from selling the Access Capital Partners stake. No league-table rankings or named competitor comparisons were located in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.alantra.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/PR-9M-2025-Financial-Results_EN-1.pdf ; https://www.fundssociety.com/es/?p=300248 ; https://capital-riesgo.es/es/articles/alantra-reorganiza-su-equipo-ejecutivo-para-implementar-su-nueva-estrategia/
thesis.main_shareholders: Per the FY2024 Annual Corporate Governance Report (filed mid-2025; year-end 2024 data): Ricardo Portabella Peralta 18.12% of voting rights, Santiago Eguidazu Mayor 17.63%, José Antonio Abad Zorrilla 7.16%, Jorge Mataix Entero 6.95%, Starr International AG 4.40%; the report also notes Trigo Capital acquired a 3.8% interest in Q1 2025. thesis.insider_ownership: Santiago Eguidazu (founder, Executive Chairman per Alantra's April 2026 press release) is shown with 17.63% of voting rights and Jorge Mataix Entero with 6.95% in the FY2024 governance report; whether these are direct or indirect holdings, and each person's current board role, was not verified in this search. Founder/partner holders together (top four named holders) account for roughly half of the voting rights (sum of the figures above, our arithmetic). Board was ten directors (four independent) per a March 2025 board report; individual director holdings beyond the above were not located. thesis.red_flags: Corporate action (Alantra is the SELLER, not a takeover target): Alantra Investment Managers agreed in March 2026 to sell its c.49% stake in Access Capital Partners to Bankinter Investment for EUR 115.1m; the board put it to the shareholders' meeting of 28 April 2026 as an essential-asset disposal (Art. 160(f) Spanish Companies Act); expected gain about EUR 69m (80% attributable to Alantra Partners); completion expected H2 2026 pending regulatory approvals. A search summary states shareholders approved it; no bid for Alantra itself was found. Other risks: concentrated founder/partner ownership; earnings are cyclical and volatile (FY2025 net profit +186% on a low base); variable compensation provision EUR 65.2m (+49.2%); the disposal removes a recurring-fee asset-management contributor (our inference). thesis.business_description: Lectra SA (Paris, France; Euronext Paris: LSS) provides software, equipment (cutting and related systems) and associated services for industries that process soft materials, mainly fashion and apparel, automotive and furniture, with a growing SaaS offer (e.g. Valia, launched 2024, for production tracking aimed at fashion and luxury). thesis.insider_ownership: Daniel Harari is Chairman and CEO (he chaired the 29 April 2026 AGM) and the founding-family figure; his stake was 17.5% in June 2017 (stale; current percentage and other directors' holdings not located in this search; treat as a research gap). Sources: https://www.lectra.com/en/investors/message-from-daniel-harari ; https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/CNS/2017/06/FCCNS155361_20170614.pdf

thesis.business_description: Helsinki-based business law firm founded in 2004 (aggregators); main offering is continuous legal services for companies (Legal Department Service, 'LDaaS') combined with traditional law-firm work across contracts, corporate, disputes, employment, IPR, M&A, data protection, tax and insolvency; operates in Finland, Sweden, Estonia and Lithuania. Net sales 2025 EUR 23.9m (2024: EUR 25.6m); headcount about 160 (about 180 a year earlier). H1 2026: Q2 net sales EUR 6.4m (+2.9%), Q2 EBIT EUR 0.4m (6.0% margin); LDaaS and other ongoing services were 62% of net sales. The company follows First North marketplace rules (per its governance statement). Sources: https://www.inderes.fi/en/companies/Fondia ; https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/fondia-plcs-annual-report-2025-has-been-published ; https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/fondia-plc-net-sales-increased-and-profitability-improved
thesis.competitive_position: An Inderes note (Dec 2025) calls Fondia the market leader in continuous legal services in Finland (analyst view). Cross-border lawyer collaboration on customer work doubled y/y in H1 2026 per the CEO; first-half sales grew 4.6% in Finland and 28.0% in the Baltics while Sweden fell 3.8%. Outlook for 2026 (growth in net sales and better adjusted EBITDA margin) was unchanged; the content of the August 2026 update to medium-term targets was not read. Named competitors not located; research gap. Sources: https://www.inderes.fi/en/yhtiot/fondia ; https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/fondia-plc-net-sales-increased-and-profitability-improved ; https://mfn.se/all/a/fondia/fondia-updates-its-medium-term-financial-targets-and-strategic-initiatives-d8e49d8c
thesis.main_shareholders: From flagging notices of early 2025 (Inderes ownership page, relayed in a search summary): Sijoittamo Oy about 16.6% of shares and votes (656,250 shares; took over Placereri AB's stake in a merger; linked to CEO Timo Lappi) and Oy Johan Hammarén & Co Ab 16.6% (656,250 shares; took over Hypericus AB's stake, merger registered 31 Jan 2025). A separate notice shows 674,764 shares = 17.07% for the Hammarén holding against 3,953,134 total shares - minor conflict, 16.6% used by Inderes. A complete, current top-10 list was not located (a May 2026 notice only shows Fondia's own treasury holding falling below 5%). Sources: https://www.inderes.fi/en/companies/Fondia/ownership ; https://investors.fondia.com/fi/en/releases-and-publications/releases/fondia-plc-notification-of-holdings-according-to-chapter-9-section-10-of-the-finnish-securities-market-act-johan-hammarn-4982201 ; https://mfn.se/cis/a/fondia/fondia-oyj-arvopaperimarkkinalain-9-luvun-10-ss-mukainen-ilmoitus-omistusosuudesta-fondia-oyj-81ff9dd5
thesis.insider_ownership: Johan Hammarén (board member) holds about 675,000 shares via Oy Johan Hammarén & Co Ab (656,250) and Oy Hammarén & Co Ab (18,514) per the 2026 AGM board-candidate CVs (about 17%); Timo Lappi (CEO) is linked to Sijoittamo Oy's 16.6% stake (link stated in a search summary of the notice); board member Sami Honkonen bought 5,000 shares at about EUR 5.24 on 13 Feb 2026 via SH Ventures Oy. Together the two largest holders (insiders) control roughly one third of the shares (our sum). Other directors' holdings not located. Sources: https://a.storyblok.com/f/101669/x/cddfe6a0c9/proposed-members-to-the-board-of-directors-2026.pdf ; https://www.inderes.fi/releases/fondia-oyj-managers-transactions-sami-honkonensh-ventures-oy ; https://www.inderes.fi/en/companies/Fondia/ownership
thesis.red_flags: Revenue fell about 7% in 2025 (EUR 23.9m vs 25.6m) with a 13% headcount cut in Q3 2025, though H1 2026 shows a return to growth and margin improvement. Listed on First North (lighter disclosure regime than the main market) and about one third of shares held by two insiders, so free float is limited. Professional-services model depends on retaining lawyers. Specific risk disclosures from the annual report and any litigation were not read; no issues identified in the sources seen. Sources: https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/fondia-plcs-annual-report-2025-has-been-published ; https://investors.fondia.com/fi/en/governance/risk-management ; https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/fondia-plc-net-sales-increased-and-profitability-improved
thesis.website: https://investors.fondia.com (investor-relations site seen in results; main corporate site fondia.com referenced there but its exact URL was not directly listed)

name: Litgrid AB
gmSourceUrl: [Nasdaq Baltic LITGRID reports page](https://nasdaqbaltic.com/statistics/en/instrument/LT0000128415/reports), [Litgrid investor relations](https://www.litgrid.eu/index.php/about-us/for-investors/financial-statements/613), [Nasdaq news audited statements announcement](https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b9ae3eb693ec0e646a01cb6a0e132d0d6&lang=en&src=listed)

thesis.business_description: Litgrid AB is Lithuania's electricity transmission system operator, based in Vilnius. It runs the national high-voltage grid (more than 7,000 km of overhead lines, more than 200 transformer substations and 17 interconnectors with other countries) and provides system balancing and ancillary services. Unaudited 2025 revenue was about EUR 431m (+14%), with ancillary-services revenue of EUR 180.2m. Sources: https://www.litgrid.eu/index.php/about-us/for-investors/606 ; https://www.litgrid.eu/index.php/news-events-/news/litgrid-2025-results-operating-more-reliably-in-continental-europe-strengthening-system-resilience-developing-interconnections/36478
thesis.competitive_position: Regulated natural monopoly: it is the sole TSO in Lithuania. It completed synchronisation of the Baltic grid with Continental Europe on 9 February 2025 and is developing the Harmony Link interconnection with Poland, which the Polish government expects to launch in 2030. Litgrid's 2025 investments were close to EUR 188m. Returns depend on regulator decisions; the regulated rate of return was not located in this search. Sources: https://www.litgrid.eu/index.php/news-events-/news/litgrid-2025-results-operating-more-reliably-in-continental-europe-strengthening-system-resilience-developing-interconnections/36478 ; https://www.gov.pl/web/climate/electricity-systems-of-baltic-states-synchronised-ith-the-system-of-continental-europe
thesis.main_shareholders: EPSO-G UAB holds 97.5% and minority shareholders hold the remaining 2.5%, according to the company's investor page. EPSO-G is 100% owned by the Lithuanian Ministry of Energy. The investor page shows no as-of date for the split; it has stayed at that level since EPSO-G received the stake in September 2012. Sources: https://www.litgrid.eu/index.php/about-us/for-investors/606 ; https://governance.lt/en/vvi/litgrid
thesis.red_flags: State-controlled, with a free float of only about 2.5%, so liquidity is very thin and minority holders have little influence. Earnings are volatile because of the balancing and ancillary-services markets: 2025 net profit fell on temporary balancing-market factors, and an aggregator summary (not verified against filings) reports an H1 2025 net loss of EUR 41.9m. Returns are exposed to regulatory decisions, and the heavy capex programme includes Harmony Link. Dividend for 2025 was EUR 0.054/share. Sources: https://www.litgrid.eu/index.php/news-events-/news/litgrid-2025-results-operating-more-reliably-in-continental-europe-strengthening-system-resilience-developing-interconnections/36478 ; https://quartr.com/events/litgrid-ab-lgd1l-q2-2026_FeWxAlg7
thesis.insider_ownership: Litgrid's management page states that board chairman Tomas Varneckas and board members Mindaugas Keizeris and Gediminas Karalius hold no Litgrid shares. No disclosure was found for the independent board members (named by governance.lt as Tim Meyerjürgens and Pierre-Henri D'haene, information as of Dec 2024) or for executives. Effectively no insider ownership; the company is state-controlled. Sources: https://www.litgrid.eu/index.php/about-us/management/601 ; https://governance.lt/en/vvi/litgrid

thesis.business_description: Swedish furniture group focused on public spaces and offices, listed on Nasdaq Stockholm Small Cap. Organised in two business areas, Office Interiors (about two-thirds of net sales) and Library Interiors; comprises twelve subsidiaries and eight brands per Affärsvärlden. The 2025 annual and sustainability report (Swedish only) was published in 2026; its contents were not read. Headquartered in Lammhult, Sweden (Inderes). An older aggregator profile (Investing.com/Zonebourse) lists three divisions including Scandinavian Eyewear and a former name Expanda AB, which conflicts with the current two-division structure and is likely stale; founding year also conflicts (1945 vs 1988). Sources: https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/lammhults-design-group-publicerar-arsredovisning-och-hallbarhetsrapport-for-2025 ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/lammhults-ommoblering-pagar ; https://m.uk.investing.com/equities/lammhults-design-group
thesis.competitive_position: Analyst commentary (Affärsvärlden, not the company) describes a weak market in recent years with hesitant customers, difficulty showing meaningful growth over time, and an average reported EBIT margin of only 0.6% over 2021-2025. Competitors and market shares were not located; research gap. Sources: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/lammhults-nar-lammet-tystnar ; https://placera.se/analys/analys-lonsamheten-sitter-lost-i-lammhults-2025-05-13
thesis.main_shareholders: Affärsvärlden stock page (aggregator, 2026, exact date not stated): Scapa Capital AB 21.2% of capital / 28.9% of votes; Input Interiör 12.2% of capital; Canola 5.5% of capital / 22.3% of votes; followed by Avanza Pension, Spiltan and individuals. Votes for Input Interiör conflict across sources (5.6% in one summary). Simply Wall St shows Input Interiör at 1,029,158 shares (12.2%). Not checked against the company's own shareholder list or annual report. Sources: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/lammhults-design-group ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/commercial-services/lse-0j6w/lammhults-design-group-shares/ownership
thesis.insider_ownership: An older Affärsvärlden analysis attributes the Scapa Capital stake to Anders Hultman and Yngve Conradsson; Peter Conradsson represents Scapa on the board and Simply Wall St separately lists him with 4.55% of shares. Sune Lundqvist is linked to Input Interiör (12.2%). Listed leadership: Per Samuelsson chair, Susanna Hilleskog CEO, while older sources name Daniel Tell as CEO and Peter Conradsson as chair (management/board turnover; dates not confirmed). Insider percentages beyond these were not located. Sources: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/lammhults-ommoblering-pagar ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/commercial-services/lse-0j6w/lammhults-design-group-shares/ownership ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/lammhults-design-group
thesis.red_flags: Dual-class structure: Scapa Capital and Canola together hold roughly 51% of votes (28.9% + 22.3%, our sum from aggregator figures) against about 27% of capital, so control exceeds economic ownership. Very thin profitability (average EBIT margin 0.6% over 2021-2025 per an analyst), weak end-market and leadership changes (Affärsvärlden headline on management reshuffle). No litigation or accounting issues identified; risk sections of the annual report were not read. Sources: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/lammhults-design-group ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/lammhults-nar-lammet-tystnar ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/lammhults-moblerar-om-i-ledningen

name: AS Commercial Industrial Company of Computers and Toys S.A.

thesis.business_description: AS Company S.A. (Athens-listed; legal name AS Commercial Industrial Company of Computers and Toys S.A.) is a Greek manufacturing and trading company whose main activity is toys, based in Thessaloniki and founded in 1990. Its import business runs on licences such as Walt Disney and Warner Bros.; it also expanded into children's clothing retail in northern Greece (older source). Subsidiaries listed in a 2018 presentation include AS Company Cyprus Ltd (100%) and AS Kids Toys S.R.L. in Romania (100%); this may be out of date. Sources: https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/AS-COMMERCIAL-INDUSTRIAL--30325872/ ; https://www.athexgroup.gr/documents/10180/5088474/846_4055_2018_Greek_+English_1.pdf/cb333277-89d6-4063-9081-b9153de0299f
thesis.competitive_position: Small-cap toy distributor/licensee in Greece with a presence in Cyprus and Romania. Reported 2023 group sales EUR 28.7m with EBITDA of EUR 5.95m (stated as 19.16% of sales, which does not reconcile arithmetically with 28.7m; one report also shows EUR 5.5m, so the sources conflict). Market share, competitors and moats were not found in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://athens.euronext.com/en/node/715463 ; https://www.athexgroup.gr/documents/10180/7369390/846_3207_2024_English_2.pdf/a59e748e-d1be-45c8-893b-5c276fa0bf23
thesis.main_shareholders: Could not locate the shareholder register in this search; treat as a research gap. The only ownership datapoint found is a free float of 35.12% from MarketScreener (aggregator), implying roughly two-thirds is held by non-free-float holders whose names were not identified. The 2024 annual financial report on the Athens Exchange site should contain the register. Sources: https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/AS-COMMERCIAL-INDUSTRIAL--30325872/ ; https://www.athexgroup.gr/documents/10180/7369390/846_3207_2024_English_2.pdf/a59e748e-d1be-45c8-893b-5c276fa0bf23
thesis.insider_ownership: Could not locate board/executive holdings in this search; treat as a research gap. A 2024 Naftemporiki article names Stratos Andreadis as an executive of the group, but the snippet does not state his role or shareholding. Source: https://www.naftemporiki.gr/business/2098279/o-epicheirimatias-poy-fovatai-to-iran-alla-kerdizei-tin-ypogennitikotita/
thesis.red_flags: None identified from the sources retrieved, but coverage was thin: no governance, audit-opinion, litigation or leverage information was located, and ownership is opaque (about 65% outside free float with unidentified holders). Conflicting 2023 EBITDA figures noted above. Likely consumer-cyclical and licence-dependence risk (Disney/Warner licences), which should be verified. Source: https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/AS-COMMERCIAL-INDUSTRIAL--30325872/

thesis.business_description: French champagne group (formerly Vranken-Pommery Monopole; renamed Maison Pommery & Associés effective 1 January 2026), listed on Euronext Paris. Champagne is about 92.7% of sales (brands include Vranken, Pommery & Greno and, until its sale, Heidsieck & Co Monopole); the rest is Rozès port/Douro wines and Provence/Camargue rosé wines. 2025 consolidated revenue was EUR 293.2m (-3.6%); H1 2026 revenue was EUR 95.7m, a decline (Zonebourse item via Boursedirect). Headquarters location not confirmed in these results. Sources: https://www.abcbourse.com/analyses/chiffres/POMRYp ; https://www.boursedirect.fr/fr/actualites/categorie/chiffre-d-affaires/maison-pommery-une-activite-2025-en-leger-retrait-boursier-38fc547ac38c5b27322c6419aeccc7fe89e4bb3b ; https://www.vrankenpommery.com/finance/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Assemblée-Générale-VPM-24-novembre-2025-11.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: One financial profile (abcbourse, aggregator) calls it the world's No. 2 champagne producer and marketer; no independent confirmation was found. In 2025 its champagne volumes rose 3.6% while sector shipments fell 2.2% (company release summarised by Boursedirect). Strategy has shifted to balance-sheet repair and portfolio pruning: agreed sale of Heidsieck & Co Monopole to Lanson-BCC for about EUR 50m (per a Nov 2025 shareholder-meeting presentation; closing not confirmed in these results), a new licensed brand (Maison Pompadour), and exclusive talks with Henkell Freixenet over a majority stake that ended on 31 July 2026 without agreement, with both sides open to resuming later. Sources: https://www.abcbourse.com/analyses/chiffres/POMRYp ; https://www.boursedirect.fr/fr/actualites/categorie/chiffre-d-affaires/maison-pommery-une-activite-2025-en-leger-retrait-boursier-38fc547ac38c5b27322c6419aeccc7fe89e4bb3b ; https://drinks-intel.com/wine/henkell-freixenet-maison-pommery-associes-talks-end-without-agreement/ ; https://www.lalibre.be/economie/entreprises-startup/2025/09/25/vranken-pommery-vend-heidsieck-co-a-lanson-bcc-YYPTV3DRD5CRDILYAQOSA74EL4/
thesis.main_shareholders: Could not locate current shareholder percentages in this search; treat as a research gap. Press reports (Boursorama/Test-Achats summaries) say the Vranken family keeps control after the Henkell talks failed, but no percentages were found. The 2025 Universal Registration Document (which would hold the shareholder table) and the AGM were postponed in April 2026; publication status not confirmed. Stale share data: 8,937,085 shares and 15,431,234 gross voting rights at 31 Dec 2022, implying widespread double voting rights. Sources: https://www.test-achats.be/invest/investir/actions/articles/2026/08/pommery-vranken-dette-champagne ; https://live.euronext.com/en/listview/company-press-release/072583?page=0 ; https://www.vrankenpommery.com/finance/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/URD-VPM-2022_UK.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: Family-controlled: a Euronext release of April 2026 announced the appointment of Nathalie Vranken as Chairwoman and CEO. Her and other directors' holdings (and those of family holding entities) could not be located in this search; research gap. Source: https://live.euronext.com/fr/listview/company-press-release/072583
thesis.red_flags: KNOWN EVENT (checked): exclusive talks with Henkell International (from June 2026) for a majority stake expired 31 July 2026 without agreement, announced 5 Aug 2026; the door was left open. HEAVY LEVERAGE: net financial debt EUR 754.4m at end-2025 (one source) versus about EUR 716m at 30 June 2026 and EUR 775.9m a year earlier (half-year results per a search summary) - figures differ by date and source; debt is about 2.4-2.6x annual revenue (our arithmetic). A conciliation protocol approved by the Reims Commercial Court covers the group and nine subsidiaries, securing financing to 19 June 2027 (possible extension to June 2028), with EUR 42.8m of new money from early Sept 2026 carrying a conciliation privilege and guarantees over vineyard assets; covenants cap shareholder payments at EUR 10.8m until it is repaid and require minimum consolidated cash of EUR 2m. The group is considering non-strategic asset sales (reports cite about EUR 200m of deleveraging; the screen's ~EUR 100m asset-sale figure and the EUR 200m were not verified in the company's own release). Also: 2025 URD and AGM postponed (April 2026); H1 2026 net loss widened with the Heidsieck disposal (headline only); revenue declining. Sources: https://www.boursorama.com/bourse/actualites/champagne-maison-pommery-n-a-pas-trouve-d-accord-avec-l-allemand-henkell-mais-s-est-refinance-c34ac9c7a717b7bf0798214397c6ca0a ; https://www.maisonpommery.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Communique-05082026-FR.pdf ; https://www.test-achats.be/invest/investir/actions/articles/2026/08/pommery-vranken-dette-champagne ; https://www.tradingsat.com/maison-pommery-amp-associes-ex-vranken-pommery-FR0000062796/actualites/maison-pommery-amp-associes-ex-vranken-pommery-perte-nette-creusee-au-1er-semestre-pour-pommery-avec-la-cession-de-heidsieck-1169744.html

thesis.business_description: Warsaw-based residential developer (registered office Grochowska 306/308, Warsaw; founded 2003 per an aggregator) listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange. It develops and sells apartments, multi-family and single-family houses and service buildings, mainly in Warsaw (notably the Gocław area) and also other cities such as Kraków; TradingView describes two segments: construction services for external investors, and sales of apartments, houses and commercial premises. 2025 standalone sales revenue PLN 47.557m versus PLN 53.967m in 2024 (about -11.9%, our arithmetic, from the selected-data table). Aggregators list about 10 employees and 12,386,687 shares; market-cap estimates conflict (PLN 62.6m to 80.2m). Sources: https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art44225331-ed-invest-spolka-akcyjna-rr-2025-formularz-dla-raportow-rocznych ; https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/PL:EDI ; https://simplywall.st/stock/wse/edi ; https://www.tradingview.com/symbols/GPW-EDI/minds
thesis.competitive_position: Small, thinly staffed Warsaw developer; no market-share data, competitor comparison or project pipeline for 2025/26 was located in this search (the 2025 board report text was not retrieved); research gap. A board shareholder letter calls 2025 standalone and consolidated results 'satisfactory' (paywalled; remainder not read). Sources: https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/147421,list-do-akcjonariuszy-grupy-ed-invest-2025 ; https://simplywall.st/stock/wse/edi
thesis.main_shareholders: Bankier shareholder table: Vesper Capital sp. z o.o. acting together with Q Investments, Maciej Krzewiński, Łukasz Deńca, Maciej Fryda and Artur Neumann holds 8,955,839 shares = 72.30% of shares (change dated 18 Sep 2024); ED Invest SA itself holds 2,458,395 own shares (about 19.84% of capital, no votes; as of 22 May 2024). At the Feb 2023 EGM Vesper alone had 90.38% of votes; 72.30% of capital is roughly 90% of voting rights once treasury shares are excluded (our arithmetic). A 2025/2026 shareholder list was not located, so these figures may be stale. Sources: https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/new-connect/EDINVEST/akcjonariat ; https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art38037971-ed-invest-s-a-akcjonariusze-dysponujacy-nie-mniej-niz-5-glosow-na-nwza-ed-invest-s-a
thesis.insider_ownership: Management is part of the controlling group: Łukasz Deńca is named among the Vesper Capital concert group and, with Alan Dunikowski, was a vice-president of the management board per Feb 2023 filings (Simply Wall St instead lists Deńca as CEO - role conflict, current board composition not verified). Individual percentages for each person were not located; research gap. Sources: https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/new-connect/EDINVEST/akcjonariat ; https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art37990551-ed-invest-s-a-otrzymanie-zawiadomienia-o-zmianie-udzialu-w-ogolnej-liczbie-glosow-spolki ; https://simplywall.st/stock/wse/edi
thesis.red_flags: Control concentration: the Vesper-led group holds about 72% of capital (about 90% of votes) and the company holds about 20% as treasury shares, so free float is very small and liquidity thin. History of change of control: preliminary agreements of 1 Sep 2022 to acquire over 50% of shares, a mandatory tender offer closing 12 Feb 2023 and a supervisory-board recall at the 28 Feb 2023 EGM. Revenue declined in 2025 and the company is very small (about 10 employees per an aggregator). Debt, bond and covenant details for 2025 were not located; research gap. No litigation or accounting concerns identified in sources seen. Sources: https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art38036791-ed-invest-s-a-odwolanie-rady-nadzorczej-ed-invest-sa ; https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art37948591-ed-invest-s-a-wyniki-wezwania-do-zapisywania-sie-na-sprzedaz-akcji-ed-invest-s-a ; https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/new-connect/EDINVEST/akcjonariat

thesis.business_description: Stendörren Fastigheter manages, develops and acquires properties and building rights in logistics, warehouse and light industry, primarily in Greater Stockholm, Västerås and the Mälardalen region, with acquisitions also in Finland. FY2025: rental income SEK 1,042m (+16%), net operating income SEK 841m (+17%), profit for the year SEK 173m (SEK 327m in 2025's prior year). In Q4 2025 it completed several warehouse/light-industrial acquisitions in Sweden and Finland totalling about SEK 620m property value. Head-office location was not stated in the results retrieved. Source: https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/year-end-report-2025-stendorren-fastigheter-ab-publ
thesis.competitive_position: Niche Nordic logistics/light-industrial landlord focused on Stockholm-area and Mälardalen; the 2025 expansion into Finland (the earlier-screen finding of a Helsinki warehouse/light-industrial portfolio acquisition with closing expected 20 Feb 2026 is consistent with the Q4 2025 Sweden/Finland acquisitions, but the specific deal was not independently re-verified in this search) signals a widening geographic strategy. Peer comparison, vacancy, portfolio size and leverage were not retrieved in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/year-end-report-2025-stendorren-fastigheter-ab-publ ; https://eqtgroup.com/current-portfolio/stendoerren
thesis.main_shareholders: Controlled by EQT through Stendörren Real Estate AB, a stake dating from EQT Real Estate II's cash offer announced 27 Nov 2018 (after the extended acceptance period 40.67% of shares and 58.14% of votes). Recent figures differ by source and date: Affärsvärlden (undated, shows July 2026 reports) lists Stendörren Real Estate AB 37.7% of capital / 54.9% of votes, Altira AB 10.3% / 14.3%, SEB Investment Management 12.4%, Fjärde AP-fonden 7.8%; Simply Wall St (aggregator, undated) lists Stendorren Real Estate AB ~37%, SEB IM ~12.6%, Altira ~11.1%, Länsförsäkringar Fondförvaltning ~8.2%; Placera (Jul 2025) cited EQT 38.8% / 56.1%. Treat exact percentages as indicative; the company's own latest ownership table was not located. thesis.insider_ownership: Altira AB (founded by Carl Mörk and Oscar Christensson per Realtid) is the second-largest holder at roughly 10-11% of capital and 14.3-14.6% of votes. An insider notification shows Altira, linked to board member Carl Mörk, bought 130,000 shares at SEK 174.69 on 23 Mar 2026. Individual holdings of other board members and executives were not located in this search; treat as a research gap. thesis.red_flags: Controlling shareholder: EQT holds about 38-41% of capital but 55-58% of votes via a dual-class structure, so minorities have limited influence. Known-event check: an earlier-screen Realtid mention of an EQT bid corresponds to EQT Real Estate II's 2018-19 offer (confirmed by Vinge and NCR sources), not a current bid; no 2026 takeover bid was found. Profit for the year fell to SEK 173m from SEK 327m (cause not examined). Stendörren is also an acquirer of a Helsinki portfolio (closing expected 20 Feb 2026, per earlier screen).
