thesis.business_description: Upsales Technology is a Nordic B2B SaaS company; its platform combines CRM, marketing automation, customer support, subscription management, project management and business intelligence, with AI features. It serves more than 1,000 customers, mainly in the Nordic mid-market, and describes itself as profitable and cash-generating. Headquarters location not stated in the results retrieved. Source: https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/upsales-technology-ab-publ-board-of-directors-proposes-distribution-and-separate-listing-of-ai-company-aira
thesis.competitive_position: Mid-market Nordic CRM/sales-and-marketing SaaS with an integrated suite; Affärsvärlden commentary frames growth as soft and sales execution as the key issue (headlines only: 'Mycket hänger på att försäljningen tar fart', 'Upsales behöver säljstöd'). Market share and competitor data not retrieved. Strategy event: the AI subsidiary Aira (AI Revenue Assistant Software Stockholm AB; pre-revenue, EUR 149 per user per month, built on licensed credit/company data on 30m+ European companies) was distributed one-for-one to Upsales shareholders after AGM approval on 15 May 2026 and began trading on Nasdaq First North Growth Market on 3 June 2026 (ticker AIRA), so Upsales is now a pure-play core SaaS business. Sources: https://www.upsales.com/investor-relations/press-releases/2026/upsales-technology-ab-publ-publishes-an-information-brochure-regarding-the-proposed-distribution-of-shares-in-aira/ ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/upsales-upp-till-bevis
thesis.main_shareholders: Founder Daniel Wikberg is the largest holder: Simply Wall St (aggregator, undated) shows 7,370,493 shares or 43.8%; earlier company disclosures put him at about 49% after a Dec 2022 sale and about 42% after a Feb 2023 placement. Upsales announced he intends to sell part of his holding via accelerated bookbuilding when he hands over the CEO role (outcome not found), so the figure may be lower now. Institutional buyers have been announced in company press releases (names not retrieved). Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/software/sto-upsale/upsales-technology-shares/ownership ; https://www.upsales.com/investor-relations/press-releases/2023/increased-institutional-ownership-in-upsales/ ; https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/upsales-technology-ab-johan-kallblad-appointed-new-ceo-of-upsales
thesis.insider_ownership: Daniel Wikberg (founder, CEO until 31 July 2026, then remaining on the board) held about 43.8% per aggregator data; stated intention to sell part of it with a lock-up on the retained shares. Other board/management holdings not located; treat as a research gap. Source: https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/upsales-technology-ab-johan-kallblad-appointed-new-ceo-of-upsales ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/software/sto-upsale/upsales-technology-shares/ownership
thesis.red_flags: Founder-CEO succession (Johan Kallblad CEO from 31 July 2026) combined with the founder planning to sell part of his roughly 44% stake creates overhang and key-person risk. Aira distribution (completed June 2026) means historical share price and financials are not like-for-like, and Aira is pre-revenue. Controlling-holder concentration until the placement completes. Known-event check: the Aira distribution is confirmed by company releases. No litigation or accounting issues found. Source: https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/upsales-technology-ab-johan-kallblad-appointed-new-ceo-of-upsales ; https://www.upsales.com/investor-relations/press-releases/2026/upsales-technology-ab-publ-publishes-an-information-brochure-regarding-the-proposed-distribution-of-shares-in-aira/

thesis.business_description: Hypothekarbank Lenzburg AG (HBL) is an independent Swiss bank, an independent stock corporation since its founding in 1868 with no group affiliation, listed on SIX Swiss Exchange. The group at 31 Dec 2025 comprised the parent and Swiss Bankers Prepaid Services AG; subsidiary HBL Finanz AG holds 9.9% of Sutor Bank GmbH (Hamburg), a strategic partnership in IT and banking-as-a-service. Share capital is 72,000 registered shares of CHF 260 nominal. Product and geographic detail was not retrieved beyond this. Sources: https://www.hbl.ch/media/apsbqc5y/2025_corporate_governance.pdf ; https://hbl.ch/media/30kndhtz/2024_corporate_governance.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: Small, independent Swiss regional bank pursuing a digital/banking-as-a-service angle (Sutor Bank stake; Swiss Bankers Prepaid Services acquisition completed 2024; participation in Swiss Immo Lab AG). Market cap CHF 290.9m at end-2024 (CHF 4,040/share). 2025 profit was slightly lower than 2024 per a swissinfo headline; 2024 dividend CHF 120/share. Market-share and peer data not retrieved; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://hbl.ch/media/30kndhtz/2024_corporate_governance.pdf ; https://www.swissinfo.ch/ger/hypothekarbank-lenzburg-macht-2025-leicht-weniger-gewinn/90899682 ; https://www.moneycab.com/finanz/hypothekarbank-lenzburg-verdient-2024-etwas-weniger/amp/
thesis.main_shareholders: Could not retrieve the 2025 shareholder section (excerpts cut off before it); treat as a research gap. The 2021 corporate governance report stated the shares are widely distributed and no holder reaches 3%; this may be stale. Full detail should be in the Corporate Governance section of the 2025 annual report. Sources: https://hpm.hbl.ch/media/astfyvaa/2021_corporate_governance.pdf ; https://www.hbl.ch/media/apsbqc5y/2025_corporate_governance.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: Could not locate board/executive share holdings in this search; treat as a research gap. Marianne Wildi is named as chair of the Board of Directors in the 2026 AGM invitation (previous chair per 2023 report: Gerhard Hanhart); her shareholding was not found. Source: https://www.hbl.ch/media/13qnje5j/einladung-zur-generalversammlung-2026_web.pdf
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources retrieved, but the 2025 shareholder and governance sections were not read. Known-event check: the 9.9% Sutor Bank stake is described in the 2024 annual report (earlier screen said bought Jan 2025, so the date is slightly inconsistent; stake is held via HBL Finanz AG); no bid for the bank found. Strategic dependence on a single banking-as-a-service partner and a modest 2025 profit decline are points to watch. Standard bank caveats (rate sensitivity, mortgage concentration) apply but were not quantified. Sources: https://hbl.ch/media/30kndhtz/2024_corporate_governance.pdf ; https://www.swissinfo.ch/ger/hypothekarbank-lenzburg-macht-2025-leicht-weniger-gewinn/90899682

thesis.business_description: Auto Hrvatska d.d. (Zagreb, Heinzelova 70; Zagreb Stock Exchange) is a motor-vehicle dealer group tracing its origins to 1952; via about 12 companies at 26 locations in Croatia, Slovenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and North Macedonia it sells new and used passenger/commercial vehicles and provides service, parts and rental. Brands mentioned include Volkswagen (60-year relationship), Peugeot and BYD (Zagreb and a Split centre opened Nov 2025). Consolidated 2025 net profit was about EUR 12.8m (Lider report). A Companywall revenue figure of EUR 33.6m for a Zagreb entity is not the consolidated figure and conflicts in scale; consolidated revenue was not located. Sources: https://www.amcham.hr/en/members/auto-hrvatska-dd ; https://en.lider.media/?p=218225 ; https://www.companywall.hr/tvrtka/auto-hrvatska-dd/MMxi1pCD
thesis.competitive_position: A large multi-brand importer/dealer in the Croatian car market (about 70 thousand passenger cars registered in 2025, +8.35%, per Novi list), with a regional footprint and expansion into Chinese brands (BYD). Market share and named competitors were not found in this search (research gap). The company pays a large dividend relative to its size: EUR 9.00 per share (about EUR 5.1m total) approved at the AGM of 23 Apr 2026, paid from prior-year retained earnings, while 2025 profit was retained. Sources: https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/AUHR/COI-AUHR-e1a816c5fcc05827a28daf1f0789883b.pdf ; https://www.novilist.hr/?p=1611502
thesis.main_shareholders: Aggregator data (Fininfo citing SKDD; Companywall), undated: Bogdan Tihava 22.20%; Igor Brigljevic 7.33%; Zlatan Jabucar 6.26%; the company's own treasury stake about 4.77% (Fininfo) and, per a ZSE filing, 28,364 own shares = 4.73% as of 1 Jun 2026. Companywall shows the Tihava and Brigljevic stakes via Zagrebacka banka custody and 'other' at 39.49%. These are not confirmed against the 2025 annual report or current SKDD register; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.fininfo.hr/Poduzece/auto-hrvatska/Detaljno/73 ; https://www.companywall.hr/tvrtka/auto-hrvatska-dd/MMxi1pCD ; https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/AUHR/COI-AUHR-d8d160d448f16e98506d6fc08de1e8e7.pdf
thesis.red_flags: Concentrated, insider-dominated ownership (top three holders about 36% if data are current; combined with 4.7% treasury shares) and a small share count, implying thin liquidity and key-person risk; ownership and board data are undated aggregator figures. Franchise dependence on a few OEM importer/dealer agreements (VW, Peugeot, BYD) and a cyclical car market. Share count/capital data are inconsistent across sources (an old prospectus shows 17,885 shares; treasury math implies roughly 600 thousand shares today), so per-share data need checking. A same-named but unrelated company exists in Split. No litigation or audit issues were found, but the 2025 audit report was not read in this search. Sources: https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/AUHR/FI-AUHR-fdafe334857f4ab8b02143eaec446d9b.pdf ; https://www.companywall.hr/tvrtka/auto-hrvatska-dd/MMxzog3q
thesis.website: https://www.autohrvatska.hr (reported by a search-tool summary of an AmCham listing; not independently opened).
thesis.insider_ownership: If the Fininfo/SKDD data are current, insiders are the largest holders: Bogdan Tihava (22.20%, listed as board chair), Igor Brigljevic (7.33%, deputy chair). Roles conflict between sources (a 2020 ZSE notice shows Tihava signing as chief executive and Brigljevic as board chair), so verify. Executive directors per Fininfo: Alen Vuksan-Cusa (CEO), Ante Belamaric, Mario Fabek, Marko Tihava (relationship to Bogdan Tihava not verified); their holdings were not found. Treasury shares add about 4.7% held by the company. Sources: https://www.fininfo.hr/Poduzece/auto-hrvatska/Detaljno/73 ; https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/AUHR/GS-AUHR-e4568b7d6ed2c93543e2bcbe05bed889.pdf

thesis.business_description: Valamar Riviera d.d. is a Croatian tourism company operating hotels, resorts and campsites on the Adriatic coast (growth reported in Rab, Makarska, Krk and Istria; it has also announced expansion into Austria). FY2025: business revenues about EUR 461m (+10.6%) and EBITDA EUR 132m (+9.1%) per a Lider press report, with a EUR 304m investment cycle in the managed portfolio; an aggregator citing the annual report filed 26 Feb 2026 shows revenue EUR 455.26m and net income EUR 55.09m. The figures conflict and an earlier 9M adjusted EBITDA (EUR 165.2m) exceeds the quoted full-year EBITDA, so definitions differ; verify against the audited annual report. Sources: https://en.lider.media/2026/02/26/valamar-and-maistra-achieved-strong-growth-in-2025/ ; https://quartr.com/events/valamar-riviera-rivp-q3-2025_FVI9egmZ ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/hr/consumer-services/zgse-rivp/valamar-riviera-dd-shares/news/valamar-riviera-dd-reports-first-quarter-2025-earnings
thesis.competitive_position: One of the larger listed tourism operators in Croatia, with a strategy to 2030 approved by the Supervisory Board on 26 Feb 2026 (investment plan about EUR 820m; 2030 EBITDA target of EUR 220-240m per reports). Strong 9M 2025 growth (revenue +10.5% to EUR 433.4m; net debt EUR 268.8m at September 2025). Independent market-share data and named competitors (e.g. Maistra, Arena Hospitality) were not located in this search; treat as a research gap. A dividend of EUR 0.27 per share was approved. Sources: https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/RIVP/COI-RIVP-06da618c9bc642e8dca6e20dc5b1d3ba.pdf ; https://quartr.com/events/valamar-riviera-rivp-q3-2025_FVI9egmZ ; https://en.hrturizam.hr/Valamar-confirms-dividend-payment-of-EUR-027-per-share
thesis.main_shareholders: Aggregator only (Simply Wall St, undated; a January 2025 article shows the same split): Wurmböck Beteiligungs GmbH about 20.4% and Goldscheider Keramik Gesellschaft m.b.H. about 20.4%, Satis d.o.o. about 5.4%; top 22 holders about 57.6%; private companies 48.4%, public 42.4%, institutions 7.9%. A 2021 analysis showed 21% each (small drift), and 2016 coverage with a different structure (Epic 44.1%) is obsolete. The company also holds treasury shares (3.28% as of Feb 2020, now stale). Official ZSE shareholder register not retrieved; treat as unverified. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/hr/consumer-services/zgse-rivp/valamar-riviera-dd-shares/ownership ; https://seenews.com/news/croatian-hotel-operator-valamar-increases-own-shareholding-to-153-613281
thesis.red_flags: No dominant holder: two foreign holding vehicles each hold about 20%, so a change of control or block sale is a possible overhang (aggregator figures). Highly seasonal, capex-heavy business with net debt EUR 268.8m at Sept 2025 and a EUR 820m investment plan to 2030, exposing it to leverage and execution risk; heavy dependence on Croatian tourism, labour availability and cost inflation. Conflicting FY2025 revenue/EBITDA figures between sources noted above. No litigation or accounting issues were identified in the sources reviewed. Sources: https://quartr.com/events/valamar-riviera-rivp-q3-2025_FVI9egmZ ; https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/RIVP/COI-RIVP-06da618c9bc642e8dca6e20dc5b1d3ba.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: Individual insiders hold only about 0.175% in aggregate per Simply Wall St (aggregator). Management Board member Marko Cizmek was reported to hold 111,035 shares (older item, date not confirmed). Holdings of the other Management and Supervisory Board members could not be located in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/hr/consumer-services/zgse-rivp/valamar-riviera-dd-shares/ownership ; https://en.lider.media/?p=119265

thesis.business_description: Enervit S.p.A. is a Borsa Italiana-listed Italian nutrition and supplements company (the Milano Finanza coverage refers to its 'integratori'). Q1 2026 revenue was EUR 22.2m (+2.4% year on year). Detailed segment, brands, headquarters and full-year figures were not retrieved in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2026-05/20260512_183861.pdf ; https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/blindati-gli-integratori-enervit-2685493
thesis.competitive_position: Could not retrieve market-position, competitor or moat information in this search; treat as a research gap. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enervit
thesis.main_shareholders: Per CONSOB (Enervit shareholder page and the 14 Nov 2025 pact notice): Sorbini family pact holding about 50.3% combined (Giuseppe Sorbini via Malmoria Srl ~17.74%, Alberto Sorbini via Amrast Srl ~17.74%, Maurizia Sorbini via M2PA Srl ~14.78%); Duke Investment Srl (linked to Nerio Alessandri, Technogym) about 31.09%, from a CONSOB page dated October 2024. It is unclear whether percentages are of capital or voting rights, so treat as indicative. Pact signed 12 Nov 2025, runs to Nov 2028, replacing a 2023 pact. Implied free float is under 20%. Sources: https://www.consob.it/web/consob-and-its-activities/w/enervit-spa-azionariato-1 ; https://www.emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2025-11/20251114_174434.pdf ; https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/blindati-gli-integratori-enervit-2685493
thesis.insider_ownership: The three Sorbini family members hold about 50.3% through holding companies (see above), bound by a voting-consultation pact with a single slate for board and auditors. Whether each holds a board or executive role was not confirmed in this search. Sources: https://www.emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2025-11/20251114_174434.pdf ; https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/blindati-gli-integratori-enervit-2685493
thesis.red_flags: Control is locked by the Sorbini pact (about 50.3%, effect described as jointly exercising dominant influence) plus Duke Investment at about 31%, leaving a small free float and limited minority influence. The pact commits to distributing 20-50% of profits as dividends per Milano Finanza. No tender offer or Duke stake sale was found in 2026 results. No accounting or litigation issues located, but sources were limited. Sources: https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/blindati-gli-integratori-enervit-2685493 ; https://www.emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2025-11/20251114_174434.pdf

thesis.business_description: BTS Group AB is a Stockholm-based professional services firm founded in 1986. It helps corporate clients with strategy execution, business acumen, leadership development, coaching, assessments, sales transformation and digital learning services, with business simulations as its original core tool. 2025 net sales were MSEK 2,703 (2024: 2,802) and EBITA was MSEK 274 (10.2% margin); North America is a key market. Sources: https://ir.bts.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bts-group-ab-publ-year-end-report-january-december-2025 ; https://craft.co/btsgroup
thesis.competitive_position: A niche global player in experiential/simulation-based corporate learning and strategy implementation, with roughly 1,100+ professionals in about 36 offices according to non-official profiles (headcount figures conflict across sources). It has grown through a long series of bolt-on acquisitions (e.g. Strategic Management Group 2005, Wizer 2013, Fenestra 2014, AVO Vision 2015, Boda 2023), often with earn-out structures. Named competitors were not found in this search. Sources: https://craft.co/btsgroup ; https://ir.bts.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bts-group-ab-publ-interim-report-january-june-2026
thesis.main_shareholders: Founder and chairman Henrik Ekelund is the largest holder: Affärsvärlden lists 20.3% of capital / 41.7% of votes (A shares carry more votes), followed by Stefan af Petersens (11.6% / 9.6%) and Lannebo Kapitalförvaltning (9.3% / 6.6%). Inderes (Millistream data) shows Ekelund at 18.9% / 40.4% and af Petersens at 11.7% / 9.9%. These are aggregator figures with differing, unstated as-of dates, so verify them against the BTS annual report or Euroclear shareholder list. Sources: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/bts-group ; https://inderes.dk/en/companies/BTS-Group/ownership
thesis.red_flags: Dual-class shares give the founder outsized voting control (about 41% of votes on about 20% of capital). Earnings were weak in 2025: EBITA fell 25%, organic growth was -1% for the year and -5% in Q4, and a profit warning in August 2025 was tied to North American weakness. Earn-out volatility is recurring: a higher Boda earn-out provision hit Q2 2026 net financial items by MSEK 52, pushing Q2 profit after tax to MSEK -1, and 2024 profit had been inflated by reversed earn-outs. Positive: 2026 EBITA guidance was raised to 'significantly better' than 2025. Sources: https://ir.bts.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bts-group-ab-publ-year-end-report-january-december-2025 ; https://ir.bts.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bts-group-ab-publ-interim-report-january-june-2026
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder Henrik Ekelund (Chairman, re-elected at the 2025 AGM; also on the compensation and nomination committees) holds about 19-20% of capital and about 40-42% of votes per aggregators. Co-founder Stefan af Petersens holds about 11.6-11.7% of capital. Holdings of the CEO and other board members were not located in this search. Sources: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/bts-group ; https://www.inderes.dk/releases/bulletin-from-bts-group-abs-annual-general-meeting-5

thesis.business_description: Martifer SGPS is a Portuguese holding company with three segments: metallic constructions (steel structures, aluminium and glass facades, industrial maintenance, oil and gas infrastructure; projects cited include the Oriente building in Lisbon, Old Oak Common station in London and the Manchester airport extension), naval industry (West Sea shipyard, Viana do Castelo) and renewables (over 1.5 GW of wind and solar developed/built). Head office is in Oliveira de Frades per a summarised source. Sources: https://www.martifer.com/en/investors/main-indicators ; https://quartr.com/companies/martifer-sgps-s-a_17612
thesis.competitive_position: Engineering/construction group with an order book of EUR 448m at end-2025 (snippet did not specify segment). H1 2025 profit EUR 7.8m (-33%), EBITDA EUR 16.3m. Competitor and share data not retrieved. Strategy is now driven by its controlling bloc (Visabeira, I'M SGPS, Mota-Engil) rather than the market. Sources: https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/economia/lucro-da-martifer-recua-33-no-1o-semestre-para-78-milhoes-de-euros_n1678581 ; https://www.martifer.com/en/investors/main-indicators
thesis.main_shareholders: A concerted block of Visabeira, I'M SGPS and Mota-Engil held 85,827,065 shares after the offer, i.e. 85.83% of capital and 87.77% of voting rights (ECO, 5 Jun 2026). Before the offer, after Visabeira bought 18% (27 Apr 2026 per press; the earlier screen says 24 Apr, a minor date conflict): Mota-Engil 37.50%, I'M 25.09%, Visabeira 23%. Free float is now roughly 14%. Sources: https://eco.sapo.pt/2026/06/05/visabeira-falha-opa-sobre-a-martifer-ao-captar-poucas-acoes-junto-dos-pequenos-investidores/ ; https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/economia/visabeira-falha-meta-e-compra-apenas-024-da-martifer-em-opa_n1745478
thesis.insider_ownership: Individual director/executive holdings not located in this search; treat as a research gap. Control sits with corporate holders (Mota-Engil, Visabeira, I'M SGPS) under a shareholder agreement.
thesis.red_flags: Takeover-in-progress/control event: Visabeira's mandatory offer at EUR 2.057 per share (6-month VWAP) ran 18 May to 3 Jun 2026; only 239,263 shares (0.24% of capital) were tendered out of 14.4m targeted (14.41% of capital; Sábado cites 14.74%), so the 90% squeeze-out threshold was missed. The bidder may call a general meeting to approve voluntary delisting, a liquidity and minority-holder risk. The offer price was a formula minimum, not a premium. Sources: https://eco.sapo.pt/2026/06/05/visabeira-falha-opa-sobre-a-martifer-ao-captar-poucas-acoes-junto-dos-pequenos-investidores/ ; https://www.sabado.pt/dinheiro/amp/opa-sobre-a-martifer-falha-meta-dos-90 ; https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/economia/visabeira-falha-meta-e-compra-apenas-024-da-martifer-em-opa_n1745478

thesis.business_description: Føroya Banki (formerly BankNordik) is a Faroe Islands-based bank listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen and supervised by the Danish FSA. FY2025 net profit DKK 288m; the board intends to propose a dividend of DKK 202m (DKK 21.04 per share, 70% of net profit); CEO is Turið F. Arge. Segment and Danish-market detail not retrieved. Sources: https://www.inderes.dk/releases/solid-performance-in-2025 ; https://www.avanza.se/placera/pressmeddelanden/2019/03/22/banknordik-major-shareholder-announcement-pf-tjaldur.html
thesis.competitive_position: Leading Faroese bank by name and listing, with year-end 2025 equity of about DKK 2.0bn (stockanalysis.com, aggregator, DKK 2,015m vs DKK 2,076m in 2024). Market share, competitors and strategy were not retrieved in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://stockanalysis.com/quote/cph/FOBANK/financials/balance-sheet/ ; https://www.inderes.dk/releases/solid-performance-in-2025

thesis.business_description: Belgian regulated real estate company listed on Euronext Brussels that owns out-of-town retail properties (retail parks and similar assets in easily accessible catchment areas) in Belgium, France and Spain. A search summary of company news put the portfolio at roughly 455,000 m2 and about EUR 770m fair value as of 31 March 2026, with a Belgian press article citing a country mix of about 54% Belgium, 42% France, 4% Spain (undated; verify against the company's reports). Headquarters not confirmed in this search. Sources: https://www.bolero.be/nl/analyse-en-inzicht/blog/ascencio-breidt-portefeuille-uit-met-franse-overname-maar-2025-resultaten-temperen-de-winstbijdrage ; https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-06/68727842-ascencio-sa-ascencio-continues-its-growth-with-the-acquisition-of-espace-shopping-hydrion-in-arlon-belgium-the-launch-of-a-capital-increase-via-399.htm
thesis.competitive_position: Niche listed owner of retail parks across Belgium/France/Spain; growth is acquisition-led. In June 2026 it bought 100% of Arlimmo SA, owner of the Espace Shopping Hydrion retail park in Arlon (about 33,000 m2, around 40 tenants, 100% occupancy, roughly EUR 4.5m annual rent), financed in part by a EUR 15m accelerated bookbuilding at EUR 48.2/share and a EUR 32.9m bond at 4.80% (EUR 13.9m 4-year and EUR 19.0m 5-year tranches). Named competitors and quantified market share could not be located in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-06/68727842-ascencio-sa-ascencio-continues-its-growth-with-the-acquisition-of-espace-shopping-hydrion-in-arlon-belgium-the-launch-of-a-capital-increase-via-399.htm ; https://www.ideal-investisseur.fr/en/actions-b/ascencio-completes-a-eur32-9-million-bond-issue-at-4-80-to-finance-arlimmo/22735.html
thesis.main_shareholders: Per the company's accelerated-bookbuilding press release (June 2026 transaction; exact date of the percentages not confirmed), Carl Mestdagh (founder), Patronale Life SA and Belfius Insurance SA hold directly/indirectly about 6.4%, 5.3% and 3.7% respectively. An FSMA transparency overview dated 24/04/2025 shows Patronale Life at 5.00% (330,000 voting rights on a denominator of 6,595,985), so figures differ by date; a 2022 notification put Mestdagh-linked holders at about 10.38% (older, likely stale). A market-data aggregator (MarketScreener) shows a free float of 83.25%, undated and aggregator-only. A current full register was not located. Sources: https://www.trivano.com/persbericht/ascencio-continues-its-growth-with-the-acquisition-of-espace-shopping-hydrion-in-arlon-belgium-the-launch-of-a-capital-increase-via-accelerated-bookbuilding-736707.html ; https://www.fsma.be/sites/default/files/issuers/files/0881334476_en.pdf ; https://uk.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ASCENCIO-SA-111964950/
thesis.insider_ownership: Carl Mestdagh (founder) holds about 6.4% directly/indirectly per the bookbuilding release (the same release says he, Patronale Life and Belfius fully support the deal). A June 2026 general meeting of Ascencio Management SA (statutory manager) was reported to have renewed eight directors including Carl Mestdagh, with Serge Fautre (vice-chair) and Alexandra Leunen leaving and Stephane Schebat and Cedric Biquet appointed. Holdings of other directors and executives, and who currently chairs the board, were not located; research gap. Sources: https://www.trivano.com/persbericht/ascencio-continues-its-growth-with-the-acquisition-of-espace-shopping-hydrion-in-arlon-belgium-the-launch-of-a-capital-increase-via-accelerated-bookbuilding-736707.html ; https://www.ideal-investisseur.fr/en/actions-b/ascencio-renews-its-board-of-directors-and-appoints-two-new-members/21106.html
thesis.red_flags: Known event confirmed: Ascencio is the acquirer of Arlimmo SA (around 10 June 2026; consistent with the dated press-release URL); no bid for Ascencio found. Leverage: post-deal EPRA LTV was guided at 46-47%, which is high. The deal was partly equity-funded at EUR 48.2/share (dilution) and partly bond-funded at 4.80%. A Belgian press article says 2025 results were pressured by lower occupancy, negative rent reviews and tenant-bankruptcy costs. Sector concentration in out-of-town retail, with about 42% of the portfolio in France (press article). Standard caveat: no litigation or accounting concerns were located, but official annual-report risk sections were not reviewed. Sources: https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-06/68727842-ascencio-sa-ascencio-continues-its-growth-with-the-acquisition-of-espace-shopping-hydrion-in-arlon-belgium-the-launch-of-a-capital-increase-via-399.htm ; https://www.bolero.be/nl/analyse-en-inzicht/blog/ascencio-breidt-portefeuille-uit-met-franse-overname-maar-2025-resultaten-temperen-de-winstbijdrage

thesis.business_description: Paper producer listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange since 2009 (per Affarsvarlden), with roots in the Swedish Munkedal mill (Onstad family majority from 1943) and the Kostrzyn mill in Poland (privatised 1993); it also owns 51% of Swedish pulp producer Rottneros AB. FY2025 group sales were about PLN 3.2bn (PLN 3,197.6m). An aggregator profile lists the head office in Kostrzyn; this was not confirmed from the company site. Detailed product mix and market split were not located in this search. Sources: https://arcticpaper.com/about-arctic-paper/history ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/arctic-paper-original-med-dolda-varden ; https://www.inderes.fi/releases/arctic-paper-reinforcing-the-group-in-challenging-times
thesis.competitive_position: European producer of graphic/uncoated papers plus a pulp arm (Rottneros, 51%); scale and market share versus competitors could not be located in this search (research gap). Management announced a cost programme across pulp, paper and energy targeting PLN 45-50m of annual savings from 2026. Sources: https://www.inderes.fi/releases/arctic-paper-reinforcing-the-group-in-challenging-times ; https://arcticpaper.com/about-arctic-paper/history
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Stockwatch (a data aggregator): Nemus Holding AB 41,374,890 shares, 59.71% (entry dated 7 Nov 2024); Thomas Onstad 5,923,658 shares, 8.55% (dated 16 May 2025). Earlier press/TradingView text put Onstad's overall stake at about 68% (68.13%), and an older Affarsvarlden piece said nearly 80%, so figures are dated and differ. Investing.com lists Arctic Paper as a subsidiary of Nemus Holding. A current register from the annual report/exchange filings was not located. Sources: https://www.stockwatch.pl/gpw/ARCTIC,akcjonariat,dywidendy.aspx ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/arctic-paper-original-med-dolda-varden ; https://m.uk.investing.com/equities/arctic-paper-company-profile
thesis.insider_ownership: Thomas Onstad (Swedish resident in Switzerland, from the Onstad family that took control of Munkedal in 1943) is reported to control the company: 8.55% directly plus Nemus Holding AB at 59.71% (combined roughly 68%, consistent with the ~68% press figure; the link between Onstad and Nemus is from press reports, not a filing seen here). Management and other board holdings were not located; research gap. Sources: https://www.stockwatch.pl/gpw/ARCTIC,akcjonariat,dywidendy.aspx ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/arctic-paper-original-med-dolda-varden
thesis.red_flags: FY2025 preliminary group results: EBITDA only PLN 28.3m (0.9% margin), EBIT about -PLN 166m and net loss about -PLN 175m versus a PLN 161m profit in 2024, driven by weak pulp; a SEK 140m impairment on CTMP-related fixed assets was reported in a quarterly update. A consolidated-statement excerpt cited operating loss of PLN 153.8m, so preliminary and final figures differ. No dividend proposed for 2025. Controlling holder owns roughly two-thirds, limiting free float and minority influence. Net debt/leverage was not located. Sources: https://www.inderes.fi/releases/arctic-paper-reinforcing-the-group-in-challenging-times ; https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/annual-report-of-arctic-paper-sa-for-2025-together-with-auditors-report ; https://www.stockwatch.pl/gpw/ARCTIC,akcjonariat,dywidendy.aspx

thesis.business_description: German listed equipment/technology group (21,749,988 voting rights outstanding per 2025 notices) with a growing ultrasound metrology business (acoustic microscopy) and a materials-solutions division per Edison research. FY2025: order intake EUR 267.6m (+77.7%), revenue EUR 244.3m (EUR 270.1m in 2024), EBITDA EUR 25.3m, gross margin 31.9%. FY2026 guidance: revenue EUR 255-275m, EBITDA EUR 26-31m; management expects revenue above EUR 300m in 2027. Headquarters and full segment breakdown were not located in this search. Sources: https://www.pvatepla.com/corporate/investor-relations/news/pva-tepla-significantly-increases-order-intake-in-2025/ ; https://www.edisongroup.com/research/guiding-for-a-gradual-recovery-in-2026/BM-2779/
thesis.competitive_position: Strategy in 2025 centred on strengthening metrology through acquisitions and vertical integration: DIVE imaging systems GmbH (now PVA Vision GmbH) and desconpro engineering GmbH (now PVA desconpro GmbH), the latter a long-standing supplier of automation components for its ultrasound microscopy systems. Edison estimates the order backlog at about EUR 175m (analyst estimate, not company-reported). Named competitors and market-share data were not located; research gap. Sources: https://www.pvatepla.com/corporate/investorrelations/news/pva-tepla-strengthens-growing-metrology-business-through-takeover-and-vertical-integration-of-a-supplier/ ; https://www.edisongroup.com/research/guiding-for-a-gradual-recovery-in-2026/BM-2779/
thesis.main_shareholders: No complete register located. 2025 voting-rights notices (EQS/WpHG): SPICE THREE Investment Cooperatief U.A. (linked to Nicolaas Hoek) reported 5.00% at a 1 Sep 2025 threshold (previous 3.04%; the same holding was also filed under Joseph van Caldenborgh with a prior 3.62%, so filings are inconsistent); Morgan Stanley fell to 1.05% on 4 Jun 2025 from 4.81%; Kempen Oranje Participaties filed a threshold notice on 23 Jan 2025 (percentage not captured). Sources: https://www.boerse.de/nachrichten/EQS-PVR-PVA-TePla-AG-Release-according-to-Article-40-Section-1-of-the-WpHG-the-German-Securities-Trading-Act-with-the-objective-of-Europe-wide-distribution/37882637 ; https://it.tradingview.com/news/eqs%3A4038a21df094b%3A0-pva-tepla-ag-release-according-to-article-40-section-1-of-the-wphg-the-german-securities-trading-act-with-the-objective-of-europe-wide-distribution
thesis.insider_ownership: Could not locate management or supervisory board shareholdings in this search; treat as a research gap.
thesis.red_flags: Known event: PVA TePla acquired desconpro engineering GmbH (announced 30 Jan 2025, effective 1 Jan 2025) as vertical integration of an automation supplier; small bolt-on, no bid for PVA TePla found. The AGM page lists a domination and profit-transfer agreement with desconpro (terms not reviewed). Revenue fell in 2025 (EUR 244.3m vs EUR 270.1m) on a lower opening backlog and delivery timing, and EBITDA margin is around 10%. Standard caveat: the equipment business is order-driven and lumpy; no governance or accounting issues were found in these sources. Sources: https://www.pvatepla.com/corporate/investorrelations/news/pva-tepla-strengthens-growing-metrology-business-through-takeover-and-vertical-integration-of-a-supplier/ ; https://www.pvatepla.com/corporate/investor-relations/annual-general-meeting/ ; https://www.pvatepla.com/corporate/investor-relations/news/pva-tepla-significantly-increases-order-intake-in-2025/

thesis.business_description: Athens-based Greek ICT services group (founded 1994 per an aggregator profile) listed on Euronext Growth Milan (Borsa Italiana) rather than in Athens. Three segments: Cyber Security Operations, Infrastructure & Cloud Operations and Field Services Operations; one profile says most revenue comes from Field Services. 2025 revenue EUR 34.74m (EUR 37.90m in 2024), EBITDA EUR 3.86m, net profit EUR 1.19m (EUR 1.68m), gross margin 23.8%, net debt EUR 0.49m. Sources: https://neurosoft.gr/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Board-of-Directors-of-Neurosoft-SA-approves-2025-Annual-Financial-Statements-31032026.pdf ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/it/software/bit-nrst/neurosoft-software-production-shares
thesis.competitive_position: Very small player (about 25.6m shares and market cap near EUR 15m in early 2026, aggregator data). Offerings include offensive/defensive cyber security, NIS 2 / DORA advisory, OT security for critical infrastructure, managed cloud/infrastructure and field maintenance services. Competitors and market share were not located, nor was the extent of business done with OPAP group; research gap. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/it/software/bit-nrst/neurosoft-software-production-shares ; https://neurosoft.gr/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Board-of-Directors-of-Neurosoft-SA-approves-2025-Annual-Financial-Statements-31032026.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: Company IR page states OPAP S.A. holds 67.72% in total. An Italian market-data page (undated; aggregator) breaks it down as OPAP Investment Ltd 38.19%, OPAP International Ltd 25.02%, OPAP Cyprus 4.51%, with IGT Plc 16.32% and market 15.96%. A 2015 transparency notice showed OPAP at only 29.53%, so the stake has risen since. Date of the breakdown not confirmed. Sources: https://neurosoft.gr/investor-relations/shareholders/overview/ ; https://mercati.ilsole24ore.com/azioni/borsa-italiana/dettaglio-completo/NRST.MI/analisi-fondamentale/bilancio
thesis.insider_ownership: Could not locate current board/executive holdings in this search; treat as a research gap. A 2021 company release on a director's resignation referred to a holding of about 2.61% (name and current status not confirmed). A 2015 release named Nikolaos Vasilonikolidakis as CEO (stale). Source: https://neurosoft.gr/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/Neurosoft-BoD-announces-Mr.-Vasilonikolidakis-resignation_rev1.pdf
thesis.red_flags: Controlled about 68% by OPAP (Greek gaming group) with another 16.3% held by IGT Plc per the aggregator, leaving a free float of roughly 16%: thin liquidity, related-party and minority-protection risk. Micro-cap (about EUR 15m) with falling revenue in 2025 and a low 23.8% gross margin; management cites softer market conditions. Related-party transaction volumes were not reviewed. Sources: https://neurosoft.gr/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Board-of-Directors-of-Neurosoft-SA-approves-2025-Annual-Financial-Statements-31032026.pdf ; https://neurosoft.gr/investor-relations/shareholders/overview/

thesis.business_description: Lithuanian dairy company headquartered in Vilnius that produces and sells milk and dairy products to retail chains directly and through distributors. Listed on the Nasdaq Vilnius Main List since 2 Jan 2002 (ticker PZV1L, ISIN LT0000111676); share capital EUR 13,088,981.51 in 45,134,419 shares of EUR 0.29 nominal (H1 2025 report). A corporate bond issue is also listed on the exchange. Product range, segment split and recent financials (2025 sales/profit) were not located; research gap. thesis.competitive_position: Could not locate market-share, scale or competitor data for the company in this search; treat as a research gap. Older Nasdaq data show a minority stake of 10.97% in Zemaitijos Pienas AB (2004, stale). Source: https://www.nasdaqbaltic.com/statistics/en/ir/1da973e651/company

thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources, but coverage is thin: no 2025 annual results or current shareholder register were found. Potential succession/ownership change following the reported death of the long-time chairman and holder Julius Kvaraciejus (TV3, single source). Founder/insider-group concentration (about 32% of votes in 2013 data, stale). Standard caveat: small Baltic stock with likely limited liquidity. Source: https://www.tv3.lt/gaires/akcijos

thesis.business_description: Genoa-based (founded 2012) maritime, port and logistics technology group listed on Euronext Growth Milan; proprietary software including SaaS used by port and intermodal operators (e.g. a tool used at the Genoa Pra' intermodal terminal, per a 2020 article). Preliminary unaudited 2025 results: production value EUR 25.1m (+72%), EBITDA EUR 6.1m (24% margin), proprietary software revenue EUR 7.5m (+131%), Milos Federative Services EUR 2.3m (+156%); multi-year backlog EUR 33.4m at 30 Sep 2025. Sources: https://financialfilings.com/it/filings/circle-group/earnings-release/2025/7830693/ ; https://www.adriaports.com/en/?p=36036
thesis.competitive_position: Specialist in port-community and logistics digital platforms with an acquisition-assisted growth plan (2025-2028 plan guided production value of EUR 24-26.4m for 2025; a headline reports the purchase of software house Progetto Adele). Partnerships seen in headlines include SAAR Depositi Portuali (June 2025) and an EU-funded decision-support software project with Laghezza (Jan 2024). Named competitors and market share were not located; research gap. Sources: https://financialfilings.com/it/filings/circle-group/earnings-release/2025/7830693/ ; https://www.shippingitaly.it/2025/06/16/circle-e-saar-depositi-portuali-rafforzano-la-partnership/?output=pdf ; https://www.portseurope.com/circle-acquires-progetto-adele-software-house/
thesis.main_shareholders: Latest full table found is dated July 2024 (stale): Innotech S.r.l. 2,157,276 shares, 46.73%; Eiffel Investment Group 514,800 shares, 11.15%; Alessandro Orsini 2.50%; Andrea Villani 2.50%; market 36.76%. Teleborsa (13 Oct 2026) reports Hoop Club entered the capital via Eracle, buying 146,040 shares, about 3.05% (single source; below the 5% disclosure threshold). Milano Finanza says Eiffel, Alkemia and Algebris have been above 5% in the past. A current register was not located. thesis.insider_ownership: Luca Abatello (Chairman and CEO, also Investor Relations Manager) is linked to Innotech S.r.l., which held 46.73% in July 2024. Alessandro Orsini and Andrea Villani held 2.50% each (their roles were not confirmed; sources describe them variously as holders with voting rights or a voting agreement). Other board holdings were not located. Source: https://borsaitaliana.it/borsa/notizie/price-sensitive/download/20145_143285_2024_oneinfo.html
thesis.red_flags: Controlling holder (Abatello via Innotech) at roughly 47% in 2024 data; an activist-style investor, Hoop Club, was reported in October 2026 as building a stake (Milano Finanza headline 'l'attivista Hoop Club punta Circle'), which could create governance contention. The 2025 figures are preliminary and unaudited, shareholder data is stale, and share buy-back programmes were announced (TipRanks headlines). Small Euronext Growth Milan stock with liquidity risk; growth partly acquisition-driven. Sources: https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/egm-l-attivista-hoop-club-punta-circle-202610121841127374 ; https://financialfilings.com/it/filings/circle-group/earnings-release/2025/7830693/

thesis.business_description: Polish convenience/prepared-food manufacturer, formerly Pamapol S.A.; the name change to FoodHub was registered on 30 Sep 2025 by the Lodz-Srodmiescie district court. Per trade press, the group aims to integrate the chain from raw material (Mitmar) to final production and is prioritising chilled ready meals. 2025 revenue PLN 883.7m vs PLN 907.0m in 2024; the snippet reported 2025 EBITDA of about -PLN 1m against a positive prior-year figure (text truncated, verify). Headquarters not confirmed. Sources: https://www.wiadomoscihandlowe.pl/handel-i-dystrybucja/marki-wlasne-i-marki-prywatne/foodhub-z-30-mln-zl-od-arp-na-rozwoj-convenience-2533644 ; https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/akcje/FOODHUB/akcjonariat
thesis.competitive_position: Positioning as a producer of ready meals/convenience food (an aggregator calls Pamapol a leader in prepared meals in Poland, unverified). Strategy: PLN 30m two-year loan from Agencja Rozwoju Przemyslu (reported 26 Mar 2026) to fund organisational and technological transformation and convenience-food growth; a May 2026 trade-press headline describes the 'new Pamapol' under cost pressure. Competitors and market share were not located; research gap. name: Société Fermière du Casino Municipal de Cannes

thesis.business_description: Cannes-based (Cote d'Azur) casino, hotel and restaurant operator, part of the Barriere family group. SFCMC's own January 2026 release describes the group as 1 casino, 3 hotels with beach and 4 restaurants; an aggregator lists Casino Barriere Croisette and Les Princes plus the Hotel Majestic, Le Gray d'Albion and Le Carl Gustaf (St-Barth), so counts differ between sources. Fiscal year ends 31 October. Revenue for FY to 31 Oct 2025 was reported as EUR176.9m (prior EUR169.3m) by a news feed; other aggregators show about EUR161.2m, probably different definitions (company revenue is gross, before state and municipal levies). The Majestic beach concession was renewed to 31 Dec 2029, and a court-ordered merger absorbing the Hotel Majestic company (SIEHM) into SFCMC was set in January 2026. The company's mid-2025 report places Casino Le Croisette 18th in the official national casino ranking and notes strong competition in Cannes. The current casino concession term was not located in this search (research gap). Fiscal-2025 revenue is up on the prior year per a news feed (EUR176.9m vs EUR169.3m, unverified against the company release). thesis.main_shareholders: Controlled by Societe de Participation Deauvillaise (SPD), the Barriere family holding company: at the 1 July 2026 filing of the draft offer SPD held 149,927 shares = 92.18% of capital and 95.02% of theoretical voting rights (AMF filing). On 8 December 2025 SPD agreed to buy Casinvest's 25.94% of capital (26.82% of votes) at a firm price of EUR1,897/share. Older filings (60-70% Desseigne-Barriere family holdings, 2009-2014) are stale. Source: https://bdif.amf-france.org/back/api/v1/documents/2026/226C0945/4B635C6D4E08EFF8D9919E3F52ABD068EE38A25B9E894156C8AD33E2B1CB929C.pdf ; https://a.storyblok.com/f/287000/x/8e62f06f91/sfcmc-communique-de-presse-spd-ravel-8-12-2025.pdf
thesis.red_flags: TAKEOVER / SQUEEZE-OUT: majority holder SPD (Barriere family) filed on 1 July 2026 a draft buyout offer (OPRO) followed by a squeeze-out (retrait obligatoire) at EUR2,700 per share over 10 trading days; the offer is pending AMF review (no AMF compliance decision, calendar or delisting date found as of this search). Price context: SPD agreed to pay Casinvest EUR1,897/share in Dec 2025; the offer price was raised to EUR2,700 on 28 May 2026 after discussions with the independent expert BM&A. The target filed its draft response note on 24 July 2026 (board opinion dated 23 July 2026); the expert's fairness conclusion was not located. Minorities (under 8% of capital) face a forced exit at the offer price, and liquidity and delisting follow a successful squeeze-out. Other: casino licence and public-service delegation renewals, restructuring (SIEHM merger), and gross-revenue definitions that differ across aggregators. Source: https://bdif.amf-france.org/back/api/v1/documents/2026/226C0945/4B635C6D4E08EFF8D9919E3F52ABD068EE38A25B9E894156C8AD33E2B1CB929C.pdf ; https://a.storyblok.com/f/287000/x/e4e49d9ab5/spd-cp-rehaussement-prix-opro.pdf ; https://a.storyblok.com/f/287000/x/839b24831c/communique-de-presse-de-depot-du-projet-opr-suivie-d-un-retrait-obligatoire.pdf

thesis.business_description: Ericsson Nikola Tesla d.d. (Zagreb Stock Exchange: ERNT) is a Croatian communications and ICT company: it provides communication products and services to telecom operators in the region (R&D, solution design, sales, network services, system integration) and ICT solutions for health care, transport, state administration and media; it calls itself Croatia's leading knowledge exporter, with about 3,000 employees (2024). FY2025: revenue EUR238.6m (-4.4%), operating profit EUR20.9m, net profit EUR17.7m (+13.8%); 2025 annual report published 29 Apr 2026. Headquarters city was not stated in the results. Sources: https://ericssonnikolatesla.com/en/news/annual-report-2025/ ; https://inter.capital/ericsson-nikola-tesla-publishes-fy-2025-results/ ; https://www.ericsson.com/en/about-us/company-facts/ericsson-worldwide/croatia/about-ericsson-nikola-tesla
thesis.competitive_position: Self-described leading regional provider in the operator segment, with a large R&D centre and service-delivery centres exporting software and services (strength in software export); backed by the Ericsson group as its largest shareholder. Named competitors and market-share data were not located (research gap), and the extent of revenue dependence on Ericsson group companies was not verified in these results. Shareholder returns are high: a EUR13.52 per share dividend was approved at the 10 June 2026 general meeting (EUR10.54 in 2025). Sources: https://www.ericsson.com/en/about-us/company-facts/ericsson-worldwide/croatia/about-ericsson-nikola-tesla ; https://ericssonnikolatesla.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Redovna-Glavna-skupstina-10062026-rezultati-glasovanja_final.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: As at 31 Dec 2024 (2024 annual report): LM Ericsson 49.07%, other shareholders 50.50%, treasury shares 0.43% (5,678 own shares) of 1,331,650 shares. The 31 Dec 2025 split was not located (research gap). Simply Wall St (aggregator, undated) shows Ericsson 49.3% (653,441 shares), top 10 holders 62.42% and a Raiffeisen pension-fund manager at 11.2%; the 49.3% conflicts slightly with the company's 49.07%. thesis.insider_ownership: Management Board (2024 report): Gordana Kovacevic (President), Hrvoje Bencic, Damir Busic, Milan Zivkovic; Supervisory Board chair Stefan Kotz (may have changed). Individual holdings with percentages were not located; Simply Wall St (aggregator) estimates individual insiders at about 0.733%. Treasury shares are used for employee award/loyalty programmes. Sources: https://ericssonnikolatesla.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/GI_2024_ENG.pdf ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/hr/tech/zgse-ernt/ericsson-nikola-tesla-dd-shares/ownership ; https://ericssonnikolatesla.com/en/news/20231006-shares
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in this search. Caveats: Ericsson holds about 49%, a strategic influence with potential related-party dealings (not examined here); FY2025 revenue fell 4.4%; dividends are large relative to earnings (EUR13.52/share, funded from 2024-2025 retained earnings, which reduces cash), and 2025 shareholder data were not located. Sources: https://inter.capital/ericsson-nikola-tesla-publishes-fy-2025-results/ ; https://ericssonnikolatesla.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Redovna-Glavna-skupstina-10062026-rezultati-glasovanja_final.pdf

thesis.business_description: Skagi hf. (formerly Vátryggingafélag Íslands / VÍS, ticker VIS) is a Reykjavík-based Icelandic financial services holding company operating in insurance, investment banking and asset management; subsidiaries include VÍS tryggingar hf. (insurance), Fossar Investment Bank and Íslensk verðbréf (ÍV). In January 2026 Skagi exercised an option to acquire a further 14.1% stake in ÍV. One aggregator (Financial Filings) cites FY2025 total revenues of ISK 6.18B and net income of ISK 1.90B (earnings release 18 Feb 2026); the revenue definition is unclear, treat as unverified. Sources: https://financialfilings.com/companies/vatryggingafelag-islands/ ; https://app.mergerlinks.com/companies/skagi ; https://mfn.se/all/a/vatryggingafelag-islands
thesis.competitive_position: Mid-sized Icelandic insurer-plus-investment-bank group built through acquisitions (Fossar acquired by VÍS in 2023; ÍV combination approved by the Icelandic Competition Authority in July 2024, which found no creation or strengthening of a dominant position, with added concentration mainly in asset management and market trading). Market-share figures for insurance or investment banking were not found in this search (research gap). Skagi remains in a commercial partnership with Íslandsbanki after merger talks ended. It runs a share buyback programme and announced a share capital increase on 17 March 2026 (details not read). A 29 Apr 2026 company announcement titled 'updated priorities and organizational changes' was seen only as a headline. Sources: https://samkeppni.is/media/akvardanir-2024/20-2024.pdf ; https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-aktien/skagi-hf.htm ; https://mfn.se/all/a/vatryggingafelag-islands
thesis.main_shareholders: No official shareholder register was located. Aggregator data (undated snapshots, figures differ by site): Simply Wall St lists Pension Fund for State Employees 8.57%, Sjávarsýn ehf. 8.51%, Skel fjárfestingafélag hf. 8.15%, Gildi lífeyrissjóður 8.13%, with the top 16 holders owning 69.88%. Investing.com lists Sjávarsýn 8.42%, Skel 8.07%, Gildi 8.05%, Frjálsi lífeyrissjóðurinn 7.29%, Lífeyrissjóður verslunarmanna 6.74%, Klettar fjárfestingar 4.72%. Skagi's own buyback notices indicate treasury shares of about 3.81% (secondary reading of mfn.se notices). The March 2026 capital increase may have changed percentages. Verify against Nasdaq Iceland / the 2025 annual report. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/is/insurance/icse-skagi/skagi-hf-shares/ownership ; https://uk.investing.com/equities/vis-ownership ; https://mfn.se/all/a/skagi/skagi-reglubundin-tilkynning-um-kaup-a-eigin-brefum-i-samraemi-vid-endurkaupaaaetlun-vika-27-db0ccdc5
thesis.insider_ownership: Group CEO is listed by Simply Wall St as 'Haraldur Poroarson' (spelling as shown by the aggregator), CEO since 2 Oct 2023 and a director since 2025 per that aggregator; his shareholding is shown as n/a. Board members' and executives' holdings, and any founding-family stake, could not be located in this search; treat as a research gap (the 2025 annual report / Nasdaq Iceland insider notifications would hold this). Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/is/insurance/icse-skagi/skagi-hf-shares/management
thesis.red_flags: Corporate-action finding (checked): Íslandsbanki and Skagi agreed head of terms for a merger in Oct 2025 (Skagi shareholders were to receive 323,859,440 new Íslandsbanki shares, about 15% of the combined entity). On 21 Feb 2026 Íslandsbanki's board announced the talks were discontinued, citing due diligence and analysis findings, changes in relative market values, and expected higher Central Bank of Iceland capital requirements for a bank owning an insurer; no revised exchange ratio was agreed. Status: terminated; partnership continues. Other points: highly fragmented register with no controlling holder (several 6-9% pension/investment holders) so no anchor owner; Skagi was reportedly removed from the OMX Iceland 15 index in late 2025 (aggregator summary); a large strategic reset (Apr 2026 'updated priorities and organizational changes') is not yet understood. No litigation or accounting concerns were identified in the sources searched. Sources: https://www.mfn.se/a/islandsbanki/islandsbanki-hf-merger-discussions-between-islandsbanki-and-skagi-hf-discontinued ; https://www.islandsbanki.is/en/ir/islandsbanki-hf-islandsbanki-initiates-merger-discussions-with-skagi-hf ; https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-aktien/skagi-hf.htm

thesis.business_description: Yanosik S.A. (formerly Neptis S.A., renamed in 2025; listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange) operates the Yanosik driver-community app, which warns of speed checks, speed cameras, accidents and police, plus navigation and a marketplace of driver services (e.g. insurance, car listings, fuel prices). The app is free and ad-supported with a paid ad-free option; the company also sells hardware (e.g. Yanosik GTR anti-radar, XS communicator with a data subscription, YANBOX GO) and, in B2B, analytics, advertising and data services. A business directory (secondary source) lists Poznań as HQ. FY2025: revenue PLN 63.34m (+8%), net profit PLN 8.09m (vs 2.64m), helped by closing less profitable activities; preliminary H1 2026: revenue PLN 36.4m (vs 29.0m), net profit PLN 5.7m (vs 1.9m). Sources: https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/akcje/YANOSIK/wyniki-finansowe ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/145777,yanosik-zamyka-2025-r-trzykrotnym-wzrostem-zysku-netto ; https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art44941841-yanosik-spolka-akcyjna-wstepne-wybrane-dane-finansowe-za-i-polrocze-2026 ; https://www.thecompanycheck.com/company/b/yanosik/c97d8829670146a5b
thesis.competitive_position: Polish crowd-sourced traffic-warning niche with a sizeable user community: a retailer cites more than 1.5m drivers monthly, while a BiznesRadar analysis cites 5.5m drivers in the community (the two figures are not reconciled and neither is from an official report). A business directory (secondary) names Waze, HERE and Inrix as competitors. Strategy cited by management: hardware (YANBOX GO), B2B data and advertising, and cost discipline; Q1 2026 revenue PLN 16.8m (+20.4%). Market cap about PLN 172m (10m shares at about PLN 17.2, BiznesRadar, 20 Aug 2026). Sources: https://www.x-kom.pl/p/541095-antyradar-samochodowy-yanosik-antyradar-yanosik-gtr.html ; https://comparic.pl/zyski-ponad-3x-w-gore-miliony-klientow-i-11-lat-ciaglej-hossy-czy-to-ukryty-gigant-gpw/ ; https://www.thecompanycheck.com/company/b/yanosik/c97d8829670146a5b ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/wiadomosci/YAN,3
thesis.main_shareholders: CONFLICTING / UNCONFIRMED. Simply Wall St (undated) lists Adam Tychmanowicz about 29.2%, Filip Kolendo about 29%, Tadeusz Sudol about 9%, Dawid Nowicki about 2.5%, top 5 holders 69.68%. A Polish ESPI notice (reproduced by Parkiet, date not visible in the result) says a Family Foundation (Fundacja Rodzinna) holds 2,839,940 shares (about 28.4% of capital) carrying 4,830,000 votes (about 34.04% of votes) after settling a donation from Atorium, crossing the 33 1/3% votes threshold; this implies some shares carry extra votes and that holdings may have moved into a foundation. The company published a list of holders of at least 5% of votes for the AGM of 24 Jun 2026, but its contents were not retrievable. Verify on ESPI/EBI. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/pl/tech/wse-yan/yanosik-shares/ownership ; https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art43174601-yanosik-spolka-akcyjna-znaczne-pakiety-akcji ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/wiadomosci/YAN,3
thesis.insider_ownership: Adam Tychmanowicz appears to be the company's CEO (named as Prezes in a comparic.pl interview piece; verify in KRS). Per the ESPI notice above he directly holds 78,410 bearer shares (0.78% of capital, 0.55% of votes) after the change, while the Family Foundation holds the larger block (identity of the foundation's founder/beneficiaries not stated in the result). Aggregator figures show Tychmanowicz at about 29.2%, Kolendo about 29% and Sudol about 9%, but dates are unknown. Board/supervisory board member holdings were not located (research gap). Sources: https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art43174601-yanosik-spolka-akcyjna-znaczne-pakiety-akcji ; https://comparic.pl/zyski-ponad-3x-w-gore-miliony-klientow-i-11-lat-ciaglej-hossy-czy-to-ukryty-gigant-gpw/ ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/pl/tech/wse-yan/yanosik-shares/ownership
thesis.red_flags: Concentrated control: the top few holders own roughly 70% (aggregator) and votes appear to exceed capital for the Family Foundation (34.04% of votes vs 28.4% of capital), so minority holders have limited influence and free float/liquidity is thin. Ownership data is inconsistent across sources and holdings appear to have been restructured around Oct 2025 (several Art. 69 notices; contents not read). Profit jump in 2025 came with only 8% revenue growth, driven by cost cuts and closure of less profitable lines, so sustainability of margins should be checked. Revenue relies on advertising, device subscriptions and data/B2B services; competition from global navigation apps (e.g. Waze per directory) is a standing risk. Company renamed in 2025 (Neptis to Yanosik). No litigation or auditor qualification identified in the sources searched. Sources: https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/145777,yanosik-zamyka-2025-r-trzykrotnym-wzrostem-zysku-netto ; https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art43174601-yanosik-spolka-akcyjna-znaczne-pakiety-akcji ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/pl/tech/wse-yan/yanosik-shares/ownership

thesis.business_description: Jacquet Metals SA is a European distributor of special metals (stainless steel flat and long products, plus engineering steels) organised in three divisions: JACQUET, STAPPERT and IMS group. Per a September 2025 company presentation: sales of about EUR 2bn (LTM), 3,336 employees, 119 distribution centres, 24 countries, with Germany the largest market at 32% of sales. FY2025 (press release 18 Mar 2026): sales EUR 1.84bn (-6.6%), current EBITDA EUR 94m (5.1% of sales, versus 4.4% in 2024), operating cash flow EUR 103m. HQ address listed by Yahoo Finance as 7, rue Michel Jacquet (city not confirmed in results). Sources: https://www.jacquetmetals.com/fichiers/presentations/2025/SFAF_11.09.25_EN.pdf ; https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260318477298/fr ; https://fr.finance.yahoo.com/quote/JCQ.PA/profile
thesis.competitive_position: Specialist multi-country distributor of stainless and engineering steels. H1 2025: sales EUR 987m (-8.1%), EBITDA EUR 48m (4.9% of sales vs 3.6%); the IMS division (engineering steels, exposed to German industry) was weakest (volumes -7.3% at constant scope) while JACQUET and STAPPERT (stainless) were more resilient. Management restructured IMS and exited some low-value product ranges. Balance sheet at 30 Jun 2025: cash EUR 200m, credit lines EUR 797m (EUR 436m unused), EUR 160m syndicated revolver extended to July 2028, gearing 25% (27% at end-2024). Named competitors and market-share data were not found in this search (research gap). Sources: https://www.jacquetmetals.com/fichiers/communiques/2025/JM_CP_H125_EN.pdf ; https://www.boursorama.com/bourse/actualites/jacquet-metals-preserve-sa-rentabilite-malgre-un-chiffre-d-affaires-en-repli-en-2025-49b4301b01f07d1c62db6abe18c05e83
thesis.main_shareholders: Latest official breakdown found is STALE (company press release of 25 Jun 2021): Eric Jacquet and his controlled company JSA together held 42.08% of capital and 59.04% of theoretical voting rights; the release said no additional information was available on other holders. Since then the share count has fallen through cancellations (21,531,967 shares at 30 Nov 2025, of which 1,237,292 treasury shares, about 5.7%), so the family percentage is likely higher today, but the current figure was not located (check the 2025 Universal Registration Document). A Morningstar-sourced aggregator profile (dated, FY2023 data) names Moneta Asset Management, Amiral Gestion, Dimensional Fund Advisors and Sextant PME among institutional holders, without percentages. Sources: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/BWR/2021/06/FCBWR134768_20210625.pdf ; https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/BWR/2025/12/FCBWR165852_20251216.pdf ; https://fr.finance.yahoo.com/quote/JCQ.PA/profile
thesis.insider_ownership: Eric Jacquet (Chairman and CEO) with JSA: 42.08% of capital and 59.04% of theoretical votes as of 25 Jun 2021 (stale; current figure not located). Theoretical voting rights (about 31.3m) well exceed shares (21.5m), consistent with double voting rights for long-held registered shares. Philippe Goczol (Deputy CEO) and Hans-Josef Hoss (CEO of IMS group) are named in an aggregator profile; their shareholdings were not located. Sources: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/BWR/2021/06/FCBWR134768_20210625.pdf ; https://fr.finance.yahoo.com/quote/JCQ.PA/profile
thesis.red_flags: Controlling founder/family holder with double voting rights (about 59% of votes in 2021 data), so minority holders have limited influence and free float is smaller than the share count implies. Cyclical, low-margin distribution exposed to German industrial demand (Germany 32% of sales) and to metal price swings; IMS division restructuring ongoing. Leverage appeared moderate at mid-2025 (gearing 25%, EUR 436m undrawn lines), but year-end 2025 net debt and any 2026 guidance/dividend were not located. FY2025 net income attributable of about EUR 10m comes from a secondary source (Boursorama). A Quartr summary mentioning H1 2026 numbers was inconsistent with other sources and was disregarded. No litigation or accounting issues were identified in the sources searched. Sources: https://www.jacquetmetals.com/fichiers/communiques/2025/JM_CP_H125_EN.pdf ; https://www.boursorama.com/bourse/actualites/jacquet-metals-preserve-sa-rentabilite-malgre-un-chiffre-d-affaires-en-repli-en-2025-49b4301b01f07d1c62db6abe18c05e83

thesis.business_description: Josef Manner & Comp. AG is a Vienna-headquartered, family-controlled confectionery maker (Wiener Börse listing, ISIN AT0000728209), best known for Manner Neapolitaner Schnitten (hazelnut wafers, invented 1898); it became a stock corporation on 23 Oct 1913 and produces exclusively in Austria. FY2025: sales about EUR 304m (+5.5% from about EUR 288m), operating result EUR 11.2m (EUR 21.1m in 2024), net income EUR 5.0m (14.4m), net debt EUR 20.2m (24.6m; net income and net debt from a Quartr summary). Segment sales: Austria EUR 123.7m, Germany EUR 87.4m, rest of world EUR 93.6m; export share 59.4%. A hazelnut farm in Azerbaijan took a EUR 4.8m impairment. The brand portfolio beyond Manner and current headcount were not located (an older biography cites about 700 employees; stale). Sources: https://www.pressetext.com/news/20260423011 ; https://quartr.com/events/josef-manner-comp-ag-man-h2-2025_F1Ma4MxL ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manner_(confectionery) ; https://www.comdirect.de/inf/aktien/AT0000728209
thesis.competitive_position: Per a company profile, Manner is number 1 in the Austrian 'Schnitten' (wafer-bar) market and number 2 in total Austrian confectionery; an older (1998) Falter article gave over 20% of Austrian confectionery and over 50% of wafers (stale). Germany is the second-largest market and exports are close to 60% of sales. Pressures: raw material costs up about 25% (notably cocoa; hazelnuts also volatile). The board was cut to three members from 1 Apr 2026; a stable to slightly higher 2026 revenue is guided and a EUR 2.00 per share dividend (unchanged) is proposed. Named competitors were not located (research gap). Sources: https://www.pressetext.com/news/20260423011 ; https://boerse-express.com/boerse/aktie/josef-manner-comp-ag+tts-399904/firmenprofil ; https://www.falter.at/zeitung/19981111/mag-man-eben ; https://quartr.com/events/josef-manner-comp-ag-man-h2-2025_F1Ma4MxL
thesis.main_shareholders: Only a STALE aggregator profile was found (boerse-express, year-end 2022): Privatstiftung Manner 42.56%, free float 27.33%, Andres Holding 24%, ÖZW Österreichische Zuckerwaren GmbH 6.11%; 1,890,000 shares outstanding. Austria-Forum describes the company as largely family-owned (Manner, Andres and Riedl families). No current official register (annual report, OeKB notifications) was located; treat percentages as unverified. Sources: https://boerse-express.com/boerse/aktie/josef-manner-comp-ag+tts-399904/firmenprofil ; https://austria-forum.org/af/Unternehmen/Manner
thesis.insider_ownership: Family vehicles hold the majority per the 2022 profile: Privatstiftung Manner 42.56% (foundation set up in 1999 by Dr. Carl Manner per Austria-Forum) and Andres Holding 24% (the Andres family; Hans Peter Andres was a Vorstand member in the 2017 and 2022 sources). Carl Manner was chairman of the supervisory board in a 2017 OeKB insider filing; that filing also records a Vorstand member selling 3,000 shares. The 2022 profile named Andreas Kutil as CEO; the board has since been reduced to three members (from 1 Apr 2026) and the current line-up and individual holdings were not located (research gap). Sources: https://boerse-express.com/boerse/aktie/josef-manner-comp-ag+tts-399904/firmenprofil ; https://my.oekb.at/issuer-info/rest/public/meldedaten/download/104971 ; https://www.pressetext.com/news/20260423011
thesis.red_flags: Family-controlled with a small free float (about 27% in 2022 data), so liquidity is thin and minority influence is limited; control concentration is likely stable but figures are stale. Margin squeeze: operating result fell 46.6% in 2025 on cocoa/hazelnut costs, plus a EUR 4.8m impairment of an Azerbaijan hazelnut farm (country and asset-specific risk). Heavy export reliance (59.4% of sales) and single-product dependence on the Neapolitaner franchise are structural concerns (the latter is an inference, not stated in sources). Leverage appears modest (net debt EUR 20.2m). Management board shrunk to three from April 2026. No litigation or auditor issues found in the sources searched. Sources: https://www.pressetext.com/news/20260423011 ; https://quartr.com/events/josef-manner-comp-ag-man-h2-2025_F1Ma4MxL
thesis.website: https://www.manner.com (brand site; investor/corporate pages appear under https://josef.manner.com)

thesis.business_description: KABE Group AB (publ.), headquartered in Tenhult, Sweden (founded 1957, listed on Nasdaq Stockholm as KABE B), manufactures caravans and motorhomes under the KABE brand, imports and sells Adria Mobil products in the Nordics through a group subsidiary, and sells camping accessories. Segments: caravans and motorhomes, accessories, other. Key markets are Sweden, Norway and Finland, with sales also elsewhere in Europe. FY2025 net sales SEK 3,212m (3,796m), operating profit SEK 68m (229m), margin 2.1%; H1 2026 net sales SEK 1,910m (1,830m), operating profit SEK 139m (73m), period profit SEK 120m (62m), equity ratio 64.9% (67.5%). Sources: https://kabe.se/en/about-kabe ; https://www.kabe.se/documents/pdf/KABE-Group-annual-report-2024_en_gb.pdf ; https://quartr.com/events/kabe-group-kabe-q2-2026_FkLhKmLz ; https://mb.cision.com/Main/1026/4385745/4226636.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: Nordic leader: the 2024 annual report puts combined market share in Sweden, Norway and Finland at about 38% for caravans (36% prior year) and 21% for motorhomes (18%); earlier reports showed about 40% and 17-19% (2021-2022). Adria is described as the largest importer and market leader for caravans and motorhomes in the Nordic region. Demand is cyclical and discretionary: management says it is still reducing inventories and adapting production to demand, notes Nordic markets outperform other European regions, and expects sales to rise as economic conditions improve. A secondary source claims Q4 2025 was the first loss-making quarter in over ten years; not verified against company filings. Sources: https://www.kabe.se/documents/pdf/KABE-Group-annual-report-2024_en_gb.pdf ; https://linclund.com/?p=2949 ; https://quartr.com/events/kabe-group-kabe-q2-2026_FkLhKmLz
thesis.main_shareholders: Aggregator data only (no annual report shareholder table or Euroclear extract found), and sources differ. Inderes (Millistream data): Familjen Blomqvist 51.1% of capital and 67.0% of votes; Nordea about 13.5%; Bengt Karlsson about 3.7-4.0%; Stig-Olof Simonsson about 2.7%. Simply Wall St (snapshot Nov 2025): Maud Blomqvist 5,157,103 shares (about 57.3%), Nordea Investment Management 1,231,265 shares (about 13.7%), Bengt Karlsson about 3.99%, BBH Capital Partners about 3.1%. An Italian-language Simply Wall St page showed 30.53% for Maud Blomqvist, which conflicts and is likely stale. Verify against the 2025 annual report. Sources: https://www.inderes.se/en/companies/KABE-Group/ownership ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/automobiles/sto-kabe-b/kabe-group-ab-publ-shares/ownership
thesis.insider_ownership: Blomqvist family is the controlling holder (51.1% of capital / 67.0% of votes per Inderes; Maud Blomqvist about 57.3% of shares per Simply Wall St, with the family-vs-individual framing unreconciled). Board per Simply Wall St: Nils-Erik Danielsson (independent chairman), Maud, Mikael and Peter Blomqvist among directors. CEO Alf Ekström (director since 1984) holds 1.46% per Simply Wall St or 1.9% of capital / 3.6% of votes per Inderes; he handed operational leadership of the subsidiary to a successor but remains Group CEO (Börsvärlden). Sources: https://www.inderes.se/en/companies/KABE-Group/ownership ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/automobiles/sto-kabe-b/kabe-group-ab-publ-shares/management ; https://borsvarlden.com/artiklar/kabe-utser-ny-vd-for-dotterbolaget-alf-ekstrom-kvar-som-koncernchef
thesis.red_flags: Family control with a two-class structure (about 67% of votes), and several Blomqvist family members sit on the board, so minority shareholders have little influence. Earnings are volatile and cyclical: 2025 operating profit fell about 70% (SEK 229m to 68m) on lower sales and dealer-inventory adjustments, before a 2026 recovery (H1 operating profit SEK 139m vs 73m; H1 2026 includes a SEK 9m currency effect). Long-tenured CEO (since 1984 as director) implies key-person and succession risk. Supplier reliance on Adria for the import business is implied by the structure but not quantified in the sources. Balance sheet looks strong (equity ratio 64.9%). No litigation or accounting concerns identified in the sources searched. thesis.business_description: Lubelski Węgiel Bogdanka S.A. is a Polish hard coal (mainly steam/thermal coal) miner in the Lublin Coal Basin, listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange and part of the Enea Group since 29 Oct 2015 (HQ address not stated in the results). 2025: gross output about 11.56m tonnes (-4.1%), commercial coal 7.6m t, mining yield 65.5%; consolidated sales PLN 2,854.3m; an impairment of about PLN 522.5m produced a net loss of PLN 159.4m (net profit PLN 263.8m and EBITDA PLN 543.1m excluding the impairment). thesis.business_description: Bitcoin Group SE is a German holding company in crypto and blockchain: 100% of Bitcoin Deutschland AG, operator of the Bitcoin.de trading platform (company states more than 1,000,000 registered users and a regulated German licence), 100% of futurum bank AG, and 50% of Sineus Financial Services GmbH (older company description). Its AGMs are held in Herford (HQ not directly confirmed in results). Bitcoin.de is being relaunched from a peer-to-peer marketplace to a broker-model platform. FY2025 (annual report published 26 Jun 2026): revenue EUR 10.0m (EUR 9.3m), EBITDA EUR 0.5m (EUR 1.8m), equity ratio 71.8%, cash EUR 12.6m, net crypto holdings EUR 293m (EUR 366m at end-2024). H1 2026 (report of 29 Sep 2026): revenue EUR 1.59m (EUR 3.78m), EBITDA EUR -3.25m (EUR -1.00m), net crypto holdings EUR 199m at 30 Jun 2026. 5,000,000 shares, so crypto holdings equal roughly EUR 40 per share (derived). thesis.competitive_position: Operator of one of Germany's best-known crypto exchanges by its own claims (more than 1m registered users; 98% of managed crypto assets in cold wallets, both company statements, not independently verified). thesis.business_description: Groupe Pizzorno Environnement is a French waste-management group headquartered in Draguignan (Var), with ~2,500 employees, led by Frederic Devalle. Activities: Proprete (collection and cleaning, EUR 229.2m 2025 revenue, +5.5%) and Traitement-Valorisation (treatment/recovery, EUR 45.3m, -18.9%, after loss of the Aboncourt public-service delegation), including operation of the Toulon energy-from-waste plant via Zephire (~EUR 34.7m revenue). 2025 consolidated revenue EUR 274.5m (flat), EBITDA EUR 40.7m (14.8% margin vs 18.3% in 2024), gross cash and investments EUR 108.8m, order book EUR 1.12bn at 31 Mar 2026 (per aggregated press summaries of the company release). Sources: https://www.boursedirect.fr/fr/actualites/categorie/resultats/pizzorno-environnement-rassure-par-son-carnet-de-commandes-boursier-c65dba45e85ee718c24f624591bed359e5745795 ; https://www.lejournaldesentreprises.com/article/pizzorno-environnement-un-groupe-devenu-roi-des-poubelles-dans-le-var-et-au-dela-2098859
thesis.competitive_position: Regional-to-national municipal waste collection and treatment operator, strongest in south-east France (Var and surroundings), with a record order book (EUR 1.12bn) and recent contract wins such as the Dracenie Provence Verdon Agglomeration collection contract (6 years from 1 Jan 2026, ~EUR 54m total revenue). Competitors (large national players such as Veolia, Suez, Paprec) and market share were not documented in the search results (research gap). Strategically, Paprec (a larger recycling group) entered the capital in 2021 and is now taking control. Sources: https://www.lejournaldesentreprises.com/article/pizzorno-environnement-affiche-un-carnet-de-commandes-record-2142431 ; https://www.tradingsat.com/pizzorno-environnement-FR0010214064/actualites/pizzorno-environnement-entre-au-capital-en-2021-paprec-s-apprete-a-prendre-le-controle-de-groupe-pizzorno-environnement-qui-grimpe-en-bourse-1154507.html
thesis.main_shareholders: Takeover situation. On 9 Jun 2026 Paprec bought 1,225,617 shares (30.64% of capital) from the Pizzorno-Devalle family at EUR 62.50 per share, taking Paprec to 50.64% of capital and ~50.02% of voting rights; the Pizzorno-Devalle family kept ~21.18% of capital. Paprec Group and concert members (Paprec, Pizzorno-Devalle family, F. Devalle) together hold 75.22% of capital and 82.43% of votes (draft offer, 2 Jul 2026). 4,000,000 shares in total; the free float outside the concert is 991,088 shares (24.78% of capital, 17.57% of votes). Paprec filed a mandatory simplified tender offer at EUR 62.50 (cash, 10 trading days, AMF calendar to be set); GPE's draft response was filed 29 Jul 2026. No squeeze-out intended. Offer opening/closing dates and results were not found (research gap). Price formula: 7x average EBITDA less net financial debt, bounded EUR 125m-250m for 100% of equity (Feb 2026 AMF filing). Sources: https://www.paprec.com/app/uploads/2026/07/communique-de-presse-norme-groupe-pizzorno-environnement-opas.pdf ; https://www.abcbourse.com/marches/paprec-lance-une-offre-publique-dachat-sur-groupe-pizzorno-environnement-a-62-5_699202 ; https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/ACT/2026/02/FCACT078220_20260209.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: The Pizzorno-Devalle family retained ~21.18% of capital after the June 2026 block sale (acting in concert with Paprec; Frederic Devalle, CEO, is a member of the concert). The exact split of Devalle's personal holding versus the family's was not located (concert total 75.22% less Paprec 50.64% = ~24.6%, an inference, not a reported figure). Sources: https://www.abcbourse.com/marches/paprec-prend-le-controle-de-pizzorno-environnement-et-lance-une-offre-a-62-50-eu_698075 ; https://www.paprec.com/app/uploads/2026/07/communique-de-presse-norme-groupe-pizzorno-environnement-opas.pdf
thesis.red_flags: Company is the TARGET of a Paprec-led mandatory tender offer at EUR 62.50 (no delisting or squeeze-out planned, so a thin ~17.6%-of-votes free float and low liquidity remain after the offer). Paprec has effective control (50.64% capital; 75.22% in concert with the family), so minority shareholders will have limited influence. Offer price is formula-based (7x EBITDA less net debt) and set under a 2021 concert agreement, which is a risk if EBITDA keeps falling (2025 EBITDA down from EUR 50.1m to EUR 40.7m). Loss of the Aboncourt delegation hit treatment revenue. Net debt data is unclear: sources cite net cash of EUR 12.9m at 30 Jun 2025 but 'net financial debt of EUR 11m' at 30 Jun 2026 (conflicting/unverified). No litigation details located; annual report risk section not reviewed. Sources: https://www.paprec.com/app/uploads/2026/07/communique-de-presse-norme-groupe-pizzorno-environnement-opas.pdf ; https://www.boursedirect.fr/fr/actualites/categorie/resultats/pizzorno-environnement-rassure-par-son-carnet-de-commandes-boursier-c65dba45e85ee718c24f624591bed359e5745795
