thesis.business_description: Televerbier SA (registered in Verbier, municipality of Val de Bagnes, Valais, Switzerland; shares listed on Euronext Paris, ISIN CH0008175645) operates mechanical ski lifts in Verbier, La Tzoumaz and Bruson, the core of the Verbier 4 Vallees domain; it co-manages the Mont-Fort sector with NV Remontees mecaniques SA. Ski passes are ~73.8% of sales (aggregator figure); the rest is technical services, catering and accommodation. FY2024/25 (to 31 Oct 2025): revenue CHF 85.3m (vs 70.7m), net income CHF 4.1m (vs 1.0m), net debt CHF 35.8m; FY2025/26 target ~CHF 90m revenue and CHF 4.5-5.0m net income; H1 2025/26 revenue CHF 79.5m vs 75.5m. Sources: https://www.abcbourse.com/marches/resultats-annuels-20242025_690347 ; https://live.euronext.com/en/product/equities/CH0008175645-XPAR/company-information ; https://www.roic.ai/quote/TVRB.PA
thesis.competitive_position: Operator of the main lift company at Verbier, one of Switzerland's best-known ski destinations, which gives a local near-monopoly on lift access in its sectors; the 2023 annual report describes a ten-year commercial collaboration with Vail Resorts (pass partnership), not a takeover, and calls February 2023 buy-out talk 'false rumours'. No market-share or competitor data were found (research gap). Strategy details beyond capex on lifts were not reviewed. Sources: https://Verbier4vallees.ch/V4V-Website/About/TVSA/infos%20financi%C3%A8res/2022-2023/Te%CC%81le%CC%81verbier-RA2023-20240229.pdf ; https://www.letemps.ch/suisse/les-alpes-valaisannes-sont-elles-a-vendre
thesis.main_shareholders: Per Euronext company-information page (Cofisem data, updated March 2025; secondary summary of the page): Christian Burrus ~26.84%, Commune de Bagnes ~25.86%, Val de Bagnes/Entremont shareholder group 8.57%, resort shareholder group 4.53%, free float ~34.20%. thesis.business_description: MARR S.p.A. is a leading Italian marketer and distributor of food and non-food products to the foodservice (out-of-home) sector, serving over 55,000 customers, with more than half of revenue from 'street market' independent operators; other segments are national accounts (chains, groups, canteens) and wholesale. FY2025: revenue EUR 2,127.4m (vs 2,098.0m), EBITDA EUR 108.8m (120.2m), net income EUR 31.0m (42.7m), pre-IFRS16 net debt EUR 203.8m; proposed dividend EUR 0.47. H1 2026: revenue EUR 1,019.5m (994.8m), EBITDA EUR 39.1m (-17.9%), net profit EUR 3.9m (-69.3%), net debt incl. IFRS16 EUR 360.9m. Acquired Bergel+ Srl (Lombardy) in Jan 2026. thesis.competitive_position: Self-described leader in Italian foodservice distribution; an investor-presentation summary (secondary source) cites a 17% value share and 25% client share in the wholesaler segment, in an Italian foodservice market of EUR 103bn (2025) where independents are ~90%. An April 2026 notice for the 28 Apr 2026 AGM still states Cremonini at 50.42% and a group of institutional investors at 4.31%. A Consob page (July 2024) shows Cremonini with 66.308% of voting rights and Fidelity entities 5.207% - this differs from the capital-based figures (possibly voting rights vs capital, not reconciled). thesis.insider_ownership: Controlling shareholder is Cremonini S.p.A. (50.42%), itself controlled by Luigi Cremonini per Consob's shareholder page (the personal % was not retrieved). thesis.red_flags: Controlled by Cremonini (50.42%), which proposes the board slate (AGM 28 Apr 2026), so minority protection is limited. Profit deterioration: FY2025 net income down to EUR 31.0m from 42.7m; H1 2026 net profit -69.3% and Q1 2026 net loss; net debt (incl. IFRS16) rose to EUR 360.9m from EUR 296.0m a year earlier; dividend payout ratio 95.9% on FY2025. Exposure to cost inflation (fuel/energy) and consumer demand. Aggregator Quartr's Q1 2026 net profit figure contradicts company data and was disregarded. Annual-report risk and litigation sections not reviewed. thesis.business_description: mwb fairtrade Wertpapierhandelsbank AG is a German securities trading bank (HQ Munich area; AGM held in Munich) specialising in exchange trading: market making/specialist roles, designated sponsoring and related services, with a presence at Munich, Hamburg, Frankfurt, Hannover and Berlin exchanges (2023 investor presentation). thesis.business_description: Polish medical-technology group. It is the exclusive distributor of Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci surgical robots (Poland, Czechia, Slovakia, and per a search summary the Baltics; Ukraine scope also extended) and sells service and consumables on the installed base, and it makes radiopharmaceuticals (described as the largest radiopharmaceutical manufacturer/supplier in Poland) and specialised medical software. Other distributed devices (e.g. ZAP-X, Insightec) have developed slowly according to an analyst note. Exact segment split and HQ city were not confirmed in this search. Sources: https://xyz.pl/poland-unpacked/synektik-is-riding-polands-medical-robotics-wave-3173/ ; https://biznes.pap.pl/download/attachment/50917796/DOC.20250220.50917796.Synektik_Update_20022025.pdf
thesis.competitive_position: Named Intuitive Surgical's best da Vinci distributor worldwide in 2023 and again in 2025 (per search summaries of company/press items); installed base of 96 da Vinci robots across its markets at end-Dec 2024 (analyst note). Moat is the exclusive distribution agreement plus recurring instrument/service revenue, and a vertically integrated radiopharma business. Market cap reportedly rose from about PLN 300m (2023) to over PLN 3bn. The cardiac-tracer development business was spun off into Syn2bio S.A. (demerger by spin-off, 1:1 share allocation, 8,529,129 Syn2bio shares issued to Synektik holders); Synektik was valued at about PLN 2.11bn (PLN 247.54/share) at 30 Jun 2025 in the split valuation, of which transferred assets about PLN 163m (7.73%). Sources: https://xyz.pl/poland-unpacked/synektik-is-riding-polands-medical-robotics-wave-3173/ ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/145810,syn2bio-juz-na-parkiecie ; https://gessel.pl/en/case-studies/gessel-advised-on-the-listing-of-syn2bio-on-the-warsaw-stock-exchange/
thesis.main_shareholders: Cezary Kozanecki (founder, via Melhus Company Ltd and directly): Parkiet register data shows 2,047,380 shares (23.45%) as of 2026-03-12; per a Biznesradar headline dated 2026-08-21 he then sold about 615k shares (about 7.2%) off-session at PLN 350/share and says his holding is now 16.8% (these two figures do not reconcile exactly; verify against current ESPI filings). Ksiazek Holding sp. z o.o. 15.76% (Parkiet listing, date not stated; an older Biznesradar item said 16.1%). NN OFE 8.96% (Bankier/money.pl, as of 2026-01-20). thesis.insider_ownership: Founder/president Cezary Kozanecki holds about 16.8% (own statement per Biznesradar, Aug 2026; previously 23.45% per Parkiet at 2026-03-12) and says he intends to remain the largest long-term shareholder with no further sales planned. He is also Chairman of the Management Board of Syn2bio S.A. (Zonebourse). Holdings of other board members/executives were not located in this search; treat as a research gap. thesis.red_flags: Corporate action: EGM approved the split unanimously on 19 Mar 2026; Syn2bio S.A. (WSE: S2B) was spun off and listed on the main market (GESSEL says first trading 15 Apr 2026; MarketScreener had planned 16 Apr; one search summary said 2 Apr - dates conflict, 15 Apr is best supported). Synektik share price was mechanically adjusted for the distribution; do not read the drop as a loss of value. Concerns: founder sold about 7.2% in Aug 2026 (insider selling, though he retains about 16.8%); dependence on a single supplier/exclusive distribution agreement with Intuitive Surgical; a comparic.pl headline suggests management has guided to slower results growth after a very large share price run (about 20x in 3 years), i.e. valuation risk (headline only, not verified). No litigation or accounting issue found in these searches. thesis.business_description: Swiss lightweight-composites group headquartered in Steinhausen (Hinterbergstrasse 20, 6312 Steinhausen), operating through its 3A Composites division (brands include ALUCOBOND, AIREX, BALTEK, DIBOND). It develops, produces and distributes composites, synthetic sheets, foamboards and core materials based on balsa wood and PET foam for visual communication/display, architecture, wind energy, industry and shipbuilding. 2025 net sales CHF 904m (-11%; CHF 891m excluding the divested Bus & Rail unit); production and sales sites in Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific; roughly 4,100-4,500 employees (sources differ: company page about 4,100, Morningstar 4,534). Sources: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/02/27/3246260/0/en/Annual-Results-2025.html ; https://www.schweiter.ch/s1f12/group-structure/
thesis.competitive_position: Positions itself as a global player in lightweight composite and core materials with a broad portfolio (balsa and PET foam core for wind-blade, marine and industrial uses; aluminium composite panels for architecture and signage); 'global leader' wording is a company self-description (via Prospeo profile), not independently verified, and no market-share or named-competitor data was found in this search (research gap). Strategy: sharpen focus on lightweight composites tied to weight reduction, sustainable materials, renewable energy and mobility, and divest non-core operations. Balance sheet is strong: net cash CHF 56m and equity ratio 68% at end-2025, adjusted EBITDA CHF 74.3m (8.3% margin vs 9.4% in 2024), free operating cash flow CHF 39m, dividend proposal CHF 15 per share. Sources: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/02/27/3246260/0/en/Annual-Results-2025.html ; https://prospeo.io/c/3a-composites-core-materials

Other points: 2025 reported net income CHF -10.0m (vs +12.9m in 2024); sales and margins are falling in weak, cyclical end-markets (display, wind, construction); H1 2026 report guides full-year 2026 net sales below prior year but profitability above prior year; one sizeable blockholder (about 25.5%) limits free float. 2024 adjusted EBIT/EBITDA differ between the press release (EBIT CHF 48.5m) and annual report (CHF 45.6m) - a minor restatement/definition inconsistency to check. thesis.business_description: Dutch sustainable ('impact') bank headquartered in Driebergen-Rijsenburg, Netherlands, focused on renewable energy, social housing, healthcare, fair trade, organic food/farming and social development; lending is organised around five transition themes (energy, food, resource, societal, wellbeing). At end-2025: customer deposits EUR 15.1bn, business loans EUR 6.1bn, mortgages EUR 5.6bn (mostly Netherlands); net loans about EUR 11.5bn (data-site figure). Operations in several European countries; the German banking business is being wound down. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triodos_Bank ; https://www.triodos.com/en/press-releases/2026/2025-annual-results ; https://stockanalysis.com/quote/ams/TRIO/financials/balance-sheet/
thesis.competitive_position: Niche player: one of Europe's best-known values-based/sustainable banks, small versus mainstream Dutch banks (e.g. ING, Rabobank, ABN AMRO - named by me as general context, not from the sources). Strength is brand and a mission-driven deposit base; CET1 ratio 17.4% at end-2025 (16.4% in 2024), return on equity -2.0% in 2025. Strategy is to concentrate on core markets after exiting Germany (target completion 2027). Competitor and market-share data were not found in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.triodos.com/en/press-releases/2026/2025-annual-results ; https://triodos.prezly.com/triodos-bank-annual-results-2025
thesis.main_shareholders: 100% of the ordinary shares (14,467,056 shares) are held by the foundation Stichting Administratiekantoor Aandelen Triodos Bank (SAAT), which issues depositary receipts (DRs) to investors; per the AFM substantial-holdings register (transaction dated 18 Jun 2025, page updated 23 Jun 2026) and SAAT's 2025 report. DRs were admitted to Euronext Amsterdam on 18 Jun 2025 and governance was changed to 'one share one vote' with substitution rights for DR holders. A list of individual DR holders above 3% was not located in this search (Wikipedia's older 10% holder cap / 1,000-vote cap and 43,521 holders at end-2021 are stale and may no longer apply). Sources: https://www.afm.nl/en/sector/registers/meldingenregisters/substantiele-deelnemingen/details?id=176411 ; https://www.saatfoundation.com/binaries/content/assets/tbsf/reports/saat-report-2025_en.pdf
thesis.insider_ownership: Could not locate board/executive DR holdings or percentages in this search; treat as a research gap (the annual report remuneration/related-party sections would show them). Marcel Zuidam is quoted as CEO in the 2025 results release. Triodos is a widely held DR structure with no founder/family control identified. Source: https://triodos.prezly.com/triodos-bank-annual-results-2025
thesis.red_flags: 2025 net result EUR -25.0m, driven by a EUR 59.7m provision on German fibre-optic loans plus EUR 27.7m other provisions and about EUR 12m one-off costs for the German wind-down; no final dividend for 2025 (interim EUR 0.60 per DR only). Triodos announced in Sept 2025 it will close its German banking business (completion expected by end-2027). It sold its roughly EUR 180m German fibre-optic loan portfolio via an auction to Deutsche Bank (announced mid-May 2026; RaboResearch dates it 13 May, Banken.nl 19 May; expected one-off negative result about EUR 3m); H1 2026 results say the portfolio is fully sold (a third-party summary cites H1 2026 net profit of EUR 29.9m - secondary source). Credit-quality risk in concentrated sector lending. No takeover or delisting found. Structural note: shares are held 100% by SAAT, so DR holders have indirect rights only. thesis.business_description: Bulgarian chemicals/fertiliser producer based in Dimitrovgrad, founded in 1951. Products include nitrogen fertilisers (ammonium nitrate), ammonia, nitric acid, ammonium bicarbonate, aqueous ammonia, NPK, desalinated water, CO2 and oxygen; one profile also lists formalin and carbamide-formaldehyde resins and calls it Bulgaria's sole producer of several of these. Exports are said to be 40-60% of revenue (Romania, Turkey, Italy, USA named in one profile - not company-verified). FY2025 revenue about EUR 181.5m (+31%) with net income about EUR 0.4m after a 2024 loss (StockAnalysis aggregator, not the filed annual report). Q1 2026 revenue EUR 81.3m (+69%) and net income EUR 10.8m on high fertiliser prices (FFBH report); H1 2026 profit near EUR 11m (Capital.bg). Sources: https://stockanalysis.com/quote/bul/NEOH/financials/income-statement/ ; https://www.ffbham.bg/en/post/neochim-with-strong-start-of-the-year-q1-26-net-income-tops-eur-10-8m-positive--177744942645861 ; https://www.capital.bg/en/business/2026/09/03/4951269_manufacturing_companies_on_the_bulgarian_stock/
thesis.competitive_position: Regional nitrogen fertiliser and chemicals producer with a domestic-niche position (sole Bulgarian producer of some products, per a third-party profile) and an export business. Highly exposed to natural gas costs and fertiliser price cycles: the 2024 loss and the strong 2026 recovery reflect swings in input costs and selling prices (the Q1 2026 source ties the improvement to price spikes linked to the Middle East conflict). Sells through distribution agreements with related parties Euro Fert and Borealis (5-year deals approved per SeeNews). Market-share and named-competitor data were not found in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://profit.bg/article/2024012320155902175 ; https://seenews.com/news/bulgarias-neochim-gets-nod-to-sign-5-yr-distribution-deals-with-euro-fert-borealis-658797 ; https://www.ffbham.bg/en/post/neochim-with-strong-start-of-the-year-q1-26-net-income-tops-eur-10-8m-positive--177744942645861
thesis.main_shareholders: Ownership is split between three roughly equal blocks (FFBH/SeeNews, figures from around 2019-early 2025; no 2026 register was found): Eco Tech AD about 24.28%; Euro Fert AD about 24.03%; and the Agropolychim group, which indirectly holds about 24.02-24.03% via Reya Ventures (wholly owned by Agropolychim): 20.3% through Feboran (bought from AGROFERT, closed Jan 2025) plus about 3.725% held directly by Reya (bought Oct 2024). Earlier history: Feboran was a Borealis / First Energy Bank vehicle (2013); in 2004 Euro Fert held 48.36%. Percentages differ slightly between reports by date (e.g. Eco Tech 24.28% vs 24.37%). Check the FSC/BSE notifications for current numbers. thesis.insider_ownership: Could not locate named board/executive holdings or percentages in this search; treat as a research gap. The significant holders (Euro Fert AD, Eco Tech AD, Agropolychim/Reya Ventures) are corporate blockholders and related parties (Euro Fert is also a distribution counterparty); their ultimate beneficial owners were not identified in the results. Sources: https://www.ffbham.bg/en/post/agropolychim-could-acquire-20-in-neochim-the-company-shuts-additional-facilities-for-planned-maintenance-procedures-neutral--173554913221187 ; https://seenews.com/news/bulgarias-neochim-gets-nod-to-sign-5-yr-distribution-deals-with-euro-fert-borealis-658797
thesis.red_flags: Corporate action: Reya Ventures (wholly owned by Agropolychim) closed the purchase of Feboran (20.3% of Neochim) from AGROFERT in Jan 2025, after separately buying about 3.7% in Oct 2024, bringing the Agropolychim group to about 24%. Neochim publicly objected, saying this gives Agropolychim a blocking minority on decisions needing 2/3 or 3/4 of capital (single-source report, FFBH). The Competition Commission did not need to review the deal (below turnover threshold). No tender offer found. Other risks: no controlling holder - three roughly 24% blocks create potential deadlock/contested-control risk; related-party distribution contracts with Euro Fert; earnings highly volatile with gas and fertiliser prices (2024 loss, FY2025 net income only about EUR 0.4m, then a sharp 2026 rebound); planned plant shutdowns for maintenance have been reported. A CB Insights profile listing AGROFERT as an investor is outdated. No litigation or accounting issue found. thesis.business_description: Swedish IT infrastructure and services group (Nasdaq Stockholm: PACT) that describes itself as Europe's leading specialist in data and information management, focused on cloud services and data-centre solutions (systems/hardware resale plus managed and cloud services, support and consulting). Around 1,100 employees in 12 countries and 2,000+ active customers (company statements in the Q2 2026 report; an older description says 4,000+ customers). 2025 revenue SEK 4,678.8m (-3.8%), adjusted EBITA SEK 316.0m (6.8% margin vs 7.2%), profit before tax SEK 137.7m (278.0m). Segments: Nordics & Baltics SEK 2.6bn (58% of sales, +4.4%), West (Belgium, Netherlands) SEK 717.9m (-15.4%), Central (Germany, Czechia) SEK 671.7m (-24.4%), and the UK reported separately. thesis.competitive_position: Mid-sized European data-infrastructure and cloud-services integrator, strongest in the Nordics (58% of sales) where systems demand is high; weaker in West and Central Europe, where sales are falling. Strategy under CEO Magnus Lönn (first year 2025): improve profitability and focus, via bolt-on acquisitions (BlakYaks UK, Consular Denmark) and portfolio pruning. An ABG/Inderes analyst note says Proact continues to evaluate divesting the West and Central segments (analyst commentary, not a company announcement). Q2 2026 adjusted EBITA SEK 105m vs 76m a year earlier (Affarsvarlden headline). Competitor and market-share data were not found in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.inderes.fi/third-party-research/proact-much-to-like-abg ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/proact ; https://www.inderes.dk/releases/proact-has-completed-the-acquisition-of-consular
thesis.main_shareholders: Third-party data only (Simply Wall St, undated): Grenspecialisten AB 13.2% (3,400,000 shares), FMR LLC 8.89%, Alcur Fonder AB 6.7%, Handelsbanken Asset Management 6.66%; top 25 holders 63.9%. A second Simply Wall St listing shows different figures (Grenspecialisten 12.5%, Skandia Fonder 11.3%, Alcur 8.02%) - conflicting, so treat as approximate. Proact's own investor page is stale (31 Mar 2022: Grenspecialisten 3,107,334 shares, Livforsakrings AB Skandia 3,041,823 shares). The official Euroclear-based list is in the 2025 annual report, 'Shareholder information' section (p.121), which I could not read; a Finansinspektionen holding-change notice dated 27 Jul 2026 exists with details not seen. Recent small insider purchases are reported (e.g. Erik Malmberg bought 5,000 shares in Feb 2026). No named board/executive holdings with percentages or founder/family control were located; treat as a research gap (see annual report). thesis.red_flags: Earnings pressure in 2025 (adjusted EBITA -9.9%, profit before tax roughly halved, West and Central sales down 15-24%); leadership transition (new CEO 2025, interim CFO in July 2026). M&A items from the screen, with discrepancies: (1) Consular ApS (Denmark): completion confirmed by Proact; deal announced 21 Oct 2025, target revenue about DKK 86m LTM; the DKK 65m price was not verified in my searches. (2) Sepago: the search found the sepago (Germany) acquisition announced June 2022 for EUR 12m plus a EUR 4m earn-out and completed 2022 - this conflicts with the screen note of a July 2026 acquisition, which I could not confirm; likely a mis-dated or different item, verify. (3) Dutch staffing sale to Resultaatgroep: only a PitchBook listing dated 4 May 2026 was found, no press release - unverified. No bid for Proact found. No litigation or accounting issues found. name: Caisse Régionale de Crédit Agricole Mutuel de Normandie-Seine Société coopérative
gmSourceUrl: [Caisse Régionale de Crédit Agricole Mutuel de Normandie-Seine official semi-annual report S1 2025](https://www.ca-normandie-seine.fr/Vitrine/ObjCommun/Fic/NormandieSeine/pdf/RapportFinancier/CANS_Rapport_financier_semestriel_S1_2025.pdf), [2023 annual financial report](https://www.ca-normandie-seine.fr/Vitrine/ObjCommun/Fic/NormandieSeine/pdf/RapportFinancier/RFA-2023.pdf)

thesis.business_description: French regional cooperative retail bank (Caisse Regionale de Credit Agricole Mutuel de Normandie-Seine, part of the Credit Agricole network; formed from the merger of Credit Agricole de Normandie, formerly based in Caen, with the Seine entity). The listed security is its cooperative investment certificate (CCI, ticker CCN, ISIN FR0000044364), one of 13 CCI issuers on Euronext Paris. Network of 71 local banks (caisses locales) and 130 branches; about 692,500 customers and 500,000 insurance contracts (FinanzWire summary of the FY2025 release); at end-2025 loans about EUR 17.2bn and savings/deposits about EUR 22.8bn. Retail, SME, agricultural and insurance banking in Normandy. Sources: https://www.easybourse.com/action-societe/crcam-norm-seine/profil/FR0000044364-25 ; https://live.euronext.com/de/product/equities/FR0000044364-XPAR/company-information ; https://webdisclosure.com/article/credit-agricole-de-normandie-seine-epa-ccn-solid-annual-results-for-credit-agricole-normandie-seine-in-2025-lkEFeelb9Ic
thesis.competitive_position: Large regional incumbent in Normandy within the Credit Agricole mutualist group, with an extremely strong capital base: CET1 24.76% and total capital ratio 25.02% at June 2025 (Pillar 3 summary), and Basel III solvency ratio 25.88% reported for FY2025 (FinanzWire; the two figures come from different dates/measures). FY2025 net banking income EUR 378.9m (+EUR 22.4m), operating costs EUR 259.1m, cost of risk EUR 33.8m. Net income is reported inconsistently: EUR 70m (+6%) per the FinanzWire/company release summary versus about EUR 86m (+8.8%) per the Ideal-Investisseur aggregator - could not reconcile; check the official release. Competitor and market-share data not found in this search (research gap). thesis.main_shareholders: Could not locate the capital breakdown (CCI / CCA certificates, parts sociales, Credit Agricole S.A. stake, free float) in this search; treat as a research gap. What is known: the entity is a cooperative with variable capital whose member shares (parts sociales, nominal EUR 1.50) are issued by its local banks; one source describes it as operating as a subsidiary of Credit Agricole S.A. without giving a stake. thesis.insider_ownership: Could not locate named board/executive holdings in this search; treat as a research gap. As a cooperative, the board is drawn from local-bank members, and the bank has noted in an AMF filing (2018) that it cannot fully apply AFEP-MEDEF corporate-governance principles because of its cooperative form. Names of the chair and general manager were not found. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/CNS/2018/03/FCCNS161783_20180302.pdf
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources. Standard caveats: (1) the CCI is non-voting and the issuer is controlled through the cooperative Credit Agricole structure, so minority holders have limited influence and dividends depend on regional-bank decisions; (2) thin free float / small market cap (about EUR 156m, undated) implies low liquidity; (3) regional retail-bank exposure (cost of risk EUR 33.8m in FY2025; real estate, agriculture and household credit cycle); (4) reported FY2025 net income conflicts between sources (EUR 70m vs about EUR 86m) - verify. No takeover, litigation or accounting issue found. thesis.business_description: Dutch energy-transition equipment company headquartered in Almere, Netherlands, that develops, produces and sells smart grid solutions, energy storage systems and electric-vehicle chargers. Three segments: EV Charging, Smart Grid Solutions (grid equipment for Dutch grid operators) and Energy Storage Systems. FY2025 revenue EUR 435.6m (-10.7% vs EUR 487.6m): EV Charging -21.2% (competitive pressure), Smart Grid -10.2% (grid-operator labour shortages and regulatory constraints), Energy Storage +1.6%. thesis.competitive_position: Established Dutch/European supplier across charging, grid and storage, but under pressure: EV Charging is losing share/price to competition per the company, and mid-term targets were tempered in H1 2025. FY2025 adjusted gross margin EUR 122.5m (28.1%), adjusted EBITDA EUR 25.5m (5.8% margin vs EUR 28.5m in 2024). Q4 2025 started a company-wide transformation from a functional to a business-unit organisation. 2026 guidance: revenue EUR 435-475m, adjusted EBITDA margin 4-7%, capex below 4% of revenue; an aggregator (StockAnalysis) reports Q1 2026 revenue up about 25% and guidance reiterated (not verified against company release). thesis.business_description: NTT System S.A. is a Polish manufacturer of desktop PCs, servers (Tytan, Atlas, Storage lines) and network devices, sold under own brands and made to order for third parties, and also a distributor of accessories, components and peripherals (brands cited by one aggregator include Lenovo, Motorola, MSI, Microsoft, Acer, Intel, AMD, HP). Own brands include HIRO (gaming) and Blue Bolt (smart home); notebooks under NTT Book were relaunched after a pause. Founded 1991; seat at Zakret, Trakt Brzeski 89, 05-077 Warszawa-Wesola, Poland; primary market is Poland. 2024 group revenue was PLN 1,489.3m with net profit PLN 21.2m (management commentary, 2024 annual report). thesis.business_description: Zaklady Magnezytowe ROPCZYCE S.A. (Ropczyce, Poland) produces ceramic refractory materials used as structural lining of high-temperature furnaces: burned shaped products (magnesia, magnesia-chrome, magnesia-spinel, magnesia-zirconia, forsterite, zirconia, alumina-chrome), unburned shaped and unshaped products. Customers are mainly steel, plus non-ferrous metals, cement/lime, glass, foundry and coking. Subsidiaries include Ropczyce Engineering and ZM Nieruchomosci. Group revenue was PLN 429.8m in 2024 (operating profit PLN 6.8m) and PLN 394.4m in 2025 (-8.2%, net profit PLN 8.1m); exports were 61% of sales in H1 2024 and 68% in Q1 2025. Sources: https://strefainwestorow.pl/wiadomosci/20240816/zm-ropczyce-podsumowuja-i-polrocze-2024-roku-stabilnosc-mimo-globalnych-wyzwan ; https://compabase.com/companies/krs/0000036048 ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/wiadomosci/ROPCZYCE
thesis.competitive_position: Niche Polish refractory producer with a large export share. The 2024 management commentary says growing competition from Asian producers significantly affected the refractory market. The CEO is Jozef Siwiec (2018 and 2024 company commentary). No market-share data or named direct competitors were located in this search (research gap); the company claims no verified leadership position in the sources found. Sources: https://strefainwestorow.pl/wiadomosci/20250428/zaklady-magnezytowe-ropczyce-sa-stabilne-mimo-globalnych-wyzwan-prawie-430-mln ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/128817,jozef-siwiec-zm-ropczyce-nasze-dzialania-w-pierwszej-polowie-2024-r-koncentrowaly-sie-na-utrzymaniu-wolumenu-sprzedazy
thesis.main_shareholders: Shareholder agreement of 10 Feb 2021 (Interminex Handelsgesellschaft m.b.H. of Vienna, Jozef Siwiec, Marian Darlak) holds 3,943,035 shares = 62.99% of 6,259,634 shares (Stockwatch, change dated 31 Dec 2024, page updated 27 Apr 2025; aggregator). Individual split not shown there. Earlier official data: at the 28 Aug 2020 AGM Interminex had 1,317,316 shares (21.04%), Siwiec 1,277,000 (20.40%), Darlak 497,413 (7.95%). CONFLICT: a 2021 filing said the parties held 5,201,809 shares = 83.10% (tied to a tender offer for 1,057,825 shares at PLN 26.73, Mar-Apr 2021, aiming for 71.99% and delisting); the current 62.99% is lower and the reason was not located. Sources: https://www.stockwatch.pl/gpw/ROPCZYCE,akcjonariat,dane-finansowe.aspx ; https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art26975751-ropczyce-wykaz-akcjonariuszy-posiadajacych-co-najmniej-5-liczby-glosow-na-zwyczajnym-walnym-zgromadzeniu-spolki-w-dniu-28-sierpnia-2020-r ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/97758,akcjonariusze-zm-ropczyce-oglosili-wezwanie-na-1-057-825-akcji-spolki
thesis.insider_ownership: Jozef Siwiec (CEO) is a party to the controlling shareholder agreement and held 1,277,000 shares (20.40%) at the 2020 AGM; his current individual holding was not located. Marian Darlak held 497,413 shares (7.95%) in 2020 (his role at the company was not confirmed in the sources found). Together with Interminex the group holds about 63% (Stockwatch, Dec 2024). Sources: https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art26975751-ropczyce-wykaz-akcjonariuszy-posiadajacych-co-najmniej-5-liczby-glosow-na-zwyczajnym-walnym-zgromadzeniu-spolki-w-dniu-28-sierpnia-2020-r ; https://www.stockwatch.pl/gpw/ROPCZYCE,akcjonariat,dane-finansowe.aspx
thesis.red_flags: Controlled by a shareholder-agreement bloc with about 63% (free float about 37%); a 2021 tender offer by the bloc was linked to an intention to withdraw the shares from the exchange (the stock is still listed and reporting in 2026, so this did not complete in the sources seen). Unexplained fall from 83.10% (2021) to 62.99% in the bloc's reported stake. Weak profitability: 2024 consolidated net loss of about PLN 1.05m (AGM draft resolutions), revenue down 8.2% in 2025, and pricing pressure from Asian producers. Exports are a large share of sales (61-68%), adding customer-industry (steel) cyclicality. Sources: https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/ROPCZYCE-Projekty-uchwal-Zwyczajnego-Walnego-Zgromadzenia-Spolki-8953566.html ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/97758,akcjonariusze-zm-ropczyce-oglosili-wezwanie-na-1-057-825-akcji-spolki ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/wiadomosci/ROPCZYCE

thesis.business_description: Castings P.L.C. is a UK iron casting and machining group: ductile (SG) iron, austempered ductile iron, SiMo, grey iron and Ni-resist castings (0.15 kg to 7 tonnes), with foundries at Brownhills (West Midlands) and William Lee (Dronfield, Derbyshire) plus the CNC Speedwell machining arm; sources conflict on whether a third foundry (Castings Ductile, Scunthorpe) still operates. Main end-markets are commercial vehicles (heavy trucks), automotive and other industrial/wind. Registered office: Lichfield Road, Brownhills WS8 6JZ. FY to 31 Mar 2026 (final results 17 Jun 2026): revenue GBP 173.2m (-2.1%), profit from operations GBP 10.0m (+109%), pre-tax profit GBP 10.3m, basic EPS 17.36p, net cash GBP 17.4m, total dividend 18.40p. Sources: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/castings--cgs/final-results/9621754 ; https://themachinemaker.com/news/castings-plc-improves-profitability-despite-softer-sales/ ; https://www.castmetalsfederation.com/foundry/castings-plc ; https://www.financialfilings.com/companies/castings-plc/
thesis.competitive_position: Describes itself as a market-leading UK iron casting and machining group. FY2026 foundry output 41,500 tonnes (+1.2%); foundry segment profit GBP 6.4m; CNC Speedwell sales GBP 30.6m with segment profit GBP 2.4m. A new line at William Lee (about 12,000 tonnes, roughly 15% of gross foundry capacity) was commissioned in Q4 FY2026. Outlook cited: potential 5-10% rise in customer schedules including new wind-energy work (customer indication, not a guarantee). Margin recovery came from efficiency, not volume (heavy-truck sales still depressed). Named competitors and customers were not located in this search (research gap). Sources: https://themachinemaker.com/news/castings-plc-improves-profitability-despite-softer-sales/ ; https://kalkine.co.uk/news/industrials/castings-adds-15-foundry-capacity-while-holding-its-184p-full-year-dividend
thesis.main_shareholders: Official 2026 holdings table (annual report/TR-1) was NOT located; data below are dated and partly from aggregators. Simply Wall St (about June 2025, aggregator): Columbia Management 17.1%, Aberforth Partners 15.3%, Ruffer 8.91%, Unicorn 6.63%, Janus Henderson 5.97%, Brian Cooke 4.62%, Nathaniel Rothschild 4.14%. RNS-based reports: Ameriprise Financial (Threadneedle) 14.664% after 17 Feb 2025 (another report says 15.078% on 26 Feb 2025 - conflicting); Aberforth 14.14% at 8 Jul 2024 (TipRanks summary). Treat as indicative. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/materials/lse-cgs/castings-shares/ownership ; https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/ameriprise-financial-increases-stake-in-castings-plc ; https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/castings-plc-stake-increased-by-aberforth-partners
thesis.insider_ownership: Finance Director Steve Mant made a Bed & ISA transfer (RNS 23 Jul 2026); total beneficial holding stated unchanged (share count not located). Executive director Adam Vicary bought 5,000 shares in Mar 2026 (Simply Wall St, aggregator). Simply Wall St lists Brian Cooke at 4.62% (his board role was not confirmed in these results). Board per ticker.app: seven directors including Steven Mant, Adam Vicary, Mark Smith and Stephen Harrison; Directors' interests table from the annual report was not located. Sources: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/castings--cgs/director-pdmr-shareholding/9684775 ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/materials/lse-cgs/castings-shares/ownership ; https://www.ticker.app/lse/CGS
thesis.red_flags: No governance or accounting issues identified from the sources reached. Risks: heavy dependence on the cyclical commercial-vehicle/heavy-truck market (sales still near depressed levels); energy-intensive foundry operations (standard sector caveat); institutional concentration (several holders above 5-17%, per dated data). Board change: Andrew Eastgate retired and Mark Smith became senior independent director per Simply Wall St, while ticker.app lists Stephen Harrison as SID - conflicting. Annual report date also conflicts (7 Jul 2026 vs 29 Jun 2026). Sources: https://themachinemaker.com/news/castings-plc-improves-profitability-despite-softer-sales/ ; https://www.financialfilings.com/companies/castings-plc/ ; https://www.ticker.app/lse/CGS

thesis.business_description: SAF Tehnika A/S (Riga, Latvia; listed on Nasdaq Riga) makes digital microwave point-to-point radio links (Integra family, plus portable Phantom), Spectrum Compact spectrum analyzers and the Aranet wireless IoT sensor line for environmental monitoring and building automation, produced at its Riga plant. FY2024/25 (1 Jul 2024-30 Jun 2025): group net turnover about EUR 25.99m (about -4% y/y), parent turnover EUR 21.92m, exports about 97% of group turnover. Founding year conflicts across company pages (1996 vs 1999). Sources: https://new.saftehnika.com/news-posts/audited-statements-and-corporate-governance-report-of-saf-tehnika-for-financial-year-2024-2025 ; https://www.saftehnika.com/company/about-us ; https://saftehnika.com/company ; https://dasenic.com/manufacturers/saf-tehnika
thesis.competitive_position: Niche supplier of licensed microwave links; company says it has stayed profitable through most of the past 15+ years (2015-16 yearbook, self-reported) and that demand for high-data-rate radios persists despite fibre (2022-23 annual report). Competitors named in a 2011 filing were Nokia Siemens, Ericsson, Alcatel and NEC (dated); CB Insights lists CG Wireless and Trango Networks. Aranet is the diversification into IoT. No current market-share figures located (research gap). Sources: https://support.saftehnika.com/upload/file/SAF_Yearbook_2015-16_edit.pdf ; https://support.saftehnika.com/upload/file/Anual_Report_SAF%20Tehnika_2022-2023_ENG.pdf ; https://www.cbinsights.com/company/saf-tehnika

Supervisory Council (re-elected 4 Dec 2024 for three years): Juris Ziema (8.71% holder), Andrejs Grisans, Ivars Senbergs, Sanda Reiharde, Aira Loite; holdings of the latter four were not located. thesis.business_description: Mersen S.A. (listed on Euronext Paris; results issued from Paris) makes graphite and other advanced materials and electrical protection/power-management products in two segments: Advanced Materials (graphite specialties, silicon carbide, carbon fibre insulation, carbon-carbon composites, anti-corrosion equipment; about 56% of 2022 sales) and Electrical Power (industrial fuses, fuse holders, surge protection, power management/cooling). FY2025 sales EUR 1,186m (organic -3.2%): Advanced Materials EUR 613m (organic -10.6%, EBITDA margin before non-recurring 18.2% vs 21.4%), Electrical Power EUR 573m (organic +6.0%, margin 17.0% vs 14.0%); group EBITDA margin before non-recurring 16%. CEO Luc Themelin. Sources: https://us.mersen.com/en/group/news-and-events/mersen-sales-eu12-billion-2025-line-expectations ; https://tedmag.com/mersen-reports-resilient-performance-in-2025 ; https://www.globaldata.com/company-profile/mersen-sa/analysis/
thesis.competitive_position: Company materials list competitors as SGL Carbon, Tokai Carbon, Toyo Tanso and Morgan Advanced Materials (Advanced Materials) and Eaton, Littelfuse and others (Electrical Power), and claim leadership positions with 15-30% market shares and No. 2 worldwide in industrial fuses (2021 deck; self-reported and dated). Exposure to solar and silicon-carbide semiconductor end-markets drove the 2025 Advanced Materials decline, while Electrical Power (including fuses for power conversion) grew. Sources: https://mersen.com/sites/default/files/files_imported/2024-01-ps-en-pres-mersen.pdf ; https://fr.mersen.com/sites/default/files/files_imported/2021-01-ps-en-mersen-oddo.pdf ; https://www.mersen.com/sites/default/files/medias/financial_results/2026-03/2026-03-ps-en-Presentation-Mersen-Results.pdf
thesis.main_shareholders: Mersen website ownership page, position at 31/12/2025 (24,418,312 shares): Bpifrance 10.8% of capital / 18.0% of voting rights; other French institutions 24.7% / 22.4%; international institutions 42.9% / 38.7%; individuals incl. employees 21.3% / 20.9%; treasury shares 0.3%. Double voting rights apply to shares held two years or more. At 31/12/2023 Bpifrance was 10.8% / 18.1% and Amiral Gestion 5.1% / 4.6% (no longer listed in the 2025 table). Sources: https://us.mersen.com/en/investors/ownership-structure ; https://fr.mersen.com/investors/ownership-structure
thesis.insider_ownership: Director/executive percentage holdings were not located (they sit in the governance section of the 2025 URD, pp. 27 ff.). Bpifrance Participations holds a board seat (mandate renewed at the 12 May 2026 AGM; Jean-Philippe Puig appointed director and Florence Lambert's co-optation ratified). Employees are included in the 21.3% individual/employee bucket without separate breakdown. Sources: https://www.mersen.com/sites/default/files/medias/financial_results/2026-03/2026-03-urd-fr-document-enregistrement-universel-mersen-2025.pdf ; https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/ECO/2026/05/FCECO081973_20260512.pdf
thesis.red_flags: FY2025 net income group share only about EUR 14m after about EUR 45m of non-cash asset impairments; non-recurring expenses rose to EUR 52.7m from 23.5m and operating income before non-recurring items fell to EUR 109.1m from 131.1m. Advanced Materials sales fell 10.6% organically on weak solar and SiC semiconductor demand (cyclical/tech-cycle exposure). Net debt was EUR 370m at end-2024 (1.8x EBITDA); the end-2025 figure was not located. Bpifrance holds 18% of votes via double voting. Sources: https://mersen.com/sites/default/files/medias/financial_results/2025-03/2025-03-pr-fr-resultats-annuels-Mersen.pdf ; https://www.mersen.com/sites/default/files/medias/financial_results/2026-03/2026-03-pr-fr-Resultats-annuels-Mersen.pdf ; https://tedmag.com/mersen-reports-resilient-performance-in-2025
